## Client Portal — master plan + Phase 1 request lifecycle (2026-07-25, gated on 0017, verified on dev-preview)
Wrote `CLIENT_PORTAL_MASTER_PLAN.md` (research + full architecture; evolves the existing magic-link
portal, doesn't rewrite it). User approved building Phase 1 and chose to stay anonymous-link-only
(no email OTP). Built the **Client Request → Internal Task lifecycle** end-to-end:
- **Decision states** on `client_requests`: pending · needs_info · approved · declined. **Delivery
  state** (In progress/Completed) is DERIVED from the linked task's `done` — never stored — so the
  client's badge tracks real work honestly (`lib/request-status.ts` `clientRequestLabel`).
- Owner inbox (`components/projects/requests-tab.tsx` v2): **Approve → task** (two-way link via
  `tasks.request_id` ⇄ `client_requests.task_id`, shows a "Linked task · In progress/Completed"
  chip), **Decline** with a reason the client reads, **Request more info** (opens a client-facing
  thread), Reopen, and an internal/again client-facing note composer (Switch "Visible to client").
- Client portal (`components/portal/portal-document.tsx`): a **"Your requests"** section shows live
  status + resolution reason + the team↔client thread + a reply box (flips needs_info → pending).
  No login — the submitter's request ids live in `localStorage` (`zb:portal:reqs:<token>`); status
  is fetched by id via the token-scoped `getClientRequestStatuses` (random-uuid id = the capability).
- Shared `components/portal/request-thread.tsx` (bubble list, internal tag). Actions reworked in
  `lib/actions/portal.ts` (approve/decline/requestMoreInfo/reopen/postRequestMessage +
  submitClientRequest returns id + submitClientReply + getClientRequestStatuses; retired
  acceptRequestAsTask/updateClientRequestStatus). Loader `lib/projects-data.ts` + realtime-sync +
  `types/database.ts` updated. Migration `0017_portal_requests_lifecycle.sql` DRAFTED, **NOT applied**
  (widen status + map legacy, +title/client_id/task_id/resolution_note/updated_at+trigger,
  tasks.request_id, request_messages table + owner-RLS + realtime). Graceful degrade: requests list
  empty until applied. **tsc clean · 88/88 tests pass ·** verified both dev-previews (owner inbox all
  4 states + Add-note Switch; portal Your-requests In progress/Needs input+reply/Declined+reason).

## Notifications — the shell bell, wired end-to-end (2026-07-26, gated on 0021, verified)
Master-plan §7O in-app channel + the last missing piece of form-builder F3. The `notifications`
table + owner RLS have existed since 0001 but were never written or read; the shell Bell was
hardcoded `notifCount = 0`. Now:
- **Emit** — `lib/notify.ts` `notifyOwner(svc, {userId, kind, title, body?, link})` — ONE best-effort
  insert (never throws, never gates the caller's action). Wired into the four PUBLIC events, each of
  which already resolves the owner token-scoped: portal `submitClientRequest` (kind `portal.request`),
  `submitClientReply` (`portal.reply`), `submitApprovalDecision` (`portal.approval`), and forms
  `submitResponse` (`form.response`, folded into the renamed `onResponseComplete` alongside the
  client-activity log so it's still one fetch). Each carries a `link.href` (`/projects/<id>` or
  `/forms/<id>/responses`). Owner id comes from the project/form we already looked up — never a
  caller-supplied user id; service role writes it, owner RLS reads it back.
- **Surface** — `components/shell/notifications-bell.tsx` replaces the inline placeholder in
  app-shell TopBar (kept the exact button + berry-badge chrome, Figma 1:764). RLS-scoped browser
  client fetches the 20 most-recent; unread count in the one berry badge (capped `9+`); panel lists
  rows (berry dot + bright title when unread, muted when read; body + relative time; truncation);
  click marks-read then navigates `link.href`; "Mark all read". Subscribes to a `zb-notifications`
  realtime channel for live INSERTs. Optional `demo` prop skips the network for the dev-preview.
- **Migration `0021_notifications_realtime.sql`** DRAFTED, **NOT applied**: adds `notifications` to
  the realtime publication + a `(user_id, read, created_at desc)` index. Table/RLS already live from
  0001. **Graceful degrade:** without 0021 the bell still fetches on open — it just isn't instant.
- **Deep-link** — portal notifications link to `/projects/<id>?tab=portal` (not just `/projects/<id>`),
  so clicking one lands the owner on the Portal request inbox that fired the bell. `[id]/page.tsx`
  reads `searchParams.tab` (validated against the `DetailTab` union, now exported) → `initialTab` prop
  → `ProjectsWorkspace` inits/syncs its tab. Form notifications already point at `/forms/<id>/responses`.
- tsc clean · 123 tests pass · verified on **/dev-preview/notifications** (badge "3", populated
  panel, Mark-all-read clears dots + badge, zero console errors) and **/dev-preview/projects** with
  `initialTab="portal"` (lands on the Portal request inbox).

## Goal rollup — the linked project finally counts (2026-07-26, no migration, verified)
Master-plan §7G/§3.2 ("goal ← projects/tasks · progress rolls up at review time"). The rollup was
already wired into the weekly review (rituals page calls `recomputeGoalProgress`), and the Horizon
card already had a project-link `<select>` + a ring — but **the linked project (`goals.project_id`)
contributed nothing**: both the display counts and the recompute only tallied `tasks.goal_id`, which
has no UI to set. So linking a goal to a project showed a chip and 0%.
- **`lib/goal-rollup.ts`** — ONE pure rule shared by all three consumers so they can't disagree: a
  goal's work = its steps (milestones) + directly linked tasks (`tasks.goal_id`) + **every top-level
  task in its linked project** (`goals.project_id` → `tasks.project_id`), deduped by task id;
  subtasks excluded (they roll into their parent). Exports `rollupTallies` / `tallyToProgress` /
  `computeBehind`. **14 unit tests** (`lib/goal-rollup.test.ts`).
- `recomputeGoalProgress` (goals.ts) refactored onto it — its task query now also pulls the linked
  projects' tasks (`.or(goal_id.not.is.null, project_id.in.(…))`).
- Horizon page (`app/(app)/horizon/page.tsx`) uses the same rule for `linkedDone/linkedTotal` (task
  count only — steps stay a separate "N/M steps" label). `goalFrac` already preferred `linkedTotal`
  for the ring, so a project-linked goal now **fills its ring live** from the project's completion.
- Weekly-review glance shows each goal's freshly-reconciled `progress %` (RGoal + rituals select).
- tsc clean · **137 tests pass** · verified on new **/dev-preview/horizon**: "Ship the rebrand"
  (linked to Balluji rebrand) → 60% ring + "3/5 tasks" + project chip; steps-only goal → "1/2 steps".

## Two visibility bugs fixed (2026-07-20, verified)
1. Documents "Trash" folder was literally labeled **"Trash2"** (the lucide icon component name leaked into 3 strings: rail item label, header, empty-state copy in documents-view.tsx). → "Trash".
2. **Workspace/account menu popover was clipped when the sidebar is collapsed.** Root cause: the popover was a `position:absolute` child inside the Sidebar root, which has `overflow:hidden` — so on the ~54px collapsed rail the ~230px popover got cut off (text showed as "WORK…"/"desi…"). VERIFIED collapsed at 1100px — menu now renders fully.
Known pre-existing nit (not fixed, out of scope): the "WORKSPACES" menu label uses font-mono, which the constitution's SectionLabel rule forbids (sans only).

### Projects layout rebuilt to editorial "memory surface" (2026-07-20, verified desktop+tablet)
The old Projects detail looked AI-generated (row of 4 giant stat tiles + 3 equal Panel cards + hero % bar). Rebuilt after LINEAR's project-overview layout, per MASTER_PRODUCT_PLAN §7E. This is now the STANDARD layout language for hub detail views — reuse it:
- KILL stat-tile rows. Header = title row + a quiet inline PROPERTY STRIP under it (middot-separated facts: `N open · N done this week · Nh logged · due <date> · Shared`), tabular-nums on numbers, PropDot separator. No giant metric tiles on a solo detail view.
- Overview = editorial two-column (`flex flex-col gap-8 lg:flex-row`): MAIN reading column (`lg:max-w-[640px]`) + right DETAILS rail (`lg:w-56 lg:border-l lg:pl-6`, NO fill — just a border, Linear-style).
- Main column sections separated by `border-t border-line-soft pt-6`, each led by `sectionLabel`: (1) STATUS — the owner-written latest activity note as an editorial `text-body-lg` sentence ("the sentence is the hill chart"), "Updated <rel>", + composer to post a new one; (2) PROGRESS — one quiet line `{done}/{total} done` + thin `<Progress>` bar, NO hero %; (3) KEY TASKS — flat rows, hairline dividers, no card-in-card; (4) ACTIVITY — DSActivityFeed.
- Details rail = DetailRow (label left ink-500, value right ink-800): Status badge · Client · Deadline · Started.
- Removed Panel/PanelHeader/PanelBody usage from projects-workspace (import dropped). Overview now takes project/notes/createdAt/deadline props. dev-preview/projects harness enriched (TASKS+ACTIVITY+activitySupported) for verification.
### ScrollArea nested-scrollbar root-cause fix (2026-07-20, DS-level, verified)
Bug: project tab bar showed BOTH a horizontal scrollbar under the tabs AND a vertical one beside them (nested-scroll feedback loop). Root cause was NOT the tabs — it was `components/ds/ui/scroll-area.tsx` setting only ONE axis to `overflow: auto`. Per CSS spec, when one axis is `auto` and the other is left `visible`, the browser COERCES the visible axis to `auto` too → spurious scrollbars whenever content sub-pixel-overflows the cross axis (the Tabs' absolute underline at `-bottom-px` triggered a 1px vertical overflow → vertical bar → stole width → `min-w-full` list overflowed x → horizontal bar). This latently affected EVERY ScrollArea in the app.
Fixes: (1) ScrollArea now pins the cross-axis: `axis==='x' → overflow-x-auto overflow-y-hidden`, `axis==='y' → overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden` (hidden+auto never coerces). (2) Added `hideScrollbar` prop + `.zb-no-scrollbar` utility in globals.css (scrollbar-width:none + ::-webkit-scrollbar hidden) — used by Tabs so the horizontal tab-scroll pattern shows NO bar, only the fade mask. (3) Tabs underline `-bottom-px`→`bottom-0` so overflow-y:hidden can't clip it. (4) projects-workspace: tab row de-nested (was flex+spacer+inline SegmentedControl → plain full-width `<Tabs>`; the List/Board/Calendar switcher moved INTO the Tasks panel, right-aligned); property strip gap `mb-7`→`mb-5`; rail + detail scroll containers got explicit `overflow-x-hidden` (same coercion class of bug). (5) Overview polish (make-interfaces-feel-better skill): status empty-state = inviting composer (Linear "write first update"), `text-pretty` on status prose, `text-balance` on project title, Pencil icon on the status composer.
VERIFIED (JS-inspected computed styles + screenshots desktop/tablet/mobile): tab scroller now overflowX auto / overflowY hidden, scrollW==clientW & scrollH==clientH on desktop (no bars); at 375px tabs degrade to hidden-scrollbar horizontal-only scroll and the PAGE has zero horizontal overflow.

Implements the CRM feedback-loop the user referenced (talk → get feedback → log → **ship** → close-deal → repeat). Feedback is a first-class object that ranks product work by the **revenue of the deals that want it**, and "Ship it" turns a feedback item into a task — the master-plan "fabric" thesis made concrete. Lives as a **third tab in Clients** (`Clients | Pipeline | Feedback`), no new top-level nav (IA-preserving).

App degrades gracefully: the Clients page queries no-op (`data:null`) until applied, so the Feedback tab just shows empty — nothing breaks.

- **UI** `components/feedback/feedback-board.tsx` (`FeedbackBoard` + `FeedbackCard` + `AddFeedbackModal`): 4 columns (Open/Planned/In progress/Shipped), cards **sorted by $ at stake desc** (top of Open = highest-revenue thing to build next), green Shipped column matching PipelineBoard, card meta `#num · title · $rollup · N deals · source`, forward actions Plan→ / Ship it (Rocket) / Mark shipped. Capture modal has a deal checklist with a **live "$X at stake"** total. Card style matches LeadCard (`rounded-lg bg-surface-raised p-3`).

## Design-precision sweep (user directive 2026-07-23) — raise the whole app to a reference-grade precision/alignment/consistency bar
The user sent 4 reference images (a Figma-style toolbar, Agently dark serif SaaS, Orra light AI app, a dark chat composer) + a precision checklist (layout, alignment, spacing, sizing, hierarchy, type, icon sizing, radii, borders, consistency, small details). The references share **precision & grid discipline**, NOT one style (they contradict — serif vs sans, dark vs light). **Interpretation (stated to user, invited correction): raise precision/alignment/consistency to that bar WITHIN Zenboard's B&G language — not a serif/pill/light restyle.** Method: fix at the **design-system level** (tokens + `components/ds/ui`) so changes propagate; audit screen-by-screen against the constitution's exact specs (row heights 32/36/44, buttons 28/32/36, type scale, icon 16/20 @1.75, one accent, tabular-nums numbers). This is a multi-pass loop.

### Pass 1 (2026-07-23, tsc clean, verified) — numbers: kill mono display figures (propagates to every KPI)
Audit of `/dev-preview/money` at 1440w surfaced a glaring flaw: the big KPI values rendered **"$4 , 300" / "$6 , 000"** — wide gaps around the thousands comma — while the table totals ("$3,200") read tight. Root cause: the shared DS **`Stat`** renders its value `font-mono text-title-1` (Geist Mono), and at 30px a monospace comma sits in a full fixed-width cell. This both **violates the enforced constitution** ("Numbers in stats and tables: tabular-nums" · "NEVER monospace, except invoice/ID strings like INV-001") and looks broken.
- **Fix (DS-level, propagates to ALL stat tiles app-wide):** `components/ds/ui/stat.tsx` value span `font-mono text-title-1` → `text-title-1 tabular-nums` (sans + tabular figures; kept `data-numeric`). Updated the header comment to cite the constitution.
- **Also fixed** `components/money/money-view.tsx:334` (new-invoice modal running **Total** — a $ figure that carried a redundant `font-mono` alongside `tabular-nums`) → dropped `font-mono`.
- **Deliberately LEFT mono:** `components/money/invoice-detail.tsx:83` = `{invoice.number}` ("INV-021") — an **ID string**, which the constitution explicitly allows in mono. (Small mono counts like task-detail "3/5" and ritual "Step 1 of 3" left for now — no comma flaw; ritual step-counter mono is a minor constitution nit noted as a follow-up.)
- VERIFIED on `/dev-preview/money` (reload after HMR): KPIs now read **"$650 · $4,300 · $6,000 · 1"** tight and clean, matching the references' large-sans-number treatment. `npx tsc --noEmit` **exit 0**.
### Pass 2 (2026-07-23, verified) — Money toolbar: unify control heights (equal-height row)
Measured the Money filter toolbar at 1440w (JS `getBoundingClientRect`): **three different heights in one row** — search input **36px** (`h-9`), DS Select **32px**, FilterChips **~26px** (`py-1`, no fixed height). The references show toolbars with uniform, equal-height controls. Fix (kept the shared DS Select at its 32px; unified the two money-local controls DOWN to it, `components/money/money-view.tsx`): search wrapper `h-9`→`h-8`; `FilterChip` `px-2.5 py-1`→`h-8 px-3` (fixed 32px height, balanced pill padding, kept `rounded-full`). VERIFIED: search + all 6 chips + select now all **h=32, vertical-center cy=240** (identical) — one clean toolbar row. className-only (tsc unaffected).

### Pass 3 (2026-07-23, verified) — card radius consistency (money cards → app-standard rounded-lg)
Audited `rounded-*` on card containers: the DS `Card` + 15 `bg-surface-raised` containers use **`rounded-lg`** (constitution: "Cards = rounded-lg"), but **6 card outliers used `rounded-xl`** — `money-view.tsx` (4: KPI strip + invoices card + payments card) and `invoice-detail.tsx` (2: line-items + payments cards). Fixed both files `rounded-xl`→`rounded-lg` (replace_all; each file's `rounded-xl` were all cards). **Left `rounded-xl` where correct:** `ds/ui/modal.tsx`, `ds/ui/dialog.tsx`, `event-composer.tsx` (elevated/floating surfaces legitimately use a larger radius), `states.tsx:102` (icon well). **Skipped:** `horizon-view.tsx` (other chat), `kibo-ui` (parked).
- **IMPORTANT — Zenboard CUSTOMIZES the radius scale** (measured live, NOT Tailwind defaults): `rounded-xs`=4 · `sm`=6 · `md`=8 · **`lg`=12** · `xl`=16 · `2xl`=20 · `full`=9999. So "cards = rounded-lg" = **12px**; the money cards went 16px→12px, now matching every other card. (Don't assume Tailwind's 8/12 — that tripped me mid-verify.)
- VERIFIED on `/dev-preview/money` (this session's OWN server on :3005 — the other chat's :3000 had stopped, freeing the per-dir lock): KPI strip + both table cards now computed `border-radius: 12px` (`rounded-lg`), DOM class confirmed; screen renders clean, nothing broke. className-only (tsc unaffected). Same edit applied structurally to invoice-detail (same mechanism).

### Pass 4 (2026-07-23, verified) — `.num` utility: mono→sans (systemic version of the numbers fix, ~20 sites)
Followed the pass-1 thread to its root: the global **`.num`** utility (`app/globals.css`) was `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-family: var(--font-mono)` — forcing **monospace on every number that uses it**: PageHeader/panel counts, all Week-view stats, Focus timer, Documents/database counts, Portal $ amounts, Ritual numbers (~20 usages across 11 files). Same constitution violation as the `Stat` bug but far broader. Since `tabular-nums` already gives fixed-width digits (no jitter, even for the Focus timer), the mono font was pure downside. **Fix: dropped `font-family: var(--font-mono)` from `.num`** → sans (Geist) + tabular everywhere; added a constitution-citing comment. Mono stays only where an ID/code string sets it directly (e.g. `invoice.number`).
- Also (this pass): **ritual step-counter** (`ritual-flow.tsx:46`, inline style) "STEP n OF total" was `var(--font-mono)` uppercase at `0.1em` — a non-ID overline → changed to sans, `font-weight:500`, `0.04em` (the SectionLabel overline standard).
- Also resolved the **PageHeader icon 24-vs-20** backlog item: measured the title = **28px** (top of the type scale); a 24px accent glyph is well-proportioned to a 28px display title (dropping to 20 would look small). The constitution's "20px header icon" governs section/card headers, not the page title. **No change — 24 is correct.**
- **Turbopack global-CSS stale cache bit again** (the [[zenboard-turbopack-stale-cache]] gotcha): after editing `globals.css`, a live `.num` probe still read Geist Mono despite the disk being correct — HMR/restart don't clear it. Did `rm -rf .next` (build cache only — safely regenerable, not source) + restarted my :3005 server. RE-VERIFIED: `.num` probe now `{isMono:false, fam:"Geist", tabular:"tabular-nums"}`; Money screen re-checked healthy (passes 1–3 all hold). This flush also unblocks CSS verification for the rest of the sweep. tsc unaffected (CSS + inline-style only).

### Pass 5 (2026-07-23) — coverage audit: Clients + Documents + Calendar verified consistent (no new defects)
Broadened the visual audit at 1440w to confirm the systemic fixes propagated and hunt recurring patterns. All three came back **clean** — the sweep's fixes are holding app-wide:
- **Clients** (memory-surface detail): numbers now split correctly — `$7,000`/`$4,200` billed/invoice amounts + `5 open · 12` counts render **sans**, `INV-014` stays **mono** (the constitution rule, verified live). Layout/badges consistent.
- **Documents** (card grid): **zero mono numbers** found; Filter button 28px (on-scale); cards consistent.
- **Calendar** (week): header toolbar Today/Day/Week all **28px equal-height**; mini-month date numbers **sans** (dense grid, tabular keeps columns aligned); no mono times/numbers.
- Observation (not a defect): header **action** buttons are consistently **28px** across screens (New invoice, Today, Filter, Log a touch), while the money **filter** toolbar is 32px — different roles (actions vs filter controls), defensibly distinct.
- **Status:** the systematic precision defects (mono numbers ×2, card radius, money toolbar heights) are fixed and verified propagating; money/tasks/settings/clients/documents/calendar all audited consistent. Remaining screens to eyeball: home (user's-taste — alignment-only, don't restructure), portal, onboarding, capture. Diminishing returns on defect-hunting — the app was already built to a high bar; further work is deeper per-component polish or user-directed.

### Pass 6 (2026-07-23, verified) — Portal section labels mono→sans (last mono inconsistency) + wind-down
Wind-down audit of the final screens: **Home** clean (capacity-line "6h"/"2h 45m"/"5h" all sans, no mono); **Onboarding** clean (0 mono — DS-rebuilt earlier); **Portal** had the last defect — a broad mono scan found **7 mono section labels** ("Meridian Studio" overline + all `<h2>` headers: Progress / Recent updates / Completed / In progress / Documents / Send a message). `portal-document.tsx` renders them with `fontFamily: var(--font-mono)` + wide `0.12em`/`0.14em` tracking (its flagged legacy inline-token treatment) — a constitution violation (section labels are SANS, mono is IDs only) and inconsistent with `SectionLabel` used everywhere else.
- **Fix** (`portal-document.tsx` lines 20 + 31): dropped `var(--font-mono)` → sans, `fontWeight: 500`, tracking `0.12/0.14em` → **`0.04em`** (the SectionLabel overline standard). VERIFIED on `/dev-preview/portal`: mono label count **7 → 0**; "Progress" now sans at 0.44px (=0.04em); screen reads as part of the same system. tsc **exit 0**.

## SWEEP STATUS — systematic phase COMPLETE (2026-07-23)
Every major screen audited at 1440w (money, tasks, settings, clients, documents, calendar, home, portal, onboarding); all now consistent. The cross-cutting precision defects are fixed + verified propagating:
1. **Numbers** are sans-tabular everywhere (DS `Stat` + global `.num` utility + money modal) — mono reserved for ID strings (INV-001). ~2 roots, ~25+ sites.
2. **Section labels** are sans 0.04em everywhere (fixed portal + ritual step-counter; `SectionLabel` elsewhere).
3. **Card radius** unified to `rounded-lg` (12px) — money/invoice cards were the outliers.
4. **Money filter toolbar** unified to one 32px equal-height row.
5. **Resolved (no change):** PageHeader icon 24px is correct for the 28px page title.

### 2026-07-25 — Finance (Money) screen polish (user: "looks unpolished, not professional") — done + verified
User flagged the Finance view as unpolished. Diagnosed the muddy/flat feel with live computed-style probes, then refined WITHIN the B&G system (no restyle, tokens only). Root-cause measurements: canvas is **near-black** (`--paper` #121212, body #000); cards are `#262626` (surface-raised); card borders are only **8% white** (`line-soft`); and **`--shadow-lift-1` is a BLACK drop shadow (`0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.24)`) → invisible on a near-black canvas.** So on this theme, shadows can't separate surfaces — the border is the only working depth lever, and the money cards used the faint 8% border with no other treatment → they read as muddy fills.
- **Filter chips → quiet tabs** (biggest declutter): `FilterChip` was six `rounded-full border` count-pills (a busy row of outlined lozenges). Now borderless quiet text (`text-ink-500`, hover `bg-surface-hover`); only the **active** chip lifts into a raised `bg-surface-raised` pill with a hairline inset ring (`shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_var(--color-line)]`). Reads as one calm group; VERIFIED the active pill slides between chips + filters the table on click (All→Draft→1 row).
- **Crisper card edges**: KPI strip + invoices table + payments card + empty state `border-line-soft` (8%) → **`border-line` (12%)**, and the KPI strip's internal hairline dividers `bg-line-soft`→`bg-line`. The only lever that adds separation on this near-black theme (shadows are dead here). Slight, defensible divergence from the DS Card's 8% default — see the systemic note below.
- **Mono dates → sans** (constitution: mono = IDs only): invoice **due date** (`fmtDate`, was `font-mono`) and payment **paid date** → sans `tabular-nums`. Invoice numbers (`INV-021`) stay mono (real IDs). Kills the techy code-y look on "4 Aug"/"19 Jul".
- **KPI cell rhythm**: `p-4` → `px-5 py-[18px]`, hint gap `mt-1`→`mt-1.5` for breathing room.
- VERIFIED on `/dev-preview/money` @894px: quiet filter row, defined card edges, sans dates, roomier KPIs; real pointer-click filter interaction works. tsc **exit 0**, **88/88 vitest**. NOT deployed.
- **SYSTEMIC follow-up flagged (not done):** the muddiness is a **dark-theme DS issue** — the canonical card (`components/ds/ui/card.tsx`) is `border-line-soft` (8%) + `shadow-lift-1`, but that shadow is black-on-black so cards across the whole app lean flat on the near-black canvas. A proper app-wide pass would either bump the card border to `line` (12%) or add a light **inset top-highlight** (works on dark) in the DS Card + the hand-rolled card containers, so every screen gets the crispness money now has. Scoped out of this contained fix to avoid unverified ripples across 12 screens; offer to the user.

### 2026-07-26 — Form Builder **F2 craft layer** BUILT + verified (logic · focus mode · analytics · templates)
Everything F2 promised, on the same 0020 schema (no new migration needed — logic lives in the existing `content` jsonb, analytics in `view_count` + `meta`).
- **Conditional logic — ONE mechanism, not two.** A block carries `showWhen: {fieldId, op, value}`. Page mode shows/hides it; focus mode skips it — which *is* branching, so there's no separate `skip_to` concept and no node-graph editor to maintain. Ops: is · is not · contains · more than · less than · answered · not answered. **Cycles are impossible by construction**: the author UI only offers questions ABOVE the current one as sources. Deleted-source rules degrade to **inert** (block stays visible) and are flagged in the summary — losing a question is worse than showing one.
  - Correctness that matters: **hidden questions are never validated** (a required question the respondent never saw cannot block their submit) and the server **prunes answers to hidden fields on submit** (`visibleFieldIds`), so a stale value from a branch they backed out of never lands in the record or the CSV.
  - Authoring: an inline "Only show this when…" row on the question (source · test · value), where the **value control is a dropdown whenever the source has fixed answers** — including `yes_no`, which has no `options` array but whose answers are just as fixed (caught in browser verification; free text there is a typo waiting to silently break a rule).
  - Reading: a **Logic summary** in the settings rail listing every rule as a sentence — "Show "Which project was that?" when "Have we worked together before?" is "Yes"" — the "see the whole map" affordance Typeform gets praised for, without the graph editor.
- **Focus mode** (the Typeform finding, ~2–2.5× completion): one question at a time, thin progress meter + "1 of 10", big question, `Enter` advances (newline in a paragraph), single-choice answers auto-advance after 180ms, Back to revisit, last step submits. Any heading/statement directly above a question rides along as its context. Branching changes the count live, and the step index is clamped so a branch can never strand you on a question that just disappeared. Failed validation on submit **jumps back to the first question that needs attention**.
- **Analytics strip** (§7R — the review, not the dashboard): five numbers on hairlines — Views · Started · Completed · Completion % · Median time. Rate is computed against **starts, not views**, because views count anyone who opened the link (including the owner testing it).
- **"Where people stop"** — the drop-off list, tallying unfinished responses by `meta.last_field_id`. Verified reading "Phone — 2 people · Budget range — 1 person". This is the single most actionable thing the screen can say.
- **Templates + duplicate**: `lib/form-templates.ts` — 6 starters (Client intake · Project kickoff brief · Design feedback · Testimonial request · Change request · Post-project review), each **under 10 questions** by policy and in Zenboard voice; two of them ship working logic. The "New" button is now a menu (Blank + the six). `duplicateForm` copies questions and settings into a fresh **draft** — never the responses, never the token.
- **Verified** on `/dev-preview/forms` (new "Focus mode" surface added): focus mode renders "1 of 10" **correctly excluding the 2 hidden conditional questions**; live branching proven in both directions on both rules (Yes→reveals, No→hides; Website→reveals, Brand→hides); analytics strip + drop-off list read correctly; Logic summary renders both rules as sentences; template menu lists all six. tsc **exit 0**, **123/123 vitest** (+16 logic/template tests). No new console errors.

### 2026-07-28 — Focus timer: system-wide overlay + analog drag-to-set
Three follow-ups to the floating timer, in response to "make it float over EVERY app (native, not an in-app popup)" and "drag the dial like a real timer".

**1. Escaping the browser — two paths.** A web DOM widget can't paint outside the browser, so:
- **Document Picture-in-Picture** (`components/focus/focus-timer.tsx`): a "pop out" control (Chromium-only, feature-detected) moves the live widget into an always-on-top OS PiP window via `documentPictureInPicture.requestWindow`, mirroring the app's stylesheets + theme into that document (`mirrorInto`). Portals swap to the PiP `document.body`; closing it (or Esc) docks back. Verified: API present, correctly gated (`NotAllowedError: requires user activation` on synthetic clicks → only real clicks open it), graceful fallback keeps the in-window float when unavailable. The floating PiP window itself isn't screenshottable from the harness browser.
- **Native Tauri v2 shell** (`../zenboard-desktop/`): a tiny always-on-top desktop app whose one window loads a new shell-less route `app/overlay/focus/page.tsx` (own auth, forced dark). `FocusTimer` gained an `embedded` mode that fills the window (no drag/portal/pop-out; OS window owns move/close). **Fullscreen fix (macOS):** `main.rs` sets `NSWindow` collection behaviour `canJoinAllSpaces | fullScreenAuxiliary` + raises the level (screen-saver, 1000) via the `cocoa` crate, so it stays visible over fullscreen apps (plain alwaysOnTop hides there). Can't compile Rust here — code-verified by inspection; user runs `npm run dev`/`build` per the README (points at `localhost:3000/overlay/focus` by default; swap to the prod URL).

**2. Analog drag-to-set (Apple-Clock / kitchen-timer).** Grab the white handle (or anywhere on the ring) and turn the dial: `angleForMinutes`/`minutesForAngle` map the pointer onto the printed NON-linear face (1·3·5·…·90), so the handle lands on the number you point at and snaps to whole minutes; a dry `playFocusTick` cue + `navigator.vibrate` fire on each minute crossing. The arc/handle now read the REMAINING time on that face, so the dial winds DOWN toward 12 o'clock as it runs (depleting, like a real timer) and shows the set duration when idle. Scrub only when stopped + not stopwatch; centre overlay is `pointer-events:none` so the ring stays grabbable while the controls still work. **VERIFIED** on `/dev-preview/focus`: dragged the handle 25→10, centre updated live to `10:00`, snapped onto the "10" mark, arc rewound to match.

**3. Tasks are shared, confirmed to the user.** The timer's "Today" list is the same account `tasks` (server-backed), so add-here-shows-there both ways — including the native overlay (same account, not a private copy). Only the timer's own settings/running state is per-surface (localStorage).

Icon seam += `Minimize2`, `ExternalLink` (already present), `SkipForward`/`VolumeX` (earlier). tsc exit 0. Web parts browser-verified; Tauri shell is scaffold-only (unbuildable here). NOT deployed.

### 2026-07-28 — The fabric, part 1: Connected panel + `mentions` (§3.4, verified)
Phase 4 opens with what the master plan calls "**the single highest-leverage new mechanic in this plan**" (§3.4) — and the discovery that most of it needed no migration at all.

- **The insight:** `task→project`, `project→client`, `pages.client_id`, `time_entries.invoiced_invoice_id` are ordinary foreign keys the app was **writing but never reading back**. The graph already existed; nothing surfaced it. So the Connected panel ships **today**, unmigrated, on real structural edges — `mentions` only adds the third producer (the ones a person types).
- **`lib/connected.ts`** — ONE projection, `loadConnected(db, {type,id})` → groups. Sources implemented: **task** (project · goal · parent/subtasks · client *via* the project · client request · feedback · invoice *via billed time*), **client** (projects · invoices · docs · meetings · feedback · forms · open tasks across every project), **doc** (project · client · parent/children), **invoice** (client · project · the tasks it bills, minutes summed per task · a payments summary line). Every source is `safe()`-wrapped and swallows its own failure — the same doctrine as `today-data.ts`, which also makes the panel immune to any of the six unapplied migrations.
- **`components/connected/connected-panel.tsx`** — the one quiet section, reused everywhere. Deliberately **not a card**: hairline-ruled 32px rows on the canvas, zero filled-accent elements, so it can drop into any screen without spending that screen's one accent. Groups past 5 rows collapse behind "Show N more" (a map of the neighbourhood, not a second task list). **Renders nothing when an entity has no edges** — an empty "Connected" heading on a fresh task is noise.
- **`omit` prop** — caught while wiring: the task drawer already lists subtasks in its own section and the parent in its breadcrumb, so Connected repeating them is duplication, not fabric. `omit={['task']}` drops the whole group; the drawer's panel goes 9 edges → 6, showing only what the drawer *can't* — the project, who it's for, the goal it serves, what it was billed on.
- **`0027_mentions.sql` — DRAFTED, NOT APPLIED.** One polymorphic edge table (source/target type+id, `anchor`, `context`, `origin`), owner-only RLS, indexed in both directions, unique per (edge, anchor). **No FK on `target_id` on purpose**: §7H wants a deleted mention target to become a **tombstone**, not to vanish — `loadConnected` resolves targets and renders unresolvable ones struck-through. Gated by `mentionsSupported()`.
- **Honest gap — deep links.** Only Tasks has a record-level URL (`?task=`); Clients/Documents/Finance are single-route hubs holding selection in local state, so those rows render **unlinked** rather than as links that can't honour themselves. `hrefFor()` is one function; §7J "deep links" lights them all up with no other change. This is the next slice.
- Polish caught in review: raw enum metas (`in_progress`) → sentence case via `statusMeta`; a raw ISO `met_at` → "2 Jun"; `via` was `hidden sm:inline` and got un-hidden — it is the only thing explaining *why* a client appears under a task, so the label truncates first instead.

### 2026-07-28 — The fabric, part 2: deep links, so Connected rows go somewhere (§7J, verified)
Part 1 shipped a Connected panel where **most rows weren't links** — Clients/Documents/Finance were single-route hubs holding "which record is open" in local state, so nothing in the app could link *to a record*. Closed that.

- **What already existed** (found by looking rather than assuming): `/money/[id]`, `/forms/[id]` and `/projects/[id]` are real routes, and **Documents already read `?page=` server-side into `initialPageId`**. The only hub genuinely missing a deep link was **Clients**. Four of the six link types cost nothing but pointing at them.
- **`lib/use-record-param.ts`** — the ONE way a hub puts its selection in the URL. Uses `window.history.replaceState`, which the bundled Next docs (`01-getting-started/04-linking-and-navigating` §"Native History API") confirm integrates with the router and syncs `useSearchParams`. That choice matters: `router.replace` would re-run the route and **refetch a `force-dynamic` page on every row click**, while replaceState is a pure client-side URL swap. `replaceState` not `pushState` so clicking through six clients doesn't bury the page you came from under six Back presses.
- **Clients** (`clients-view.tsx`): `activeId` local state → `useRecordParam('c')`. This also **deleted a reconciliation effect** — `active` now falls back to the first client by derivation, so a URL naming a deleted client lands somewhere sensible instead of flashing an empty pane and correcting itself a render later.
- **Documents**: the link worked on arrival but the address bar then went stale — you could be *sent* to a doc but never *send* anyone to one. Now syncs `?page=` as you move between docs. Temp (`tmp-`) rows are skipped since their ids aren't addressable.
- **`recordHref(type, id)`** (was a private `hrefFor`) is now exported — the single place that knows how to address a record, so search results and the command palette get the same answer later. Still unlinked, honestly: **goals, meetings, client requests, feedback** have no record route; each is a one-line addition once one exists.
- The dev-preview harness now builds its hrefs *from `recordHref`* rather than hand-rolling them, so it can't advertise links the app doesn't have. Tombstones explicitly get no href — linking to a deleted record is worse than not linking.
- **VERIFIED** on `/dev-preview/clients`: clicking Fernwood writes `?c=c2`; arriving at `?c=c3` selects Atlas Coffee with its detail pane; `?c=deleted-client` falls back to the first client with a **full** pane (931 chars, not blank). On `/dev-preview/documents`: opening "Projects tracker" writes `?page=pDb`; "New Note" correctly writes **nothing** (temp row). On `/dev-preview/connected`: **7 of 9 rows are now real links** (was 3) — `/projects/p1`, `/clients?c=c1`, `/tasks?task=…`, `/documents?page=d1`, `/money/i1` — and the 2 that aren't are exactly the goal and the tombstone.
- tsc **exit 0**, **164/164 vitest**, **zero new eslint errors** (the 7 in clients-view/documents-view are pre-existing prop-sync effects at 475–478 / 65–66 / 140 and a refs hit at 526).
- **Not run: a production build** — another chat's dev server owns `.next` in this folder and building would disrupt it. The `useSearchParams`-needs-a-boundary risk is covered: both host pages are `force-dynamic` (still valid per the bundled docs, merely no longer *preferred* over `connection()`), and the harnesses `notFound()` before the view renders. NOT deployed.

Wiring the Connected panel onto Documents exposed the real hole: **`pages.client_id` had no writer anywhere in the app**, and `project_id` was settable only at creation and only from Project Docs. Both columns have existed since 0007. So a doc's Connected panel was empty *by construction*, no matter how much work the doc belonged to.

- **`setPageLinks(id, { projectId?, clientId? })`** in `lib/actions/library.ts`. `undefined` leaves a column alone, `null` clears it — that distinction matters, or setting a project would silently unset a client.
- **`components/documents/doc-links.tsx`** — two rows, Project and Client, in the doc's properties zone. Optimistic with rollback + toast on failure.

Ordered **before** `PropertyList` so the doc's identity reads first and "Add a property" stays the last row.

### 2026-07-28 — Search looks inside things (§7J "Search v2", no migration, verified)
Phase 4's own proving test is *"a week's notes, briefs & lists live in Docs; **search finds everything**"*. Search matched **titles only**, so a note called "Untitled" whose body discussed the Meridian rebrand was unfindable — precisely the case Docs has to win.

- **`lib/search.ts`** — `searchDeep()` plus two pure helpers. `docText(content)` flattens a page's stored blocks to the plain visible text a person typed (mirrors `lib/blocks.ts`: `text` is always plain, table `rows` keep their cells, the legacy `{ text }` prose shape still reads). `snippetAround(body, term)` returns the matching **line**, windowed with ellipses if long.
- **Two-stage, and the second stage is the point.** The database does a coarse jsonb pre-filter (`content->>blocks ilike`), which also matches block ids and type names — noisy. `snippetAround` then re-checks the real visible text client-side and **drops the hit entirely if the term only appeared in JSON scaffolding**. So stage 1 can be swapped for an FTS index later without touching stage 2.
- **Results show the matching line.** Added a distinct `snippet` field to the palette's `Item` rather than reusing `hint`: a hint is a short trailing note ("Paid", "Inbox") and stays on the row, but a snippet is a sentence, and sharing one field let it squeeze the title down to an ellipsis. Snippets render as a second line under the title. Task notes are searched too, de-duplicated against title matches.
- **VERIFIED the jsonb filter actually executes**, which mattered because RLS returns empty with or without a session — an empty result proves nothing. Probed the live REST endpoint directly: `pages?content->>blocks=ilike.*zzz*` → **200**, and a **control** with a bogus column → **400 `column pages.nonexistent does not exist`**. So the 200 is real evidence the filter is valid server-side, not a silent no-op. `tasks?notes=ilike.*` → 200 as well.
- Row structure verified in the DOM: the label block is now `flex-direction: column` (ready for the snippet line), the inline hint still sits right of it, `overflowX: 0`. A snippet with **real** data needs a session, so that one visual is unexercised; the extraction behind it has 10 unit tests.
- **Deliberately did NOT draft an FTS migration.** A GIN/tsvector index is the right optimization eventually, but seven migrations are already waiting to be applied and `ilike` over a solo user's document count is fine. Adding an eighth for a perf win that can't currently be measured would be growing the queue for nothing. Noted as the future path in the module header instead.
- tsc **exit 0**, **176/176 vitest** (+10), `lib/search.ts` eslint clean (the 3 in command-palette.tsx are pre-existing effects at 80/81/95). Six harnesses re-checked, all 200, no error markers. NOT deployed.

### 2026-07-28 — One page-header system (user directive, DS-level, verified)
User: every page had its own header layout, spacing and action placement. Reference layout = Cloudflare's two-row chrome; aesthetics stay Zenboard's. Explicit requirement: **not hardcoded per page — put it in the design system so it applies app-wide.**

**The audit found the actual defect.** The "•••" page menu was a **shell overlay** absolutely positioned at `top:10 right:14` over the content — so it never lined up with the actions beside it, and each page started its own action row at a different height (Finance y≈94, Goals y≈89, Habits y≈96, Tasks y≈72). Also found: a `PageHeader` existed but only **5 of ~13** screens used it, and `portal-document.tsx` had a **local fork of the same name** with different props (`size`/`caption`/`action`).

**The two headers, now distinct** (settled with the user after a wrong first cut):
- **Global app header** (44px bar) — names the **current page**, plus the actions that work everywhere. Unchanged from before.
- **Page header** (`components/ui/page-header.tsx`) — that page's **actions only**, ••• always last. It does **not** repeat the page name. It carries a left label only where the page has a genuine *scope* the app header can't show — "Today" in Habits, "July 2026 · Week 31" in Calendar, a project's name in Projects.

**Tokens, not hardcoded values:** `--page-header-h` (48px; 40px at compact density) and `--page-header-gap` in `globals.css`. Retune the row app-wide by editing those — never a component.

**The ••• handover is CSS, not a React handshake.** `PageHeader` renders `data-page-header`; the shell's fallback is hidden by `[data-view-shell]:has([data-page-header]) [data-page-options-float] { display:none }`. A JS claim would render **both for one frame**; `:has()` is correct on the first paint. Pages not yet migrated keep the shell's ••• — so the menu is never duplicated and never missing mid-rollout.

**Migrated:** Finance · Goals · Inbox · Habits (its date stepper became the `lead`, the date the scope). **Settings** and **ViewPlaceholder** deliberately do NOT use it — they have no page-level actions, so the row would be an empty 48px band; they keep the shell's •••.

**Two real bugs caught by verifying, not by tsc:**
1. First cut put the title in the page header *and* the app header — "Finance" twice, 40px apart. The user caught it in a screenshot. Corrected: `title` is now optional and documented as a **scope**, never the page name.
2. The harness rendered with a **zero-size box** and the ••• handover silently failed. Cause: `<Suspense>` (added to satisfy `useSearchParams`) left the whole subtree parked in React's hidden streaming container `<div hidden id="S:0">` — the same trap that blanked the Settings harness earlier. Fixed by making the harness page a **server** component that reads `searchParams` and passes the variant down as a prop.

- **VERIFIED** on `/dev-preview/page-header` (mounts the real AppShell, `?v=` per variant): header `49px` (48 + hairline), `spansPanel: true`, last control's aria-label is **"Page options"** with a 40px (`--view-px`) right gap, `shellFloatVisible: 0`, and "Finance" appears **once** (sidebar nav only). All controls 28px, `overflowX: 0`.

### 2026-07-28 (cont.) — Module-by-module review + the date vocabulary (remediation #1)
User asked twice for an app-wide consistency pass. The first pass was cross-cutting **by interaction**; this one is **per module**, which is what "one section at a time" actually meant.

**Per-module matrix** added to `INTERACTION_STANDARDS.md` §1b. Findings:
- **Documents is the outlier** — 0 page header, **0 EmptyState**, **5 unconfirmed deletes**, **3 bespoke overlays**. It predates most of the DS and never got a conformance pass. Next module to take.
- **Forms + Documents hold 9 of the app's 10 unconfirmed destructive actions** — that is where data actually gets lost.
- **Four modules still have no page header**: Home, Tasks, Documents, Calendar (they keep the shell's fallback •••).

**Remediation #1 — one date vocabulary. DONE.**
- **`lib/date.ts`** gains `formatDay · formatDayWithWeekday · formatMonthYear · formatRelativeDay · formatAgo`, all on a `DateOpts` object (`locale`, `weekday`, and `precise` for `formatAgo`).
- **The locale rule, now written down:** client components pass no locale and get the user's own calendar; **server-generated** strings pass an explicit `{ locale }` because formatting with the user's locale on the server would use the SERVER's locale and mismatch on hydration. That distinction is why the file has two families, and it was previously undocumented.
- **A real bug fixed on the way:** `new Date('2026-06-02')` parses as UTC midnight, which renders as **1 Jun** in any negative-offset zone. `toDate()` pins bare dates to local midnight. Test guards it.
- **Duplication found and removed:** `forms-hub` and `forms-panel` had **byte-identical** private `rel()` helpers, both hardcoding `'en-US'`; `requests-tab` and `portal/request-thread` had a second near-identical pair; `habits-board` had a private reimplementation of `formatRelativeDay`. All five now call the shared helpers.
- Migrated: forms-hub · forms-panel · requests-tab · request-thread · horizon · habits. **Remaining `'en-US'`:** portal-document, tasks-view, calendar-view, schedule-section (each needs a shape the helpers don't yet cover — long weekday, custom composition).
- **VERIFIED live** on `/dev-preview/horizon`: Quarter renders **"27 Aug"** (year dropped — same year) and Year renders **"13 Feb 2027"** (year kept). Forms hub reads "yesterday · 4d ago · 1w ago"; Habits reads "Today". This mattered because a helper returning `undefined` would silently *blank* every date and tsc would still be green.
- tsc **exit 0**, **188/188 vitest** (+12, incl. the UTC-parse guard and a calendar-day-vs-24h check). 8 harnesses 200.

### 2026-07-29 — Remediation #2–#5, #7: destructive acts, the missing Toaster, touch reach, tabs, empty lines

**#1 closed out.** The last four `'en-US'` sites are migrated. `DateOpts` grew
`weekday: 'short' | 'long'` and `year: true` (force the year on standalone record
dates), plus two new shapes: **`formatDayTime`** ("2 Jun, 14:30") and
**`formatWeekday`** ("Tue"). Two more private `ago()` ladders died — `documents-view`
said "3 months ago" where the app said "2 Jun"; `clients-view` had three of its own.

**A test bug the code caught.** `lib/date.test.ts` built fixtures with
`toISOString().slice(0,10)` — the **UTC** date. Run after local midnight in a
positive-offset zone (IST), "today" was yesterday's string and two tests failed
while `date.ts` was right. Fixtures are local now; the suite passes under both
`TZ=Asia/Kolkata` and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`.

**#2 Destructive actions. DONE — the one finding that could lose data.**
- **`useConfirm()`** (`components/ds/ui/use-confirm.tsx`) is the new DS primitive.
  `<ConfirmModal>` was already correct and almost unused because wiring it cost three
  pieces of state per call site; the hook makes a guarded handler one function.
  A hook, not a global host — the portal and the shell are different trees.
- All ten unguarded deletes triaged **by reversibility, not by module** (§2.2a table):
  five got a confirm that *counts the consequence* ("Its 15 responses are deleted too",
  "3 of 40 rows have a value"), five got **act-now + Undo** because a dialog would have
  been worse — a builder block is removed by Backspace too, and a database row already
  had an inverse op recorded that nothing in the UI ever mentioned.
- `DbStore.removeRow` now returns its `UndoEntry`, and **`undoEntry()` only undoes it
  while it is still the newest** — a blind `undo()` 8s later would revert whatever the
  user did next.

**The bigger find: nothing was rendering toasts.** 12 components called `toast()`;
only **6** mounted a `<Toaster/>`. Every toast from Forms, Habits, Settings and the doc
surfaces — including the Undo offers above — went nowhere. The host now lives **once**
in `app-shell.tsx` inside `[data-view-shell]`; the six per-view mounts are removed. The
store is a module singleton, so a second mount would double every toast.

**#3 Touch reach. DONE — and the audit had the shape wrong.** The remaining reveals
weren't `opacity-0 group-hover:`; they were **CSS rules in `<style>` blocks**
(`.zb-db-row:hover .zb-db-del`, `.doc-proprow:hover .doc-prop-x`, `.doc-cover:hover
.doc-cover-actions`) with no coarse-pointer branch. Delete-row, open-row, open-link,
delete-comment, the property chips and the cover actions were invisible *and*
unreachable on a phone. All on `reveal-on-hover` now; two of those rules also reached
across files into `doc-properties`. Verified live: rest 0 · hover 1 · focus 1, and the
compiled `@media (pointer: coarse)` branch is present in the stylesheet.

**#4 Clients tabs. DONE, and it moved.** `<Tabs>` in the 211px rail measured **287px** —
"Feedback" scrolled out of sight and `hideScrollbar` left no hint it existed. The tabs
went into the **page header's left lane** instead: full panel width, same grammar as
Forms. Verified all three visible and switching.

**#5 Primary button sizes. DONE — the finding was wrong.** "Four sizes" read as drift;
the app already sizes **by context** and does it consistently. Forcing `sm` everywhere
would have broken working modal footers. That rule is now written down (§2.9), and only
two call sites actually violated it: a `md` button beside a 28px input, and a **filled
primary on a repeating pipeline card** (one accent per proposal-stage deal).

**#7 Empty states, partly.** The app wants **two** shapes and only had one. Added
**`<EmptyLine>`** — a section of a populated page that is empty wants one quiet
left-aligned sentence, not a centred heading with 100px of air. Seven places had worked

### 2026-07-29 (cont.) — Header alignment as a token, and the Focus timer's dead play button

**Header alignment — the extra gap was a phantom cluster.** The page header's switcher
sat **28px** from the panel edge while the app header's first box sat at **8px**. Cause:
`PageHeader` always rendered its left cluster, so on a page with no scope to name it
still contributed its own `--app-header-lead-px` ×2 (8px) **plus** the row's `gap-3`
(12px) = **20px of dead space** before the tabs lane.

Fixed in the shared component, not per page, so it propagates everywhere at once:
- the left cluster renders **only when it has content** (`lead || icon || title ||
  subtitle || count`);
- the row's inter-cluster gap moved out of a literal `gap-3` into
  **`--app-header-cluster-gap`** in `globals.css`, beside the other header tokens;
- `globals.css` now states **the invariant** both header rows keep: *the first content
  box starts exactly `--app-header-px` from the panel edge, and the last one ends there.*

**Measured, in one tree**: the shell harness rendered a static breadcrumb, so the one
alignment that matters — app header above, page header below — could not be measured
anywhere (every page-header harness renders *outside* AppShell). `/dev-preview/shell`
now renders a real `PageHeader`. Result, in absolute page coordinates:
`first box 247 / 247`, `content start 251 / 251`, `right edge 1003 / 1003` — **delta 0
on all three axes.** Finance (actions-only, no tabs) unchanged: ••• still at 8px.

**Focus timer.**
- **The play button was unclickable.** The centre overlay sets `pointer-events: none` and
  its comment claimed "the controls re-enable them" — nothing did. The press hit-tested
  straight through to the ring, which read it as the start of a drag-to-set. `onDialDown`
  already guarded `closest('button')`, but the button was never the target, so the guard
  never fired. The controls row now takes `pointer-events: auto` with `z-index: 2`, and
  the guard also honours a `[data-timer-controls]` attribute so anything the centre grows
  later is safe without having to be a `<button>`.
- **State colour, one derivation.** `runState` = `running` → `paused` (a session exists
  but is stopped) → `idle`, feeding `runAccent`: `--color-warning-500` running,
  `--color-danger-500` paused, ink when idle. It drives the lit ticks, the handle, the
  play button **and** the minimised pill's ring, so those four can't disagree. Semantic
  tokens only — no literal hex. *Cancel/reset returns to `idle` on purpose:* reset clears
  `baseElapsed`, so there's no half-finished session to warn about and a red that never
  cleared would just become furniture.

**Verified live** at `/dev-preview/focus`: click starts the timer (25:00 → 24:48, label
flips to Pause) and **`focusMin` is unchanged**, proving no drag fired; running paints
`rgb(210,161,80)`, paused `rgb(229,103,94)`, reset returns to ink; a pointerdown on a
ring tick still drags (25 → 20 min). tsc exit 0 · 199/199 vitest · `page-header.tsx` and
the shell harness lint clean (focus-timer's remaining errors are pre-existing).

- Rail said **"All Projects"** in a Documents rail. Glossary: "All documents".

**#6 Bespoke modals — and only ONE of the four was a modal.**
`new-space-modal` is a form with a footer: it goes through DS `<Modal>` and gains
a focus trap, Escape, a labelled dialog and "Discard changes?". The other three —
**triage**, the **ritual flow**, the **portal preview** — plus the image
**lightbox** are full-screen *modes*; pouring one into a 560px card would destroy
it. They were re-implementing a layer the DS didn't have, so the DS got it:

**`<FullScreenLayer>`** (`components/ds/ui/full-screen-layer.tsx`). The four had
each landed on a different subset of the same contract:

| | z | role+label | Esc | focus in | focus back | scroll lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ritual flow | `100` | ✗ | ✗ (the × was *titled* "Leave (Esc)") | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| triage | `190` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| portal preview | `z-modal` | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| image lightbox | `200` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

Three raw z-values for one layer, one of four announced to a screen reader, and
**none gave focus back** — dismissing any of them dropped a keyboard user at the
top of the document. The layer owns all six columns; each surface keeps only what
is genuinely its own (triage its Escape *ladder*, the lightbox its ←/→ paging).
Deliberately **not** Radix Dialog — a focus trap fights both of those. Two named
entrances (`fade`, `blur`) so the ritual keeps its slower arrival without a
`style` escape hatch. SSR-safe via `useSyncExternalStore`, because the ritual flow
renders straight off its route.

**The z registry gained a floor and a ceiling.** `--z-fullscreen: 300` is the one
value for this layer. And `--z-toast` / `--z-tooltip` moved **55/70 → 320/330**:
the DS scale topped out at 70 while app overlays improvise in the 100–210 range,
so **a toast raised from quick-capture or the command palette rendered behind
it.** Both moved together, so every relation *inside* the DS scale is unchanged.

**#7 Hand-rolled empty states — the count was inflated.** Most "11 files" hits
were **menu/popover internals** ("No options", "No results", "No project"); a
menu's empty row is not an empty state and stays. The genuinely section-level
ones — **15 across 7 files** — are `<EmptyLine>` now. They had been written five
ways: centred vs left, `text-ui`/`text-caption`/`text-body-lg`, three different
ink steps, one in *italic editorial*.

### 2026-07-29 (cont.) — The header, made consistent (user report: "cramped · duplicate ⋯ · poor hierarchy")

User reported the headers looking inconsistent and cramped across pages, with
duplicate three-dot buttons, and asked for one balanced layout. Three separate
causes, all found by measuring rather than by eye.

**1. Five header tokens were DEAD, so the row ran at zero.** `--app-header-px`,
`--app-header-lead-px`, `--app-header-cluster-gap`, `--page-header-h` and
`--page-header-gap` all resolved to the **empty string** in the browser:
`padding: 0px · min-height: 0px · gap: normal`. That is exactly what "cramped"
looks like — controls flush against the panel edge, buttons touching, the row
collapsed to 36px instead of 48px.
- Cause: all five are **uncommitted** additions to `globals.css`, and Turbopack
  was serving a CSS bundle built from the HEAD version of that file. Neighbouring
  tokens in the *same `:root` block* (`--view-px`, `--card-pad`, `--accent-deep`)
  were served; only the five new ones were absent. Verified by diffing the served
  stylesheet against the source, then fixed with `rm -rf .next` (the recorded
  remedy — restarting alone does not do it).
- **This invalidates the previous session's header-alignment "verification".** It
  asserted `first box 247/247 · right edge 1003/1003` — two rows agreeing. With
  every token dead, both rows had zero padding, so they agreed *because both were
  broken*. The standard now says: **assert a token's computed VALUE, not that two
  things match.**

**2. The page header ended with a `•••` that held exactly one item.** A
device-wide "Full width" toggle — page-independent, set once — sat in the most
valuable slot on **every** screen, pushed each page's real action inboard, and on
Documents landed 30px from that module's own ⋮. That is the "duplicate three-dot"
the report names.
- The preference moved to **Settings → Appearance**, beside theme/density/accent/
  sound. The `•••` and the shell's absolutely-positioned floating fallback are
  both **deleted**, along with the `:has([data-page-header])` CSS rule that hid
  one from the other. Every page header now ends with its own primary action.
- **`useViewWidth` became a module store on the way.** It was context-only with a

### 2026-07-29 (cont.) — Header tokens get FALLBACKS (user: "you made it all ugly")

User sent shots of Calendar with a ~100px header, "July 2026" set huge and bold
with "Week 31" stacked underneath, and Forms as a tall empty band with only
"+ New form" — the segmented filter not rendering at all.

**That is the dead-token state, and my consolidation is what made it visible.**
The five header tokens have never been in the served CSS bundle (uncommitted
additions + a stale Turbopack CSS cache — see the entry above). What changed is
the *blast radius*: Calendar used to draw its own heading with a hardcoded
`text-lead font-semibold` span, so it survived the missing tokens. Routing it
through `<PageTitle>` — an `<h1>` whose size is `var(--text-h4-size)` — meant
that when the var went missing the declaration was dropped and the **UA
stylesheet's `h1 { font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold }`** took over. That is
exactly the giant title in the report, and the collapsed `min-height`/`padding`
is the tall empty band. Consolidating onto tokens made more of the UI depend on
tokens that were not being served.

**Fix: every header dimension now reads its token WITH A FALLBACK**, in both
header primitives — `var(--page-header-h, 48px)`, `var(--app-header-px, 12px)`,
`var(--app-header-cluster-gap, 16px)`, `var(--app-header-lead-px, 4px)`,
`var(--page-header-gap, 8px)`, `var(--text-h4-size, 15px)`. The fallbacks are the
same numbers `globals.css` declares, so the token still governs — it simply can
no longer take the layout down with it. `px-[var(--x)]` utilities became inline
`paddingInline` so the fallback is expressible.

**VERIFIED by deliberately killing the tokens at runtime** (`:root{--app-header-px:
initial; …}` injected over the page) and re-measuring: header **49px**, padding
**12px/12px**, min-height **48px**, gap **16px**, h1 **15px / weight 500** — i.e.
identical to the healthy state, with `getPropertyValue('--app-header-px')`
confirmed empty. Before the fallbacks the same state gave 37px / 0 / 0 / normal
and a 2em bold h1. Then restored the tokens and re-shot both reported pages at
1280px: Calendar is one 48px row with "Week 31" **inline**, Forms shows its
`All · Live · Draft · Closed` segmented beside "+ New form".

**Also learned, the hard way:** running `git stash` for an eslint baseline while
the dev server is up **poisons the CSS bundle** — it rebuilds from the stashed
(HEAD) `globals.css` and does not recover on `git stash pop`. That is what made
the tokens die a second time after I had already cleared `.next`. Use
`git show HEAD:<file>` into a temp path for baselines instead. And `rm -rf .next`
only works with the server STOPPED — doing it under a running server yields
"Internal Server Error" until a full restart.

### 2026-07-29 (cont.) — "Today" finally means the user's today (the UTC day-id bug)

The bug I flagged earlier and deferred. `scheduled_date`, `log_date`,
`ritual_date`, `paid_on`, `last_reviewed` are **calendar dates** — "that square
on the wall calendar wherever you're standing" — and ~20 places computed them
with `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is the **UTC** date. In IST
(UTC+5:30) that makes "today" *yesterday* from midnight until 05:30, so Home
listed the wrong day's tasks for five and a half hours every night, and a habit
checked off at 01:00 was logged against the day before.

**It was worse than "inconsistent" — one function disagreed with itself.**
`today-data.ts`'s `dayBounds()` took the task date from `toISOString()` (UTC)
while the calendar-event window came from `getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate()`
(runtime-local). So the two halves of the same "day" could describe different
dates, and on Cloudflare — where the runtime IS UTC — "local" bought nothing.

**The missing piece: the server cannot know.** A browser knows its zone; a Worker
doesn't. So:
- **`<TimezoneSync>`** reports `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`
  into `profiles.preferences.timezone`, and only when it actually changes (first
  run, or the user travelled) — not a request per page load.
- **`lib/user-tz.ts`** — `userTimezone()` reads it server-side, **falling back to
  UTC**, i.e. exactly the old behaviour, so an unsynced profile is never worse
  off. `dayWindow(dayISO, tz)` gives the timestamp range for that zone's midnight.
- **`lib/date.ts`** gains the day-id vocabulary: `isoDateIn(v, tz)` ·
  `todayISO(tz?)` · `addDaysISO(dayISO, n)`. `isoDateIn` formats with `'en-CA'`,
  which yields `YYYY-MM-DD` directly — no hand-rolled offset arithmetic and no
  DST bugs. Client code omits `tz` and gets the browser's own date, which also
  makes "today" agree with what a date picker writes (it never did before).

Migrated: `today-data.ts` (dayBounds, the streak walker — it compared UTC ids
against calendar-date logs, so streaks drifted by one for part of every night —
the 120-day log window, and "yesterday" for the leftovers count), the server
actions that WRITE day ids (`tasks`, `habits`, `rituals`, `goals`, `money.paid_on`),
the `/focus` page, and the client sites (`today-view`, `projects-workspace`,
`money-view`, `onboarding`, `invoice-detail`, `task-detail-drawer`).

**3 new tests** (202 total) pin the behaviour from both sides: 01:00 IST on the
29th is `2026-07-29` local and `2026-07-28` in UTC; 18:00 in Los Angeles is the
28th while UTC is already the 29th; and `addDaysISO` stays a calendar date across
the US spring-forward, where naive `+86400000ms` lands on the same day twice.
Suite passes under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` **and** `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`.

**Deliberately left:** the two export routes stamp a UTC date into a *filename*
(`zenboard-tasks-2026-07-29.csv`). Cosmetic, and not a stored day id.

## 2026-07-30 — Habits: the schedule is real, so the numbers are true

Habitify as a **feature** reference only — none of its UI, and pointedly none of
its psychology. What was taken: time-of-day grouping, a countable per-day goal, a
repeat schedule, a date navigator, calendar heat. What was refused: **Fail** as a
logging verb, the daily performance score, "peak focus zones", streak-loss
framing. §7G is explicit — gentle streaks, no fire emoji, no loss-shaming.

### The bug under the feature request

Every habit was implicitly due **every day**. Nothing stored which days it was
meant to happen, so:

- A **weekday-only habit followed perfectly** was scored as having failed every
  Saturday and Sunday of its life — a broken streak and ~71% consistency.
- `goal_target` was stored *and displayed* ("3×/day") while the only control was
  a binary checkbox. There was no way to log two of three; the day counted as a
  flat failure until the third. The goal was decorative.
- The heat grid drew two invented "missed" cells every week of a perfect record.

A number that quietly tells you you're failing when you aren't is the loudest
loss-shaming there is, and it was coming from the one surface meant to be kind.

### `lib/habit-schedule.ts` — the one rule

`daily` · `days` (weekdays) · `weekly` (N times a week). Everything that judges a
day goes through it: `isDue` · `isJudged` · `currentStreak` · `bestStreak` ·
`consistency`. The distinctions that matter:

- **`off` ≠ `missed`.** A day the habit wasn't due is drawn as nothing and counted
  as nothing. The heat grid gained the state; the seven-day trail gained it too.
- **A `weekly` habit is judged by its week, never by a Tuesday.** Its streak is in
  weeks, and the row reads "2/3 this week" instead of a day count.
- **A skip leaves the denominator** rather than counting as a failure — deciding
  not to do something isn't forgetting.
- **A run steps over not-due days without breaking.** Mon/Wed/Fri kept perfectly
  is an unbroken streak.
- The current period never counts against you while it's still in progress.

**27 tests**, passing under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` — day
ids are parsed at local midnight, since `new Date('2026-07-27')` is UTC and lands
on the wrong weekday west of Greenwich, which would shift an entire schedule.

**Home uses the same module.** `today-data.ts` had its own daily-assumption streak
walk; it now calls `currentStreak` and filters the morning row to habits actually
due today. Two surfaces, forty pixels apart in the user's day, cannot disagree
about the same habit — and an unchecked row reads as a debt whatever the
arithmetic says.

### Also fixed here

The **UTC-as-today bug**, still live in this module after the app-wide sweep:
`habits-data.ts` and `habits-board.tsx` both computed the day with
`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, so in IST the journal opened on yesterday
from midnight until 05:30 and the date navigator wouldn't advance. `today` now
comes from the loader, resolved in the user's zone.

### UI

- **`<RepeatPicker>`** — one control, shared by the create modal and the detail
  drawer. The reference app splits this across "Repeat" *and* "Goal", two
  overlapping dropdown pairs where "3 times a week" can be said twice. Here the
  two questions are separated and asked once: Repeat = which days is it due,
  Goal = what counts as done on such a day.
- **`<HabitCount>`** — `− 3/8 +` for a goal above once a day, with a ring that
  fills as the tally rises. A once-a-day habit keeps its plain checkbox; making
  the ordinary case worse to serve the rare one is not a trade worth taking.
- **Not-due habits leave the journal**, into a collapsed "2 not scheduled today"
  disclosure — one click away, because "I'll do it anyway" is a good reason.
- The **detail drawer can now edit** schedule, goal and time of day. Rename was
  previously the only edit a habit could ever receive.
- Journal ⇄ Review moved to the header's **right lane** — it's a layout switch,
  same rule as Tasks and Documents.

### Verified

Harness at `/dev-preview/habits`, seeded through the real module so it can't drift.
Strength training (Mon/Wed/Fri, kept): trail `done, off, off, done, off, done, off`
→ **47d streak, 100% over 30 days**. Call family (Weekends) → **100%**. Long run
(3× a week) → **"2/3 this week", best 6w**. Drink water → the `3/8` counter.

migration **0025 extended** with `schedule_kind` / `schedule_days` /
`schedule_count` / `habit_logs.count`, plus a backfill turning the old
`goal_period='week'` into the weekly schedule it was trying to express. Every
statement is guarded, so **the file is safe to re-run** — re-apply it if you
already ran an earlier version. Until then the module degrades to a plain daily
list, as before.

Areas/grouping beyond time of day, reminders (no notification infra), mood

## 2026-07-30 — Database view: menus that get clipped, and the row drawer

### The clipping (user report)

The column-header menu was **cut off**: open "Status" and the last items — "Hide
in view", "Delete property" — were sliced off behind the table's edge, and a wide
menu added a phantom horizontal scrollbar.

Cause: `Pop`, the local popover every menu in `database-view.tsx` opens through
(column header, view options, filter rules, colour rules), was
`position: absolute` inside the header cell. The header cell lives in the table
wrapper, which is `overflow-x: auto` — and **once `overflow-x` is `auto`, CSS
computes `overflow-y` to `auto` too**, so the panel was clipped on *both* axes by
a box that only meant to scroll sideways.

Fixed at the seam rather than per menu, so every menu in the file is fixed at
once. `Pop` now:

- renders in a **portal on `document.body`**, positioned from its trigger's rect —
  the same thing Radix does for the DS menus, and the only arrangement no
  ancestor's `overflow` can reach;
- **flips above** the trigger when there's more room there, clamps into the
  viewport on both axes, and scrolls internally instead of running off;
- **follows its trigger** on scroll (the portal costs you the automatic tracking
  an absolute child got for free — without this a scrolled table strands the
  menu), and **closes when the trigger leaves the viewport**, rather than sitting
  clamped over content it has nothing to do with.

Verified: `clipper: null` — no clipping ancestor between panel and `<html>`; all
six items present with the last fully visible; on a 60px scroll the panel moved
`top 472 → 412`, tracking exactly; scrolling the trigger to `-1128` closed it.

**Harness gotcha worth knowing:** the browser pane runs with
`document.visibilityState === "hidden"`, and **native scroll events are not
dispatched** in that state — a 200px programmatic scroll fired a capture-phase
window listener **zero** times. Two of my tests "failed" on that alone. Pair the
scroll with an explicit `dispatchEvent(new Event('scroll', { bubbles: true }))`.
Same family of trap as the zeroed layout metrics.

### Row drawer → DS `<Drawer>` (the last overlay)

`RowPeek` was the one overlay left not going through a DS primitive
(INTERACTION_STANDARDS §1b): a hand-rolled fixed scrim with Escape, but **no focus
trap, no `role="dialog"`, and no focus restore**. It's `<Drawer size="lg" modal>`
now — Radix supplies all three, plus the interaction lock (verified:
`body { pointer-events: none }` while open).

One thing fell out of it: the drawer's heading is the row's name, so the giant
editable H1 that used to sit 44px below it was saying the same thing twice. The
title **joins the property list**, where in a database it always belonged — which
also retires the `p.type !== 'title'` filter that list carried purely to avoid
printing the name twice. `Cell` already had a title case; it just had nowhere to
render. Verified: `role=dialog` · `aria-labelledby` → "Design homepage" · focus
moves inside on open · property rows now read Name · Status · Tags · Label ·
Created · Updated.

### Rituals: the habit step

Three problems, all the same shape as ones already fixed elsewhere.

- **`todayISO` was the UTC date** — the fourth site. Worse here than anywhere:
  it both filters the day's tasks *and* stamps the `rituals` row, so in IST every
  run between midnight and 05:30 planned yesterday's list and recorded itself
  against yesterday, and shutdown carried tasks to a "tomorrow" that was today.
- **Habits weren't filtered by schedule** — every active habit appeared, so a
  Mon/Wed/Fri habit sat unticked in Tuesday's ritual. Now goes through
  `lib/habit-schedule.ts`, like Home and `/habits`.
- **Counted habits were binary.** "3 of 8 glasses" collapsed to an empty
  checkbox; the ritual now carries the tally and shares `<HabitCount>`.

And the copy: the step was titled **"Keep your streak."** — precisely the framing
§7G rules out. A planning ritual that opens by invoking something you could lose
has already made the morning about anxiety. It reads "Today's rhythm. What's due
today. Tick anything you've already done."

## 2026-07-30 — Block editor: gutter alignment + Notion-style link paste

### Drag handles didn't line up with their blocks (user report)

The gutter was `top: 3px` — a **constant**, which can only ever be correct for one
block type. It happened to be correct for a 16px/1.5 paragraph (2px content
padding + (24−22)/2 = 3) and wrong for everything else. An h1 is 30px/1.3 with an
18px top margin, so its `+`/`⠿` floated ~25px above the cap height they were
supposed to sit beside — exactly what the screenshot showed.

Now derived from `TYPE_STYLE`, the same map that sets the typography, so the
handles can't drift from it: `marginTop + contentPad + wrapperPad +
(fontSize × lineHeight − 22) / 2`. Container blocks (code, table, image, embeds)
have no line of prose to centre on, so they align near the container's top edge,
which is where the block visually begins.

**Measured after:** offBy **0** for h1 (30px), h2 (20px), paragraph, bullets,
checklist and quote; −1 on the callout (sub-pixel). Code −40 and image −338 are the
intentional container cases.

### "Paste as" for a pasted link

Pasting a URL now offers **Mention · Embed video · Bookmark · URL**, like Notion.

- `lib/unfurl.ts` — the classifier. `isBareUrl` gates the whole feature: a URL on
  its OWN qualifies, a sentence that happens to contain one does not, because
  popping a menu when someone pastes a paragraph is hostile. `isVideoUrl` decides
  whether "Embed video" appears at all — offering it for a blog post and rendering
  a broken frame is worse than not offering it. **10 unit tests.**
- `app/api/unfurl/route.ts` — the metadata fetch, because the browser can't read
  another origin's HTML. Signed-in only (an open fetch-any-URL endpoint is a proxy
  for whoever finds it), SSRF-guarded by the same `isSafeWebhookUrl` the form
  webhooks use, capped at 512KB and stopped at `</head>`, with an in-process memo.
  The fallback IS an answer: a site that blocks us still yields a card with its
  hostname.
- `use-link-meta.ts` — one fetch per URL per session, negative results cached so a
  dead link isn't retried on every mount.
- **The paste is never blocked.** The URL lands as a plain link immediately and the
  menu offers to upgrade it; Escape or a click away leaves exactly what you pasted.
  That's why "URL" is a choice rather than a cancel button.
- **The choices depend on the block.** Turning a block into a bookmark card would
  throw away any other prose in it, so the block-level options appear only when the
  block is *just* the link. Otherwise you get the inline ones.
- The **bookmark card** was a bordered link: hostname and raw URL, both of which
  the plain link already said, because nothing ever fetched the title. It now has
  favicon, site name, title, description and the og:image as a thumbnail — each
  part optional, degrading to the old card.
- **Mention** replaces the pasted URL's text with the page's own title (author in
  front, as Notion does) keeping the link mark, and bails if the text was edited
  while the fetch was in flight.

tsc **exit 0** · **239/239 vitest** · build clean · eslint 0 on every touched file.

**Verified:** the menu appears on a real bare-URL paste ("PASTE AS | Mention |
URL"), and the block-scope rule works — pasting into a paragraph that already had
prose correctly withheld Bookmark and Embed video.

**NOT yet verified end-to-end**, and worth a manual pass: the four-option menu on a
block that is only the link (the option list is unit-tested and the filter is one
condition, but I could not drive the harness into that state with synthetic
events); clicking Bookmark/Embed producing the block; the unfurl route against a
live site (needs a session); and the Mention substitution.
