# Consistency sweep #2 — every record opens the same way (2026-08-17)

Second sprint under `CONSISTENCY_PRINCIPLE.md`, and the completion of a standing
directive: **every record opens through one `<PageView>`, never a per-module
detail panel.** The component was built; three surfaces had never adopted it.

## What the contract already said

`components/ds/ui/page-view.tsx` opens with:

> Every openable record goes through this component: task, document, project,
> client, invoice, form, **habit**, goal, calendar event, database row, meeting,
> finance entry, contact. […] RULE: never build a module-specific detail panel.

`habit` was already in the `ContentType` vocabulary, with `side-peek` as its
default, waiting for a caller that never arrived.

## Two converted, one deliberately not

**Habit detail → PageView.** It was a `modal` Drawer, which made the habits board
the one place in the app where opening a thing could not be side-peeked, could
not be widened, and did not remember how you like that kind of record to open.
Archive and Delete moved from a button row at the bottom of the body into the
shared ⋯ menu, where every other record keeps them.

**Form response → PageView.** A submission is a record. It takes the new
`form-response` content type rather than `form`: a form is the thing you came to
*build* and defaults to full page, while a submission is read **while working
down a table that has to stay visible behind it**, so it defaults to side peek.
Extending the DS vocabulary first is what the constitution asks for, and the
`Record<ContentType, …>` maps then forced every switch to be updated — TypeScript
caught a second exhaustive map (the pluralisation table) that I had missed.

**The share panel stays a Drawer**, and the reason is now written where the code
is rather than left to be re-litigated. PageView opens a *record*; this is one
project's settings for one capability. It has no canonical URL, so "Open in new
tab" would point at nothing; it has no siblings, so back/forward-through-records
is dead; and there is nothing to remember about how you like sharing settings to
open. Rendering it through PageView would put a toolbar of three inert controls
above a settings list — consistency of appearance bought by making affordances
lie. This is the principle's "design, not drift" case, and it carries its reason.

## Verified in the browser

Habit (`/dev-preview/habits`) and response (`/dev-preview/forms` → Responses)
both now report `aria-modal: null` — **not modal** — with the shared toolbar
`["Open in full page", "View mode", "More", "Close"]`, and the response keeps its
"Open the task" action pinned in PageView's own footer.

Non-modality was proved rather than asserted: with the habit panel open, clicking
a row **behind** it landed focus on that row and the panel stayed open. The old
modal Drawer blocked that entirely — which is the concrete thing a user gains
here, not just visual sameness.

**1161 tests**, `tsc` clean, **0 lint errors** on every touched file.

## Owed

- `components/ui/panel.tsx` (dead, zero importers) and the `ViewContainer` /
  double-`PageHeader` items remain recorded and unstarted — still the next
  consistency sweep, not this one.

# Consistency sweep #3 — one page container, three named widths (2026-08-17)

Third sprint under `CONSISTENCY_PRINCIPLE.md`, closing the trio recorded during
sweep #1.

## The drift

`ViewContainer` is the app's page-width primitive and its own comment claimed
*"No page hand-rolls margins to fake centering anymore."* Four places did:

```
cn('px-[clamp(18px,3vw,40px)] pb-16 pt-8', !full && 'mx-auto max-w-[1200px]')
```

— Clients (×2), Projects, and the invoice detail, which had gone so far as to
re-implement the component's own `full` opt-out and to use `--view-pb` for its
bottom padding while hard-coding the width and gutter beside it. Four copies of
one idea is precisely the duplication the principle forbids.

## The decision: name the second width, don't force one

**1200 was not arbitrary.** A two-pane hub's detail pane lays content out in
columns beside a rail, and the 978px reading column is genuinely too tight for
it. So the fix is not "make everything 978" — it is to put the second width in
the system. `ViewContainer` now takes one `width` prop with three named values
instead of a `full` boolean:

| | token | for |
|---|---|---|
| `reading` | `--view-maxw` 978px | one column you read down — Home, Tasks, Forms, Habits, Memory, Money, Settings |
| `wide` | `--view-maxw-wide` 1200px *(new)* | a detail pane with columns beside a rail — Clients, Projects |
| `full` | none | canvas pages that want every pixel |

That is the principle working as intended: the layout adapts because the use
case differs, while both come from one component and two tokens.

## The mistake that made this sprint worth doing

**Consolidating adopted the WORSE behaviour, and only the browser caught it.**
`--view-px` was a flat `40px`; the hand-rolled hubs used
`clamp(18px, 3vw, 40px)`. Measured at 390px after the swap: **content width fell
from 348px to 304px** — a fixed 40px gutter costs 80px of a 390px screen and
started truncating text that had been readable.

The hand-rolled rule was simply better. So the token took the clamp rather than
the hubs taking the 40:

```css
--view-px: clamp(18px, 3vw, 40px);
```

Identical at ≥1334px (3vw = 40px), better below. **Every view gained it** —
Home, which never hand-rolled anything, went from 310px to 354px of content on a
phone. A consolidation that made three screens worse and four better would have
been a bad trade; this one made all of them better.

I also corrected a false claim I had carried forward from the old comment:
`--view-px`'s "28px ≤tablet" is the **compact density** value, not a breakpoint.

## Two recorded items that turned out differently

- **`components/ui/panel.tsx` — dead, deleted.** Zero importers. Its own comment
  called it *"the ONE section-card language"* while the live one is
  `components/ds/ui/panel.tsx`. Two files each claiming to be the one.
- **`documents-view` renders two `PageHeader`s — NOT a defect.** They are the two
  arms of a ternary: one header row whose contents change with what is open.
  My recorded item was a grep count, not a reading. Corrected rather than
  "fixed".

## The guard

`components/ui/view-container.test.ts` — a source-scanning test, the same shape
as the one guarding `EmptyState`, because types cannot catch a page re-deriving
a container by hand.

Its first version was **too broad**: it flagged `max-w-[36ch]` on a paragraph and
the forms builder's 720px measure. Both legitimate — a content measure inside a
pane is not a page container, and the client portal and DS portal are separate
chromes. A guard that cries wolf gets deleted, so it now matches only the
fingerprint of the container being rebuilt: centering **+** a hard-coded pixel
cap **+** one of the page's own vertical padding tokens on the same element, plus
a flat ban on re-typing the gutter clamp. Verified against the real historical
offenders and the real legitimate measures — catches both of the former, passes
both of the latter. Comments are stripped before scanning, or the test would
fail on the example in its own docstring.

**1164 tests** (71 files), `tsc` clean, project-wide lint errors unchanged at the
pre-existing baseline of 17 (all the same async-fetch-in-effect pattern; none in
files touched here).

## Verified in the browser

Clients and Projects resolve `max-width: 1200px` from `--view-maxw-wide` and
`padding: 40px` from `--view-px` at desktop — visually identical to before, now
from tokens. At 390px both gutters step to 18px with no body overflow.

# Consistency sweep #4 — one list keyboard grammar (2026-08-17)

## The gap

The §6.3 list grammar was built for the Tasks list, and its recipe was written
down with the note *"extend to Today + project lists next."* It never was. So
`j`/`k`/`↵`/`e` moved and acted on one screen and did nothing on the others —
the clearest possible case of the principle's test: **somebody who learned this
gesture in Tasks was wrong on Today.**

## Why it was extracted rather than copied

Copying the recipe would have put the same ~30 lines of guard in three views,
and **the guard is the half most likely to drift**. Every clause in it is a bug
somebody already hit: without the `g`-chord check, `g t` navigates to Today *and*
schedules the focused row for today; without the typing-target check, typing in
the composer completes tasks; without the popper and `?task=` checks, the list
acts on Enter while a menu or a record owns the keyboard. A copy that misses one
re-opens that bug silently.

`lib/list-keys.ts` now owns the two halves that must be identical:

- **`listKeysActive(ctx)`** — pure, taking a *described* context rather than a
  DOM event, so all six clauses are testable without a DOM.
- **`useListCursor(length)`** — the roving cursor. Visual state, never DOM
  focus. It clamps **during render** when the list shrinks, so a list that
  shortens under the cursor never paints a frame pointing at a row that is gone.
  It also exposes `el(i)`, because a view that anchors a popover to a row would
  otherwise keep a second ref map beside the cursor's and the two go out of step
  the moment the list re-orders.

What stays per-view is which keys do what — and that genuinely differs.

## Tasks first, to prove the extraction is faithful

Refactored before extending: the guard block, the arrow handling and the window
binding all deleted in favour of the shared ones, `rowsRef` and `focusRow` gone,
and the hand-rolled clamp replaced by the hook's.

Verified in the browser rather than assumed: `j` `j` lands on row 2, `Escape`
clears the cursor, and typing `jjj` into the composer puts "jjj" in the input and
moves the cursor **zero** times.

## Today, which had none of it

Same guard, same cursor, same `↑ ↓ j k / ↵ / Esc`. The actions are Today's own:

- `e` completes, `h` highlights, `1 2 3` set priority.
- **`t` is deliberately not bound.** Everything in this list is already today, so
  the key would either do nothing or quietly mean something else. A key that is
  inert on one screen beats a key that means two things.
- The cursor walks the **open** list only — the completed group is behind a
  disclosure, and a cursor that can travel into rows nobody can see is a cursor
  that appears to vanish.

Priority editing did not exist on Today, so `setPriorityFor` was added (same
optimistic-and-revert shape as `toggle`) rather than dropping `1 2 3`. Silently
having fewer keys here would have been exactly the unexamined difference the
principle calls a defect.

Verified: `j` `j` focuses the second row, `3` flips "Prepare weekly report" from
Medium to High optimistically. `H` is now advertised in Settings → Keyboard.

## Two things the tooling caught

- **`isTypingTarget` returned `undefined`, not `false`**, for an object without
  the property — the signature promised a boolean. It had been defined *twice*
  (privately in `keyboard-shortcuts.tsx` and inlined again in the tasks list);
  there is one definition now, with `=== true`, and the test that found it.
- **The React Compiler rule was right about ordering.** Today's key handler read
  `toggle`/`toggleHl` declared eighty lines below it. Function declarations hoist
  so it ran, but a callback that reaches forward is harder to follow than the two
  lines it costs to move it — so it moved rather than being suppressed.

**1174 tests** (72 files), `tsc` clean, project-wide lint errors unchanged at the
pre-existing baseline of 17.

## Owed

- **The project detail's task list is the third surface** from the recipe's note
  and still has no grammar. It renders through the shared `TaskRow` inside
  `projects-workspace.tsx`'s `TaskList`; the hook is ready for it. Recorded, not
  started — no parallel work.

# The project document flow (2026-08-17)

Reported by the user with two screenshots: opening a doc from Projects → Docs
lands on a full-bleed page showing "Untitled" twice and nothing else. *"Its looks
so broke flow — I want it to open like a document with breadcrumbs."*

Run through the `impeccable` skill in **Operate** mode (an editor is a task
surface). Its context script confirmed this as narrow refinement on an incumbent
visual system, so the B&G DS stays the authority.

## The cause

A project doc opened through `PageView` with `contentType="document"`, which
defaults to **full page** — correct, it is the thing you came to write. But full
page *replaces the workspace*, and no breadcrumbs were passed. So the only
evidence of where you were was a close button, and a brand-new doc (empty title,
empty body) is a blank screen you cannot place.

`components/documents/doc-breadcrumbs.tsx` had said this was coming:

> "Keeping the three apart is what lets **Projects** or Clients grow a trail
> later without copying any of this."

The architecture anticipated it; Projects never got it. Four defects, in the
order polish triages them:

| | defect |
|---|---|
| **Broken state** | no trail — you cannot tell where you are or step back |
| **Missing state** | `Loading…` as a centred line of text, not a skeleton |
| **Hierarchy** | the title rendered twice, in the toolbar and as the H1 |
| **Detail** | the caret landed nowhere, and the editor's placeholder only renders on the FOCUSED block — so a new doc showed no hint that anything was typeable |

## What shipped

- **The trail:** `Projects / <project> / <doc>`, through the DS `Breadcrumbs`
  that `PageView` already accepts — no copy of the Documents wiring, because a
  project doc's parent is a *project*, not a folder in the documents tree. The
  project crumb **closes** rather than navigates: that page is directly
  underneath this one, so closing is both instant and literally what "go up one"
  means. "Projects" is a real link, because that is a different page.
- **The title renders immediately**, seeded from the row you clicked. It was
  already on screen in the list behind the panel; opening into a skeleton and
  then replacing it with the same words is the app forgetting what it just
  showed you. Only the **body** waits now.
- **A body skeleton** shaped like paragraphs (operate.md: skeletons, not
  spinners in the middle of content), so content lands without the layout
  jumping.
- **The caret lands in the title** on a new doc — and only on a new one, since
  focusing the title of a doc you opened to *read* would hijack scroll position
  and risk an accidental rename. Every editor worth copying does this.
- **Enter in the title moves into the body.** It is a one-line field; the key had
  no other meaning and was doing nothing.
- `DOC_MEASURE` declared once and shared by the skeleton and the document, so
  the two cannot drift.
- With breadcrumbs present `PageView` already drops its own title, so the
  duplication resolved itself — the fix was upstream of the symptom.

## Verified

Browser, `/dev-preview/projects` → Docs → a doc: crumbs read
`["Projects", "Balluji rebrand", "Logo — final direction"]`, the real title
paints in the first frame, the body skeleton shows while loading, and the
toolbar carries only its three real controls.

The skill's mechanical detector returns `[]` on the changed file.
**1174 tests**, `tsc` clean, 0 lint errors.

## Owed

- **The fully-loaded editor could not be exercised in the harness.** `getPage` is
  session-gated, so the dev preview reaches the loading state and then closes.
  Everything above the fetch — trail, seeded title, skeleton, measure, toolbar —
  is verified; the populated body and the autofocus-on-new path are not, and
  need a signed-in pass.
- The user also asked for a broader UI detailing pass across the app
  ("looks generated"). That is a separate sprint, not this one — this closed the
  reported flow. Recorded.

# One scrolling architecture (2026-08-17)

User brief: project tabs shift horizontally when switching between a tab that
scrolls and one that does not; fix it as an app-shell/scroll-container problem,
not per-tab styling.

## 1. Root cause

**Measured**, on the same project, same pane:

| tab | detail pane width | scrolls |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | **648px** | yes |
| Money | **654px** | no |

A classic scrollbar takes **6px of layout width**. Every crossing between a long
tab and a short one moved the content sideways by exactly that.

The shell architecture was already correct — `height: 100dvh` root, one primary
scroller, `min-h-0` in the flex chain, body not scrolling. What was missing was
that **twelve page-level scroll containers across six modules had each declared
`overflow-y-auto` independently, and not one reserved the scrollbar gutter.**
`scrollbar-gutter` appeared **zero** times in the codebase.

So this was not a broken hierarchy. It was a missing *rule*.

## 2. Changed

- `app/ds-theme.css` — **new `scroll-region` utility** (the rule itself)
- `components/shell/app-shell.tsx` — the primary content scroller
- `components/projects/projects-workspace.tsx` — rail + detail
- `components/clients/clients-view.tsx` — rail + detail
- `components/tasks/tasks-view.tsx` — list body
- `components/tasks/tasks-rail.tsx` — rail
- `components/documents/documents-view.tsx` — rail, list, editor
- `components/forms/form-builder.tsx` — main

## 3. Before

```
100dvh shell ✓ → main column ✓ → primary scroller (overflow-y:auto, NO gutter)
                                   └─ each module: its own overflow-y-auto, NO gutter
```
Twelve independent declarations, twelve chances to differ, no shared rule.

## 4. After

```
100dvh shell → main column → .scroll-region  ← the ONE rule
                               overflow-y: auto
                               overflow-x: hidden
                               scrollbar-gutter: stable
```
One utility, twelve call sites, all inheriting the same policy. A new module
gets it by using the class, not by re-deriving three properties.

`overflow-x: hidden` is part of the rule rather than a separate decision: a
content region that scrolls sideways *and* down is a layout bug. Surfaces that
genuinely pan horizontally opt out by owning their own scroller inside this one.

## 5. Verified

All six project tabs, measured after the change:

| Overview | Tasks | Docs | Files | Money | Portal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 648 (scrolls) | 648 | 648 | 648 | 648 | 648 (scrolls) |

**Zero shift**, in both directions across the scroll boundary.

At **390px**: rendered, `bodyScrolls: false`, `pageOverflowX: false`,
**exactly one** active scroller. No double scrollbar, no body scroll, no
horizontal overflow.

**1174 tests**, `tsc` clean, project-wide lint errors unchanged at the
pre-existing baseline of **17** (all the same async-fetch-in-effect pattern;
none in the scroll containers touched here).

## 6. Intentional nested scrollers, left alone

- **Board columns** (`tasks-board.tsx`) — a per-column scroller is the kanban
  interaction. A stable gutter on each of eight columns would cost 48px of board
  width to solve a shift nobody sees, since all columns share one height.
- **Bounded overlays** — command palette, notifications, dropdowns, mention menu,
  cover picker, doc-property lists, rich-text panels. Sized by their own
  `max-height`; a reserved gutter there is a permanent empty strip inside a menu.
  The utility's doc comment says both of these explicitly so the next person does
  not "finish the job" by applying it everywhere.

## 7. Worth addressing later

- **The rule is a convention, not enforced.** A new view can still write
  `overflow-y-auto` by hand. The `EmptyState` and `ViewContainer` guards are
  source-scanning tests; a third could assert that no *page-level* container
  declares `overflow-y` without `scroll-region`. Not written yet — the honest
  scoping is that it needs a reliable way to tell a page scroller from a bounded
  overlay, and I would rather add it with a real rule than a fragile regex.
- **`documents-view.tsx` holds three page-level scrollers** (rail, list, editor)
  which is legitimate for a three-pane editor, but it is the one module where
  "which one scrolls" depends on state. Worth a dedicated pass.
- The dev server's Turbopack cache was corrupted mid-session by deleting `.next`
  while it ran. Unrelated to app code — but `rm -rf .next` needs the server
  stopped first, and the resulting Internal Server Error made a DOM audit report
  a **false pass** (zero scrollers found) until `body.innerText.length` was
  checked. Always confirm the page rendered before trusting a clean measurement.

# The third list gets the grammar (2026-08-17)

Closes the item recorded in sweep #4: the project detail's task list was the last
of the three lists the §6.3 recipe named and the only one still without keyboard
navigation. Same guard, same roving cursor, same `↑ ↓ j k / ⏎ / Esc` from
`lib/list-keys.ts` — nothing copied.

## The decision that mattered: a flat cursor over a grouped list

This list is grouped (loose tasks, then each workstream). The cursor walks a
**flat** order, not the groups: the eye reads straight down the card across every
section heading, so `j` at the end of Discovery must land on the first row of
Design rather than stopping at a boundary the reader does not perceive. Rows
carry their index in that flat order via a per-group offset, not their index
within their own section.

Completed rows are excluded — they sit behind a disclosure, and a cursor that can
travel into rows nobody can see appears to vanish. Same rule as Today.

**`1 2 3` are deliberately not bound here.** Priority is not editable from this
list — no handler is plumbed for it — and a key that silently does nothing is
worse than a key that is absent. Recorded rather than faked, which is the
difference between an examined difference and drift.

## A real bug the linter caught

`TaskList` had an early return (`if (tasks.length === 0 && sections.length === 0)`)
**above** where I put the hooks, so `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` fired. It was
right, and it was not cosmetic: that guard fires on precisely the render where
the list flips between empty and populated, which is the render where a
conditional hook changes the call order and React crashes. The guard moved below
the hooks rather than the rule being suppressed.

## Verified in the browser

- `j` → "Stakeholder interviews" (Discovery) → `j` → **"Finalize primary
  logotype" (Design)** → `j` → "Dark-mode logo variants". The cursor crosses the
  section heading, one focused row throughout.
- `e` on the focused row flipped its checkbox `false → true`.
- Typing `jjj` into the task composer put "jjj" in the input and left the cursor
  on **one** row — the shared guard yielding to a typing target.

**1174 tests**, `tsc` clean, **0 lint errors** in the file.

## Recorded, not started

- **Home renders the same task three times** — verified independently this
  session: "Send invoice for July to TechSpark" appears in the highlight card,
  the plan list and the Schedule twin. Not touched, and deliberately: the user
  has explicitly rejected a Home re-architecture before ("this home design not
  good, old is better"), and removing the hero or trimming the plan list is that
  change. Needs their call, not mine.
- **The `scroll-region` rule is a convention, not enforced.** A source-scanning
  guard needs a reliable way to tell a page scroller from a bounded overlay.
- **The worker is at 96% of the 3 MiB ceiling** (2949.59 / 3072 KiB). It came
  down slightly this session from consolidation, but the trimming pass is due
  before the next sizeable feature.

# One section heading (2026-08-17)

The user asked for the UI detailing pass, saying the product "looks generated".
That word turned out to be measurable.

## The evidence

Five nominally identical section headings on ONE screen, measured in the browser:

| heading | tag | size | space below |
|---|---|---|---|
| Update | h3 | 15px | **10px** |
| Milestones | h3 | 15px | **0px** |
| Key tasks | h3 | 15px | **0px** |
| Activity | h3 | 15px | **12px** |
| Memory | h3 | **12px** | 0px |

Across modules there were **four** recipes for the same idea
(`mb-2 font-display …ink-600`, `mb-2.5 …ink-900`, `mb-3 …ink-900`, and no margin
at all) — and **Clients wrote its section titles as `<span>`**, so five sections
did not exist in the document outline and a screen-reader user could not navigate
by heading.

That is what "looks generated" means in practice: every instance locally
plausible, the set incoherent. It was not the typography — the type scale
measured clean at 28/16/15/14/12 with correct weight steps and tracking inside
the -0.04em floor.

## The fix

`components/ui/section-heading.tsx` — the primitive that was missing. One size,
one ink, and **the space below belongs to the heading** while the space above
belongs to the section, because a heading must sit closer to what it introduces
than to what it follows. That rule is exactly what the 0px versions broke.

Adopted in Projects (3), project milestones (1) and Clients (1), and the five
Clients `<span>`s were promoted to real `<h3>`s.

## Verified

All four project section headings now render `h3` / 15px / **10px** gap —
uniform, where they were 0/10/12 with one at 12px. **1174 tests**, `tsc` clean,
**0 lint errors** in every touched file.

## Recorded

`PRODUCT_THINKING.md` added as a governing document from the user's brief.

# Waiting on others (2026-08-17)

First build against `PRODUCT_THINKING.md`. Its §3 asks Today to answer six
questions on open. Five it already could. This was the one it could not:

> **What is waiting for someone else?**

## Why this one first

The data already existed — an approval sitting `awaiting`, a request bounced back
as `needs_info`, an invoice sent and past due — but each lived on a *different
screen*. Answering the question meant visiting three places and remembering what
you saw: the fragmented workflow the product exists to remove, reproduced inside
the product. Highest value-to-work ratio in the brief, and **no migration**.

## The definition, and why it is narrow

**Waiting means the next move is not yours.** That is the entire value: it is the
exact complement of a to-do list, and the moment it includes something you could
act on, it becomes a second to-do list and you stop trusting either.

Two consequences, both tested:

- **A `pending` client request is NOT here.** `pending` means they asked and *we*
  have not decided — the ball is in our court. Only `needs_info` (we asked, they
  have not answered) qualifies. This is the easiest mistake in the file and has
  its own test.
- **A task blocked by another of your tasks is NOT here.** That is sequencing,
  not waiting; the move is still yours, just later. `lib/task-links.ts` already
  greys those in place, which is the right treatment for work you own.

Every branch reads a status **explicitly** rather than "not done", so an
unrecognised status can never default into a list you are meant to trust.

Today every item is waiting on a *client*, because the app is single-owner —
there is no teammate to be blocked by. The shape already carries `who`, so team
seats add a fourth source without changing the rule.

## Ordering

Overdue first, then oldest. A missed **date** is a different category of late
from "nobody has answered yet", however long the latter has sat — so it leads
regardless of age. Tested with an approval older than the overdue invoice.

## What shipped

- `lib/waiting.ts` (10 tests) — the projection, `waitingSummary`, `waitingLabel`.
- `lib/today-data.ts` — the three reads join Today's **existing** `Promise.all`
  rather than adding a fifth wave. Each degrades to empty on error: a failed read
  must leave the section absent, never show a wrong "nothing is waiting", which
  is the one answer here that actively misleads.
- `components/today/waiting-section.tsx` — renders **nothing** when nothing is
  waiting. An empty "waiting on others" panel is permanent furniture on the
  calmest screen in the product; the absence of the section is the answer.

Placed between the plan and the schedule — what you can do, then what you cannot,
then when. **Inside the existing single column**, in the existing Panel language:
the user rejected a Home restage before, and this is a section, not a re-layout.

## Verified in the browser

`/dev-preview/home` renders:

```
Waiting on others   3 things, 1 overdue
INV-018                          Awaiting payment from TechSpark   Overdue
Logo — final direction           Awaiting approval from TechSpark   6d ago
Send the updated brand colours   Awaiting an answer from TechSpark  2d ago
```

Overdue leads despite being younger than the approval — the sort rule, visible.
`?empty=1` → the section is **absent**, not empty.

**1184 tests**, `tsc` clean, project-wide lint unchanged at the baseline of 17.

## A bug TypeScript caught

I wrote `invoices.issued_at`. The column is `issue_date`. The Supabase client
types the select string, so `tsc` refused it — the generated types earning their
keep on a column name I would otherwise have shipped and discovered as an empty
list in production.

## Owed

- **Not wired to the real page yet beyond the loader** — `loadTodayData` returns
  `waiting` and `TodayView` accepts it, and the app route passes `{...data}`, so
  it flows. Verified through the harness; the signed-in path is unexercised.
- Still open from the brief: **meetings → tasks** (§8) and the **content module**
  (§9). Both are larger and neither has a data model yet.

# Meetings become work — PRODUCT_THINKING §8

**"Nobody rewrites a meeting into tasks by hand."** The `meetings` table has
existed since 0016 and the panel has always had a transcript; what it did with
that transcript was extract *feedback* — what the client wants. It had no answer
for the other half of every call: **what we just agreed to do.** That got
retyped into Tasks by hand, and the note that produced it never learned what
became of it.

Shipped with **no migration**, and the reason is the finding.

## An action item is not a new object

§8 reads "action items → tasks", and the plan's own law is that information is
never entered twice. A staging row that exists only to be copied into `tasks`
*is* the second entry. So an action item is one of exactly two things:

- a **checklist line** in the meeting's notes, written while you were listening;
- a **task**, once you have promoted it.

`lib/meeting-actions.ts` is the one projection that merges the two into a single
list (22 tests).

## `[ ]` is the whole contract

Nothing is guessed. A parser that also caught *"I'll send the palette Friday"*
would be right often enough to be trusted and wrong often enough to poison the
list — and a list of commitments is worthless the moment it holds something you
did not commit to. There is a test that ordinary prose, `TODO:` and a bare
`- send the deck` all produce **nothing**.

`[ ]`, `[]`, `- [ ]`, `[x]` are exactly the forms `lib/blocks.ts` already accepts
as a to-do at the start of a document block. One vocabulary for a checkbox,
wherever you type one — and the transcript is parsed **as you type**, not on
blur, or writing `[] call the printer` looks like the feature is broken.

## The link is an edge, which is why there is no migration

A promoted item is a `mentions` row — `meeting → task` (0027, applied). That is
the whole persistence layer, and it buys the Connected panel on both ends for
free: `resolveSummaries` already knows how to name a meeting.

**Without the edge there is no feature, so the action refuses rather than
degrades.** A task created with nothing pointing back is offered for promotion
again on the next render, and making two tasks for one commitment is this
feature's single unacceptable failure. If the edge insert fails, the task is
deleted and the click reports an error.

Pairing is by normalised text, because a line in a textarea has no id. Editing a
promoted line therefore un-pairs it — which is why a task whose line has gone is
**appended and labelled "Not in the transcript"** rather than dropped. A
commitment may fall out of your notes; it must not fall out of the list. (When
meeting notes become a doc — §7D, Phase 4 — the key becomes the block id, and
only `actionKey` changes.)

## Where the task goes

`meetingDestination` — one live project ⇒ that project, otherwise **Inbox**.
Finished and archived projects do not count, which is what makes the rule useful
rather than merely safe: a two-year client has one live project and four dead
ones, and "more than one project" would send every action item to Inbox forever.

Wrong project costs more than Inbox: it is counted in that project's progress and
may be published to that client's portal. **The panel and the server call the
same function** — the browser's project list is a snapshot, so the row that gets
written is decided against the database, but against the same rule, or the panel
would promise a destination the server would not honour.

## The third copy of a rule nobody had written down

`lib/task-intake.ts` — how a task that **arrives from elsewhere** is built.
`lib/actions/forms.ts` and `lib/actions/portal.ts` had each decided it
separately and `clients-view` disagreed with both. Three rules, now one (5 tests):

1. **No scheduled date.** `addTask` puts a task on *today*; agreeing to something
   in a Tuesday call is not agreeing to do it on Tuesday, and silently loading
   someone's day is the fastest way to make them stop trusting the plan.
2. **A project or the Inbox, never neither** — a task in no pile is invisible.
3. **A title that always exists, clamped.** Intake titles are prose written for
   another purpose.

Both prior copies now call it. `priority: 'low'` stays portal's own decision and
deliberately outside the shared rule.

## Verified in the browser

`/dev-preview/clients` → Meridian Studio → *Q3 planning call*:

```
Action items   5 action items · 2 done              [Make 1 task]
 ☑ Send the revised colour palette          Brand identity
 ☐ Book the photographer for the launch shoot        Inbox
 ☑ Share the Q3 invoice schedule
 ☐ Draft the launch announcement copy            [Make task]
 ☐ Confirm the print run with the supplier   Not in the transcript
Filed under Brand identity.
```

Two prose lines in that same transcript produced nothing. The meetings list now
reads **"Q3 planning call · 3 to do · 2 feedback"** — counted by the same
function, so the list and the panel cannot disagree — and *Kickoff*, which owes
nothing, shows no count and an empty state that teaches the `[]` shortcut in
place.

**1211 tests**, `tsc` clean, project-wide lint unchanged at the baseline of 17.

## Two things the browser caught

- **A done task and a done line rendered in different colours** — `rgb(230,229,227)`
  against `rgb(145,145,142)`, measured. A row's colour has to mean its state, not
  which of its two shapes it is in.
- **The task link was a bare `<a>`**, so clicking it did a full page load. It is
  `next/link` now.

## Owed

- **The signed-in path is unexercised.** The harness has no session, so every
  promotion there returns *Not authenticated* — the button's `finally` recovers
  and the row stays, which is itself worth knowing, but the write has only been
  proven by construction.
- **`→ project updates`**, the last arrow in §8's chain, is not built. A meeting
  is client-scoped and an update is project-scoped and written prose; that is a
  separate feature, not a tail of this one.
- Meetings are still reachable only through a client. §8's promise is bounded by
  that until meetings become addressable (`recordHref` returns `undefined` for
  them — the remaining §7J work).

# Documents: full width, and a security pass

## Full width

The measure change in the previous entry made this a prerequisite rather than a
nicety: a 708px reading column is right for prose and wrong for a wide table, and
until now there was no way to say so. `DocMeta.wide` rides in the page's content
JSON beside the cover — **no migration** — and the sheet drops its `max-width`.

Two decisions worth keeping:

- **The menu stays open when you toggle it.** Every other row in that menu is a
  verb that takes you somewhere; this one changes what you are looking at, and
  the only way to judge it is to see it. Closing would make "was that better?"
  cost two more clicks every time.
- **The switch is a picture, not a control.** The row is the control
  (`role="menuitemcheckbox"`), so a real `<Switch>` inside it would be a
  focusable button inside a focusable button — two tab stops for one decision.
  `MenuSwitch` copies the DS Switch's classes so they are the same object.

Measured at a 1280px pane: **1144px wide on, 708px off**, `aria-checked`
tracking, menu still open across the toggle.

## Security

`lib/safe-url.ts` — the one rule for a URL that came from a person and is about
to become an `href` or an iframe `src` (9 tests). A document is not a trusted
document: its links arrive by paste, by Notion import, and by `liftText` reading
`[label](url)` out of stored text — and the document is then shown to **clients**
through the portal and through proposals. "The owner typed it" is not a safety
argument when the reader is someone else.

Two functions, because an anchor and a frame are not the same risk. `safeHref`
allows http/https/mailto/tel plus relative routes (an internal mention *is* a
link) and refuses everything else. `safeEmbedSrc` is https only, because a frame
runs without a click.

**Fixed**

1. **Stored XSS via link marks.** `staticSpans` rendered `<a href={sp.link}>`
   for any stored span and wired a click handler that navigates. A
   `javascript:` href there runs in our origin with the reader's session.
   Refused now at three points: `normalize()` (storage), the mark's `toDOM`, and
   `staticSpans` (render). `resolveLink` checks again before navigating, because
   `window.open` on a `javascript:` URL executes it.
2. **Unsandboxed embeds.** The embed/video/PDF iframes took a raw user `src` and
   granted the default sandbox — including top-level navigation. `EMBED_SANDBOX`
   withholds `allow-top-navigation`, so an embedded page can no longer replace
   the tab, and the tab it would have replaced is often a client portal.
3. **SSRF past the guard in `/api/unfurl`.** `redirect: 'follow'` validated the
   URL the user pasted and then let the remote server pick the next one, so
   `https://attacker.example` answering `302 → http://10.0.0.5/` went straight
   through. Every hop is checked now, up to four.

**Checked and sound** — the client portal re-validates the token *and*
`portal_enabled` *and* the relevant channel flag on every read and every write
path; tokens are `randomBytes(18)` (144 bits); the public read goes through the
service role with a fixed column projection; `/portal` is `noindex`; both cron
routes refuse every request when their secret is unset; `/api/unfurl` requires a
session and caps body size and time; there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
carrying user data anywhere in the app.

**The browser caught what the tests could not.** The ProseMirror `toDOM` guard
passed its unit tests and changed nothing on screen: almost every block is
*static*, so the anchor that actually exists is built by React in `staticSpans`.
The page still contained a live `javascript:` href — neutralised only by React
19's own blocking, which is a framework courtesy, not our control.

## QA

There was no gate: 1224 tests and nothing that runs them before a deploy, no CI,
no hooks. `npm run check` (tsc + tests) now runs, and `npm run deploy` runs it
first. `eslint` is deliberately **not** in the gate — the repo carries 17
pre-existing lint errors, so including it would make the gate fail on day one and
be switched off within a week. It joins the day that count reaches zero.

**1224 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at the baseline of 17, Impeccable
detector clean on the changed files.

## Owed

- The **content module** (§9) is still not built — it is the largest remaining
  gap in PRODUCT_THINKING and needs its own plan.
- No E2E suite, no automated a11y or dependency scanning.
- `DocContextMenu`'s rows fire on `mousedown` only, so they are not reachable by
  keyboard. Pre-existing across that whole menu; the Full width row handles
  Enter/Space, the rest still do not.

# Content — the module §9 asked for (M1)

**No migration.** A content piece is a `pages` row typed `content`, and the
pipeline rides in the page's content JSON beside the cover — the same place doc
properties and Full width already live. `pages.type` is plain `text` with no
CHECK and the app already writes note/doc/template/database.

## The decision: a content piece is a page

Not because a migration was inconvenient. The thing a creator spends their time
on is the **script**, and a script is a document — so the moment content is a
page it inherits the block editor, comments, version history, @-mentions,
Connected, search and `client_visible` sharing to the portal. A `content` table
would have started with a `body text` column and spent a year growing back
toward what `pages` already is.

`lib/content.ts` (20 tests) is what a page does *not* have: a pipeline.

## What the vocabulary decides

- **Seven stages** — idea → script → shoot → edit → review → scheduled →
  published. Each carries its **verb** (`STAGE_ACTION`), because a board that
  only names states makes you translate every time you look at it. `review` is
  the one whose verb is not yours — the same "the next move is not yours" rule
  `lib/waiting.ts` is built on.
- **Two dates, deliberately.** `shootAt` is when it gets captured, `publishAt`
  is when it goes out, and **a piece appears on both days**. Collapsing them is
  exactly the mistake the spreadsheet makes: you find out you booked a shoot for
  the morning it was supposed to be live.
- **Late** means a publish date that has passed *while the piece is still being
  made*. Published is never late — it went out. Scheduled is not late either:
  the date is the plan, and the plan has not failed until the thing that
  publishes it does.
- **An unknown stage lands on `idea`.** A JSON-persisted enum has no database to
  reject a bad value, so the reader is the only guard — and a card in a column
  that does not exist is a card you cannot see or drag back. Same lesson as
  `asBlockType`.
- **Channel is free text with suggestions, not an enum** — a creator's channels
  are theirs, and an enum here is a list we are permanently one platform behind.

## Verified in the browser

`/dev-preview/content` — board reads **"7 in progress · 1 late"**; *August
recap* carries the only red badge; *Imported from the old spreadsheet*, stored
with `stage: 'filming'`, sits correctly in **Idea**. The calendar shows *Studio
tour, part one* on the 7th (shoot) **and** the 21st (publish), and *The
3-question client brief* on the 9th and the 14th — one object, two appointments,
which is the whole point.

## Motion

`motion` v12 was in `package.json` and imported by **zero files**. Two uses, both
carrying information rather than decorating:

- **`layout` on board cards** (DS `Board`, so every board gets it). A card's
  column is its state, and state usually changes somewhere else — without this,
  a card you were reading is simply somewhere else next time you look. Honest
  caveat: the only path that changes a stage today is the detail panel, which
  covers the board, so this mostly matters once drag-and-drop and realtime land.
- **Direction on the calendar's month change.** Which way you moved is
  information the grid otherwise throws away. Verified: the outgoing grid is
  removed, four steps settle back to one grid, no leak.

Both are ease-out (0.2–0.24s), not the library's default spring — a work board
that overshoots and settles reads as a toy — and both are off under
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

**This contradicts CLAUDE.md line 49** ("No scale, bounce, or entrance
animations"). Taking the newer instruction as the decision; the line should be
amended rather than left to disagree with the code.

## Two guard tests caught this build

`date-vocabulary.test.ts` caught a raw `toLocaleDateString` in the calendar
header, and `empty-state-copy.test.ts` caught a 64ch description against the
52ch one-line rule. Both were mine, both fixed.

**1244 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17, detector clean.

## Owed

- **No list view, no drag-and-drop, no shot list.** The shoot is a date today,
  not a plan: call sheet, shot list and gear are M2.
- **Client review** reuses nothing yet — the `approvals` table exists and
  `review` should feed it (and the Waiting section) in M3.
- The DS `Board` still has no drag-and-drop, which is why Content passes its own
  `emptyLabel`: the default copy promised a drop target that does not exist.

# Content M2 — the shoot day

The half of "planning shoot" M1 skipped. M1 gave a shoot a *date*; this gives it
a *plan*. Still **no migration**.

## A shoot day is a date, not an object

Every piece carrying that `shootAt` is on it. There is nothing to create, nothing
to keep in sync, and no way to be filming something that is not on the call
sheet. The question a creator actually asks on Tuesday morning — "what am I
filming today" — is answered by a date, without anyone having built a shoot.

`?shoot=2026-09-07` is a real address, so the call sheet is a link you can send.

## A shot is a to-do line in the script

The same `[ ]` contract the rest of the app already uses. You write *"cutaway of
the swatches"* once, while writing the script, and that is the line you tick on
set — the plan's own law that information is never entered twice, and the same
finding as meeting action items. Ticking it here writes back into the script.

Two consequences worth keeping:

- **The pipeline is merged back on save.** `serialize` owns `blocks` and knows
  nothing about the shoot date, so a naive save would strip the piece out of the
  very day you are standing in.
- **"No shots yet" is a real answer, not an error state.** Plenty of pieces are
  filmed straight off the script, so the line says what would change it rather
  than implying something is missing.

## Location lives on the piece

Not on the day. Two pieces filmed the same morning in two places is a real
Tuesday, not a conflict to resolve — so the day lists both, and each piece names
its own only when the day has more than one. Call time appears only once there
is a shoot date: a time on its own is not a fact about anything.

## Verified in the browser

`/dev-preview/content?shoot=2026-09-07`:

```
Mon 7 September
2 pieces · 5 shots · 1 done
📍 Studio   📍 Rooftop
  09:00  Studio tour, part one            Studio
    ☑ Wide of the studio from the door
    ☐ Slow push in on the desk
    ☐ Cutaway: swatch book, shallow depth
  11:00  The 3-question client brief      Rooftop
    ☐ Talking head, rooftop, golden hour
    ☐ B-roll: notebook and the three questions written out
```

Call-time order, both locations, shots read out of each script's to-do blocks.
Ticking *Slow push in on the desk* moved the summary from **1 done to 2 done**
and struck the line through.

In the calendar a **shoot** chip now opens the day and a **publish** chip opens
the piece — on a shoot day what you need is the call sheet, not one script.

**1252 tests**, `tsc` clean, detector clean on the module.

## The harness had to gate the write too

`demoScripts` replaces the fetch **and** the save. A demo prop that gates only
the read leaves the write pointed at a server the harness does not have — which
is how a tick would have looked fine and then thrown.

## Owed

- **No drag-and-drop** on the board, and the DS `Board` still has none — which
  is why Content passes its own `emptyLabel` rather than advertise a drop target.
- **`review` still feeds nothing.** The `approvals` table exists and a piece in
  review should appear in the Waiting section; that is the next join.
- Gear and people are not modelled. Location and call time were the two that
  change where your body is at 9am; the rest can wait for a real need.

# Content M3 — moving a piece, from the piece

Changing a stage cost four actions: click the card, wait for the panel, change a
select, close it. On the most-used screen, for the action you do most. It is one
now, from the card.

## A menu, not a drag

Every pointer gesture in this app ships a menu twin anyway — the twin is what
works on a phone, with a keyboard, and with a screen reader — so **the twin is
what got built first**. Dragging can land on top of it later without changing
anything here.

## The write had to move to the server

A piece's stage lives inside the page's content JSON, next to its script. The
board does not have the blocks, and `updatePage` replaces the whole column — so
saving a stage from a card would have **deleted the script**. `setContentStage`
does the read-modify-write server-side, preserving every other key in there:
blocks, cover, properties, comments, the full-width flag.

Optimistic, reverting on failure. The card moving *is* the feedback; waiting for
a round trip would make the action feel broken.

## The DS Board learned to carry a control

`BoardCardData.action` renders on hover — and **outside** the card, laid over it.
The card is `role="button"`, so a control nested inside it is a button inside a
button: one tab stop swallowing another, and ambiguous to a screen reader.
Verified in the browser: 9 stage menus, **0** of them inside a card button.

This is also what makes M1's Motion `layout` stop being latent. The caveat then
was that the only thing changing a stage was the detail panel, which covers the
board — now the card moves while you are looking at the board.

## Verified in the browser

Moving *August recap* from **Edit** to **Scheduled** via the card menu took the
header from `7 in progress · 1 late` to `6 in progress` — one fewer in flight,
**and the late badge gone**, because a scheduled piece is not late. The `isLate`
rule proving itself live rather than in a unit test.

Menu measured on screen at 200×262 with all seven stages.

**1252 tests**, `tsc` clean, detector clean.

## The harness needed one flag, not two

`demo` now gates every write in the module. `demoScripts` supplied data and
implied harness-ness; leaving the stage write live meant an optimistic move that
snapped straight back. A harness that gates the reads and leaves one write live
is a harness that lies.

## Owed

- **Drag-and-drop** can now be added as an enhancement over a working twin.
- **`review` still feeds nothing.** `approvals.project_id` is `NOT NULL`, so a
  content piece needs a project before it can carry a client approval — that is
  a real join (a Project field on the piece), not a one-liner, and it is the
  next thing.
- No list view; gear and people still unmodelled.

# Content M4 — the client's sign-off, and a correction

`review` finally means something. It also turned out I had encoded a claim that
was too strong, and this sprint is mostly the correction.

## The correction: a stage cannot tell you whose move it is

M1 shipped `isWaiting(stage) === (stage === 'review')`. That is wrong, and it is
the exact mistake `lib/waiting.ts` was built to refuse. **`review` says a piece
is being looked at; it does not say by whom, and most reviews are your own.** A
stage-only rule would have filled "waiting on others" with your own homework.

What makes the next move someone else's is a real, outstanding **ask** — an
`approvals` row a client has not answered. `isAwaitingClient(piece)` replaces it,
`needsChanges(piece)` is its own state (they answered, and the answer was no),
and there is a test for each of the three review cases.

## Everything it needed already existed

- `pages.project_id` — a content piece is a page.
- `setPageLinks` — written for docs, attaches a project.
- `requestApproval(pageId)` — works for **any** page with a project: marks it
  client-visible and opens an awaiting approval.
- `approvals.page_id` (0019) — already points at a page.
- `today-data.ts` already loads every awaiting approval, so a content piece
  reaches **Home's "waiting on others"** with no new plumbing.
- `lib/portal.ts` already shows approvals to the client.

So M4 wrote no server actions at all. The one honest constraint:
`approvals.project_id` is `NOT NULL`, so a piece needs a project first — which
is why Project sits with the other facts rather than hidden behind the button
that needs it, and why a piece without one says *"Attach a project to send this
for client sign-off"* instead of offering a button that would fail.

## Sending is explicit, never a side effect of the stage

Reaching `review` does not ask anyone anything. "Send to the client" is its own
button, because it makes the piece visible in their portal — and showing a
client something is not a thing to do by inference. Same reasoning as the two
buttons on client updates.

## Verified in the browser

Board header: `9 in progress · 1 late · 1 needs changes`. Three pieces sit in
**Review** and read differently, which is the whole point:

| piece | state | card |
|---|---|---|
| Client spotlight — TechSpark | awaiting | `With client` |
| TechSpark case study film | changes_requested | `Changes` |
| Behind the scenes — week one | in review, nobody asked | *no badge* |

Opening the rejected one shows the client's actual note — *"Love it — can we cut
the intro to 10s and swap the logo shot for the new mark?"* — with **Send
again**. Opening the un-asked one offers no button and says why.

`tsc` clean, detector clean.

## Owed

- **Not verified against a live portal.** The harness has no session, so the
  round trip through `requestApproval` → portal → client decision is proven by
  construction and by reading the existing code, not by running it.
- Drag-and-drop; a list view; gear and people.

# Content M5 — Home, and a bug my own note had hidden

## The bug

`app/(app)/today/page.tsx` passes props to `<TodayView>` **explicitly**. It does
not spread `data`. So `waiting` — computed by the loader, tested, verified in
the harness — **has been thrown away on the signed-in Home since it shipped**.

My own PROGRESS entry for that sprint said *"the app route passes `{...data}`, so
it flows"*. It does not, and I did not check. The harness passed the prop by
hand, which is exactly why the harness could not catch it. Both `waiting` and
`content` are wired now.

The general lesson is in the comment left at the call site: a loader that returns
a new key reaches nothing until that list grows.

## Content today

A studio's own output now appears on the screen the day starts on. Without it the
Content module is a place you have to *remember to visit*, and remembering where
to look is the exact work Home exists to remove.

It sits directly under "Waiting on others" because it answers the same kind of
question — what today holds that is not on the task list — and it follows the
same rule: **renders nothing when nothing is happening.**

- A **shoot** row leads with its call time and its location, because on a shoot
  day the only fact that changes what you do next is when to be there.
- A **publish** row does not. Nothing is asked of you; it goes out.
- A shoot opens the **day** (the call sheet), a publish opens the **piece** —
  the same split the calendar makes, for the same reason.

`contentToday` reuses `byDay`. Home and the calendar must never disagree about
what a date holds, and two implementations of "what is on this day" is precisely
how they stop agreeing.

## Verified in the browser

```
Content today   Filming at 09:00 · 1 going out
  Studio tour, part one                 Studio   09:00
  Five fonts we keep coming back to             Goes out
```

`?empty=1` → both Content today and Waiting on others are **absent**, not empty.

Home now reads: what you can do · what you cannot · what today holds · when.

## Two things the harness would have taught wrong

- It built its date with `toISOString().slice(0,10)` — the UTC date, which is
  yesterday for half the world after 5pm, and the exact bug `lib/date.ts` exists
  to prevent. Rebuilt from local parts.
- `NO_CONTENT` is a module-level constant, not a `= []` default: a fresh array
  every render is the identity change that turns a reconciling hook into an
  infinite loop.

`tsc` clean, detector clean.

## Owed

- **Still unverified against a live session** — every content sprint has been
  proven through the auth-free harness. The signed-in path deserves one pass.
- Drag-and-drop; a list view; gear and people on a shoot; the published URL has
  nowhere to live.

# PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md, and the leaks the audit found

`PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md` is now governing, above `PRODUCT_THINKING.md`. Its rule —
**never build a feature in isolation** — is what this sprint is about, because
the first thing it caught was the module I had just finished.

## Content was not in the graph at all

I built Content across five sprints and never connected it. `lib/connected.ts`
is THE projection of relationships in this product, and `content` was not an
`EntityType` in it. So:

- a **project** could not show what had been made for it,
- a **client** could not answer "what have we made for Acme",
- a **piece** had no Connected panel,
- and the command palette and @-mention picker did not know the type existed.

That is exactly the failure PRODUCT_CONTEXT §5 names, in a module built the week
it arrived.

## Three leaks, all the same shape

A content piece is a `pages` row. Three separate queries read `pages` without a
type filter, so the same object surfaced in modules that have no business with
it — **not duplicate data, which would be bad; the same object filed under a
heading that is not its own, which reads as another place to manage.**

1. **Documents' default view.** A content piece has no folder, and Draft is
   "pages with no folder" — so **every piece in the pipeline appeared in Docs**
   as a stray document.
2. **A client's Connected panel** listed pieces under *Documents*.
3. **Search** returned pieces as docs, linking to `/documents?page=…` — a route
   that opens the wrong module for that object.

`lib/page-kinds.ts` is the one rule: a page belongs to Documents unless another
module has claimed its type. An **unrecognised** type still shows — hiding
someone's writing fails silently and permanently, showing it costs a row.

## What the type system caught for me

Adding `content` to `EntityType` broke four `Record<EntityType, …>` maps at
compile time — the Connected panel's glyphs, the hover card's glyphs and labels,
and the command palette's groups. Exhaustive records are why a new record type
cannot be half-added.

What it could **not** catch: `recordHref` is a `switch` with a `default`. I added
the forward direction and missed `parseRecordHref` — the exact failure its own
comment warns about ("one mapping written twice… silently stops producing
backlinks"). There is a round-trip test now.

## Content joined the graph properly

- `content` is an `EntityType` with a route, a glyph, a label and a group.
- `docEdges` serves it — a piece **is** a page, so its project and client edges
  are already exactly what that builder reads. A second builder would be the
  same three columns queried twice and drifting apart.
- A client's panel gains a **Content** group, each row showing its stage.
- A piece gains a Connected panel.
- Search returns it as content, and it is @-mentionable.

## Verified in the browser

A `type: 'content'` page seeded into the Documents harness: **absent from Draft
(7 cards) and absent from All documents (22 cards)**, while real docs render in
both. That probe stays, the same way the invalid-block-type row does.

**1266 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17, detector clean.

## Owed, against the new framework

Scenario D — *project complete → content idea* — still has **no path**. A piece
can now be attached to a project by hand, but a finished project cannot offer to
become a case study. That is the next highest-impact gap, and it is the one
PRODUCT_CONTEXT §15 is most explicit about.

---

# Scenario D — a finished project becomes content

PRODUCT_CONTEXT §15: `completed project → case study → reel → LinkedIn post →
X post`. This is the connection that turns client work into the studio's own
marketing, and it is the one a studio reliably fails to make — not because it is
hard, but because **the moment passes**. Three months later the project is cold
and the blank page wins.

## The moment already existed

The close-out modal has been there since Projects Phase 3, and it already says
*"jot a line for future you before it goes quiet"*. Content belongs in exactly
that sentence, so the offer went there rather than into a new surface.

Four presets, mapped from §15's own list: Case study (article · Blog), Reel
(short · Instagram), LinkedIn post, X post. Each piece is created carrying the
**project and its client**, read from the project rather than passed in — one
object, referenced, never copied (§24). Not retyping those is the whole point;
that re-entry is what §25 calls a leak.

## Three decisions

- **Nothing is pre-selected.** Offering four things and having three appear
  because nobody unticked them is how a pipeline fills with work no one chose.
- **Everything starts at `idea`.** The project is done, the content is not; a
  pipeline that starts things half-written lies about where the work is.
- **Only structure is seeded, never claims.** The case study gets three headings
  — *The brief · What we did · The result* — and nothing writes a hook or a
  description. An invented line about work it has never seen is precisely what
  makes a product feel generated. There is a test asserting the hook stays empty.

## The more common case

Almost nobody thinks about marketing in the ten seconds after ticking a project
done. They think about it three months later, when they need something to post —
and until now the only route back to that moment was to un-complete the project
and complete it again. **The close-out is reopenable**: a completed project shows
a "Wrap up" action in its header. Verified: absent while active, present once
completed.

## Verified in the browser

Completing *Balluji rebrand* opens the close-out, which now reads: tasks and time
· unbilled with **Create invoice** · **Retro** · **Make content from it** with
the four presets. Nothing pressed on open; picking Case study and LinkedIn post
turns the button into **Create 2 pieces**.

**1271 tests**, `tsc` clean, detector clean, lint unchanged.

## Owed

- The pieces are created but not opened — you get a toast, not a jump into
  Content. Deliberate for a multi-create; worth revisiting for the single case.
- A case study should be able to pull the project's real deliverables (docs,
  files, before/after) into its body. That is the next depth on this seam.

---

# Scenario B — calendar → meeting → notes → tasks

Two gaps, both in the first half of the chain.

## A meeting was not addressable

`recordHref('meeting')` returned `undefined`, so **every meeting row a Connected
panel drew was text you could not click** — including the ones the meeting→task
edges create. The panel was local state in Clients, so there was nothing to
address.

It is `?meeting=<id>` now, and the id is enough on its own: Clients resolves the
meeting's own client from it, so a link arriving from a task's Connected
panel — which knows nothing about the client — still lands on the right page
with the right panel open. Verified cold: `/clients?meeting=m1` opens *Q3
planning call* with Meridian Studio selected.

A guard test caught the consequence I had not thought about: `MENTIONABLE_TYPES`
must equal the set `recordHref` can address, because a mention **is** an internal
link. Meetings became addressable, so they became mentionable — and searchable,
which is the same argument (a record you can link to but cannot find is half a
record).

## The calendar could not start a meeting

§14's first arrow — `calendar event → meeting` — did not exist. Calendar events
were not records at all, which §13 also wants fixed from the other side: *"the
calendar should connect time with context"* is not possible while an event has no
identity.

`event` is an `EntityType` now, with a route, a glyph and a label. The composer
on an existing event offers **Take notes**, which creates the meeting and opens
it. Verified: the footer reads *Delete · Take notes · Cancel · Save* on an
existing event, and a **new** event offers no Take notes — there is nothing to
take notes on until it exists.

## Two objects, deliberately

An event is the appointment — movable, declinable, synced from Google. A meeting
is the record of what was said. Merging them would mean deleting a calendar entry
deletes your notes.

What must not happen is two meetings for one event, so the link is a `mentions`
edge, checked before creating and written after. If the edge fails, the meeting
is deleted rather than left unlinked — an unlinked meeting means the event offers
to take notes again and starts a rival set, which is the one failure the whole
function exists to prevent.

The event's title and time are **copied once** at creation, not referenced: a
meeting has to keep the title it was held under even if the calendar entry is
renamed or deleted later.

**1273 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17.

## Owed

- The meeting created from an event has **no client** — an event carries no
  client_id, so it cannot be inferred. The meeting panel needs a client picker.
- `connectedFor({ type: 'event' })` has no builder yet, so an event's own
  Connected panel is empty; the edge exists and reads from the meeting's side.
- `month-grid.tsx:174` carries a 3px coloured `border-left` the craft detector
  flags. Pre-existing, untouched, and a calendar-wide visual decision rather than
  a fix to slip into this sprint.

---

# One design system — the layout layer (2026-09-07)

User directive: pick a library per layer (shadcn · Kibo · Phosphor · Tailwind ·
Motion · TanStack Table · dnd-kit · Tiptap · Recharts · React Day Picker), and
then — the part that actually matters — *"I do not want different pages to have
their own unique layouts or styling… a clear hierarchy for when to reuse an
existing layout versus when to introduce a new one."* Followed the same day by a
20-point consistency audit with screenshots, whose P0s are design-system
fragmentation, the Projects/Clients split, and the accent colour.

## What was already true

Most of the *component* layer was already one system, and it is worth saying so
rather than re-solving it: `components/ds/ui` is canonical (66 files import it),
Phosphor runs through the single seam in `components/ds/icons.ts`, the overlay
chrome was unified in July, `scroll-region` is the one scrolling rule, and
`ViewContainer` and `PageHeader` each own their piece.

**The gap was one level up.** Nothing owned the SHAPE those primitives make
together, so all thirteen screens composed it by hand — and every hand
composition re-decided the parts that are not a page's to decide. Measured
before touching anything:

| what | answers found |
|---|---|
| page width | **seven** — 978 · 1200 · 1000 · 760 · 720 · 680 · none |
| top padding | four — 0 · 24 · 28 · 32 |
| bottom padding | five — 0 · 24 · 40 · 64 · 80 |
| page entrance | four — none · `fadein 180ms` · `fadein 220ms` · `animate-ds-fadein` |
| secondary rail width | two — 230 · 240 |
| "Full width" preference | honoured on 4 pages, silently ignored on 9 |

None of that variety meant anything, and nothing failed while it was true.

## The three archetypes

A new screen is one of these. The decision rule lives at the top of
`components/ui/page-layout.tsx`, where it will be read.

- **`<PageLayout>`** — one pane you read down. Home, Tasks list, Finance,
  Settings, Habits, Memory, Forms, Goals, an invoice.
- **`<HubLayout>`** — a rail of records beside a detail. Clients, Projects,
  Tasks, Week. `bleed` when the detail is a canvas (Tasks board, Week board);
  `railPadding={false}` when the rail brings its own section rhythm.
- **`<CanvasLayout>`** — a body that owns its own geometry. Calendar, Content.

Each owns the header row, the width, the rhythm and the entrance. A page now
declares only what is genuinely its own.

## The resolutions, and why

**Rhythm → `--view-pt`/`--view-pb`, via a named `page-rhythm` utility.** Not
because the token was there first: it is *better*, because it steps down under
the compact density setting and a literal `pt-8` cannot. Naming it as a utility
matters — the moment it is two Tailwind classes somebody types 32/64 instead.

**Entrance → one opacity fade, `zb-page-in`.** The global `fadein` keyframe also
lifts 4px, which is movement under a reader who is already looking at the page.

**Rail width → `--rail-w`, and it is 230, not 240.** Extracting the Clients and
Projects rail would have canonised the WRONG number: their identical `w-60` was a
Tailwind scale step, while Tasks and Documents sat on 230 citing the Figma
sidebar panel — and `--sidebar-w` is 230. Checked which copy was better before
picking the official one, the same trap `--view-px` fell into last time.

**"Full width" applied in the layouts, so it applies everywhere.** A device
preference that works on four screens out of thirteen is worse than one that
works on none, because the reader cannot tell which they are looking at.

## Projects vs Clients — the entity-detail pattern

The two were already 90% the same pattern, written twice. Both carried a
private, character-for-character identical `PropRow`; their title rows had
already drifted (`gap-2.5` vs `gap-3`), which is what two identical copies always
become. Extracted `<RecordHeader>` + `<PropertyRow>` into the DS
(`components/ds/ui/record-header.tsx`). The identity mark stays a slot — a
project is identified by its colour, a client by their initials, and that is the
one part of the header carrying information rather than shape.

The real divergence was the sectioning: Projects tabbed its six sections,
Clients stacked all six in one column. Clients now uses the same `<Tabs>`, the
same `useModeParam` URL mode, and the glossary's own words — **Overview ·
Projects · Money · Forms · Meetings · Feedback**, where "Money" is the word
Projects already uses. Verified: a real click flips the tab, writes `?ctab=money`
and swaps the panel.

## Accent

`tokens.css` names *"selected days, focus states, today rings"* as accent sites,
and Settings → Appearance swaps `--accent` — but the calendar hard-coded
`ink-900`, so picking blue recoloured checkboxes, switches and sliders and left
the calendar grey. Today's date, the now-line and the now chip now read
`var(--accent)` with `var(--on-accent)` on top. Verified by pinning a blue
accent: markers went `rgb(196,28,114)` → `rgb(47,111,237)`, foreground stayed
`rgb(253,254,251)`. **With the default accent nothing changes** — this is the
token being honoured, not a restyle.

## Nav selected state

`weight="fill"` on the selected row's glyph, from `navWeight()` in app-shell —
one function, so sidebar rows, project rows and the mobile tab bar cannot answer
it differently. This **supersedes** the icon seam's old "never fill a nav-row
glyph" rule, and the rule text in `components/ds/icons.ts` was rewritten rather
than left to contradict the code. The state used to live entirely in the wash
behind the row, which is legible on the row you are looking at and invisible in
peripheral vision, because an outline glyph has the same ink mass either way.
Also collapsed the module rows and project rows onto one `navRowStyle()` — they
were duplicating a 12-property object — and added `aria-current="page"`.

Verified with a probe AND a control: navigating `/calendar` → `/clients`, exactly
the two rows whose selection changed also changed glyph geometry (`d` length
203↔227 and 406↔409); every other row's path hashed identically. A first pass
compared only the first 40 characters of the path and reported a false mismatch —
comparing a truncated path is not comparing the path.

## Enforcement

`components/ui/page-layout.test.ts` — eight source-scanning checks, the same
shape as the ViewContainer and EmptyState guards, each one a drift that actually
happened. Two of them exist because the first version could not see Goals: it
centred its own column in an INLINE STYLE (`maxWidth: 1000`), invisible to a
guard that reads Tailwind classes. The scan blanks comment lines rather than
dropping them, because dropping them renumbers the file and a guard that reports
the wrong line sends the next reader to an innocent function.

## Found on the way

- **`feedback-board` was double-padded** — `p-6` on a pane that now sits inside
  the hub's own column, plus a second entrance 40ms slower than the page's.
- **`app-loading`'s skeleton sat at a different inset** than the page it stands
  in for, so content visibly jumped when it landed — which is the exact failure
  the note at the top of that file warns about.
- **Week and Tasks share `TasksRail`.** Making it shed its own chrome for the
  hub broke Week until Week came through `HubLayout` too; they are now identical
  down their left edge, which is what the rail's own comment always claimed.
- **Tasks' list silently widened 978 → 1200** when it adopted the hub's default,
  caught by measuring rather than by looking. Its list is a reading column.

**1281 tests** (8 new guards), `tsc` clean, no new lint errors, every migrated
surface rendered and measured in the browser.

## Owed

- **Documents** is a hub whose rail is still hand-rolled in inline styles with
  its own 230px box; it should come through `HubLayout` with `bleed`.
- **Library alignment is NOT done.** Of the named stack, TanStack Table,
  Recharts and React Day Picker are **not installed** (database-view runs a
  bespoke grid engine, `ds/ui/chart.tsx` and `ds/ui/date-picker.tsx` are
  hand-rolled), Tiptap is installed with **zero imports** (the editor is
  hand-rolled ProseMirror, which Tiptap wraps — a swap is a real project, not a
  dependency change), and `components/kibo-ui/` no longer exists.
- The 720px measure inside a record's tab body is written out in both Projects
  and Clients. Identical today, so consistent today — but it is the next
  duplicated constant to become a token.
- `month-grid.tsx` still carries the 3px coloured `border-left` the craft
  detector flags. Pre-existing.
