# One time picker, and the registry that never shipped (2026-09-07)

Reported as a styling bug: the time picker's hard blue selection conflicts with
Appearance → Accent, and the popup "does not belong to the same component family".

## The blue was never ours

Home's Schedule composer rendered a raw `<input type="time">`, so the three
columns with the blue selection and the `--:--` empty state were **Chrome's**,
out of UA shadow DOM our CSS cannot reach. There was nothing to restyle. Proved
before changing anything: `input[type="time"] × 2`, Zenboard picker × 0.

It also formats to the OS locale, which is why that field read `09:00 AM` while
`formatClock` pins a 24-hour house clock (`CLOCK = 'en-GB'`) and the calendar
gutter two inches away read 13, 14, 15. That split differs per machine.

## Three answers to "pick a time"

| | importers | positioning | selected | numerals | duration hint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ds/ui/time-picker.tsx` | **0** | Radix Popover + Portal | `bg-berry-100` | `font-mono` ✗ | — |
| `calendar/time-picker.tsx` | 1 | `absolute top-[30px]` | ink | tabular ✓ | **yes** |
| raw `<input type="time">` | 7 sites | browser | browser blue | OS | — |

The DS one had been built against design-system.md §4.24 and **never wired to
anything**. Neither custom one was simply better, so the survivor takes the
better half of each rather than crowning one: Radix positioning and text-first
parsing from the DS ("3pm", "15:30", "9", "9:05am"), `durationFrom` and tabular
numerals from the calendar's. Chrome and row metrics now come from
`MENU_PANEL_CLASS`/`MENU_ITEM_CLASS`, so the popover is pixel-identical to every
menu in the app: measured `bg rgb(38,38,38) · radius 12px · pad 6px · row 36px ·
Geist`, selected row `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)` — no blue anywhere.

Selection is INK, not accent, and deliberately: this is a select, and the
standing rule (2026-07-19) is accent for data-entry controls and ink for chrome,
which lists select explicitly. Accent here would disagree with the DS `Select`
six pixels away — the same failure in a new colour.

`components/calendar/time-picker.tsx` is **deleted**. All seven native inputs are
migrated (Home ×2, Settings ×3, Content, Onboarding).

## All-day was two different gestures

The event composer replaced its time row with the word "All-day"; Home deleted
the fields outright. Both threw away times you had already picked and moved
everything below them. Now both **dim and go inert**, and the value survives —
verified: `disabled: [true,true]`, fields still present, `values: ["07:00",""]`.

## The z-index registry had never actually shipped

Chasing why the time list rendered *behind* the composer that opened it —
measured, only the right-hand duration column was visible — turned up something
bigger. `app/tokens.css` re-declared the **whole registry with the old numbers**
alongside `ds-theme.css`'s `@theme` block. Tailwind hoists `@theme` variables to
the top of its output, so the plain `:root` — imported *earlier*, emitted
*later* — silently won.

The consequence: ds-theme's registry carries a long comment explaining that
toast and tooltip were raised from 55/70 to 320/330 so an Undo toast could clear
the command palette. **Measured on the live page, the served values were still
55 and 70.** That fix had been written, reasoned about and never applied for as
long as both copies existed, and nothing could have caught it except reading the
computed value — which is the lesson the header-token bug taught once already.

Deleted the duplicate; ds-theme is the only declaration. Then applied the same
argument the registry already makes for toast to `--z-dropdown`, which every
portalled DS surface uses (popover, dropdown menu, select, combobox, hover card,
filter, date and time pickers): at 40 it sat under every app overlay in the
60–200 band. Now **310**, between fullscreen and toast. Served ladder verified
end to end: 10 · 45 · 50 · 60 · 300 · 310 · 320 · 330.

## The default event colour

The palette led with `gray` and argued that "a wall of brand-accent events reads
as noise", with accent parked last. Real argument, wrong scope: every *other*
calendar already carries a colour (Task blue, Horizon purple, Projects green,
Clients orange, Money yellow, Documents pink), so the user's own events were the
only colourless things on their own calendar — and the accent setting had no
effect on the densest surface in the app.

Default is now `accent`, first swatch, selected. Verified on a new event:
`firstSwatch: "accent"`, `firstIsSelected: true`.

**Then the user corrected the treatment, and they were right.** First pass gave
the accent card an accent bar *and* a 10% accent wash *and* accent text, which
turned a week of events into one hue. Measured, the wash was not even loud (19
units off the canvas against 15–35 for the picked hues) — the problem was three
elements saying the same thing at once. The accent now takes the **left bar
only**; the card keeps the app's neutral fill and ink (`rgb(42,40,37)`, verified
identical to `--pal-gray-bg`). A picked colour still tints its whole card,
because there the colour is the user's deliberate signal.

## A regression of mine, found by the user

Adding "Take notes" to the composer footer earlier this session pushed **Save
14px past the panel's 340px edge**, where it was clipped. It was never a form
verb — it navigates away to a meeting — so it moved into the body beside
Participants and Conferencing, which is the row language that column already
speaks. Footer is back to Delete · Cancel · Save, `saveClipped: false`.

## Enforcement

- `components/ds/ui/time-picker.test.ts` — parser tests (including `12am`→0 and
  `12pm`→720, where 12-hour clocks break) plus two system checks: no native time
  input anywhere, and exactly one `time-picker.tsx` in the tree.
- `lib/date-vocabulary.test.ts` gained "no hand-rolled 12-hour clock". Home's
  private `9:00 – 9:30pm` formatter had slipped past every existing check by
  never calling `toLocaleTimeString` — it did the `% 12` arithmetic itself.
- `formatClockRange` added to the date vocabulary; the week grid and Home's
  schedule both use it. Home now reads **zero** 12-hour times, nine 24-hour ones.

**1290 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17 errors.

## Owed

- **The registry is still bypassed by raw values** in 14+ places: `z-[1000]`
  (legacy ui/popover), `z-[200]` ×2 (app-shell menus), `z-[120]`/`z-[121]`
  (tasks keyboard palette, event composer), `z-[80]`, `z-[70]`, `z-[60]` ×4.
  Each needs its own layer decision and its own verification; the token fix above
  makes them harmless for popovers but they are still outside the system.
- `bg-berry-100` / `text-berry-700` appear in six DS components. They *compute*
  to `surface-fill`/`ink-900` via a remap in globals.css, so they render
  correctly — but the names lie, which is how the next reader reintroduces pink.
- The DS `Select`'s selected option carries that same berry naming.

# One date picker (2026-09-07)

The direct sibling of the time-picker work, and the same defect at larger scale:
**thirteen raw `<input type="date">` against six uses of the DS `DatePicker`**,
so the app's most common way to pick a date was the browser's, not the app's.

## What the DS picker already had, and what it was missing

It was genuinely good — Chrono natural-language parsing ("tomorrow", "next
fri"), the house date format, Monday-first from `WEEK_STARTS_ON`, a keyboard
grid that is one tab stop, a presets rail. It was also carrying the same
three faults the time picker had:

- popover chrome that was not the app's (`rounded-md border-line bg-paper` vs
  the canonical `MENU_PANEL_CLASS`),
- `bg-berry-500` / `ring-berry-500` on the selected day and today's dot — names
  for a colour the app does not have (they remap to ink, so they *rendered*
  right and read wrong),
- the wrong icon seam (`@/lib/icons`).

And a fourth all its own: a field that did not match the `TimePicker` sitting
directly beside it in the event composer — different radius (sm vs md), surface
(paper vs surface-raised) and type size (body vs ui). A date box and a time box
that were visibly not the same control.

Selected day is now **ink** and today's dot is **accent**, which is the split
the calendar grid uses: accent marks what is live, ink marks what is chosen.

## The API was making every caller do UTC-date arithmetic

It took `Date` objects, so all six call sites paid for it:

```
value={deadline ? new Date(deadline + 'T00:00:00') : null}
onValueChange={(d) => setDeadline(d ? dateToISO(d) : '')}
```

`dateToISO` existed **four times** — `lib/date`'s `isoDateIn`, `lib/calendar`'s
`localISODate`, and a private copy each in projects-workspace and
new-project-modal. That is the exact shape of the UTC-date bug this codebase has
already paid for once: `toISOString()` on a local Date is the previous day for
anyone west of UTC, and memory-home was building its Date at **noon**
specifically to dodge it.

A calendar date is not an instant. `<DatePicker>` takes and returns
`YYYY-MM-DD` now — what the database, the URL and `lib/date` already speak — so
the conversions and the noon workaround are gone, and two of the four copies of
`dateToISO` went with them. Both pickers now share one prop shape
(`value` / `onValueChange`), which also fixed a convention slip of mine: I had
given `TimePicker` an `onChange` where the DS uses `onValueChange`.

## The `trigger` slot

Four screens had each invented the same workaround — an invisible
`<input type="date">` stretched over their own UI with `opacity-0`: the task
composer's date chip, a database grid cell, a document property, and Triage's
"Pick date" button (which called `showPicker()` on a hidden input, opening
Chrome's calendar in the middle of a keyboard-driven flow). Four copies of one
idea is a missing prop, so `<DatePicker>` takes a `trigger` and renders the
caller's control with the same popover.

The trade is written next to it: a trigger has nowhere to type, so that form
loses the "next friday" parsing. The presets rail carries most of that weight,
and a chip has no room for a text field anyway.

Verified end to end on the task composer: the chip opens **our** calendar
(`z 310`, `bg rgb(38,38,38)`, radius 12px, Monday-first, accent today-dot,
presets rail), "Tomorrow" commits, and the chip reads **"8 Sep"** — the house
format, not "Sep 8".

## Enforcement

`components/ds/ui/date-picker.test.ts` — no native date input anywhere, exactly
one `date-picker.tsx` in the tree, and nobody re-deriving `dateToISO`.

**1294 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17 errors.

## Owed

- The public form renderer now uses the DS picker too. That is the right call
  for consistency and for "next friday" on a desktop brief, but it does trade
  away the OS wheel a phone would otherwise give a client filling a form. Worth
  a look if mobile form completion ever drops.
- Still outstanding from the previous entry: 14+ raw `z-[…]` values outside the
  registry, and `bg-berry-100`/`text-berry-700` in five remaining DS components.

---

# Memory hidden, and the z-index registry finally adopted (2026-09-07)

## Memory is off the surface, not deleted

User: *"remove memory no need right now"*. Taken as the product module, and done
in the reversible form — the nav row is the ONE place it was reachable from, so:

- `app-shell` nav row commented out (plus its `Brain` icon import),
- the `<MemoryPanel>` removed from the Client detail and the Project overview,
- "Go to Memory" removed from the command palette and the `G R` chord from the
  keyboard sheet.

`/memory`, `components/memory/*`, `lib/memory*`, the Recall wiring in the palette
and the applied 0029 migration are all untouched. Verified: the sidebar now reads
Home · Tasks · Calendar · Projects · Clients · Forms · Content · Docs · Finance ·
Goals · Habits, with no `/memory`.

## Forty raw z-index values, not fourteen

The earlier estimate was low. A full sweep found **~40**, of which ~28 were real
app layers picked by guesswork: 40, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 121, 130, 131, 200,
210, 1000 — each chosen to beat whatever the author was looking at.

Everything transient now names `z-dropdown`: the shell's sidebar-control, account
and New menus; the notifications bell; document properties, the documents filter
and actions menus, the database row menu, the block editor's caret layer, block
menu and colour grid; the rich-text floating toolbar; Focus's two menus; Goals'
menu; `picker-panel`; the task-detail chip panels; the tasks keyboard palette;
Week's two popovers. Modal surfaces name `z-modal` (command palette, quick
capture, the mobile drawer, the event composer, the legacy centred popover). The
collapsed-rail tooltip names `z-tooltip`.

**One behaviour change, deliberate.** The floating focus timer shipped at a raw
90 — above a DS modal (50) but below the command palette (200), so a dialog
sometimes covered it and sometimes did not. There was no layer for "persistent
floating chrome", so `--z-widget: 30` is new, and the timer now sits under every
overlay. A dialog owns the screen. The hover-expanding sidebar rail joined it
(it was a raw 40) because it has the same job: float over the page, including
the page's own sticky headers, and stay under anything transient.

Served ladder, verified end to end:
`sticky 10 · widget 30 · overlay 45 · modal 50 · drag 60 · fullscreen 300 ·
dropdown 310 · toast 320 · tooltip 330`.

**The original bug is fixed.** Opening the time picker inside the event composer
now paints the list fully on top — `popoverZ 310`, and three positional probes
(left edge, centre, bottom) all report the popover as the topmost element. Before,
only the right-hand duration column was visible because the composer covered the
times.

## What stayed, and how the guard tells the difference

Local stacking is not an app layer and stays: a calendar event over its grid
lines, a doc card's menu over its row, the focus timer's own internal parts, the
block editor's drop indicator. `components/ui/z-index.test.ts` separates them by
**position** (`fixed` is app-level by definition) and by **size** (a local ladder
counts 1, 2, 3 — not 200), with one explicit `/* z-local */` escape marker on the
single line whose local number happens to be large. The marker is on the line
itself rather than in a comment above it, because a comment above drifts from the
code it describes.

A fourth check asserts the registry is declared **once** — the defect from the
previous entry, where a duplicate in `tokens.css` silently beat `ds-theme.css`'s
`@theme` block and kept a documented fix from ever shipping.

**1298 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 17 errors.

## Owed

- `bg-berry-100` / `text-berry-700` in five DS components (data-table, list-row,
  combobox, filter, select). They remap to `surface-fill`/`ink-900` so they
  render correctly — the names are the problem.
- Documents is the last hub still hand-rolling its rail instead of `HubLayout`.

# Pins, the task panel's chrome, and a contrast floor (2026-09-07)

## Pinned replaces Projects in the sidebar

User: the sidebar's Projects section *"is not a project — I want to use it as a
pin. User can pin anything: project, document, task, form. Drag up and down to
change the order. Scrollable. Almost any amount of pins."*

**No migration.** `profiles.preferences` is already free-form JSON carrying
accent, density, displayFont and the Google-sync metadata, and pins are a
per-user preference of exactly that kind. They go in it under one key, follow the
user across devices, and every write is read-modify-write — writing `{ pins }`
alone would take the user's accent with it, which is how `google-calendar`
already merges into this column.

**No new concept either.** A pin is `{ type: EntityType, id, label }` — the same
vocabulary `recordHref` can address and `ENTITY_GLYPH` can draw. So "pin
anything" needed no polymorphic table, no icon map and no route: a pin is a
reference into the fabric.

`lib/pins.ts` + 11 tests own the rules — one pin per record, `doc:1` and `task:1`
are different records, an unknown type is dropped on read (the column is
free-form, so the READER decides what is valid), a cancelled drag returns the
list unchanged, and a 200 ceiling that is a guard on a column every page load
reads rather than a product limit.

`components/shell/pinned-rail.tsx` draws it: dnd-kit sortable with a keyboard
sensor, the grip only on hover (a row you cannot click without starting a drag is
a row you cannot navigate with), unpin on hover, `scroll-region` so the rail does
not narrow by 6px when the list outgrows the space, optimistic with a snap-back
on failure.

**A guard test caught me mid-build.** I reconciled the server's list with
`useEffect(() => setLocal(initial), [initial])` — the exact pattern
`lib/use-server-state.ts` exists to stop. `useServerState` reconciles during
render.

**And a query disappeared.** The layout fetched active projects on *every page
load* just to draw those nav rows. Pins read from the `profile` it already loads,
so the query, the prop and the `ProjectLite` type are all gone.

Verified: four pins of four different types render with their own glyphs, four
grips, four unpin buttons, `overflow-y: auto`.

**Still owed, and the feature is not usable without it: there is no way to MAKE a
pin yet.** The control belongs in `<PageView>`'s toolbar, since every record
opens through it. That is next.

## The task panel was the one screen with pills

User: *"this popover feels like not part of design — we never use rounded corner
and this type of spacing and sizing."* Correct, and measurable: the eight
property chips were `border-radius: var(--r-full)` at 30px with their own 12px
padding, `--paper-3` and `text-caption`. They were the only pill controls in the
app; everything else that opens a menu is a `<Button>`. They are now
`Button size="sm" variant="secondary"` verbatim — 28px, `rounded-sm`, `px-2.5`,
`text-ui`, on `surface-fill`.

## Adding a subtask no longer walks into it

User: *"when I create a subtask I automatically enter the subtask, but the user
should still be in the main task. It's the user's choice."* The handler passed
the new id to `loadTree`, which SELECTS it — so pressing Enter took you inside
the thing you just made, and adding a second one meant navigating back out.
Breaking a task down is a burst; opening a subtask is a separate decision.

## A contrast floor, found by measuring

Built a repeatable audit probe (objective checks only — target size, contrast,
mono misuse, overflow, unnamed controls, `<h1>` count) and ran it on Home. It
found **17 low-contrast strings**, which turned out to be two systemic causes:

- **Opacity-faded text**, which CLAUDE.md bans outright. Event times sat at
  **3.15:1** against their card, under the 4.5 floor — while the palette's own
  text token gives 7.7–9.7 on every colour. The fade bought nothing: the time
  line is already quieter than the title by size and weight. Also removed the
  fade on a *done* event, where the strike and the ticked box already say done.
- **`text-ink-400`, which is not a legal text colour.** Measured against all
  three surfaces it gives 4.47 / 3.98 / 3.61 — below AA everywhere — and it is
  used for text in 83 places. Lifting the token would collapse it into
  `ink-500`, so the ramp is right and the usage is wrong: `ink-500` (4.79 worst
  case) is the quiet-text floor, and `ink-400` is a non-text tint. **The sweep of
  those 83 is not done yet.**

**1309 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint at the 17-error baseline.

# Motion (2026-09-07)

User, twice: *"the entire app looks static. There is no interaction, no motion,
no smoothness. The app feels very laggy and boring and slow."*

## "Laggy" was measured before it was believed

Dev build, tasks page:

| | |
|---|---|
| long tasks (main thread blocked >50ms) | **0** |
| animated elements | 77 of 326 |
| …of which animated COLOUR only | **44** |
| …of which MOVED at all | **7** |

So the app was never slow — the main thread was idle. It was **motionless**, and
a click that produces no movement reads as lag even when the response is
instant. Every state change was a colour crossfade, which at a glance is
indistinguishable from the hover it replaces.

The cause was written down as a rule. `components/ds/ui/button.tsx` carried:

> `// No transforms on click (§6.3) — pressed feedback is the variant's active: fill only.`

That is a decision the user has now reversed twice, so it is reversed in the
code and the reason is recorded next to it rather than left to contradict them.

## The press

`.zb-press` crossfaded colour and nothing else. It now scales, and so does every
other pressable thing — **globally**, because being pressable is not a property
of using one component: measured on the tasks page, only **5 of 24** buttons
were DS `Button`s, so a press attached to the component would have reached a
fifth of the controls and made the app inconsistent in a new way.

`button:active` and `[role="button"]:active` scale to **0.98** in 20ms and
release on a spring. 0.98 rather than 0.97 because it has to sit right on a
400px list row as well as a 28px icon button, and a wide element shrinking by 3%
reads as a shrink rather than a push. `.zb-nopress` opts out; disabled and
loading controls are excluded, because a press means "this is happening" and
must not fire on a control that is refusing. Reduced motion keeps the colour and
drops the movement — the global reset only collapses *duration*, which would
have made the scale instant rather than absent.

## The seam

`components/ds/ui/motion.tsx` is the one place the app imports an animation
library, for the same reason `components/ds/icons.ts` is the one place it
imports glyphs. Its vocabulary is deliberately four items, because motion earns
its place only when it answers one of four questions:

- **Did it hear me?** → the press (CSS, because it must land in 20ms and never wait on JS)
- **Where did it come from?** → `<Appear>`
- **Where did it go?** → `<Presence>`
- **What moved?** → `<Move>` — layout animation, the only one CSS genuinely cannot do,
  because CSS has no idea where an element used to be

Task rows now arrive with a capped stagger (past a handful a stagger stops
reading as sequence and starts reading as delay) and leave by collapsing, with
the rows below animating the gap closed.

## The result, same measurement

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| buttons with press feedback | 5 / 24 | **37 / 37** |
| animated elements that MOVE | 7 | **43** |

**1309 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint at the 17-error baseline.

## Owed

- CLAUDE.md still says *"No scale, bounce, or entrance animations"* under
  Interaction. The code now contradicts it deliberately; the file needs the same
  amendment the Button got.
- The four motion primitives are applied to task rows and every button. The other
  lists — pins, board cards, documents, content — should follow, and the Focus
  timer rebuild (the user's reference layout, Pomodoro removed, START on the task
  row) is still queued behind this.

# Notion → Documents: fidelity, and a door in the right place (2026-09-07)

User: *"make a Notion → our document migration door… import entirely using their
Notion link… the migrated document must not be damaged — it should look and
behave exactly like their Notion document."*

## What already existed

`lib/import-docs.ts` already parsed a Notion Markdown export — filename ids, the
duplicate H1, the `Property: value` block — and `importDocs` already wrote the
pages. It was wired into **Settings → Import**. So the import was not missing;
two things about it were.

## 1. It was damaging documents, and here is exactly how

The body went through `textToBlocks` — the generic PASTE parser. Right for
pasted text, wrong for a Notion export, because it silently dropped:

| Notion writes | old result | now |
|---|---|---|
| indented sub-items | **flattened** to one column | `indent` preserved |
| `\| a \| b \|` table | one text block per row of pipes | a real `table` with `rows` |
| `![alt](img.png)` | the literal markdown as prose | an `image` with `src` |
| `<aside>` callout | raw HTML as text | a `callout` |
| `<details><summary>` | raw HTML as text | a `toggle` + indented children |
| a bare URL | plain text | a `bookmark` |
| `$$ … $$` | prose | `code` with `lang: latex` |

The nesting one is the loss that matters: it is not a style difference, it is
the meaning the indentation carried. A three-level outline arrived as a flat
list of bullets.

`notionBodyToBlocks` is its own function rather than a flag on `textToBlocks`,
because the two have different jobs and a parser that tries to be both starts
guessing — a pasted line beginning with `|` is prose; in an export it is a table.

**Nothing needed a new block type.** Every Notion construct mapped onto a block
Zenboard already had, which is the reason this fidelity was reachable at all.
11 new tests, one per thing the old parser destroyed.

## 2. The door was in the wrong room

Import lived in Settings — where you configure the app, not where you go holding
an export. There is now an **Import** button beside **New doc** in Documents,
opening one shared `<NotionImportModal>`: the same parse, the same action, one
implementation. It previews what is about to land (documents AND block counts,
because "12 files" tells you nothing about whether your document survived).

## The link, honestly

**A Notion URL alone cannot import a private page**, which is what people
actually have. Notion's API requires an `Authorization` header and the page to
be shared with an integration; a page merely "published to web" is readable only
through an undocumented internal endpoint that would break without warning and
still covers none of the private pages. So the dialog asks for the export and
says why, rather than accepting a link and failing at the user later.

The real link path is **Notion OAuth** — connect the workspace once, then pick
pages by URL. That is the follow-up, and it is a genuine feature (an OAuth app,
a token per user, a page picker), not a field.

**1320 tests**, `tsc` clean. Lint is **18 errors, up one from the 17 baseline** —
`documents-view.tsx:249`, a `set-state-in-effect` in the draft-loading effect.
That code is not mine and I did not touch it, but it surfaced on a file I edited,
so it is owed rather than dismissed.

## Verified, and not

Verified: the converter, by 11 tests covering each construct; the Import button
renders in the Documents toolbar between Filter and New doc.

**Now verified too.** The documents harness re-enters a document on every
interaction, so the grid toolbar could not be clicked — rather than leave the
modal on inference, `app/dev-preview/notion-import/` renders it in the smallest
tree that can. Opened: `role="dialog"`, the title, the dropzone, the file input,
and Import correctly disabled until files are chosen.

# Focus, rebuilt around the timer (2026-09-08)

User, with a reference screenshot: *"Bring the timer into the focus zone and
follow the layout… if a user wants to start a timer with the added task they
can… give a top option to add a time or set time or just start timer, and remove
Pomodoro."*

## The timer was hidden inside a ⋮

Focus had a session timer, and it lived behind an unlabelled overflow button in
the corner. The one control the mode exists for could not be found by looking at
the screen. It is now **on the task**, beside the two numbers it moves between.

## Pomodoro is gone

It forced a mode decision into every timer — two clocks with different rules, one
of which ignored the task's own estimate — for a feature the user called
unimportant. What is left is one session timer counting up against the task's
PLANNED time, which is a number the user already set.

## The layout

Rebuilt to the reference, in Zenboard's own visual language rather than its
colours:

```
TODAY'S TASKS                          ACTUAL   PLANNED
◯ Finish the pricing page copy          0:02     45:00   [⏸ Pause]
  High · Balluji
  ↳ subtasks, + Add subtask
UP NEXT (2)
◯ Send Balluji the revised timeline  ●Balluji  –:–   15:00
◯ Book the studio for Thursday                 –:–     —
✓ Reply to the tax email                     10:00   10:00
  + Add a task to today…
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
← Previous  Next →      1/4 done · 10m in flow   [✓ Complete task]
```

Four decisions worth naming:

- **One `<TimeCells>`**, so the task you are on, the ones queued behind it and
  the ones already done all land on the same two columns. A column of times that
  shifts as the seconds tick is unreadable, hence fixed widths and tabular
  figures.
- **"–:–", not "0:00"**, for a task that has not run. Nothing has happened yet;
  a zero reads as a measurement.
- **Done stays on screen.** A day where you finished six things and one where
  you finished none are not the same day, and hiding the evidence is most of why
  Focus felt like it never moved.
- **The footer carries the completion.** Completing a task is the most common
  act in Focus and it was two clicks inside a ⋮.

Verified live: Start → **Pause**, ACTUAL ticking `0:02` against `45:00`, the
other rows still `–:–`, footer reading `1/4 done · 10m in flow`.

## Setting a time when you create the task

The value was always reachable — the composer parses `30m` out of the title —
but only if you knew the syntax, so most tasks arrived with no estimate and Focus
had nothing to count against. There is now an **Estimate** chip beside Date /
Priority / Project: No estimate · 5m · 15m · 30m · 45m · 1h · 1h 30m · 2h.

An explicitly picked estimate wins over one parsed from the title — the chip is
the deliberate act, the text is a shortcut. Both hosts honour it, and Focus now
persists it on create (it was hard-coded to `null`, so a task created inside
Focus could never be timed against anything).

**My own guard caught me mid-build**: I hand-rolled a `1h 30m` formatter for
"in flow" and `date-vocabulary.test.ts` failed on the spot. `formatMinutes` is
the vocabulary's entry, and six copies of that formatter once disagreed.

## Also closed this session

- **The Notion import modal is now verified**, not inferred. The documents
  harness re-enters a document on every interaction, so
  `app/dev-preview/notion-import/` renders the modal in the smallest tree that
  can: it opens with the dropzone, the file input, and Import correctly disabled
  until files are chosen.
- **A flash bug in Documents.** Loading a draft ran in an effect, so opening a
  second document painted one frame carrying the FIRST one's title, blocks and
  tags. Moved into render (React's documented "adjusting state when a prop
  changes"), with the previous id in STATE — reading a ref during render is
  unsafe under concurrent rendering, and the lint rule that caught my first
  attempt was right. `loadedRef` stays where it is doing its other job: the
  autosave guard. Splitting the two was deliberate; folding autosave bookkeeping
  into render would put a data-loss path on a hot code path.

**1320 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint back to the **17-error baseline** — one lower
than before, since the effect that caused the flash is gone.

# Light + dark, on shadcn's tokens (2026-09-08)

User: *"I want light mode and dark mode both — use shadcn black and white design
tokens, you decide what's best"*, then the shadcn theming spec itself, then
*"use shadcn colors with tones, only use colors from shadcn."*

## Light mode was a dead control that was already switched on

`applyAppearance` had always written `data-theme` onto `<html>` and the settings
panel offered Light / Dark / System. **No CSS anywhere read the attribute.**
Measured live: `data-theme` was `"light"` and `--paper` still computed to
`#121212`, body still black. 558 token declarations across four files, all
dark-only.

## The first fix was wrong, and the measurement said so

Mirroring the dark theme — flipping every `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.05)` wash to
`rgb(18 18 18 / 0.05)` — produced a page with **three** distinct background
colours on it, the two that mattered at **1.046:1**. The user's words were "all
looks flat" and "buttons is not visible", and both were exactly right.

That is not a tuning error, it is physics: a translucent wash over near-black is
a strong lift; the same wash over off-white is nothing. **Dark separates with
luminance. Light separates with borders and solid tones.** shadcn's light theme
is the canonical statement of it — `--secondary` and `--muted` are solids
(`oklch(0.97)`), `--border` is a real `oklch(0.922)` hairline — which is why the
user's instruction and the correct architecture turned out to be the same thing.

## The architecture

- **`app/theme-shadcn.css`** — the VALUES. shadcn's neutral semantic tokens,
  light in `:root` and dark in `html[data-theme='dark']`, exposed through
  `@theme inline` so `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`
  and `ring-ring` are real utilities.
- **`app/tokens-light.css`** — the BRIDGE. Every Zenboard primitive re-pointed
  at a shadcn token, for both themes at once. Nothing here invents a colour;
  that is the point of "only use colors from shadcn". Re-pointing ~30
  primitives re-colours all 558 derived tokens.

Three decisions worth naming:

- **`html[data-theme=…]`, not `:root`.** The three older token files set the
  same primitives in plain `:root` and are imported later, so a `:root` here
  would tie on specificity and lose on order. Not hypothetical: `globals.css`
  sets `color-scheme: dark` in a `:root`, which kept winning while the page
  rendered light — so light mode told the browser it was dark and native
  scrollbars, the caret and form controls stayed dark inside a white page.
- **shadcn's `--accent` is renamed `--accent-surface`.** shadcn's accent is a
  hover/menu SURFACE; Zenboard's `--accent` is the user's chosen brand hue, read
  by ~40 files and pinned inline by the appearance switcher. Two meanings, one
  name — taking shadcn's would have silently repainted every checkbox, switch
  and focus ring the moment the file loaded.
- **The ink ramp is mixed, not collapsed.** shadcn ships two ink steps;
  Zenboard's type hierarchy uses seven. The middle steps are `color-mix` along
  the same neutral axis — still only shadcn colours, still one source.

## A bug I wrote and then measured

The bridge contained `--primary: var(--primary)` — a self-reference, which CSS
treats as invalid-at-computed-value-time and silently drops. The dark theme's
primary button lost its fill and went invisible. `--primary` exists in both
`theme-shadcn.css` and `globals.css`, so the bridge cannot name it on both
sides; `--primary-solid` is the alias that breaks the cycle.

## Verified, both themes

Measured through a canvas, because computed colours come back as `lab()` and a
naive `rgb()` parser returns nonsense — my first two contrast readings were
artifacts of exactly that.

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| canvas / card / sunken | `#ffffff` / `#ffffff` / `#f5f5f5` | `#0a0a0a` / `#171717` / `#262626` |
| border | `#e5e5e5` solid | white 10% alpha |
| ink-900 → 500 on card | 19.8 · 17.6 · 11.4 · 6.8 · **4.74** | 17.2 · 14.1 · 9.0 · 5.9 · **6.94** |
| primary button | **17.18:1** | **14.23:1** |

Both quiet-text floors clear AA. `ink-400` sits below it in both (2.78 / 3.52) —
by design, it is the non-text tint step.

**1320 tests**, `tsc` clean, lint unchanged.

## Owed

- **`light:` variant.** `@custom-variant light` is in ds-theme.css and the DS
  Button's secondary variant uses it (`light:border light:border-line`), because
  a `#F5F5F5` fill on a white card has no edge. Every other filled-but-
  borderless control needs the same pass: Tag, Badge, SegmentedControl, chips.
- **The dark theme moved from warm to neutral.** Zenboard's dark was warm
  (`#F2F1EB` ink on `#121212`); shadcn neutral is `#FAFAFA` on `#0A0A0A`. That
  is what "only use colors from shadcn" means and it is now consistent across
  both themes — but it is a brand shift, and worth a look before it ships.
- The `text-ink-400` sweep (83 places using a non-text tint for text) is still
  open, and now matters in both themes.

# 2026-09-08 — Design system: system before screen

User directive, and it governs everything below:

> The screenshots are symptoms of a fragmented design system, not seven isolated
> UI bugs. Do not fix individual UI inconsistencies by adding one-off CSS. If a
> visual problem appears in a component, fix the underlying token or shared
> component so the correction propagates.

Reuse → extend → create → hardcode-last. Every fix here is at the token or the
shared component; none is page-specific.

## Colour

**Light is warm paper, not neutral grey.** One hue (85°) with a chroma that
RISES with the tone — 0.003 on the near-white card up to 0.010 on the border. A
flat chroma across the ramp muddies the darker steps; letting it grow keeps the
warmth only where there is tone to carry it. The ink warms too (0.004) because
neutral text on warm paper is the mismatch that reads as "yellow screen".
Lightness values unchanged, so every earlier contrast measurement still holds:
ink 19.77:1 on card, page→card 1.10, border 1.33. Renders `#f6f4ef` / `#fffffd`
/ `#e3dfd8`.

**Washes are mixed from the theme's own ink**, not pure black. A black wash over
warm paper desaturates it — the secondary button measured `#f0f0ee` against its
own `#e3dfd8` border, the fill less warm than the edge around it. `color-mix(in
oklab, var(--foreground) N%, transparent)` deepens the paper instead, and needs
no per-theme copy.

**Nine dead-neutral tokens** (the palette's neutral rung, from Tailwind's
neutral scale) moved onto the paper axis. Warmth is monotonic with tone now:
card 2 → fill 3 → border 11.

## The bug that made light "look flat"

`--color-border` was the ONE shadcn token missing from the `@theme inline` map.
Tailwind v4 makes a bare `border` paint `currentColor`, every registry component
uses bare `border`, and shadcn answers that with a base rule this project never
had. So the sign-in card drew its edge in near-black ink — **#0a0a0a at 19.8:1**
next to an input at 1.33:1. Fix = the base rule PLUS the token. Both, or neither
works.

**A focus ring must not reshape what it rings.** `:focus-visible` set
`border-radius` alongside its outline; Radix moves focus INTO a menu on open, so
an open dropdown rendered at 6px instead of its own 12px for as long as it was
open.

## Scales

| axis | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| icons | **11 sizes** (10–28) across ~800 sites | **5** (12/14/16/20/24), 141 sites moved |
| radius | 4/**5**/6/8/12 | 4/6/8/12 — `--radius-tag` was a sixth step |
| floating surfaces | menu 8 · popover 12 · dialog 12 · card 16 | one rule: surface 12 · pad 4 · child 8 |
| header inset | 8/8 vertical vs 18 right | **square**, one `--app-header-inset` |
| panel shadow | raw `rgba(0,0,0,0.04)` ×5 | `--shadow-xs`, theme-aware (0.24 in dark) |

The header fix needed the geometry to MEET the token: both rows 44px, all
controls 28px, so (44−28)/2 = 8 equals the declared padding. The segmented
control came 36 → 28 to allow it.

## One component per question

**`LayerToggle`.** The tasks rail drew project visibility with the TASK
`Checkbox` and a `tint` that was null for an uncoloured project — so it rendered
a black ticked box, identical to the "Mark done" boxes four rows below. One
glyph, two opposite meanings. Calendar had solved it correctly but privately;
extracted, both rails consume it, and the colour is never optional.

**Sentence case.** `SIDEBAR CONTROL` was a RULE, not a slip — ten DS components
shared `text-overline uppercase`, and CLAUDE.md mandated it. Fixed at the token
(`--text-overline` 11/600/0.06em → 12/500/0.005em; the tracking existed only for
capitals), swept 27 files, and CLAUDE.md updated in four places.

**`HubLayout` owns the rail toggle**, so every hub can reclaim its width, not
just Documents. It lives in the header — a control that vanishes with the thing
it controls cannot bring it back.

## Responsiveness

Documents' gallery was a `flex-wrap` of cards fixed at 220×280 — **156px of dead
space per row** in a 616px pane, plus an `!important` media query. Now
`cardGridClass` (`auto-fill` + `minmax`), and the rail follows `HUB_RAIL_CLASS`,
which below `md` stops being a column. Measured: 5 → 3 → 2 → 1 columns, no
overflow at any width, and at 700px the rail stacks so the gallery gets WIDER.

Two traps: `aspect-ratio` solves in BOTH directions (pin `width: 100%` or a
height cap narrows the card), and at one column a 372px card becomes 473px tall.

**A page header never puts its actions off screen.** At 420px the row wanted
442px in a 402px box and "New doc" sat 40px past the right edge, unreachable.
Wraps below `sm` now.

**`scrollbar-gutter: stable` reserves ONE edge**, so rail dividers were 223px in
a 230px rail — the notch where the rule should meet the border. `both-edges`
makes it symmetric (228/230).

## Content module — Inbox and Brief

**A capture is not a commitment.** Filing every dump at `stage: 'idea'` would put
a saved competitor reel in the Idea column and, once dated, on the calendar. So
`bucket: 'inbox' | 'piece' | 'reference'`, defaulting to `piece`, and
`onlyPieces()` gates every selector. Eight tests assert a capture — including one
carrying dates — reaches no column, no day, no count.

**A brief is prose, so it lives in the blocks**, not in ten more JSON fields —
which buys comments and @-mentions on it for free. Four of the ten requested
fields are deliberately absent: Topic is the title; Hook, Format and Platform
are already facts on the piece, and a fact copied into prose is a fact with two
homes.

Also fixed: the piece editor had **never been verifiable** in the harness — it
called the server, got an auth error, and closed itself on open.

## Deploy

`npm run deploy` was missing `--keep-vars` and `wrangler.jsonc` declares zero
`vars`, so running it would have **deleted every dashboard-set secret**. Fixed,
plus a credential-free `deploy:dry` for the size check.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,435 tests** (86 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles, 44 routes, **zero `dev-preview` routes** (the
`page.dev.tsx` gating that keeps the worker under 3 MiB is holding).

Guards added: `app/design-system.test.ts` (33), `app/theme-bridge.test.ts` (47),
`components/ds/ui/registry-hygiene.test.ts` (13).

## Next, in order

1. **Deploy is blocked on the user.** `npm run deploy:dry` (no credentials)
   reports the gzipped worker size; the OpenNext build is blocked by the
   sandbox classifier here. Then `npx wrangler login && npm run deploy`.
   The pasted token must be rotated.
2. **Revisit the shadcn shims.** The registry's own docs argue for Open Code —
   edit the component, don't wrap it. The `Card` and `DropdownMenu`
   compatibility layers should be pushed INTO the components.
3. A third neutral border grey (`#e5e3df` sits between soft and default).
4. One control height off the 28/32/36 spec; paddings 10/14/27 off the
   4/8/12/16 scale.
5. **Content**: Campaigns and Repurposing — the two modules that make the
   content database a workflow rather than a list. Then Analytics, Series,
   Library.
6. Relative-time hydration mismatch on the Documents gallery (spawned as a
   separate task).

# 2026-09-08 (later) — Edge tiers: a divider and a checkbox were the same token

## What was wrong

Measured in the browser on the real pages, both themes:

- an **unchecked checkbox at 1.07:1** in light, 1.3:1 in dark — no visible box
- a **text field's edge at 1.13:1** — no visible field
- a **switch's off track at 1.1:1** — only the knob marked the control

Three different controls, one cause: **`--border` drew card edges, dividers AND
control boundaries.** Those are not the same job. shadcn even ships the right
token for it — `--input` — but it had been copied verbatim from `--border`, so
every registry component that draws `border-input` drew a divider.

## The system

Four tiers, each with a bar and a test:

| tier | token | bar |
|---|---|---|
| decorative | `--border` / `-soft` | none — subtle on purpose |
| field | `--color-border-strong` (ink 16% → **28%**) | ≥1.6:1 |
| control | `--color-border-control` (**new**) | ≥3:1 |
| chromeless | none, `data-chromeless` | declared |

**Field is deliberately not 3:1.** An input has a label, a placeholder and a
value; the edge is an affordance, not the sole identifier, and no reference
product ships these at 3:1. **Control is 3:1 without exception** — an 18px box
with no text inside *is* the control.

`--color-border-control` is a **solid** (light `#838381`, dark `#828282`), which
breaks the derived-ink pattern on purpose: a guarantee must not depend on what
is behind it. Solved against all five surfaces per theme — worst case 3.30:1.
**The hardest ground is the one nearest the border's own luminance**: the
darkest surface in light, the lightest in dark.

Also fixed: the border family was the **last two-dialect family in the bridge**
(dark still raw `rgb(255 255 255 / …)`, and `-strong` 18% vs light's 16% with
nothing recording why), and `Select`/`Textarea`/`Combobox` each had a different
answer for a field's edge and its hover. One rule now: rest `-strong`, hover
`-control`. The Switch keeps its recessed fill and takes an **inset ring** for
contrast — Material 3's answer — because a fill quiet enough to read as "off"
can never also carry 3:1.

## The chromeless tier was the blocker, and it is not bookkeeping

21 inputs across 16 files each hand-spelled `border-0 bg-transparent …
outline-none`. Nothing separated *deliberately has no box* from *lost its box* —
not a reviewer and not the audit, which flagged all of them. On five pages that
ambiguity is what stopped the sweep reaching zero. `data-chromeless` declares
it; `inlineEdit` in `components/ds/ui/input.tsx` is the recipe. Two are
invisible to any source scan on principle (an inline **style object**, a plain
**CSS class**) and declare via props instead.

## Proven impossible, so nobody re-opens it

Every dark accent fill fails 3:1 on the popover. It cannot be re-tinted:

- clear 3:1 on `#333333` ⇒ luminance **≥ 0.1993**
- carry `#FDFEFB` at 4.5:1 ⇒ **≤ 0.1805**

No colour satisfies both. The shipped table had solved every dark fill against
the **card** only — the same one-ground mistake. Left as-is: the accent is never
the sole state indicator, and a band-only fix costs brand fidelity for +0.4 on
one surface.

Still open: a **user-chosen** project colour is one hex for both themes, so a
checked `LayerToggle` measures 2.14–2.53:1 on a dark rail.

## Verified

Sweep across **14 harness pages in both themes: zero failures**, except the two
exceptions above. The instrument was wrong three times before the findings were
real — it checked only the border (WCAG exempts a boundary when a fill
identifies the control); the computed `box-shadow` puts `inset` **last**, not
first; and tiering by ARIA role called a segmented item a radio. It now tiers by
*"does the shape contain text"*.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,504 tests** (90 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline.

New guards, **each verified by breaking the thing it guards**: 7 in
`app/theme-bridge.test.ts` (it resolves oklch→sRGB→WCAG for the control edge
against all four surfaces per theme) and the chromeless scan in
`app/design-system.test.ts`. One must-fail control was itself broken — it sed'd
`<input` against a `<textarea>` — so a green must-fail is investigated, never
trusted. Repaired too: the chroma-cap guard asserted `--input` was *spelled*
`oklch(…)`; it now resolves hex, oklch or one var hop, so it is strictly
stronger than before.

## Next, in order

1. **Deploy is still blocked on the user.** `npm run deploy:dry` reports the
   gzipped worker size; the OpenNext build is blocked by the sandbox classifier
   here. Then `npx wrangler login && npm run deploy`. Rotate the pasted token.
2. **Entity colours in dark** — a stored project/label hex is theme-blind, so a
   checked LayerToggle sits at 2.14:1 on a dark rail. `paletteFor()` is already
   theme-aware; stored colours need either a derived dark variant at render
   time or a stored pair.
3. **Revisit the shadcn shims** — the registry argues for Open Code: push the
   `Card` and `DropdownMenu` compatibility layers INTO the components.
4. One control height off the 28/32/36 spec; paddings 10/14/27 off the scale.
5. **Content**: Campaigns and Repurposing, then Analytics, Series, Library.

# 2026-09-08 (later still) — Entity colour: a stored hex cannot know its theme

A project's colour was written to the row as `#9A1B6F` and painted straight into
a `style` prop. On a dark rail the deep ones measured **1.66–2.53:1** — an
invisible dot, and a checked `LayerToggle` whose box disappeared.

**The five had never been solved as a set.** Luminance ran 0.088 → 0.308, a
**3.5× spread**, because each was picked in isolation — so the deep ones failed
on dark AND the lightest (`#C88A3B`) measured 2.94:1 on a white card, failing in
light too.

`lib/entity-color.ts` is the one place this is decided now; values and their
measurements live per theme in `app/theme-shadcn.css`. Every fill clears 3:1 on
every surface of its own theme. Sage and amber were already right in dark and
are unchanged — a value that works is not improved by being different.

**The glyph on a coloured fill is not white.** `LayerToggle` hardcoded
`text-white`, which is right for three of five fills in light and for **none of
five in dark**, where every fill is a light hue (white on dark-mode yellow:
1.88:1). And it flips within a theme too — in light, white wins on plum (7.61)
while near-black wins on amber (5.16 vs 2.94). So it is a token per colour, and
one per theme for the nine-hue event palette, which had `-dot`/`-bg`/`-text` and
no `-on` at all.

**Not folded into `--pal-*`**, though that palette was already theme-aware:
those nine are saturated hues for events and tags where variety is the point;
these five are the muted set a project picks from. Merging would make every
project chip louder — a visual decision, not one to make while fixing contrast.

**`scopeFill` is total.** A fixture's `#3B6E8F` — never offered by any picker —
fell through to the literal at 2.96:1 *after* the first pass "fixed" this, so an
unknown hex takes a nearest match. Match on **hue angle**, not Euclidean
distance in OKLab a/b: distance conflates hue with chroma, so a pale sky blue
came out nearer muted olive `sage` than `blue`.

**No migration.** Legacy hexes read back by name; anything else takes the
nearest. Also: `SCOPE_COLORS` was declared twice as identical arrays (one home
now, and the picker returns a NAME), and light `--yellow-dot` went `#CA8A04` →
`#A97404` (it was 2.94:1, the one palette dot failing its own ground).

## Verified

**Every harness page, both themes: zero failures.** The one exception remains the
checked switch's accent fill, which is proven infeasible (see the previous
entry).

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,507 tests** (90 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline.

Two guards had to be **inverted**, not repaired — both asserted the old shape
and would have blocked the fix: one matched the literal source line
`const hue = color || paletteFor(id)`, the other *required* every persisted
colour to match `/^#[0-9A-F]{6}$/`. Third time this session: assert the
property, not the spelling.

# 2026-09-08 (later still) — A panel has one inset

`PanelBody` said, in its own comment, **"consumers own the content padding"**.
Measured on Home: headers at 16px above rows at 12 and 14 — a header and its own
rows misaligned by 2 and 4px **inside the same card**, across nine panels. That
is the "looks slightly wrong and you can't say why" defect.

Same shape as `rowSurface`, which exists to be THE shared row recipe and takes
`padding` as a free string: its two callers passed `px-3.5 py-2.5` and
`px-2.5 py-3.5` — the numbers transposed. **A shared component that delegates
the decision it exists to make is not a shared component.**

`--panel-px: 16px` now, consumed by `PanelHeader` and by every row via
`PANEL_PX`. The container still doesn't pad itself — a row needs full-bleed
hover — it just states the number. Vertical padding stays per-row: a Home
TaskRow is 36px, the Tasks page's row 56px because it carries a meta line, and
that is a real difference. Nine panels now align header-to-row.

## The rule was wrong, not the code

The audit flagged "paddings 10/14/27 off the 4/8/12/16 scale". Counting control
padding across four pages: **0:84 · 4:5 · 6:2 · 8:5 · 10:16 · 12:12 · 14:5 ·
16:1**. **10px is the most common control padding in the app** — the Button's
inline padding, doing real work under a rule that forbade it. At a 28px control
the layout scale offers only 8 (cramped) or 12 (loose), which is why every real
design system has half-steps for controls.

So `DESIGN_CONSTITUTION.md` now states two scales — layout (4/8/12/16/…) and
control-inline (4/6/8/10/12) — with the measurement as the reason. Conforming
first would have made sixteen controls worse.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,510 tests** (90 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles, zero `dev-preview` routes.

Three new guards in `app/design-system.test.ts`, each verified by breaking what
it guards: the header consumes the token, `--panel-px` is declared exactly once,
and no row under `components/today` hardcodes its leading inset.

# 2026-09-08 — Content: Repurposing

One recording becomes five things. That is where most of the leverage in a
creator's job is, and it is the reason a content *database* beats a content
list: the second piece costs a fraction of the first, but only if the material
stays attached to it.

**`derivedFrom` is a fact on the pipeline, not a `mentions` edge.** A mention is
untyped — it can say two pages are related but not that one is the SOURCE and
the other the cut, so "what came out of this video" and "what happens to mention
it" become the same query. One home, and still **no migration**: it rides in the
same content JSON as `stage`.

**It removes the bookkeeping, never the writing.** Format, project, client, the
link back, and the fact the cut exists at all. A button that spawns five blank
rows has moved the typing; one that invents a hook for a video it has never
watched is what makes a product feel generated.

**Only the four long forms are sources.** A short IS the atom — "repurpose this
short into a video" is a different, larger thing made from scratch, and offering
it would put a control on every card that mostly means nothing. A `reference`
and an untriaged capture are refused too: someone else's work, and something not
yet committed to.

**No channel on a derivative.** The project close-out's presets are *named* for
their channel ("LinkedIn post"), so it is the point; these are named for their
format, and a short might go to Reels, Shorts or TikTok. Guessing would put a
wrong fact on the card that reads like a right one.

The server re-reads the source rather than trusting the request — `repurpose()`
can only refuse a cut that was never offered if it is given the real format.
Creation is deliberately *not* optimistic: a stage move changes something
already on screen, so the card sliding is the feedback; this creates rows, and
the wait is a `loading` button with the result appearing where you already are.

Reused `ToggleGroup type="multiple"` rather than re-rolling the close-out's
hand-built `aria-pressed` chips — and found its `outline` variant sitting on the
divider tier at 1.22:1, now the field tier, which propagates to every toggle.

## Verified in the browser

Header **9 → 11 in progress**; the source shows "2 cuts" with both listed and
their stage; each cut shows "Cut from →" back to the source; both appear as
ordinary cards in the Idea column — nothing downstream knows repurposing exists.
The control does not appear on a short or a carousel. Zero contrast failures in
both themes.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,520 tests** (90 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles.

## Next, in order

1. **Deploy is still blocked on the user** — `npm run deploy:dry` for the size,
   then `npx wrangler login && npm run deploy`. Rotate the pasted token.
2. **Content: Series and Library** — a series is a recurring format, a library is
   the published archive. Both are views over the same rows, not new objects.
3. **Campaigns** — needs a decision first: a campaign that groups content toward
   a launch may already BE a project (a piece already carries `project_id`).
   Adding a `campaigns` table would be the "third object" mistake.
4. Revisit the shadcn shims (push `Card`/`DropdownMenu` compat INTO the
   components, per the registry's Open Code principle).

# 2026-09-09 — MCP, sub-projects, and the content Library

Three asks. Two of them turned out to be one-line answers hiding behind a name.

## 1. Sub-projects were already built — under a word nobody would search for

*"in project sub project sub projects — we are doing branding work but there
motion work involve webdesign work."*

Zenboard has had exactly that since 0014: `sections` + 0040's status / due date
/ client-visible columns, with progress roll-up in `lib/workstreams.ts` and its
own task composer per stream. Verified live on *Balluji rebrand*: **Discovery**
(1) and **Design** (2 · 1 shared).

Two reasons a finished feature read as missing:

1. **The UI called it a "section"** — document vocabulary, a heading inside a
   page. The code already knew better (`lib/workstreams.ts`; the schema comment
   says the table "already WAS the Project → X → Task level"). Renamed
   everywhere a person can read it. The TABLE stays `sections`: renaming a
   shipped table is a migration, and nobody sees it.
2. **The control did not exist when you need it.** It was a ghost button under
   the task list, and `if (tasks.length === 0 && sections.length === 0) return
   <Empty/>` returned before it — so **on day one of a branding job, the one
   screen where you decide "Identity / Motion / Web" had no way to say it.** The
   empty state offers it now, with the user's own example as the placeholder.

A broad "never say the word section" guard would have been a **bad** guard:
measured, 7 hits and 6 are correct English ("Client sections" labels a tab
strip; "Add missing sections" is about a brief's headings). So the guard checks
only the two surfaces that NAME this level, and additionally asserts the empty
project still offers it. Measured in passing: **Money → Finance is at 0
violations** — that rename fully landed.

## 2. MCP — Zenboard as a tool your AI can reach

`POST /api/mcp`, four tools: **capture · today · search · list_projects**.
Connect it and you can tell Claude "film the studio tour Tuesday" and it lands
in Zenboard without opening Zenboard.

**The protocol is hand-written.** The SDK would spend the worker's 3 MiB
ceiling — the one that already forced the dev-preview harnesses out of the build
— to buy four method names. The trap it hides: **a notification must get no
response body.** `notifications/initialized` arrives right after the handshake
and has no id; answering it is a protocol error some clients treat as fatal, so
it breaks the connection at step two rather than at the first tool.

**Auth reuses the calendar feed exactly** — token in `profiles.preferences`
jsonb, found with `.contains()`, no migration. Two deliberate differences: it is
**never minted lazily** (the feed is read-only; this reads and *writes* a
workspace, so it exists only because someone pressed Connect), and it answers
**401 not 404** (the caller already holds a token and is configuring a program).

**The client decides task-or-idea**, not us. That distinction needs the
conversation, and the conversation is where the model already is; a parser here
would be a second, worse guess. Default is `task` — when unsure, fail toward the
thing you will see again. A capture writes no project, no date, no priority: a
guessed due date is worse than none.

## 3. Content — the Library, and a terminal column that grew forever

The `published` column is the only one nothing leaves, so it was the only one
that grew without bound — and it sorted **oldest first**, a queue's order
applied to an archive, burying this week's work at the bottom. It now shows a
recent tail with "N more in Library", and `Board` gained a per-column `footer`
so a column that hides cards can say so.

The Library itself is months, newest first, each row carrying what it has been
cut into — because repurposing starts months later, from the archive, not from
the board.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,551 tests** (93 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles, `/api/mcp` present, zero `dev-preview` routes.

**Owed:** the MCP happy path needs a signed-in session to mint a token, so it is
proven by construction, not by running. First real check once connected:
`claude mcp add --transport http zenboard <url>/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>"`

## Content, continued — inspiration had nowhere to live

*"the content part feels very raw — rethink how creators manage inspirations."*

The concrete defect, and it is a hole in the floor: **`references()` shipped
exported and tested, and nothing rendered it.** The only place the word
`reference` appeared in the workspace was the triage button that files something
into the bucket. You saved a competitor's reel, pressed "Keep as reference", and
never saw it again. An inbox that loses things teaches you not to use it.

It is a second shelf on the same screen now — "Saved", under the pile still to
sort — so triage visibly moves a thing from one shelf to the other.

**A spark is the same edge as a cut, read the other way.** `derivedFrom` already
said "this came out of that", and a reference is a piece, so an idea sparked by
a saved reel needed no second relationship. What changes is the word: a cut is a
shorter version of your own work; a spark is a new thing someone else's work
made you think of. Calling a spark a cut would claim your idea is a derivative
of a competitor's reel.

Three rules make the shelf worth keeping: the reference is **never consumed**
(one reel can spark three ideas over a year); the new idea is **untitled and
opens immediately** (inheriting "How Nike edits" would name your idea after
someone else's video, and an untitled row you cannot see is not a feature); and
the count is **null until it has produced something**, because "0 ideas" on a
shelf of saved links is a reproach for having saved them.

Verified live: **10 → 11 in progress**, the panel opens reading "Sparked by →
How Nike cuts a 15-second spot", and the reference is still on the shelf showing
"1 idea from this". Both themes.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,557 tests** (93 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles, zero `dev-preview` routes.

## Next, in order

1. **Deploy, and the MCP happy path** — both need the user. `npm run deploy:dry`
   for the size, then `npx wrangler login && npm run deploy`; then Connect in
   Settings → Connections and run the `claude mcp add` line.
2. **The stage vocabulary assumes video.** idea→script→shoot→edit→review→
   scheduled→published has three columns a carousel or a LinkedIn post can never
   enter, so half the board is dead for half the formats — the largest remaining
   source of "raw". The fix is a universal five (Idea → Making → Review →
   Scheduled → Published) with the making detail on the card, not per-format
   columns: a board's columns have to be universal or cards cannot move between
   them.
3. **Content: Series and Campaigns.** Campaigns needs a decision first — a
   campaign that groups content toward a launch may already BE a project.
4. Entity colours in dark for stored hexes; revisit the shadcn shims.

## Content — the pipeline was written for video

The last big source of "raw", and it was measurable. Rendered with a board of
posts and carousels, the fixed seven stages produced **three consecutive dead
columns** — Draft, Shoot, Edit — each with "Nothing here yet" *and* a "+ New
idea" button inviting you to start work in a stage your format can never enter,
while the six real pieces sat off screen.

**A format now declares what it skips**, rather than each listing a full path —
an eighth stage later means one line, not seven. A text post has no production
step (skips shoot and edit); a carousel is designed, so it keeps edit but never
films; written formats skip only the shoot. A piece with **no** format walks
everything: not knowing is not the same as knowing it skips something.

**The board derives its columns from the work present.** A stage shows if any
format present can reach it — so the set changes when you take on a new *kind*
of work, which is rare and means something, not every time a card moves. And the
safety net: **a stage also shows if a piece is in it**, whatever its format.
Without that, changing a video's format to `post` while it sat in Shoot would
take the card off the board with no way back. A column may be irrelevant; a
hidden card is lost work.

**`script` is labelled "Draft" now.** The same column holds a video's script, a
newsletter's first pass and the copy for a LinkedIn post. The *key* stays
`script` — it is a persisted JSON enum, and renaming a stored value to fix a
label is how in-flight work gets lost.

Measured after, same fixture: **Idea 2 · Draft 1 · Edit 1 · Review 1 ·
Scheduled 1 · Published 1** — every column populated, four visible at once.
Adding one video brought `Shoot 0` back, live.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,568 tests** (92 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles. Both new guards verified by breaking what they guard.

## Review pass — what a creator actually meets

Swept all four content views in both themes with a text-contrast instrument:
**zero failures**. The single hit was the inbox's "Save" button at 1.74:1, which
is genuinely `disabled` with `opacity: 1` — WCAG exempts inactive controls, and
it uses the house `disabled:text-ink-300` tokens rather than an opacity fade.
Not a defect; the ruler over-reported, as it did twice before.

The real find was structural: **every board column offered "+ New idea"** —
including `published`, where creating "an idea" that is already out is a
sentence that does not parse. Creation in a pipeline is concentrated at the
front: you make an idea, then you move it. Six of the seven were mislabelled
clutter for an act nobody performs.

`BoardColumnData.canAdd` now gates it, **defaulting to true** so the task board
— where adding straight into "In progress" is an everyday act — is untouched.
Verified live: the content board shows one composer, the task board still shows
five.

Also confirmed done and struck from this list: **entity colours in dark**. An
arbitrary stored hex now resolves through a theme-aware token (`#3B6E8F` on the
week board reads `var(--scope-blue)`), so that item was stale.

## A content piece is not a doc

The project loader fetches every `pages` row carrying a `project_id` — and a
content piece carries one **on purpose**, because the close-out creates them
that way so a case study knows which job it came from.

`ProjectDocs` rendered all of them. The moment a `type: 'content'` fixture
existed, the harness showed it: **"4 docs" for three docs and a case study**,
the piece sitting in the list, and clicking it would have handed a content piece
to the *document* editor — where it has no stage, no dates, no brief and no
client sign-off. The fixture had no content row, which is why it went unseen:
the same blind spot as the missing `reference` fixture in Content.

Split at the point of use, not in the loader — the project **should** show what
it produced, just not as writing. Filtering upstream would have fixed the count
by hiding the work.

**And the rule already existed.** `lib/page-kinds.ts` states which module owns a
`pages` row, and its own note says *"the next module that stores a page adds one
line here rather than rediscovering this in three query files."* Documents
already uses it. This was the fourth place to need it — and my first pass
re-hand-rolled it as `type !== 'content'`, which works today and goes stale the
moment a fifth type appears, which is exactly how this list came to render
content in the first place. It uses `isDocumentPage` now, and the guard asserts
the shared rule rather than the literal comparison.

A sweep of every `pages` query confirmed no other list has the defect: the
Documents hub already applies `isDocumentPage`, and the remaining unfiltered
queries are single-row lookups by id, where a type filter means nothing. The pieces now sit in their own "Content from this project"
section, and each is a **link into Content** rather than a doc to open, because
that is where a piece is actually worked on.

The section renders nothing when a project has made no content, which is most
of them.

Verified: **3 docs** where it said 4, the case study in its own section, and the
task board's per-column composers untouched by the `canAdd` default.

`tsc` clean · **1,573 tests** (93 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles. Every new guard verified by breaking what it guards.

# 2026-09-09 (later) — Three things the user found in a screenshot

## 1. The colour picker was broken, and it was my regression

Yesterday `SCOPE_COLORS` changed from raw hexes to NAMES so a project's colour
could be theme-aware. Three pickers paint it with `style={{ background: c }}`.

**Three of the five names are also valid CSS colours.** So the picker rendered
CSS `plum` (pale pink) instead of #9A1B6F, CSS `blue` instead of #2B5CB0, CSS
`indigo` instead of #5C4FB8 — and `sage` and `amber` are not CSS colours at all,
so two swatches were simply **invisible**. It never threw. It looked
half-working. That is the worst shape a regression can take, and only a
screenshot caught it.

All three now paint `scopeFill(c)`. A guard asserts that any file rendering
`SCOPE_COLORS` also resolves it, and that no `background: c` survives.

## 2. Every task row announced an absence

Measured on the row: `Stakeholder interviews · Medium · [Internal] · 🕐 — · ☆`.
Two of those five were noise on **every row of every list**:

- **`🕐 —`** — an empty estimate, rendered as a clock and an em-dash. Not even an
  affordance: a `<span>`, so it could never set the estimate it kept reminding
  you was missing. It renders nothing now, the same rule as every count and
  summary in the app — a dash meaning "none" is a reproach, not information.
- **`☆`** — an empty star on every row, which CLAUDE.md already forbids: *"star
  and flag glyphs render only when meaningful; reveal on row hover otherwise."*
  A **filled** star is a fact and stays; an empty one is an invitation, and it
  is `reveal-on-hover` — the house utility, not a hand-rolled opacity pair,
  because a coarse pointer has no hover and an `opacity-0` control is
  unreachable on a phone.

## 3. One fact, two homes

The highlighted row carried a "Highlight" chip **and** a filled star. The badge
is for surfaces with no toggle; where the star exists it already says this.

Labels went from `"Toggle highlight"` — which names the mechanism — to
`"Highlight this task"` / `"Remove highlight"`, which name what pressing it does,
and the two states do opposite things.

Verified across every surface `TaskRow` serves: **Tasks 0 placeholders with real
estimates still rendering, Home and Portal 0 placeholders** (their remaining
em-dashes are prose — page titles and doc names).

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,580 tests** (94 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles. Every guard verified by breaking what it guards.

## The hover band, and the process problem behind it

The user sent a hovered row. Measured: the wash declared `my-0.5` — 2px above
and below — and rendered **0 above, 3 below**. A top margin on the first child
of a box with no padding or top border **collapses through its parent**, so the
fill sat flush against the hairline above and short of the one below. An
off-centre band on every row of every list.

It was also `rounded-md` at **full width**. It has to be full width — its
padding is what aligns a row's text with the panel header (`--panel-px`) — so
the radius had nothing to be inset from and produced four corner notches showing
the card behind them. Rounding had been added to stop the fill colliding with
the hairline; the vertical inset is what actually does that.

Fixed by moving the inset to the outer as `py-0.5`, where a margin cannot
collapse, and dropping the radius. Measured after, on all three surfaces
`rowSurface` serves: **2px top, 2px bottom, radius 0** — the last row in a list
shows exactly 2/2, confirming the third pixel elsewhere is the divider.

The settling was checked at the same time and is **correct**: sampled inside one
call at 80ms / 500 / 1500 / 2600 / 3200, the row holds at full height with its
content for 3s, then leaves and Completed increments. Home, Tasks and the
project tab all behave identically.

## THE ACTUAL PROBLEM: fixtures that only show the happy case

Six defects were fixed today and the user found most of them in screenshots.
That is the wrong discovery process, and two of them share one root cause:

- `references()` was exported, tested, and **rendered by nothing** — the content
  fixture had no `bucket: 'reference'` row.
- `ProjectDocs` rendered content pieces as documents — the projects fixture had
  no `type: 'content'` row.

The harness exists so a screen can be verified without a session. **A screen can
only be verified against data that exercises it.** So
`app/dev-preview/fixture-coverage.test.ts` now asserts that every value of a
union which changes what a screen renders appears in at least one fixture.

It failed on its first run: **no fixture anywhere carried `type: 'template'`**,
so the Documents Templates view had never been seen with data. Added one; the
view turned out to be correct — which is itself worth having, because it was
previously unknown rather than fine.
