`tsc` clean · **1,592 tests** (96 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
production build compiles, zero `dev-preview` routes.

# 2026-09-10 — Deploy: the worker was 113 KiB over the ceiling

First real deploy attempt, and it would have been **refused**. Measured:
**3,185 KiB gzipped against Cloudflare's 3,072 KiB free-plan limit.**

One import shape was the entire overage. `BlockEditor` is ProseMirror, and it
was **statically imported at three call sites**, so the whole editor compiled
into the server bundle. Loading it with `next/dynamic` + `ssr: false` took the
worker to **2,788 KiB — 284 KiB under**. A 398 KiB saving from three lines.

It is not a size hack: a ProseMirror view needs a real DOM to build itself, so
it can never produce meaningful server HTML — every one of those bytes was work
thrown away on first paint — and the editor only appears in a panel that opens
on interaction. `database-view.tsx` already loaded it this way; the other three
had drifted.

Verified the editor still works: a real pointer click yields
`DIV.ProseMirror ProseMirror-focused` with the right text. A *synthetic* click
does not, because the editor keeps a single active-block PM — `contenteditable`
exists only on the focused block. Measurement artifact, not a break.

`lib/worker-budget.test.ts` guards the import shape, including the case that
looks fixed and is not: `dynamic()` **without** `ssr: false` still
server-renders and saves nothing.

## Gate

`tsc` clean · **1,595 tests** (97 files) · lint at its 17-error baseline ·
OpenNext build succeeds · **worker 2,788 KiB, 284 KiB of headroom**.

## The deploy itself needs the user

`wrangler whoami` reports not authenticated, and credentials are not something
this session should handle. `npx wrangler login`, then `npm run deploy` — which
runs the gate, builds, and deploys with `--keep-vars` (mandatory:
`wrangler.jsonc` declares zero `vars`, so without it the deploy deletes every
dashboard-set secret).

## Deployed — 2026-09-10

**`https://zenboard-web.designdotrushil.workers.dev`** · version
`16a2feac-eddd-45d1-be4b-c485ff736d43` · worker **2,812 KiB gzipped** ·
startup **22 ms**.

The two failed attempts before it were a wrong directory, not a broken build:
`npm run deploy` must run from `zenboard-web/`, not the repo root.

Live smoke results: `/` → `/today` → **`/login`** (the decisive one — that path
calls `requireUser()`, so a clean redirect proves the worker reached Supabase);
`/login` 200; `GET /api/mcp` 200 and `POST /api/mcp` **401** exactly as designed;
**`/dev-preview/ds` 404**, so the `page.dev.tsx` gating holds in production.

**One correction to our own runbook.** It claimed `/f/does-not-exist` should
return 404. It returns 200, and that is right: the route renders one calm page
for every unavailable reason — unknown, unpublished, closed, expired, at its cap
— specifically so a stranger cannot tell which, and it already sets
`robots: { index: false }`. A 404 for "unknown" beside a 200 for "closed" is a
token-enumeration oracle. The note was wrong, not the code.

## Projects structure review + Phase 1, "the quiet list" — 2026-09-10

The user asked for a three-hat review of the project / workstream model
(advanced PM · product designer · design engineer), researched against Linear,
Notion, Height, Asana, ClickUp, Monday, Basecamp, Things and Todoist. Full
brief, nine ranked findings and the four-phase plan:
`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5fd1a86b-5c2b-438e-92cc-7c87fb7ed77e`

**The finding that reframed the brief.** Workstreams are not badly designed —
they are unused, and the UI charges every project screen for them anyway.
Queried against the live workspace: `tasks.section_id` is **null on 88 of 88**,
there is **one** `sections` row, and `tasks.status` is null on 78 of 88. A
stream costs two clicks to create and a drawer round-trip to fill (there is no
drag, no row menu, no bulk move), so the container ships and the work never
arrives. `lib/workstreams.ts` — "THE one projection" — turns out to have a
single caller, `lib/portal.ts`; the owner's own Tasks tab re-implements
grouping inline, so every rollup rule in that file runs only for the client.

### Phase 1 shipped — pure subtraction, no migration, no model change

Six rules, each one already stated somewhere in the codebase and simply not
enforced where it mattered:

1. **Priority renders only when set.** `low` is the DB default (78/88), and the
   shared `TaskRow` was the one call site of six with no guard — so the chip
   was wallpaper on Home, the project tab and the portal at once.
2. **A row declares its height** (`heightClass: 'h-[var(--row-task)]'`). It read
   `py-2.5` and its comment claimed 36px; it measured **48**, because a 28px
   star and a 24px share pill had joined the trailing cluster — and on an
   internal task that pill sits at `opacity: 0`. An invisible control was
   sizing the densest list in the product.
3. **`--row-group: 32px`** for list furniture (workstream heading, stream
   composer, Completed disclosure). Deliberately a separate name from
   `--row-nav` despite the shared value — see the comment in `globals.css`.
4. **The group heading is heavier and shorter than its rows** (14/500 against
   12/400 above 14px rows). The container had been rendering *smaller* than its
   contents, which is most of why the list did not parse.
5. **The header states facts, not absences.** "Started" gone; "Client" only when
   linked; properties inline via a new `layout` option on the shared
   `RecordHeader` (Clients keeps `stack` — its values are long, and the choice
   follows the shape of the values, not the screen).
6. **Two always-visible add controls, not four.** The per-stream `+` moved into
   the workstream heading. Hiding the old ghost row in place was tried first and
   rejected: a hidden row still occupies the flow, so it traded clutter for a
   32px hole between groups.

### Measured, 1440×950 on `/dev-preview/projects`

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| top of the first task row | 604px | **345px** |
| distinct row heights in one card | 4 (29/36/41/53) | **2 (32/36)** |
| task row | 48px | **36px** |
| property block | 285px | **49px** |
| card, 3 tasks + 2 streams | 338px | **207px** |
| always-visible add controls | 4 | **2** |
| task rows on the first screen | ~5 | **16** |

**One miss, stated:** 345px against a ≤300 target I set myself. The remaining
45px would cost either the composer or predictable wrapping; on a real project
(three properties, not the fixture's six) it measures nearer 315.

`tsc` clean · **1609 tests / 98 files** green, including 14 new guards in
`components/tasks/quiet-list.test.ts`. Every guard was checked with a must-fail
control — the rule reverted, the test confirmed to fail — and one of those
controls caught a bug in the guard itself (the sweep's regex never matched
`level={task.priority}`, so it would have passed an ungated row forever).

**Awaiting the user:** whether Milestones merge into Workstreams, and whether
the Board keeps its status columns. Both delete something visible.

## Phase 2, "workstreams earn their place" — 2026-09-10

The user handed back both open decisions, so they are made: **Milestones merge
into Workstreams** and **the Board keeps its columns but groups by workstream**,
both still scheduled for Phase 3. Phase 2 does not depend on either.

### What shipped

1. **Every task row can file itself.** A `⋯` on hover lists the project's
   workstreams plus *No workstream*, ticked at the current one. A FLAT list, not
   a "Move to →" submenu: one verb does not need a second surface to aim at. The
   control is absent entirely when there is nowhere to move to — a menu whose
   every item is a no-op reads as broken, not as empty.
2. **Workstreams reorder.** `sections.sort_order` has existed since 0014 and
   nothing could ever change it, so streams were stuck in the order they were
   typed — on a phased job, the one order you never want. New `setSectionOrder`
   renumbers from 0 rather than swapping, because rows created before this
   feature can share a `sort_order` and a swap between two 0s is a no-op that
   looks like a broken control.
3. **The owner's screen reads the same projection the client does.**
   `lib/workstreams.ts` had exactly one caller (`lib/portal.ts`). The Tasks tab
   now groups through it, its inline second derivation is deleted, and each
   heading carries real progress — computed from `tasks`, never from `active`,
   because `active` has already had the finished work split out and a count
   taken there reports every stream as 0 done.
   Order changed with it: named streams lead, unfiled comes LAST and is finally
   named ("No workstream") whenever there is anything to tell it apart from.
4. **A subtask belongs to its parent's project.** `addSubtask` copied only
   `space_id`, so 12 subtasks belonged to no project, could not be filtered to
   one, and could never be shown to a client — the Asana anti-pattern named in
   the research. It now inherits `project_id`, `section_id` and
   `client_visible`, behind the house retry gate so an unmigrated account still
   works. **Paired with scoping every project read to top-level tasks**
   (`!t.parent_task_id`), or one task split into ten would outvote nine whole
   ones in the list, on the board and in the progress bar.

### Verified

Browser, end to end: opening the row menu on a filed task and choosing *No
workstream* moved it out, created the unfiled group with its own heading in last
position, left the emptied stream visible so the next task has somewhere to go,
and kept the row at **36px** — the new control did not grow it, which is Phase
1's declared height paying for itself immediately.

`tsc` clean · **1624 tests / 99 files**, with 15 new guards in
`components/projects/workstream-fill.test.ts`, each checked with a must-fail
control.

### Two process notes worth keeping

- **An instrument lied before the code did, for the third time on this project.**
  The first probe reported "Move up" disabled on *both* workstreams — a real bug
  if true. It was reading a Radix menu still unmounting from the previous open.
  Re-check from a clean slate before believing a UI measurement.
- **Two Phase 1 guards had to be rewritten.** They pinned `{g.section.name}` — a
  local variable. Phase 2 renamed it while keeping the rule exactly, and the
  tests failed anyway. A guard anchored to a spelling punishes refactoring; they
  now match on the rule.

## Clutter correction + Phase 3 (A and B) — 2026-09-10

### The correction, from user feedback

Phase 1 laid the project's seven properties out on one line: **285px → 49px**,
every acceptance number met. The user's reaction was still "cluttered", and
they were right. **Height was never the complaint.** Seven facts drawn as
glyph + label + value is twenty-one things above a tab strip whether they are
stacked or inline. Compressing clutter makes it denser, not calmer.

So the fix was to remove facts, not to compress them. Everything cut failed one
of two tests — it stated the **default**, or it stated an **absence**:

| cut | why |
|---|---|
| Status "Active" | the default. Shown now only when paused/completed/archived |
| Progress bar | one fact drawn twice beside the figure; the figure is precise and a fifth the width |
| Deadline's trailing task name | that name is in the list directly below it |
| Client "Linked" | asserts a relationship exists without naming it |
| Sharing "Portal on" | a setting, not a fact you steer by; the Portal tab is right there |

`RecordHeaderLayout` `'inline'` became `'facts'`: no label column, no icons,
self-describing values ("2/5 done", "Due 12 Sep"), `label` kept as the
accessible name. **Property block 285px → 49px → 20px.** Clients was cut to the
same absence rule (Contact/Email no longer render an em-dash) but KEEPS the
label column — its values are long, and the two layouts are a pair chosen by
the shape of the values, not by the screen.

The composer moved from a bordered `composer-shell` above the card into the
card as its **first row**, so the heaviest element on the tab is no longer the
one holding no work. It stays a slot rather than moving into `TaskList`,
because the page header's "New task" focuses it and that ref belongs to the
page (verified: still focuses).

**Measured, 1440×950: first task row 604 → 289px. Rows on the first screen
5 → 17.** Title, tabs, one card. Nothing floating between.

### 3A — the workstream is a dated, schedulable thing

0040 added `status` and `due_date` to `sections` a year ago and **neither was
ever rendered or settable**. Both are now: a deadline on the heading (overdue
is the only colour), Pause/Resume in the ⋯ menu, and a "Paused" badge that
appears only when someone SET it — `statusOf` derives active and completed
from progress, and both are already legible in the n/m beside the name.

A workstream deadline now feeds the project header. Adding that third source is
what made the rule worth extracting: `lib/project-deadline.ts` replaces eight
inline lines whose comparator **never returned 0**, so two dates on the same day
resolved in whatever order the database returned them. Precedence is now stated
— project, then workstream, then task — and tested.

### 3B — milestones become workstreams

**Migration 0041 is written and needs applying by hand.** It STAMPS rather than
deletes (`milestones.migrated_at`): nothing is destroyed, rollback is one
UPDATE, and the stamp is also the application's gate. Goal milestones — that
table predates projects and belongs to Goals (0001) — are untouched, and a test
asserts every write scopes itself to project rows.

The transition is correct on both sides without a flag: the loader asks for
`migrated_at` optimistically and drops it on an unmigrated database, the old
checkpoint list renders only while un-stamped rows remain, and the Overview's
new read-only **Workstreams** section (name · progress · date) shows either way.
The calendar reads both sources for the duration, so dated phases do not vanish
from it when checkpoints leave.

`tsc` clean · **1654 tests / 102 files**. Every guard checked with a must-fail
control; one of them caught the guard reading the migration's rollback COMMENT
as a statement.

## MCP correctness pass — the tools said things that were not true — 2026-09-10

A review of the MCP server shipped yesterday found that it broke its one
promise ("I just say my raw thought and it holds all things") three ways, and
that none of its 22 tests could have noticed, because the tools were written
inside a route handler that builds its own database client.

### What was wrong

1. **A captured task landed in no pile.** The row was hand-built with no
   project and `is_inbox` left at its default of `false`. `lib/task-intake.ts`
   already states the rule — *a project or the Inbox, never neither* — because
   a task in no pile exists and appears nowhere. The tool replied "added to
   your inbox"; the task was not in the Inbox, or anywhere else in the app.
2. **`today` asked the Board's question.** It filtered `.neq('status','done')`.
   `status` is null on 78 of 88 tasks, and `NULL <> 'done'` is NULL rather
   than true, so most open work silently fell out of "what am I doing today".
   Open is `done = false` — what the list writes.
3. **`today` read the worker's clock.** `todayISO()` with no zone is UTC on
   Cloudflare, so an IST evening past midnight got yesterday's list.

Plus: archived pages came back from `search` and `today`, and `search` marked
a task done from `status`.

### The fix is one projection, not three patches

The morning digest already answered this exact question — one person's day,
read from the server with no session, in their zone — and answered it
correctly. So `buildDigest` moved out of its cron route into
**`lib/digest-data.ts`**, and both surfaces render what it returns through
**`digestBlocks`**. `today` inherited the digest's capacity line, waiting-on
and client requests for free. Along the way, each a real defect:

- **`readTimeZone(preferences)`** (`lib/date.ts`) is now the one reader of the
  stored zone. There were three: one fell back to `undefined` — the runtime's
  zone, UTC in production but IST on a laptop — and one never read it at all.
  It also validates: a damaged zone used to throw inside every server render.
- **`dayWindow` moved to `lib/date.ts` and got its first tests.** Its end was
  `start + 24h`, wrong on both DST days; the digest's own event window used
  zoneless `T00:00:00` strings, which the database reads as UTC, so an IST day
  began at 05:30. The start is now solved in two passes and checked against
  the day, because Santiago springs forward *at* midnight.
- **`lib/todays-plan.ts`** — Home's rule (scheduled today, or an undated ★)
  in its query and JS shapes. The digest had silently dropped the ★.
- **Content and meetings joined the day.** A shoot day now makes the digest
  worth sending, in Home's words ("Filming at 09:00"). Meetings are in the
  loader but switched *off* for the email — it informs the plan and the
  calendar is the schedule — and on for MCP, where the model has no calendar
  open.
- **`splitThought`**: the first line becomes the title (clipped at a word),
  and if anything was left out the whole thought is kept in the notes. v1 cut
  at 200 characters and discarded the rest.
- **`inboxCapture`** is now the one builder for an untriaged idea, used by the
  app's capture and by MCP; the tool had copied the shape inline.
- Tool results carry `recordHref` links, so the model can hand you a URL.

### How it is tested now

`test/fake-db.ts` records every query-builder call and deliberately never
evaluates a filter — a fake PostgREST would be a second database to be wrong
about, and every one of these bugs lived in *which filter was asked for*. The
security property (every query scoped to the token's owner — the service role
has no RLS) is now asserted twice: behaviourally over every query every tool
makes, and statically over the source, cut at each `.from(` instead of the old
400-character window that let one query borrow the next one's filter.

**A must-fail control was run for every fix** — the fix reverted, the test
confirmed red. Two controls were initially missed and both were test gaps, now
closed: the fall-back-across-midnight case had no direct test, and a "blank is
not a note" assertion read a value that is normalised on the way back in.

`tsc` clean · **1,704 tests / 104 files** under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` *and*
`America/Los_Angeles` · eslint clean on every touched file · `next build`
clean.

**Owed, with the reason:** the tools have still never run against a live
account, because that needs an MCP token only the account owner can mint. The
query shapes are the ones Home and the digest already run in production.

**Noticed, not in scope:** the Tasks rail counts "Today" as
`scheduled_date === today` and so leaves out an undated ★ that Home shows.
Whether a star belongs to today in the planning view is a product question;
`lib/todays-plan.ts` makes the answer a one-line change either way.

**Deployed** as version `94d42fd8-0b6e-41dc-af3b-e8e785a85a7c` — worker
**2,825 KiB gzipped**, startup 29 ms — carrying this fix and Projects Phases
1–3, which had not been live. Smoke: `/` → `/today` → `/login`, `/login` 200,
`/dev-preview/ds` 404, `GET /api/mcp` lists the four tools, `POST` with no token
and with a well-formed unknown token both 401. Migration 0041 is still unapplied
and the code is gated for it.

## Project identity + nav rhythm — 2026-09-11

### The project mark ("this pink dot looks amateur")

A project identified itself with a 10px filled square. Five projects in a rail
were five near-identical muted squares, so the colour carried almost no
information — and the rail painted `project.color` as a **RAW HEX**, which is
the theme-blindness `lib/entity-color.ts` exists to end: a stored `#9A1B6F`
measures **1.86:1** on the dark rail. The mark that looked amateur was also one
you could barely see.

**`components/ui/record-icon.tsx`** — a tile, the reference being Linear:
rounded square, the record's colour at 14% as the ground, a glyph on top.
Three sizes (20/24/32). The ground is `color-mix(… 14%, transparent)` off the
per-theme `--scope-*` token rather than a pale hex per hue, so it keeps the
theme-awareness that file was written for. An **emoji** gets a neutral ground —
it brings its own colour and should read as itself, not as a sticker on a
patch. No icon → the Projects nav glyph, so an un-iconed project reads
*undecorated*, never broken.

**Migration 0042** adds `projects.icon` — one text column, the same grammar
Documents already stores (`"🎨"` / `"ph:Rocket"` / an image URL), so it reuses
the existing renderer and picker instead of inventing a second. Read through a
fourth tier of the loader's existing cascade, so a migrated account still pays
one round trip. **Not yet applied.**

### The sets ("we have limited emoji and icons")

Measured: **~380 emoji** and **~70 icons**.

- **Emoji 380 → 1330**, same 8 categories, same compact `glyph name` format,
  so search, skin tones and recents all keep working.
- **Icons 70 → 260.** They live in the SEAM as `PICKER_ICONS`, not in the
  picker, because `components/ds/icons.ts` is the only module allowed to import
  an icon package — a picker reaching for Phosphor directly would be the second
  importer and the one-file-swap property would be gone. A catalogue rather
  than 260 named exports: nothing imports these by name, they are looked up by
  a stored string. Objects and subjects only — no chevrons or arrows; letting
  UI chrome into the picker is how an icon set stops meaning anything.
  `PAGE_ICONS = { ...PICKER_ICONS, ...LEGACY_ICONS }` — legacy WINS, so a row
  that stored `ph:Tree` years ago cannot silently become a different glyph.

The header tile is now the control that opens the picker, which is Linear's
arrangement and the right one: the thing you want to change is the thing you
click.

### Nav rhythm ("inter section navigation padding is not consistent")

Two navigation columns sit side by side — the app sidebar and the hub's record
rail. Same kind of row (32px, 20px glyph, label), and they disagreed on every
measurement around that glyph:

| | sidebar | rail |
|---|---|---|
| column inset | 8px | **14px** (`p-3.5`, the only unnamed number) |
| glyph → label | **4px** | **8px** |
| row → row | **4px** | **2px** |
| radius | **6/8 literal** | `rounded-sm` |

Compounded: a sidebar label started at **x=40**, a rail label at **x=50**.
Nobody chose the stagger; it is what two hand-written versions of one idea
drift into. Four tokens now name it (`--nav-inset` / `--nav-px` / `--nav-gap` /
`--nav-row-gap`) and both columns read them. The radius is one value in BOTH
states — a row that changes shape when you select it wobbles. The stray
`width: 34` collapsed row is gone too (the same unnamed 34 the row-height sweep
found sixteen times).

**Every use carries a fallback**, and a test pins each fallback to its token.
Turbopack serves stale CSS across restarts, and an inline style has no cascade:
an unresolved `var(--nav-gap)` computes to `gap: normal` and `padding: 0`,
which is a hard break rather than a graceful one. I hit exactly that mid-change
and the sidebar collapsed until the fallbacks went in.

`tsc` clean · **1710 tests / 105 files**. Controls verified.

**Owed:** 0042 not applied. Verification of the icon picker was done against
another session's dev server (Next 16 refuses a second one in the same
directory), and its CSS was stale — the fallbacks make correctness independent
of that, but the token values themselves have not been seen resolving live.

## Documents gallery contrast — 2026-09-11

User: "this section contrast is so off, not looks any things properly."

Measured on the real page (canvas-resolved, ruler self-tested first):

| | |
|---|---|
| gallery canvas | `#EFEFEC` |
| card | `#FFFFFF` |
| **card preview body** | **`#F1F1EF`** |
| card border | `#E9E9E7` |
| **preview vs canvas** | **1.02:1** |
| border vs canvas | 1.06:1 |

The bottom two-thirds of every card was the same colour as the page, so a card
read as a floating white strip with a hole under it. Text contrast was fine
(5.4 / 6.1) — it was never the ink, it was the surfaces.

**An earlier pass had introduced this and verified it** — preview vs CARD is
1.128, a real step, with a test asserting the structure. It never measured
preview vs CANVAS. A step checked against one neighbour is not a step.

Fix is CLAUDE.md's own rule: one fill per card, header and body separated by a
hairline — which was already there and already doing the job. The list row had
the identical fill and the identical result, and now shares the card's surface
and hairline, so a doc looks like a doc in both layouts. The hover edge rule
lost its `:not(.doc-listrow)` exclusion, which only existed because a list row
had no border to change.

After: card is one uniform surface, **1.15:1** on canvas in light and
**1.20:1** in dark. Verified in both themes.

**Two guard bugs fixed on the way**, both in the DS test that caught this:
the "no raw hex in the card" scan was reading the hexes in an explanatory
COMMENT as code; and once comments were stripped, the region marker
`// ── Grid card ──` disappeared with them, so the region was `''` and every
assertion passed against an empty string. Regions now anchor on code and
assert the anchor was found.

`tsc` clean · **1717 tests / 106 files**. Control verified.

### Documents editor — the writing surface is paper (2026-09-11)

User: "keep this as a white, this is writing space."

The doc scroller painted `--paper-2` inside a `--paper` pane — and its own
comment had read **"the redesign's white sheet"** since the redesign. Intent
and implementation had disagreed for months, and the comment is what kept it
hidden: reading the file, you saw the word "white".

The gallery and the editor are two different jobs and want two different
grounds. The gallery is a place you BROWSE — a recessed canvas is what lets the
cards read as objects on it, and that stays. The editor is a place you WRITE,
and a tinted writing space reads as a *preview* of a document rather than the
document. The doc region is now one surface with no seam, which is also why the
cover, title and columns need no fill of their own.

`--paper-2` is untouched where it belongs: image handles and the embed toolbar
sit ON the content and are affordances, not surfaces. A sweep that removed them
all would have flattened them into the page — guarded explicitly.

`tsc` clean · **1719 tests / 106 files**. Control verified cleanly (the first
attempt's perl corrupted the file, so its failure proved nothing — redone).

### Record headers — the reader arranges the properties (2026-09-11)

The other session's unfinished task: per-property label menus, a hover drag
handle, an "N hidden" restore, saved in profile preferences without SQL.

**Why this and not a better default.** The user called the seven-row project
header cluttered, and after a pass cut it to three, directed "this information
is gone — I want it back as it was." Both are true, and no list of rows
satisfies both — seven facts are noise to someone who reads a project by its
progress and reference to someone who bills by its dates. So the header stopped
choosing, which is what Notion and Linear do.

**What shipped, on Project and Client headers (one implementation):**
- A drag handle that shares the property glyph's slot and swaps in on hover
  (the pinned rail's arrangement) — the label column does not move and
  nothing reaches outside the row. Every row 32px. (It first shipped in a
  gutter; see the same-day review below for why that was wrong.)
- The LABEL is the menu: Move up · Move down · Hide, plus "Reset properties"
  once something has been arranged. Keyboard-complete (Enter opens it, arrows
  skip a disabled item), and the same act is draggable for a pointer.
- "N hidden" discloses the hidden rows WITH their values, each with Show.
- Saved per person and per record KIND in `profiles.preferences` — read-modify-
  write like pins, no migration, zero extra round trips (the profile is already
  request-cached by the layout).
- `lib/property-layout.ts` rules: the order keeps hidden and off-screen keys, so
  unhiding restores a row's place and a conditional row (Deadline) never drifts
  to the end; a key the order has never seen is appended, so a new built-in
  shows up; a hidden key that is not on this record is not counted.
- Optimistic, and reverts with "Could not save your properties." on failure —
  verified in the browser.

**Not built, on purpose:** custom properties with VALUES on a project or client.
A value is per-record data that the portal, exports and other people in the
space need; it belongs in a column, not on one person's profile.

**Found on the way:**
1. **Every drag list in the app hydrated wrong.** dnd-kit's fallback id is a
   module-level counter: the server kept counting (`DndDescribedBy-1`), the
   browser restarted at `-0`, and React discarded the subtree. All six
   `DndContext`s now take `id={useId()}` — three had no id, two had literals
   that collide when two instances mount, and the first fix for tasks-board was
   `id ?? useId()`, a conditional hook call. Guarded app-wide.
2. **The handle failed contrast** at `ink-300`: 1.90:1 light, 1.75:1 dark, for
   the only sign a row can be dragged. Now `ink-500` (6.09 / 6.08), the same ink
   as the pinned rail's handle. Guarded.
3. **My own DS comment was wrong by 4px** — it said the trigger is the column
   plus two insets; the negative margin cancels one, so it is 124 + 4 = 128.
   The test asserts the sum instead of trusting prose.
4. Two Phase 1 header guards failed on a JSX spelling while their rules held;
   re-anchored on the property block. One new pure test passed for the wrong
   reason (the hidden key was never in `order`); rewritten as the real sequence.
5. The projects dev-preview had no Toaster, so every failure there was
   invisible; mounted like the other harnesses.

`tsc` clean · **1772 tests / 108 files**. Must-fail controls verified for the
arrange rules, the hidden count, the DndContext id and the handle's ink.

### Record headers — the same-day review (2026-09-11)

Three defects in the block above, all mine, all found by measuring rather
than looking:

1. **The gutter clipped.** The handle lived in a 24px gutter pulled left of
   the page inset, but `--view-px` is fluid (18–40px; 14–28px in compact). At
   375px, 6px of every handle was cut off by the scroll region, and touch
   showed all seven permanently as stubs down the left edge. The handle now
   shares the glyph's slot, so nothing reaches outside the row at any width.
   Touch gets no handle; the label menu moves the row.
2. **Fourteen Tab stops for a monthly act.** Seven handles plus seven label
   menus took the header from 3 Tab stops to 17. The menu is the keyboard
   path, so the handle left the Tab order (`tabIndex={-1}`, after dnd-kit's
   spread or its `tabIndex: 0` wins): 10. The pinned rail keeps its handle
   tabbable — there it IS the only keyboard path.
3. **A handle you could see but not grab.** On hover the glyph fades to
   opacity 0, and a transparent element still hit-tests — while anything below
   opacity 1 paints in the positioned layer AFTER the handle. The invisible
   glyph took every press. `pointer-events-none` on the glyph: hit-testing the
   slot now returns the handle, and a real one-row drag lands where dropped.

The "N hidden" state is now previewable (`/dev-preview/projects?hidden=
started,sharing`): the disclosure row sits on the label axis (its icon on the
glyph column, its text on the label text) and reveals the hidden rows with
their values, dimmed, without handles.

**A note on instruments.** Synthetic `PointerEvent`s and `KeyboardEvent`s did
not drive dnd-kit at all — both "drags" changed nothing — and a long
single-jump tool drag reported a drop over the last row. Only a real, short
drag was evidence. rAF measured 122/s, so this was not pane throttling.

## Phase 4 — the project page on a phone (2026-09-11)

The brief defined three phases and all three have shipped; it has no Phase 4.
This one was chosen from evidence: checking the header work at 375px found
the project Tasks tab broken on a phone in three ways.

Measured at 375px:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tabs covered by the view switcher | Docs, Files, Money (3 of 6) | none |
| workstream names visible | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| task title width | ~6 characters ("Stake…") | 151px ("Stakeholder interviews") |
| share pill | 74px, worded | 24px, eye only |
| priority | bars + word | bars (the word stays for screen readers) |

At 320px every name and title still reads (titles 96px). On the 604px desktop
pane nothing moved: rows 36, headings 32, a 37px tab bar with the switcher on
it, one hairline, no tab hidden.

**The fixes, all systemic:**
- **DS `Tabs` gained an `end` slot.** The switcher had been absolutely
  positioned over the bar's right end. As a sibling in the bar's own flow it
  can never cover a tab: beside the list when the bar is at least 37.5rem wide
  (sharing one hairline), on its own line below otherwise; in between, the
  list gives up width and scrolls under its fade. The threshold is a CONTAINER
  width, because the same bar sits beside a rail on a laptop.
- **The threshold is measured.** My first value, 38rem, was an estimate and
  stacked the switcher on a 604px bar where it fit — re-adding the very band
  Phase 1 removed. Measured: 405 + 12 + 185 = 602px. A guard now requires
  every class in the bar to agree on one number.
- **The task list CARD is the query container**, and its headings and rows
  give way under 28rem: the share pill drops its word, priority drops its word
  (`PriorityBadge` gained `labelClassName`), "Add a date" keeps its calendar,
  the "· N shared" tally hides. The card, not each row — a row made a
  container can no longer size to its content and would collapse in any
  shrink-to-fit context.
- **Why every quiet control was showing on the phone:** `reveal-on-hover` is
  always visible on a coarse pointer, because touch has no hover. That is
  right, and it means a narrow container has to shed width rather than hide.

`tsc` clean · **1783 tests / 109 files** · 9 phone guards in
`components/projects/project-phone.test.ts`, must-fail controls verified.

**The rest of the page, swept at 375px.** Overview, Docs, Files, Money,
Portal, and the Board and Calendar layouts: no sideways overflow anywhere.
Two more lists had the task list's fault and got its fix — a query container
for their share pills. Doc titles had been cut to ~14 characters; they now get
159px and all three read in full. The Overview's update text had been cut
mid-sentence; it now gets 218px and reads in full. The Files list got its
container too, but the harness has no files, so that one is guarded rather
than measured.

**Known limitation, not fixed here:** the Calendar layout on a phone gives a
task chip ~30px ("S…"). A seven-column month grid at 375px has no more to
give; the right answer is a phone-specific design (a dot per day, the day's
tasks listed below on tap), which is a feature rather than a fix.

**Harness note:** the Clients preview logs six 400s. They are its own Supabase
queries (projects, pages, feedback, mentions) sent with the fake client id
`c1`, which is not a UUID — the preview's data, not a product fault.

`tsc` clean · **1784 tests / 109 files** · 10 phone guards (the Files check
joined an existing one), controls verified.

**Home, the same day.** The shared task row compacts only inside a query
container, and Home's lists had none — at 375px its titles were cut to 63px and
61px. Home's plan panel body and its completed list are now containers (opted
in per list, not on the DS `PanelBody`: containment would also make every panel
body the containing block for every absolutely positioned popover inside it).
The row's other chips learned to give up their words the same way: the project

`PriorityBadge` already had, so every chip drops its word the same way. The

## The Board groups by workstream; `tasks.status` is retired — 2026-09-10/11

Phase 3's last item from the structure review: *"Board groups by workstream,
not status; retire `tasks.status`; client review stays in approvals."* Built
on 2026-09-10 and interrupted by the header requests; finished, tested and
recorded here.

### Why

The project Board drew To do / In progress / Review / Done from `tasks.status`
— a fourth vocabulary for a task's state, null on 78 of 88 tasks, invisible in
the List, Calendar, Home and portal, and **lossy**: drag a card Review → Done,
untick it in the List, and it came back in To do, because the List writes
`done` and never `status`. Switching layout changed what the columns *meant*.
That vocabulary also produced a shipped bug the same week (the MCP `today`
tool filtered on it and lost most open work).

### What shipped

- **The columns are the workstreams**, from `boardGroups` — the List's own
  projection (`groupByStream`) plus one deliberate difference: "No workstream"
  is always the last column, because on a Board it is how a card *leaves* a
  stream, and a drop target that appears only once something is in it is no
  drop target. Drag files a card; the tick on the card finishes it and folds it
  into that column's Completed group after the house 3-second beat.
- **It is the Tasks board, not a third kanban.** `components/tasks/tasks-board.tsx`
  now takes columns with a name, an optional swatch, a title/facts/actions
  slot, and an in-place "new column" composer. The hand-built status kanban in
  `projects-workspace.tsx` is gone, dnd-kit and all.
- **Workstream controls are one set, two compositions.** Progress, Paused, the
  deadline, rename and the menu (Rename · Move left/right or up/down — the label
  follows the axis — · Pause · share all · Delete) moved out of the List's
  heading into `workstream-controls.tsx`, and both views draw them.
- **`tasks.status` has no reader and no writer.** `setTaskStatus` is deleted, the
  loader stopped asking for the column (and dropped an extra round trip on
  unmigrated accounts), `statusSupported` is gone. The column stays in the
  table — no DDL — and in the task export, because it is still the user's data.

### Defects found on the way, all fixed in this sprint's area

1. **Keyboard drags on BOTH boards dropped nowhere.** `pointerWithin` answers from
   the pointer, and a keyboard drag has none. `boardCollision` keeps it for the
   pointer and uses `closestCorners` for the keyboard. Must-fail control: with
   `pointerWithin` restored, Space-lift + → + Space announced "put back".
2. **Screen readers heard ids** ("Draggable item 6f1c… over droppable 91be…").
   Announcements now say the task, the column and the position
   ("…is in Design, position 1 of 3"). Cards are list items, not buttons that
   contain buttons.
3. **A thrown failure left the screen lying.** Seven workstream writes rolled
   back only on a *returned* error; `requireSession` *throws* on an expired
   session. Measured in the harness: a dragged card stayed in its new column
   while the console said `Not authenticated`. All seven now go through
   `applyShare` (revert on either); rename, which never reverted at all, too.
4. **The Tasks board's "New list" clicked another button by its label** — and
   with the rail off screen the only match was its own. It names the list in
   place now, through the same `createList`.
5. **`setTaskOrder` saved a column one row at a time** — ~228ms each, so a
   ten-card renumber took over two seconds, on both boards. Parallel now.
6. **"New workstream" had two inline copies**, one silent on failure, both
   computing the new `sort_order` from every project's streams. One
   `createStream`, which reports a throw and mirrors the server's max + 1.
7. **Rename opened with the caret at the end** (measured selection `[6, 6]` on
   "Design") because the closing menu reclaimed focus. The menu now leaves
   focus in the field and the name is selected, so typing replaces it.
8. A literal DndContext id (`"project-board"`) survived the app-wide `useId`
   sweep through a `TasksBoard` prop nobody else used; the prop is gone.
9. Dead code the refactor exposed: `doneWeek`/`timeWeek` (computed every render,
   never read), the `weekStart` prop and `weekStartISO()` that fed only them
   (itself a UTC `toISOString` day, the bug `lib/date.ts` forbids), `PropDot`.

### Verified

In the browser (dev harness), end to end: a pointer drag filed a card and the
List agreed at once; a keyboard drag moved it; ticking held the card for the
beat and folded it into Completed with the header going to 1/2; the column menu
opened from the keyboard with Move left/right enabled for a middle stream; a
move, a rename and a new stream each applied at once and, because the harness
has no session, rolled back with "Could not save that — check your connection
and try again."; Escape discarded a rename even with the blur that followed.

`tsc` clean · eslint clean on every touched file · **1,813 tests / 110 files**
under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` and `America/Los_Angeles`. 18 guards in
`components/projects/project-board.test.ts` and 9 rule tests for
`boardGroups`/`landAt`; a must-fail control for each, one of which exposed a
test gap (a -3 index clamps on its own; -1 is the case that proves the clamp).

**Instrument notes.** In the hidden Browser pane a pane `visibilitychange`
fires every ~2s and dnd-kit rightly cancels any drag it interrupts, and timers
are throttled (a "15 × 40ms" drag took 12s). Drive drags with MessageChannel
yields, not `setTimeout`. Keys sent through the pane can arrive late and land on
whatever holds focus — the app's single-letter shortcuts then switch tabs — so
drive menus from inside the page. `document.hasFocus()` is false in a hidden
pane: an input can be the active element without any focus events firing.

**Deployed** as version `ff9bd4fa-84e5-4c74-89ad-977d17f0ee0a` (startup 22 ms),
carrying the board sprint above and the other session's 2026-09-11 work
(project identity, nav rhythm, Documents contrast, arrangeable properties,
Phase 4 on a phone). Smoke: `/` → `/today` → `/login`, `/login` 200,
`/dev-preview/projects` 404, `GET /api/mcp` 200, unauthenticated `POST` 401.
Migrations 0041 and 0042 remain unapplied; both are gated.

**Worker size: 3,006.5 KiB gzipped of the 3,072 KiB ceiling — 65 KiB left**,

## Worker headroom: 65 KiB → 286 KiB — icons ship two weights, not six (2026-09-11)

The deploy above measured the worker at **3,006.5 KiB gzipped against
Cloudflare's 3,072 KiB free-plan ceiling** — one more feature from a deploy
that fails. Measured, not guessed: one server chunk was **464 KiB gzipped**,
seven times the next largest, and it held **378 Phosphor icons, each carrying
its paths in six weights** (bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin). The
picker catalogue had grown 70 → 260 that day, and a stored icon is looked up
by NAME (`ph:Rocket`), so none of it could be tree-shaken.

**The seam only ever draws two of the six.** Its adapter mapped the DS
`<Icon>` to Phosphor's `regular`, or `fill` for `weight="fill"` — the DS "bold"
is a stroke width, which Phosphor's filled paths ignore. Four weights were
dead on arrival, in every icon, on every page.

**What changed.** `scripts/gen-icon-glyphs.mjs` reads Phosphor's own
definitions and writes `components/ds/icon-glyphs.generated.ts`: regular +
fill for the 210 interface glyphs, regular alone for the 169 picker-only ones
(a stored record icon is always drawn regular). `glyph()` in the seam draws
them with **the same markup Phosphor's `IconBase` produced** — same
attributes, same order, same `1em`/`currentColor` defaults. Phosphor is still
the one family; its components simply no longer ship, and no runtime module
imports the package. The seam and its generator remain the only two places
that know which icon library the app uses.

**Nothing on screen moved, and that is proven rather than eyeballed:**
`components/ds/icon-glyphs.test.ts` renders every interface glyph (both
weights), every picker glyph and the bare-props defaults through the seam AND
through Phosphor's own component, and requires byte-identical markup. It also
holds the table and the seam to each other (no missing glyph, no dead data,
fill exactly where the interface can ask for it) and forbids a runtime import
of the package. Five must-fail controls, all caught: a corrupted path, a wrong
viewBox, the fill weight ignored, the package import returning, and one
interface glyph losing its fill.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| worker, gzipped | 3,006.5 KiB | **2,786.1 KiB** |
| headroom under 3,072 | 65 KiB | **286 KiB** |
| the icon chunk | 464 KiB | 248 KiB (the table is 70 KiB) |
| Phosphor weight maps in the bundle | 378 | **0** |

The same icons leave every page's client JavaScript too, so this is a load-time
win as well as a deploy one.

Two generator lessons: a Phosphor name is not always a file name (renamed
icons keep their old export as an alias — `FolderNotchIcon` lives in
`Folder.es.js` — so it resolves through the component files' own imports), and
it strips comments before reading `glyph("…")` calls, because the seam's own
how-to comment was the first thing it tried to generate.

`tsc` clean · eslint clean · **1,821 tests / 111 files** in both timezones.

## Login: a blank first paint, and an open redirect — 2026-09-11

Found while checking the icon deploy's live HTML: production `/login` was
**12 KB with no form in it** — only the theme script and an empty canvas —
where the dev server rendered 33 KB with the form. The page carried
`BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING`: it read `?next=` through
`useSearchParams()` inside a Suspense boundary, and in a statically built
page that hands the whole subtree to the browser. The first screen anyone
sees was blank until its JavaScript arrived. Every smoke test had passed,
because they checked status codes, not content.

Reading the same code found the worse problem: **after sign-in the page did
`router.push(next)` with `?next=` unchecked** — an open redirect. A crafted
link could send someone to any site in the moment after they had typed their
password into ours, which is the most convincing step a phishing page can
borrow. Nothing in the app links to `/login?next=` today, but anyone can.

**The fix.**
- `next` is read at the moment it is used — `window.location.search` in the
  submit handler — so no hook touches render, no Suspense is needed, and the
  page prerenders whole. Nothing about the form depends on `next`; only where
  it goes afterwards does.
- **`safeNextPath` (`lib/safe-url.ts`)** beside the app's other URL rules: a
  single-slash path on this site, or `/today`. The input must not start `//`
  or `/\`, it is resolved against a placeholder origin and must stay there, and
  **the normalised OUTPUT is checked too** — `/.//evil.example`,
  `/x/..//evil.example` and `/./\evil.example` pass every input check and
  normalise to `//evil.example`, protocol-relative again. My first version let
  them through; the must-fail control that removed the origin check *passed*,
  and asking why is what found them. (`safeHref` does not share the flaw: it
  returns the raw string, which a browser resolves once, in place.)

**Verified live** (version `55db9bc8`): `/login` is **19,752 bytes with the
form in the HTML and no bailout marker**, the route is still static, and the
shipped login chunk contains the rule. 14 attack spellings refused and three
legitimate paths kept in `lib/safe-url.test.ts`, plus a guard that the page
never reads the query through the hook. `tsc` clean · eslint clean ·
**1,825 tests / 111 files**. Worker 2,787 KiB gzipped.

**Noticed, not in scope:** `requireUser()` redirects to a bare `/login`, so a
deep link opened while signed out (an email pointing at a project) lands on
Home after sign-in instead of where it pointed. Preserving it means passing
the path as `?next=` — which `safeNextPath` now makes safe to do.

### Phone width, continued — Calendar, Documents, the viewport hook (2026-09-11)

A 375px sweep of Tasks, Clients, Documents, Week and Calendar found two more
faults; Tasks, Clients and Week were clean.

- **The Calendar opened on the Week grid on a phone.** Seven days in 375px cut
  12 event labels to ~28px ("K…", "C."). The view is now DERIVED, not stored:
  your choice if you made one, otherwise Day on a narrow screen and Week on a
  wide one. Verified: 1280px opens on Week (7 columns), 375px on Day with
  every label readable. Picking a view wins at every width.
- **Documents clipped its own verb.** The header lane held Filter 89 + layout
  76 + Import 82 + New doc 98 in 357px and clips, so "+ New doc" lost its right
  edge. Filter and Import become named 28px icon buttons when the header is
  tight (the page's existing `headerTight`); the verb keeps its word. Not a
  container query, on purpose: that lane sizes to its content, and a container
  there would collapse to nothing.
- **`useNarrow` reads a store now** (`useSyncExternalStore`), not an effect. The
  effect was right for hydration and wrong for every client navigation: a view
  mounting on a phone still rendered wide first, painted, then switched — a
  flash, and a real one where the answer picks WHICH grid renders. The server
  snapshot stays `false`, so hydration is unchanged; a client-side mount is
  right on its first render. Seven callers benefit. Four guards.

Pre-deploy: `npm run check` — **1834 tests / 113 files** green on the shared
tree; worker **2,787.44 KiB gzipped**, 285 KiB under the 3,072 KiB ceiling.
Light and dark both checked by eye on the project page before shipping, since
another session's theme work rides in the same tree.

**Deployed** (the user asked for everything built to ship): version
`41a68504-6919-4bdd-be1b-ec98ecdb266b`, worker 2,787.43 KiB gzipped, startup
26 ms. Live smoke probes all as designed — `/` 307 → `/today` 307 → `/login`
(the worker booted and reached Supabase), `/login` 200, `/dev-preview/ds` 404
(harnesses still excluded from production), `/f/does-not-exist` 200 (by
design, no enumeration oracle), `GET /api/mcp` 200, `POST /api/mcp` 401.

**The project Calendar on a phone — the known limitation, closed.** The Tasks
tab's Calendar layout was a seven-column month grid at every width, so at 375px
a task chip got ~30px ("S…"). Its card is now a query container: under 28rem the
grid gives way to an agenda of the same tasks — the days that have something, in
order ("Tue 8 Sep", "Sun 13 Sep", "Wed 16 Sep"), every title in full (281px),
rows 44px on a touch screen. Both shapes are in the markup and the card's own
width picks one, so the right shape is there on first paint with no viewport
hook and no flash. At 1280px the month grid is unchanged, and its weekday heads
now read "Mon", not "MON": the overline role went sentence case on 2026-09-08
and this was the last place still shouting. Guarded, controls verified.

### Sentence case, enforced — the four ways a label shouted (2026-09-11)

The user's 2026-09-08 directive made sentence case the rule for every label. A
375px screenshot of the client portal still read "PROGRESS", "AWAITING YOU",
"BALANCE DUE" — on the one surface a CLIENT sees. The existing guard only caught
`text-overline … uppercase` in a className; the same shout arrived three other
ways, and a sweep found every one:

- **The shared role.** `TYPE.label` in lib/typography.ts still carried
  `textTransform: 'uppercase'`. It has no caller today, which is exactly when to
  fix it — before the next one shouts.
- **Inline styles:** the portal's labels, the focus timer (four), rituals'
  "Step n of m", the week board's rail label, a database menu.
- **`{name.toUpperCase()}` in markup:** the Calendar month grid's weekdays, the
  command palette's group names, the week board's group titles (and the project
  calendar's, fixed earlier today).
- **A bare `uppercase` class:** the new-project template preview (which also
  hand-set an off-scale 10px — now the `text-micro` token), and the design-system
  page itself, whose typography specimen documented section labels as UPPERCASE:
  the reversed rule, presented as current. Its rail group names and "Used in"
  label now use the real `text-overline` role.

Letter-spacing went with the capitals everywhere — CLAUDE.md records that the
tracking existed only to keep capitals legible. Two dev-only harnesses were
fixed too; one also faded its text with opacity, now a solid ink step.

**Kept, on purpose:** initials (avatars, the portal's studio mark), hex codes and
first-letter capitalisation all uppercase into a VARIABLE, never inline in
markup, and a date picker's weekday initials are single capitals by convention
and aria-hidden. The guard's shape keeps exactly those out of its net.

Verified: the portal and the focus timer render nothing in capitals, and the
design page's rail reads "Foundations", "Primitives", "Forms". Guard widened in
`app/design-system.test.ts` (+2 tests), with four must-fail controls (inline
style, markup, bare class, the role). `tsc` clean · **1838 tests / 113 files**.

Noticed, not touched: the design-system page keeps a fixed-width rail at 375px,
leaving ~90px for content. That page belongs to the Redesign session.

### The client's two actions were invisible until you typed (2026-09-12)

A contrast pass over the portal in both themes flagged "Reply" at 1.34:1 and
"Accept" at 1.20:1. Both were false alarms in WCAG terms — the buttons were
DISABLED, and disabled controls are exempt — but the finding underneath was
real. The DS renders every disabled button as a pale wash
(`bg-surface-disabled` + `ink-300`), so on the two things a client comes to the
portal to do — sign a proposal, answer a question — the action read as ABSENT
until they had already typed.

Both are pressable now, and both explain themselves:
- **Accept** keeps `disabled` only where signing is impossible (the owner's own
  view) or already in flight. Pressing it with no name runs the same
  `validateSignerName` a typed name does — "Please type your full name.",
  `role="alert"`. The block had been built for this all along.
- **Reply** is disabled only while sending. Pressed empty it says "Write a reply
  first." and puts the cursor in the box.

**The bigger bug was underneath.** `send()` returned SILENTLY four ways: an
empty reply, the owner's preview, a link with no token, and a server refusal.
The first was hidden behind the disabled button; the other three meant a client
could press Reply and get nothing back at all. Every exit says something now,
and the server's own error text reaches the client.

**One more distinction:** a hint knows whether it is about the FIELD or about
the link. Only a field hint marks the textarea `aria-invalid` — a red box around
text that is perfectly fine tells a screen reader the wrong thing.

Verified in the browser, which runs these buttons in their real enabled state:
Accept empty → "Please type your full name.", typing clears it. Reply empty →
the nudge, and focus lands in the textarea (`TEXTAREA · Reply…`); typing clears
it; pressing with text on a tokenless link → "This link can't send a reply.",
with the field NOT flagged. The message reads 10.84:1 in light, 9.55:1 in dark.
`tsc` clean · **1843 tests / 114 files** · 5 guards, two must-fail controls.

**Owed, and scheduled as the next sprint:** the DS gives every disabled button
`bg-surface-disabled` + `ink-300` — a label nobody can read (1.2–1.7:1 measured
here). WCAG exempts disabled controls from contrast; legibility is a different
argument, and Notion and Linear both keep a disabled button plainly visible.
That is a design-system change touching every screen, so it gets its own sprint
rather than a detour inside this one (SPRINT_RULES: a defect outside the current
sprint's area is recorded and scheduled, not started).

### A disabled control you can actually read (2026-09-12)

Scheduled by the portal sprint above, and measured on the real DS Button: the
disabled label sat at **1.54:1 in light and 1.34:1 in dark** on its own wash,
where an enabled button on the same page reads ~7:1. WCAG exempts disabled
controls from contrast, so nothing had ever flagged it — and the portal's two
client actions had been hiding behind exactly this treatment.

The bar is the house one rather than WCAG's: the edge tiers already say a
CONTROL is 3:1 solid, and a disabled control is still a control — you have to be
able to read what the button would do. Candidates measured on the real ground:
ink-400 fails in both themes (2.13 / 1.99); **ink-500 clears it (4.95 / 4.66)**
and is the lowest step that does.

Swept every disabled-label spelling in the app — 15 across 13 components, in the
`disabled:`, `peer-disabled:` and `data-[disabled]:` forms: Button, Input,
Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Segmented, Tabs, Toolbar, Toggle, Pagination, Date
picker, Time picker and habit-count. The disabled FILL is unchanged: the quiet
wash and the not-allowed cursor still say "inactive", which is exactly why the
label can afford to be legible.

Verified in both themes on the DS page — 4.95 / 4.66 disabled against 7 / 6.85
enabled. Guard in `app/design-system.test.ts` rejects ink-100…400 on any
disabled label and pins the Button as the foundation; control verified.
`tsc` clean · **1844 tests / 114 files**.

A note on instruments: the first attempt measured the TOKENS instead of rendered
elements and produced impossible numbers (a primary label at 1.48:1 on its own
fill). Custom properties do not resolve the way the browser paints them. Measure
the element.

### A target a finger can hit (2026-09-12)

Measured at 375px with a coarse pointer, by probing outward from each control's
centre until it stopped responding — which counts the invisible expanders the DS
already uses, and which a bounding box misses:

| surface | controls | under 24px (WCAG 2.5.8 AA) |
|---|---|---|
| Tasks | 26 | 4 |
| Project · Tasks | 49 | 19 |
| Home | 14 | 6 |
| Portal | 4 | 1 |

The worst was the control people touch most: the task checkbox, 16×16, with a
16×14 hit area.

**`touch-min`** is the fix — an invisible centred `::after` with a 24px floor, on
coarse pointers only, changing no layout. The floor is 24 rather than 44 ON
PURPOSE: a task row carries three chips six pixels apart, and 44px expanders
overlap, so the topmost steals its neighbour's taps. A bigger target that hits
the wrong control is worse than a small one that hits the right control.
`IconButton` keeps 44 where an icon control stands alone; `touch-row` keeps 44
for a row.

Applied to the bare checkbox, the share pill, the row and heading menus, the
workstream date chip and the portal's "View all". Two things the first pass got
wrong, both found by re-measuring rather than by reading the diff:
- **A truncating title clips its own expander.** `truncate` is overflow:hidden,
  so the `::after` never escapes — still 61×20 after the "fix". A text control
  takes the floor as a real min-height instead, invisible inside a 36px row.
- **Our own 44 was the thief.** The star's expander reaches ±22px and was eating
  the share pill's edge — 20 measured against a 24 floor. Inside a dense cluster
  the reach is capped back to the floor.

After: Tasks 0 · Project 0 · Portal 0 · Home 2 — and those two are one link
inside a sentence ("Highlight: …"), which WCAG 2.5.8 exempts precisely because
its size is set by the text around it. Desktop is untouched — rows 36, headings
32, titles 20 — because every rule here sits behind `(pointer: coarse)`.

A measurement note: the probe under-reports by up to a pixel (it samples whole
pixels), which is why a 24px share pill read 23; `getBoundingClientRect` says
74×24 exactly. And the first run of the must-fail controls proved nothing,
because three of the new guards were already red — they matched against an array
of lines instead of the file's text. Controls were redone from green.

`tsc` clean · **1848 tests / 114 files** · 4 guards, two must-fail controls.

## No action fails in silence — 2026-09-12

A sweep of every place the app swallows a failure. The first version of the
guard reported 68 offenders; 36 of them were fine, because it only read ONE line
past the `if` and this codebase says the same thing in eight local dialects —
`fail()`, `flash()`, `note()`, `setErr()`, `setFormError()`, `setNote()`,
`setState('error')`, `throw`. A five-line branch ending in `toast(...)` looked
identical to one ending in nothing. Taking the whole brace-balanced branch, and
teaching it the real vocabulary, left **25 genuinely silent sites** — and they
were all one thing:

**An optimistic edit reverting with no message.** You tick a task, it un-ticks
itself 300ms later, and nothing says why — which reads as a missed click, so you
press again. The house had already decided this: `mutation-worker.tsx` says
*"silently reverting an edit is worse than never applying it"*, and the QUEUED
path has always honoured it. The direct write path never got the memo. Same
principle, one path short.

`toastReverted(reason)` now owns the sentence for both paths, so they cannot
drift — the queue's own toast was rewritten to call it. Two sentences, not one
clause: every server error here is already a capitalised sentence, so the old
`didn’t save — ${reason}` composition read as a capital mid-sentence. The
wording is a pure `revertedMessage()` with tests, because the failure mode is a
seam nobody notices in a toast that shows for four seconds.

Applied at 26 sites. The 26th was not on the guard's list at all: `renameTo` in
documents-view never checked its result, so a refused rename sat on screen
looking saved until the next reload — worse than a silent revert, because a
revert at least tells the truth eventually.

### The bigger thing this uncovered, measured

`requireSession()` **throws**. 161 of the 211 server actions open with it, so an
expired session, a dropped connection or a 500 REJECTS the promise — and
`if ('error' in res)` never runs. Verified in the browser on
`/dev-preview/home` with no session: ticking a task left the checkbox **ticked**,
with only `Uncaught (in promise) Error: Not authenticated` in the console. The
row looked saved. It was not.

That is strictly worse than the silence this sprint fixed — mode one at least put
the state back — and it is the data-loss-dressed-as-responsiveness that
`lib/mutation-queue.ts` was written about. The queue handles it (`{thrown:true}`
→ retry → give up → revert + toast). The direct path does not.

Making 211 actions honour the type they already declare is **its own sprint**
(289 call sites); rule "if a sprint turns out to be two sprints, say so and
finish the first". What ships now is a net that is complete in itself:
`ActionFailureNet` in the shell reports any server-boundary rejection nobody
caught. It deliberately does NOT borrow `toastReverted`'s wording — it cannot
revert anything, so "your change was undone" would be a second lie on top of the
first. It says *"Something didn’t save. What’s on screen may be out of date."*
and offers Reload, which is the only honest remedy. `digest` is the
discriminator: Next.js stamps it on errors leaving the server and it survives
into production, where the message itself is redacted.

DS extension it needed: `toast({ dedupeMs })`. §4.41's 2s window is right for a
confirmation ("Task added" twice really is twice) but wrong for a standing
condition — the screen is not more out of date for being told three times. Five
minutes, so a run of failures collects as ×N on one toast, which usefully says
how many edits are in doubt.

### Harness gap, found on the way

Six dev-preview harnesses (week, home, tasks, clients, documents, focus) render
surfaces that toast, and **none mounted a `<Toaster/>`** — so every error those
six surfaces have ever raised in the harness was invisible, which is why this
was never caught by looking. They now mount the Toaster and the net, for the
same stated reason the other harnesses already did.

### Verified

- Portal approval, no token: the exit now speaks — `role="alert"`, *"This link
  can’t record a decision."* (screenshotted).
- `/dev-preview/home`, no session: the tick stays (mode two, above) and the net
  raises *"Something didn’t save…"* with Reload. Same click, minutes earlier,
  said nothing at all.
- `toastReverted`'s sentence is unit-tested rather than eyeballed; its rendering
  is the same `toast()` call the net's verified toast goes through.
- Six must-fail controls, all from green: a one-line branch going silent, a
  multi-line one, and the **boundary** case — a silent branch sitting directly
  above an unrelated `toast(` must still be caught, or the branch scanner is
  reading too far and every result is worthless. Plus three on `code()`.

A guard bug worth keeping: the guard matched its own prose, because
`if ('error' in res)` appears in the comment explaining what it forbids. The fix
belonged in the shared `code()` helper, which knew only comment lines that START
with `//` or `*` — a JSX block comment's middle lines start with neither. Now it
tracks blocks across lines, so every guard in the suite benefits. That change
then blanked every `// silent:` exemption, because a justification IS a comment:
detection reads the stripped copy, justification reads the raw one.

`tsc` clean · **1852 tests / 114 files** · 26 sites, 1 net, 1 DS extension,
6 harnesses, 6 must-fail controls.

## Content: the section answers "what needs me" — 2026-09-12

Two things were asked for: the named tabs from the Forms hub, and for Content to
stop being so basic. They turned out to be the same problem.

**The tabs were four glyphs** — a tray, a stack of cards, a calendar, an archive
box — legible only to someone who already knew the module. They now read
`Inbox · Board · Calendar · Library`, and they moved from the `actions` lane to
the `tabs` lane, which is where `page-header.tsx` says "where you are" belongs:
Inbox is what has landed and Library is what is finished, so these are four
different SETS of pieces, not four shapes of one list. It also stops four labels
from crowding the primary button. The Inbox count came out of hiding while I was
there — it was locked inside an `aria-label`, so a screen reader was told "2 to
sort" and everyone else was told nothing.

**"So basic" was not about the pipeline.** The model is rich — seven stages,
formats, channel, publish and shoot dates, hook, location, call time, source,
approval, lateness. The board showed title, channel, date. And the section's
answer to "what needs me" was the subtitle, as prose: `10 in progress · 1 late ·
1 needs changes`. Three true numbers you cannot act on, describing pieces that
were — measured on screen — **scrolled off the right-hand edge**, because
lateness and rejected work live in `edit` and `review` and the board is ordered
by stage. The one thing you opened the page to find was the one thing the page
made you hunt for.

So: `needsYou(pieces, today)` in `lib/content.ts`, and a strip above the board.

It is the exact mirror of `lib/waiting.ts` and keeps that module's one hard rule
— **whose move is it?** `waitingOn` lists what you cannot act on and so must
never fill with your own homework; this lists what you can and so must never
fill with someone else's. **An overdue piece sitting with a client is therefore
absent**, which is the test that defines the function: listing it would tell you
to go and do a thing you cannot do. Chasing is a different act from making.

The strip **renders nothing when empty** — not an empty state, nothing. Same
rule as the waiting-on panel: a heading over a blank space is a permanent
reminder of an absence, and "nothing is slipping" needs no billboard. Capped at
four, with the true total on the heading, so a capped piece is never hidden
silently — it is still on the board with its own badge.

### A contradiction the screen showed me

The first render put `Changes` beside the words **"Waiting on a look"** on the
same card. `STAGE_ACTION` is keyed on the stage alone, and its own comment
admits the hole: `review` resolves to "Waiting on a look" whether or not anyone
was ever asked. A piece whose client has come back asking for changes is firmly
yours again, and it was being told to wait for a look it had already had.

Fixed in the model, not on my new card — `nextAction(piece)` reads the approval
as well as the stage, and **the detail panel had the identical bug from the
identical cause** (it read the same raw map). It prefers the client's own words
when there are any: "cut the intro to 10s" is a better instruction than anything
we could compose, and it is the note they took the trouble to write. That line
gets two lines on the card, because one truncated line read "Love it — can we
cut the intro to 1…", which is a notification rather than an instruction.

### Verified

- Board at desktop, dark, and 375px. The strip shows both slipping pieces and
  correctly omits the third, which is awaiting the client — the rule's defining
  case, confirmed against the fixture on screen rather than only in a test.
- Strip cards are 300px on a 12px gutter — the board's own column width and gap,
  so each card sits exactly over the column it belongs to and the strip reads as
  the top of the board rather than a banner above it.
- At 375px the strip stacks inside the gutters and the tab lane scrolls with a
  visible thumb; all four tabs switch, and the subtitle stays view-aware.
- Two must-fail controls from green: deleting the `isAwaitingClient` guard, and
  reverting `nextAction` to the raw stage map. Each goes red and names the one
  test that defines the rule.

Recorded, not started: the calendar's day chips truncate to unreadable stubs
("The 3-question c…") at month width, and the board leaves roughly 60% of the
canvas empty below three short columns.

`tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · **1864 tests / 114 files** · 2 rules, 11 tests,
2 must-fail controls.

## Content: three places, one pipeline drawn two ways — 2026-09-12

Follow-up to the same day's Content sprint, from three notes on screenshots.

**"Content" twice.** The app header row already says Content, with this module's
icon, because that is what the nav says you are looking at; the page header
underneath repeated it in bold. Before removing it I checked every other module,
because "fix the system, not the screen" cuts both ways and a duplicate on
eleven pages is a different job from a duplicate on one. The result was
unambiguous: **Content was the only module in the app that restated its own nav
label.** Home shows the date, Calendar the month, Projects the project's name,
Tasks/Clients/Forms/Finance pass no title at all, and Documents and Habits both
pass `title={undefined}` DELIBERATELY to avoid exactly this. So: a local fix,
and with `icon`, `title` and `subtitle` all gone `hasScope` goes false and the
left cluster collapses entirely. The header alignment invariant survives it —
measured, `--app-header-px` is 8px and the row's first box (now the tabs) starts
at 8px with the primary ending 8px from the other edge.

**"8 in progress" — gone.** Prose you cannot act on, and the two numbers in it
that mattered are the Needs you strip, which names the pieces instead of
counting them. `contentSummary` and `librarySummary` therefore have no consumer;
both are kept with a header comment saying so, why, and what would give them a
home again (`PageHeader`'s `count` slot). Their tests encode real answers — a
capture is not "in progress" — and there is no version control here to recover
them from.

**Board and Calendar were never two places.** They are one place drawn two ways:
the same pieces, grouped by stage or laid out by date. As two tabs they asked
the user to treat "where am I" and "how is this drawn" as one question, and
`page-header.tsx` is explicit that they are not — a layout switch is a setting
ON the current view and belongs in the actions lane. `task-view-toggle.tsx`
already said the same thing, in the same words, for List ⇄ Board on Tasks:
*"this control is icon-only while the module switchers keep their words — those
change WHAT you are looking at, this only changes how."* So the tabs are now
three PLACES — **Inbox · Pipeline · Library** — and the layout is a pair of bare
16px glyphs beside the primary button, rendered only in the pipeline, because a
dead toggle is worse than no toggle.

"Pipeline" rather than a new word: the module's own empty state already says
"Nothing in the pipeline" for exactly this set. It is also what Clients calls
its deal stages, which is not a glossary collision but the same concept applied
to a different object — deals move through a pipeline, so does content.

**One param, not two.** The layout could have been `?layout=board|calendar`,
which would have needed an alias and a migration. Instead `?view=` keeps naming
exactly what is on screen and the tab's own value is DERIVED from it (`PLACE_OF`).
`?view=calendar` — a link `content-today.tsx` already sends for a shoot day —
therefore keeps working with nothing changed: verified live at
`?view=calendar&shoot=2026-09-07`, which lands with both radios checked
(Pipeline, Calendar) and the call-sheet dialog open.

The Needs you strip moved up to the pipeline REGION, so it sits above either
layout. It belongs to the place, not to one drawing of it — the same pieces need
you whether you are looking at columns or at a month, and a panel that appeared
and vanished with the layout is the drift CONSISTENCY_PRINCIPLE.md is about.
Both layouts gave up their own `px-4 py-3` and `h-full` to the shared region and
now claim `flex-1 min-h-0`, since the strip is a sibling and `h-full` would be
the height of both together.

### Verified

- Header: no title, no subtitle, insets 8/8 measured against the token.
- All three tabs switch; the layout toggle appears only on Pipeline and is
  absent on Inbox and Library. URLs: `?view=inbox`, `?view=library`,
  `?view=calendar`, and bare for the default board — a URL never carries its own
  default.
- The strip shows above both the board and the month grid, and the grid still
  fits without scrolling after giving up ~90px.
- 375px: all three clusters share one row and the tab lane scrolls, thumb
  visible.

`tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · **1864 tests / 114 files**.

### The board's empty columns were slabs — same day

Reported from a screenshot of the live board: tall grey columns ending abruptly
part-way down the page. Measured, not guessed — the column heights were all
identical to the tallest, and in the harness the region under them held 519px of
nothing.

`components/ds/ui/board.tsx` set no `align-items`, so flex defaulted to
`stretch` and **every column inflated to match the fullest one**. A pipeline with
cards in two stages and nothing in five drew five 830px rectangles of empty
grey. The fill was all padding, which is why it read as a fault rather than as
an empty stage.

One word — `items-start` — and a column is as tall as what is in it: measured
316 / 148 / 148 / 213 / 295 / 148 / 148 where all seven had been 316. It is also
what the app's OTHER kanban already did: `database-view`'s board row has
`alignItems: 'flex-start'`. Two boards, one object, two rules; the DS one was the
outlier, and it is the shared component, so the fix is there rather than in
Content's wrapper.

Noted, not changed: with columns at their natural height a very long one grows
the page rather than scrolling inside itself. That is exactly what
`database-view` does, so it is consistency rather than drift — and `published`
already caps itself with "N more in Library". Worth a bound if a stage ever
holds tens.
