## The content board becomes directly manipulable — 2026-09-12

Three asks: a menu on the card, dragging a card between stages with a landing
point "like Notion", and renaming the default stage columns.

**The card already had its ⋯.** `StageMenu`, with every applicable stage in it,
revealed on hover (and always visible at `pointer: coarse`, which is the DS's
`reveal-on-hover` rule). What it did not have was a reason to be discoverable,
because it was the only way to move a card. It is now the drag's **menu twin** —
the rule the timebox rail set: every gesture has one.

**The landing point is deliberately NOT under the cursor.** Notion draws an
insertion line where you point because in Notion you are choosing the position.
A content column is a QUEUE SORTED BY DATE: dropping decides the stage, and the
publish date decides the row. A line under the pointer would promise a choice
that does not exist — you would aim at the bottom of a column and the card would
appear at the top. So the slot opens at the index the DATE gives it, and
`landingIndex(rows, pieceId, stage)` computes that by asking `board()` with the
move already applied. Not a second comparator: the marker and the outcome are
the same function, so they cannot disagree. Seven tests, including the published
column's reverse order and its cap (a piece sorting past the visible tail gets
no slot rather than a wrong one).

**The keyboard promise was removed rather than faked.** dnd-kit's `attributes`
announce `aria-roledescription="draggable"` and tell a screen-reader user to
press space. Space cannot work: the card's own `onKeyDown` owns Enter, and
dnd-kit's arrow step is 25px — thirteen presses to cross a 312px column. My
first version spread `attributes` anyway AND clobbered dnd-kit's keydown by
declaring `onKeyDown` after the spread, so it announced a gesture that did
nothing. The twin menu moves a card in two keystrokes and lists every stage, so
it is the keyboard path, and nothing now claims otherwise.

**A guard caught the architecture.** The first version put dnd-kit inside
`components/ds/ui/board.tsx`; `property-block.test.ts` failed with *"the DS draws
shapes; features bring the drag"* — the barrel is imported by dozens of files and
a primitive that drags costs every one of them, which matters against a 3 MiB
worker ceiling. The comment even says "same boundary the DS `Board` keeps". So
the DS grew two SHELL props (`ColumnShell`, `CardShell`) and a `landingAt`
callback, and `components/content/pipeline-drag.tsx` brings the behaviour.
Shells, not `(id) => props` callbacks, because `useDroppable`/`useDraggable` are
hooks — they must be called inside a component, one per column and per card —
and because the shell owns the ref, so dnd-kit measures the real `<section>`.
Both shells are MODULE-LEVEL: built inside the component they would change
identity on every drag-state change and remount every column mid-drag.

**Collision detection is `pointerWithin` with a `rectIntersection` fallback.**
The first version was `pointerWithin` alone, and a card released in the 12px
gutter between two columns silently went home — the pointer was inside no
column. The fallback asks which column the held CARD overlaps, which is the same
question asked of the card rather than of the cursor. This also fixed the first
end-to-end drop that had failed with `over: null`.

**Renaming: the label moves, the id never does.** `idea`…`published` are not
decoration — `isSettled`, `stagesFor`, `STAGE_ACTION`, `board()`'s reverse sort
for the archive and `landingIndex` all read them. A studio calling its edit stage
"The cut" is naming the same step, so `lib/stage-labels.ts` overrides LABELS only
and every rule keeps working. Stored in `profiles.preferences` beside the
property layout, with the same read-modify-write in the action (that column is
shared with the accent, density, timezone, Google-sync metadata and pins) and the
same JSON-enum normalising `readContent` and `lib/properties.ts` both learned:
unknown stage keys dropped, non-strings dropped, a stored blank is no override,
and a label equal to the default is not stored — otherwise a later change to the
default would silently skip whoever had "kept" it. Emptying the field IS the
reset, because clearing a name and asking for the default back are one
intention, so they are one control. 16 tests.

The title itself is the rename affordance — click it and it becomes an input,
the way every other rename in this app works. The alternative was a `⋯` menu
with one item in it. The column header's hard-coded `⋯` IconButton, which had NO
handler on every column of every board, is gone: `BoardColumnData.action` now
renders only what a consumer supplies, because a control that does nothing
teaches people that pressing it is pointless.

One reader, `named(stage)`, feeds all four surfaces that show a stage name — the
column head, the card's move menu, the piece's stage select and the repurpose
list. A rename reaching three of four would be worse than none; the harness
seeds one renamed stage so the case is always on screen.

### Verified

- Rename end to end: `Shoot` → `Filming day` commits on blur, the input closes,
  and the new name appears in the column head AND in a card's ⋯ stage list.
- Seeded rename (`edit: 'The cut'`) reaches every column header on load.
- A move via the twin menu: card goes Idea 3→2, Review 3→4, landing in date
  order.
- Before the DS/feature split, a full pointer drag worked end to end in the
  browser: the held card lifted, the target column ringed, a slot opened at the
  honest index (top of Shoot, above a piece publishing a week later), and the
  drop committed there.
- `landingIndex` and the stage-label rules are unit-tested (23 tests total).

**Owed, and stated plainly:** after the split I could not re-run a full pointer
drag through the harness. `left_click_drag` delivers a trusted pointerdown with
`button: 0` and `isPrimary: true` — confirmed by capturing the event — and
dnd-kit accepts it, but the harness's atomic press-move-release does not deliver
the follow-up `pointermove` that the 4px activation constraint needs, so
`onDragStart` never fires; invoking the activator directly announces "Picked up
draggable item c1" as expected. The logic is unchanged by the split (the hooks
only moved), but that is an argument, not a measurement. **A real mouse is the
test.** If a card does not lift on the live board, the sensor wiring in
`pipeline-drag.tsx` is where it is.

## One kanban column — 2026-09-12

"I want that board column styling consistent in all places." It was not, and the
divergence was bigger than styling.

Measured, three implementations of one object:

| board | column |
|---|---|
| Content pipeline (DS `Board`) | 300px `paper-2` well, `rounded-lg p-2`, `h-9` header, round dot, 12px gutter |
| Tasks — and Projects, which reuses it | 288px UNFILLED lane, divided by `border-r` hairlines, `h-11` header, square swatch, 8px gutter |
| Database board | 264px `paper-3` well, 10px gutter, all inline styles |

Seven differences between two of them, for the same thing, one screen apart.

**The well wins, and the losing side had a real argument.** The Tasks lane was
not an accident: `project-board.tsx` reasons explicitly from CLAUDE.md's rule 1,
"never nest two fills", and chose an unfilled column so the raised card would be
the only fill. The counter-argument that decided it: a column's whole job is to
GROUP its cards, and a hairline between lanes groups by implication where a well
groups by enclosure. The DS `Card` also already takes `on="paper-2"` — the DS
saying this particular nesting is sanctioned rather than overlooked — and the
reference the user pointed at (Notion) encloses too.

`BOARD_COLUMN` in `components/ds/ui/board.tsx` is the spec: width, gutter, well,
header, dot, body, drop tint, and the card width its drag overlay uses. All
three boards draw from it. Measured after, on all three: 300px wide, 12px
radius, identical fill, 8px padding, 12px gutter, 36px header with 4px inset,
8px round dot — the same numbers on every board.

**Height came into the spec too, against my first instinct.** I had written that
height would stay per-surface, on the theory that a dedicated board page wants
full-height lanes with their own scroll. Drawing it settled it: Tasks' wells
became seven-hundred-pixel shafts of grey with one card in them — the same slabs
that made the content board look broken earlier today. Notion does not do it
either: an empty column there is a header and a `+ New` button, not a shaft. So
`items-start` everywhere, and the page scrolls when a column outgrows it.

**The week board is deliberately NOT a consumer.** Its seven day columns FLEX to
fit a week on screen instead of taking a pile's fixed width — that is the whole
finding behind `zenboard-week-board-fit`, and a difference in kind rather than
drift. The guard names it as an exclusion so the next person does not "fix" it.

### Verified

- All three boards measured identically on eight properties (above).
- Tasks, Projects (framed, via `TasksBoard`) and the database board all
  screenshotted after the change.
- Two must-fail controls from green: a board re-hardcoding `w-[288px]`, and one
  dropping the spec for its own `w-[264px] bg-paper-3`. Each goes red and names
  the file.

A guard I wrote and then narrowed: the first version also scanned for
`bg-paper-3` anywhere in a board's FILE, which fired on five unrelated panels
inside `database-view.tsx`. An over-broad guard that cries about unrelated code
is worse than no guard — the third time that lesson has come up today — so it
now checks only that each board uses the spec and that none hard-codes a
column-sized width. The first run also caught a real one: a `w-[284px]` drag
overlay, derived by hand in two places, which is now `BOARD_COLUMN.cardWidthClass`.

`tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · **1889 tests / 115 files**.

**Found on the way out, recorded not started:** `eslint` reports errors in **31
files** across `components/`, `lib/` and `app/` — `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`
("calling setState synchronously within an effect"), `Cannot access refs during
render`, and `Compilation Skipped: Existing memoization could not be preserved`.
None are from today's work (the one in a file I touched, `database-view.tsx:1644`,
is in the month grid I never edited). They matter beyond tidiness: each is a
component the React Compiler then declines to optimise, so this is a performance
finding wearing a lint coat. `npm run deploy` runs `tsc` and `vitest` but not
`eslint`, which is why they have accumulated unseen — worth its own sprint, and
worth adding `eslint` to the check script once the count is zero.

## The owed drag verification, and the 8px it found — 2026-09-14

Last sprint ended with a debt stated plainly: after moving the drag out of the DS
into `pipeline-drag.tsx`, a full pointer drag could not be re-run, because the
in-app browser's `left_click_drag` fires press, move and release as one atomic
step, which never satisfies dnd-kit's 4px activation constraint.

**Paid, with real input.** No Playwright here, and installing it means a ~170MB
browser download, so the check drives the Chrome already on the machine over the
DevTools protocol instead — headless, in a throwaway profile, with a real
`mousePressed`, twelve interpolated `mouseMoved` steps 35ms apart, an inspection
and screenshot while held, then `mouseReleased`. Zero dependencies (Node's
`--experimental-websocket`). Result, on the content harness:

- While held: dnd-kit announced *"moved over droppable area script"*, the Draft
  column was ringed, and the dashed slot sat **after** "The 3-question client
  brief" — exactly what `landingIndex` predicts for an undated piece.
- On release: the card left Idea and landed in that slot, *"dropped over
  droppable area script"*.

So the refactor was sound; the old harness was the only thing broken, which was
the hypothesis, now a measurement.

**And the screenshot caught a real defect.** The lifted card was visibly wider
than the cards it was being dropped among. `BOARD_COLUMN.cardWidthClass` said 284
— "the column less its 2×8 padding" — and forgot the body's own `p-1`. Measured
in the DOM: column 300, card 276. Now `w-[276px]`, and a test DERIVES the number
from the spec's own classes (300 − 2×8 − 2×4) rather than restating it, so
changing the column, the well padding or the body padding without the card
width fails. Must-fail control: putting 284 back goes red. Re-measured with the
real drag: held 277 against 276 in the column — the 1px is the `rotate-1` tilt
enlarging the bounding box (276·cos1° + 70·sin1°), so the element itself is
exact. Tasks' overlay reads the same constant and is corrected with it.

## A failed save no longer looks saved — 2026-09-14

The sprint recorded on 2026-09-12: 161 of 211 server actions open with
`requireSession()`, which THROWS, while every call site handles only a RETURNED
`{ error }`. A failed edit stayed on screen looking saved. The plan on record was
to rewrite the actions to honour their declared type — 289 call sites.

### What shipped

**A client-side fix instead, because the server-side plan could not have been
complete.** Reading Next's own source (`server-action-reducer.js`) showed three
ways an action rejects, and only one of them runs any server code:

| class | how it arrives | remedy |
|---|---|---|
| server threw — expired session, DB exception | rejection with a string `digest` | `router.refresh()` |
| **stale deployment** — tab opened before a deploy | Next throws `UnrecognizedActionError`, **no digest** | offer **reload**, never refresh |
| unreachable — offline, network drop | `fetch` rejects with a `TypeError` | say so; refresh when back online |

A server-side `try/catch` in 211 actions would have caught the first and missed
the other two, because in both the action never runs. The stale case is the
commonest in practice — we deploy several times a day, and every tab left open
across a deploy called an action ID that no longer existed. The old net was deaf
to it: it matched on `digest`, which that error does not carry.

- `lib/action-failure.ts` — `classifyRejection` (pure, tested against Next's
  REAL `UnrecognizedActionError`), the copy for each class, and `RESYNC_EVENT`.
- `components/shell/action-failure-net.tsx` — rewritten around the classifier.
- `lib/use-resync.ts` — for surfaces that load their own rows on the client.
- Four surfaces brought under the fix: the task drawer and focus timer listen for
  the resync; the tasks rail and focus view moved from plain `useState` to
  `useServerState`.

### The decision that mattered

**The revert already existed; it just was never pointed at failures.**
`useServerState` snaps every view back to its server props whenever a refresh
delivers new ones, and `RealtimeSync` already relies on exactly that for every
row change another device makes. So on a server failure the net refreshes, and
the unsaved edit visibly disappears across all 17 server-owned surfaces at once
— with no call site touched. That is what the 289-edit sprint was for.

**Stale deployments get a reload, not a refresh**, following Next's own guidance
on `unstable_isUnrecognizedActionError`: a refresh would fetch a React payload
built by a different deployment than the code rendering it. Offered, not forced,
because the page may be holding unrelated typing.

**The copy caught a lie in my own design.** "The page now shows what's saved" was
true for server-prop views and false on four surfaces that load their own rows.
Rather than soften the sentence and leave those surfaces showing failed edits,
they were fixed — which surfaced two latent bugs: the tasks rail and focus view
seeded server props into plain `useState`, so they had ignored EVERY refresh
they were ever sent, including other devices' live edits. Converting them armed
a known trap — both parents defaulted `savedViews = []`, a new array per render,
which loops `useServerState` — so `NO_SAVED_VIEWS` (frozen) came first; week-view
already used that pattern for its other props and had missed this one.

**`zb:resync`, deliberately not `zb:realtime`.** The drawer's loader is six
queries, and `realtime-sync.tsx` documents what reacting to every row change
costs. Resync fires only when a write fails. Whether those surfaces should also
follow other devices live is its own decision with its own cost — recorded below.

**Checked and rejected: `deploymentId`.** Next's docs say it protects Server
Functions across deployments. The source says the `x-deployment-id` request
header is for the HOST to route an old tab to the old version — and OpenNext
disables that routing on `*.workers.dev`, which is where this app lives. Setting
it would have changed nothing for actions. (Computing it in `next.config.ts` with
`Date.now()` could also have given build workers different ids and made every
request hard-reload forever.)

### Verified — with real input, not the in-app browser

`scripts/verify/verify-action-failure.mjs` drives headless system Chrome over the
DevTools protocol (zero dependencies) against `/dev-preview/action-failure`, a
new SERVER-COMPONENT harness with a real action that throws the way
`requireSession()` does:

| step | row 1 | row 2 | row 3 | client-loaded reloads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| failure, +120ms | ☑ optimistic | ☐ | ☐ | 0 |
| failure, after | **☐ reverted** | ☐ | ☐ | **1** |
| network cut (CDP), tick | ☐ | ☐ | ☑ | 1 — correctly held |
| back online | ☐ | ☐ | **☐ reverted** | **2** |
| a save that succeeds | ☐ | **☑ kept** | ☐ | 2 — no pointless reload |
| full reload | ☐ | ☑ | ☐ | server agrees |

- **Must-fail control:** with only `refresh()` removed, row 1 stays ticked after
  the failed save — the original bug. The refresh is causal.
- **Stale deployment, end to end** (`verify-stale-deployment.mjs`): the page's
  real save is intercepted with CDP `Fetch` and answered as a newer deployment
  answers — `404` + `x-nextjs-action-not-found: 1`, the exact header the live dev
  server returns for an unknown action ID (checked with curl). Next's own client
  threw its own error; the net showed "That didn't save — Zenboard has been
  updated." with Reload, and did not force it.
- Tasks, week and focus harnesses load with no console errors or render loops —
  after first self-testing the console reader, which turned out to persist
  across navigations (so an empty read meant something).
- 10 classifier tests; my own "no action fails in silence" guard caught the new
  harness reverting without a toast, and was right.

`tsc` clean · `eslint`: zero errors in any file touched, repo-wide erroring files
still exactly 31 (none new) · **1907 tests / 116 files**.

### Owed, recorded not started

- **Live cross-device updates for client-loaded surfaces.** The task drawer and
  focus timer do not follow `zb:realtime`, so another device's edit does not
  appear in them until they reload. A real gap, with a real query cost per event
  — its own decision.
- **`deploymentId` for navigations** (not actions): would turn a stale tab's
  client-side navigation into a hard reload instead of applying an RSC payload
  from another build. Needs `?dpl=` asset serving verified on Workers Assets
  first, and the id set once in the deploy script's environment — never computed
  in `next.config.ts`.

## The content calendar, readable at every width — 2026-09-14

**Measured first.** At 1440px only 1 of 9 titles truncated, so truncation was not
the desktop problem: the titles were set in `text-micro`, which computes to
**10px** — below the type scale's own 11px floor, for the one thing on the
surface a person actually reads. At 375px the failure was total: 48px cells,
**all 9 titles cut to 15px of text** ("A…", "Fi…", "T…"). You could see THAT
something was on a day, never WHAT. The constitution's "never desktop-only".

**Benchmark (rule 7), stated specifically:** on a phone, Apple Calendar and Google
Calendar do not put titles in a month grid. The grid carries dots — which days are
busy — and tapping a day lists its events underneath, full width.

**Shipped:**
- **Wide:** chip titles at `text-caption` (12px). A publish date that has passed
  on unfinished work reads in danger ink with a "Late:" tooltip — the same rule as
  the board's `Late` badge, so the pipeline's two layouts agree.
- **Narrow**, switched by the calendar's OWN width (a container query, CSS-only, so
  no layout flash on load): dots in the grid, and an agenda for the chosen day with
  full titles, kind, channel and a `Late` badge; 44px touch rows. One tab stop for
  the whole grid, arrow keys move by day/week, Home/End to month edges, clamped to
  the month on screen. The trailing week drops when it is all next month's days.
- `agendaDay` (lib/content.ts, 5 tests): opens on today when today is in the month
  — even if empty, it is still the day you came to see — else the first day with
  something on it, else the 1st.
- Threshold `42.5rem`, from arithmetic then measured: a chip gives its title the
  cell less 32px; ten readable characters at 12px need ~65px; so seven cells need
  ~680px. Walking the viewport, the layout switches between a 662px container and
  a 682px one.

**Caught in my own draft:** the container-query classes were built as
`` `${breakpoint}:hidden` ``. Tailwind finds classes by scanning source text
literally, so the variant would never have been generated — the phone layout
hidden forever, silently. Now two whole class strings, with the reason beside them.

**Verified with real input** (`scripts/verify/verify-content-calendar.mjs`): opens
on Sat 5 Sep with one tab stop and 35 cells; three real ← presses land on Wed 2 Sep
with focus following, and the agenda shows "August recap · Publish · TikTok · Late";
↓ moves a week; a real tap on the entry opens `?piece=c5`. Contrast measured on the
rendered elements with a self-tested ruler (21:1 black-on-white): the late title
**6.47:1 light, 7.05:1 dark**; a normal title 10.04 / 9.24.

## Four semantic colour names that never existed — same day

The calendar's late state rendered in plain ink. Measured: `.text-danger` had
**zero CSS rules** and computed to the body colour, while `.text-danger-600` was a
real `rgb(185,28,28)`. CLAUDE.md documents the semantic vocabulary as "success /
warning / danger / info", and `accent` has always worked bare — but those four were
never tokens, so authors followed the docs and wrote classes that did nothing. Seven
error and late states were grey because of it, including the portal's
`role="alert"` hints ("This link can't record a decision" — built last sprint, and
grey in its own verification screenshot, unnoticed) and the signature form's
validation line.

Fixed at the token layer, beside `accent`: `--color-{danger,warning,success,info}`
alias their 600 step, which is the ramp's text shade and already theme-aware.
Measured after, in both themes: danger `#B91C1C` / `#EF9189`, warning `#92400E` /
`#E3C07E`, success `#166534` / `#7FC49E`.

**Two counting mistakes, both corrected by measuring.** A grep said 60 dead
`text-danger` uses; the `\b` in it also matched `text-danger-600`. A static scan —
every `--color-*` token the theme declares, against every colour utility in source —
says **7**, and **32 dead colour-class uses across 15 classes** overall.

Frames extracted from the recording with ffmpeg, then each defect measured in the
harness before any code changed.

1. **Cards cut off at a hard edge.** Each column body was still `overflow-y-auto`,
   from when columns had a fixed height. Since `items-start` they are content-height
   and the page scrolls, so the overflow scrolled nothing and only clipped — and CSS

   now `visible` both axes, with a guard and a must-fail control.

   **74 → 211 → 260 → 309 → 329 → 337 → 340** — the lifted copy vanished and the card
   flew back in from its origin column, though it had already been carried there.
   The shared `layoutId` flight is right for moves made elsewhere (the ⋯ menu,
   another device), so it stays; a drop now renews that card's animation key, so the
   landed card has nothing to fly from. After: **340, 340, 340…** from the first
   frame. And a ⋯ menu move still flies: 28 → 188 → 747 → … → 1276. (Removing the
   `layoutId` for one render is not enough — framer keeps the old snapshot.)

   Paper-OS recipe, `border-berry-500 … ring-2 ring-berry-alpha-20`. The border

   the `berry-*` UTILITIES are remapped to the ink ramp on purpose — globals.css, the

### "I don't like this border is cutting" — the carried card

A frame of a card being dragged. Three lines crossed it; each was measured before
anything changed (real drag held mid-flight, photographed at 2×):

- **The lift shadow notched the card's corners.** The overlay wrapper carrying
  `shadow-lift-2` had a 0px radius around a 12px card. Now `rounded-lg` — measured
  12px = 12px.
- **The origin column drew a "drop here" outline.** The over-state ring lit the
  column the card came FROM, where dropping does nothing, and ran a grey line
  through the card for the whole drag. The column shell now reads the held card's
  origin (a context, since the shells are module-level) and never highlights it;
  measured `ringed: false`.
- **The ring itself is gone** from `BOARD_COLUMN.over`: tint only. The precise
  indicator is the dashed landing slot. `surface-active` rather than `-hover`,
  measured over the well: 1.17:1 light / 1.25:1 dark against 1.10 / 1.12.
- **No tilt.** The 1° rotation made every edge of the card cross the board's
  straight lines at an angle and resampled its title soft. Notion carries flat.

The tint measurement caught a broken ruler first: a hover wash came out near-black
in light mode, because the canvas resolver ignored alpha. Fixed to composite each
candidate over the real well, self-tested (50% black over white → 127).

### "Open content the same way a document opens — not full window, with breadcrumbs"

**Found:** `PageView`'s `full-page` mode was `fixed inset-0 z-modal` — the whole
window, sidebar and top bar included — while a Docs page opens inside the app. So a
content piece was a takeover one click away from a document that was not. Notion's
full page never covers its sidebar either.

**Fixed in PageView, not in Content** — the directive is that every record opens
through the one component, so the fix reaches documents, forms and any type opened
full page, together:
- A full page renders **inside the app's content pane** when there is one
  (`[data-view-shell]`), portalled there, non-modal, filling the pane exactly. Clicks
  on the sidebar and top bar are the app, not "outside a dialog", so they don't close
  it; Esc and a **back arrow** do, and the ✕ goes, as on a Docs page. Where no shell
  exists (harnesses, public pages) it still takes the window — checked.
- The pane surface is now ONE definition, `CONTENT_PANE_SURFACE`, used by both the
  shell's panel and the page — so a page is visually the panel, measured identical in
  dark mode (background, border, radius).
- Focus lands on the PAGE, not its first control: the back arrow's tooltip was
  popping on every open.
- **Content's breadcrumbs say where the piece lives:** `Content / Draft / The
  3-question client brief`. The stage crumb opens its siblings — the other stages —
  so a piece can be moved from the crumb that names where it is (the app's
  interactive-breadcrumb rule). The stage select and the crumb share one
  `offeredStages` list.
- A new registry layer, `--z-page: 20`: above the view it covers and that view's
  sticky headers (10), below the widget band (30) where the hover-expanding sidebar
  floats over content.

**A dead class, caught by measuring again.** The first version used `z-page` with the
token declared but no `@utility` line, and the page measured `z-index: auto` — it
only looked right because it came later in the DOM. Every registry token needs its
own utility in Tailwind v4, so `z-index.test.ts` now asserts it; must-fail control
(delete the utility) goes red and names `page`.

**Verified with real input inside the real AppShell** (`?shell=1` on the Content
harness, `scripts/verify/verify-page-in-pane.mjs`): the page rect equals the pane
rect `[238, 56, 1198, 840]` in a 1440×900 window; z-index 20; the sidebar's Tasks
link is hit-testable; back arrow present, no ✕; crumbs `Content / Draft / …`; the
stage menu lists all seven stages (with the renamed "The cut"); choosing Shoot moves
the piece and the crumb follows; Esc returns to the board; focus inside the page,
no tooltip open.

## Overlay states: highlights you could not see, and faint text on a washed menu — 2026-09-12/14

The two-theme sweep was clean AT REST. Opening the overlays found two bug classes.

**1. A state painted with an elevation.** `--color-paper-3` IS the popover tone. The
⌘K palette painted its selected row with it on a raised container — invisible in both
themes. paper-3 and paper-4 are also WHITE in light, so the Select's highlighted option,
the Combobox's active option, Pagination's current page, `Button toggle`'s pressed state
and every `hover:bg-paper-3` on a white card showed nothing in light. The guards counted
29 class variants, 2 inline styles and 3 state branches.
- States are washes now: `bg-surface-hover / -selected / -active`.
- An element with its OWN fill (radio card, dropzone, bookmark card, filled search)
  cannot take `hover:bg-surface-hover` — that replaces the fill, and the wash then
  composites against the parent. New DS utility `wash-over` layers the wash as a
  background-image over the element's own fill, and works on `<input>`.
- The live notification bell's rows were `zb-press` (which already washes through
  `::after`) AND `hover:bg-surface-hover`: washed twice. So was the DS `Menu` item.
- **Every floating list paints the raised tier.** Select, Combobox and the Filter wizard
  painted the CARD tone, so in dark a select list opened darker than its own trigger
  (#202020 under #333333) — while `MENU_PANEL_CLASS` already specified raised, in words.
  Moved, with the field-tier edge. The DS notifications panel's sticky header had the
  same mismatch.

**2. In dark, a wash on the popover fails faint text, and only the text can move.** The
popover (#333333) is dark's lightest surface, and 9% ink makes it #414141: ink-500 3.78,
ink-600 4.26, `--muted-foreground` 3.67. First sighting: the New project dialog's chosen
card, "Start from scratch". What could not move, each ruled out with numbers:
- **the ground** — the ladder the user asked for ("all looks flat") holds it up, and the
  lowest ladder-legal popover still fails;
- **the ramp** — ink-500 would need ~83%, which IS ink-700;
- **the wash** — #333333 has three sRGB units of headroom, so any wash you can see fails;
- **a CSS re-scope of `--color-ink-500` inside overlays** — the aliases rows actually use
  (`--muted-foreground`, `--text-muted`, `--color-text-tertiary`) resolve at `:root` and
  inherit as computed values, so the override never reaches them.

**The decision:** a row that takes a wash brings its secondary text forward to ink-700
while the wash shows. Resting visuals are unchanged in both themes. It is wired on NAMED
groups, because a bare `group-hover:` fires for any hovered ancestor: Radix menu
shortcuts and descriptions (`group-data-[highlighted]/item`), cmdk shortcuts
(`group-data-[selected=true]/item`), the New project cards (`group-aria-pressed/card`,
`group-hover/card`), notification rows, and the ⌘K palette's hint.

**Guards** — `app/theme-bridge.test.ts`, 57 → 64. Every scan was watched failing before
its fix: no state variant paints an elevation (bracket-aware, with one documented
allowance: `bg-paper/NN` on the inverted selection bar IS that surface's wash); no inline

every `z-dropdown` list is raised; each washed row carries the forward step. And a
contrast proof: ink-700 clears 4.5:1 on every surface under every wash in both themes,
with ink-500 on a pressed dark popover held as a control that must keep failing.

## A first visit follows the reader's OS theme — 2026-09-14

**What shipped.** `DEFAULT_THEME` is `system` (it was `light`). Nobody who picked Light or
Dark is affected — only an explicit pick is ever stored — and anyone who never picked now
gets their OS setting, and follows it live when the OS flips at sunset.
- The boot script in `app/layout.tsx` is GENERATED from `lib/theme.ts`, so the change is one
  constant; `layout.tsx` was not touched.
- `watchSystemTheme` already existed, and `AppearanceBoot` mounts it in the ROOT layout, so
  public pages — login, onboarding, portal, forms — follow live too.
- **The public form's captcha was pinned `theme="dark"`** on a token-driven page: on any form
  with the spam check on, every light-mode respondent already got a black Turnstile widget
  on a white form. Removing the pin alone would fall back to Turnstile's `auto` (the OS),
  which ignores an explicit choice — so `TurnstileWidget` now defaults to the page's
  RESOLVED theme.
- The resolved theme has one reader, `lib/use-resolved-theme.ts` (`useSyncExternalStore` on
  `data-theme` + `zb:appearance`). The sidebar's appearance toggle moved onto it from an
  inline `data-theme` read.

**Why now, and why `system`.** Light was the default only while dark was unverified. Both
themes are now measured in every state, overlays open included (entry above), and Notion
and Linear both follow the OS by default. Forcing light onto a dark desktop is the harsher
first impression.

**Verified in the browser**, on a second dev server run from a scratch copy (another
session held this folder's dev lock). A new port is a new origin with empty storage, so
every check was a genuine first visit; colour-scheme emulation stood in for the OS.
- OS dark, nothing stored → `data-theme="dark"` before any interaction.
- OS flipped light → dark with no reload → the page followed both ways: a listener on the
  same media query found `data-theme` already flipped when `change` fired. (One earlier
  reading, taken straight after the page's cold first compile, stayed dark; it did not
  reproduce.)
- Stored Dark → stays dark after a reload under a light OS, and through OS flips.
- The public form in dark, never swept before: builder 31, public form 27 and focus mode 11
  text elements — **0 below AA**, self-tested ruler.
- And the last sprint's owed check: the Select list opens on #333333, the same tier as its
  trigger, with its highlight visible against it (1.16:1).

**Guards.** `lib/theme.test.ts` runs the boot script against stubbed globals — a first visit
follows the OS, an explicit choice beats it, and the accent is picked for the RESOLVED
theme (the first-visit and accent cases were watched failing against the old default) —
and drives `watchSystemTheme`: it re-resolves when nothing was chosen, leaves an explicit
choice alone, and unsubscribes the same listener. `components/forms/turnstile.test.ts`: no
call site pins the captcha, and the widget itself defaults to the page theme — both watched
failing first.

unseen. The only instances in the app were the client portal's nav:

**What shipped.** Tailwind v4 generates a colour utility only for a `--color-*` declared inside
`@theme`. Anything else generates no CSS and raises no error. The runtime audit found 17 uses of
10 such classes. Each was replaced with what its site meant, and each was measured before and
after, in both themes, with real pointer and drag input (`scripts/verify/verify-colour-fixes.mjs`).
"Before" is exact: a dead class has no CSS, so removing its replacement from the live element
reproduces it.

**Found on the way, in the Content editor.** A piece with changes requested printed the client's

lines below. The hint now steps aside while a sign-off is out, because the approval block owns that

**A correction to this log.** The screen-recording entry above said the `berry-*` names "are declared
but have no values". That was wrong. The berry UTILITIES are remapped to the ink ramp on purpose
(globals.css), so `border-berry-500` drew ink-900 as declared, while `var(--color-berry-500)` read

**Guard.** `app/design-system.test.ts` → "a colour class names a colour the theme declares". Every

## Content: three places, and everything opens as what it is — 2026-09-14

The user shared Eden as a reference: "take inspiration, don't copy; no AI, no chat, no tables; the
pipeline is right; we already have Inbox and Library, so think carefully about how everything fits."

### What was wrong, measured before designing
- **The Inbox held two things with opposite lifecycles.** The pile you are meant to empty sat above a
  permanent "Saved" shelf of references, so the Inbox could never look empty once you had kept
  anything. And "that reel I saved in June" is not something anyone looks for in an inbox.
- **The Library held only published work.** In the fixture that was one row on an empty page.
- **A saved link could not take you to the link.** Its URL was grey text inside the button that
  opened the editor. Opening it showed the production editor for someone else's reel: breadcrumb
  `Content / Idea / …`, Stage "Idea — Decide if it is worth making", Format, Channel, Shoot, Publish,
  and "Attach a project to send this for client sign-off". There was no `href` anywhere on the page.
  The stage crumb even offered to "move" it, which could never put it on the board (`onlyPieces`).
- **Links were addresses.** A bare link was named `youtube.com/watch`, and stayed that way.
- **No search, no filter**, and no way to discard a capture you did not want.

### The reference, and what was deliberately not taken
Eden's Library: a search box first, then a narrowing filter, then a grid of things that look like
what they are. Readwise Reader: an inbox where each thing is decided once. Raindrop: cards drawn
from the page's own image. Notion's bookmark block: favicon, site, title, image. **Not taken:**
Eden's Custom AI, chat, tables, the Discover outlier feed (it needs third-party data and is not
this product's job), boards, and a grid/list toggle (one good layout beats two).

### What shipped
**Three places, one job each** (`lib/content.ts` carries the model in words):
- **Inbox, what landed.** Only the pile. Each capture shows its page's favicon, title and site, and
  is decided once: **Add to pipeline** · **Save to library** · **Move to Trash**, with Undo, using
  the Documents rule for reversible deletes.
- **Pipeline, what you're making.** Unchanged.
- **Library, what you keep.** Saved references and published work together. Search, an
  All · Saved · Published filter with counts (in the URL as `?kind=`), month sections, and a card
  grid on the DS `CardGrid`'s medium track, rendered 48 at a time behind "Show more".

**Everything opens as what it is** (one editor, split by bucket):
- **A saved thing:** crumb `Content / Library / …`, the source as a real link card (new tab), Link,
  Made by, *Why you kept it* (the long-unused `note`), what it has sparked, and *Make something from
  this*. No stage, format, dates or sign-off.
- **A capture:** crumb `Content / Inbox / …`, its source card and note, and the same three decisions
  as the list. Deciding turns the page into the view that fits.
- **A published piece** gains **Live link**, shown as the live post's card. The Library draws a
  published card from it too.

**A link is named by its page.** The page's own title replaces our placeholder (`isAutoTitle`) and
never a name someone typed. That covers every row and card; it is written through the normal save
when a capture is opened; and it rides along when a capture is sorted straight from the list, where
`sortInboxItem` re-checks against the stored row. Without that last part, a link sorted without
opening would have reached the board as "youtube.com/watch".

### Found on the way, fixed in this sprint's area
- **The editor dropped the last edit if you closed within 600ms.** The debounced save's cleanup
  cancelled its timer on unmount, so typing a title and pressing Esc lost it. The pending save now
  runs as the page closes.
- **`PageView` put focus on the first toolbar control in three of its four modes**, so the "View
  mode" tooltip popped on every open. That rule was already fixed for in-pane mode, and is now one
  shared `focusPage` for every mode.
- **One Library link, one Back step.** "N more in Library" set view and filter as two history
  entries. The new `writeModes` pushes once (tested).
- **The doc editor's `BookmarkCard` became the DS `LinkCard`**, now that Content is its second reader.
  It's presentational: features bring the metadata. `use-link-meta` moved to `lib/`, gaining
  `primeLinkMeta` (harnesses have no session to unfurl with) and `peekLinkMeta`. The two
  cut/spark lists became one `RelatedList`.
- The Content harness had no `<Toaster/>`, so "moved to Trash" and its Undo were invisible there.

### The design review, before calling it done
The first screenshots had three problems, each fixed and re-shot:
- The search box sat on the header's rule. Fixed with `page-rhythm`, the house gutter.
- Cards at the small track had 118px thumbnails and truncated "instagram.…". Moved to the medium track.
- A thought kept without a link was a grey slab with a lightbulb. It now shows its note.

The theme guard also caught a `text-ink-400` glyph (a tint, not a text step).

### Verified — real input, both themes, and a phone
`scripts/verify/verify-content-places.mjs`: **67/67** checks across light, dark and 390×844 touch, with
no console errors. Among them: the inbox holds only the pile, with titles from the page; Save,
Trash and Undo put the row back in place; a capture opens with an Inbox crumb, an adopted title, a
real new-tab source and no stage; *Add to pipeline* turns it into the production editor and the
piece reaches the board under the name the inbox showed; months newest first (1 · 3 · 2); filter
counts 6 · 4 · 2 and the filters live in the URL; search needs every word and reaches a title only
the fetched page knows ("selected work"); spark opens a piece "Sparked by" the saved one; the saved
view has no stage or dates, a ≥400px link field and a crumb that goes home; a published piece
shows its live post; a card opens from the keyboard; on a phone the grid is one column and the
touch actions are visible. Documents' bookmark cards were re-checked after the move: identical
href, target, rel, margin and fallbacks.

`writeModes`) · eslint clean on every touched file, apart from the pre-existing
`block-editor.tsx:1289` refs error. **Deployed `21e25936`** (`/login` 200, `/content` 307 when signed
out) · worker 3,019 KiB gzipped: the whole sprint cost 8 KiB, and 53 KiB of headroom remains.

## Content: a screenshot is a capture — 2026-09-14

**What shipped.** The inbox takes pictures. The user's original ask named them first ("a screenshot,
a YouTube link, a random thought"), and until now the box took text and links only.
- **Three ways in, one flow.** Paste an image into the capture box (a clipboard screenshot is the
  fastest capture there is), drop files anywhere on the inbox (the whole place is the target and the
  box says "Drop to capture"), or pick through *Add an image*. One capture per image.
- **Named sensibly** (`imageCaptureTitle`): what you typed wins, with a link in it becoming the
  source. Otherwise the file's own name ("nike_ad-frame_03.png" → "nike ad frame 03"). A name that
  says nothing ("image.png", "IMG_1234", a string of digits) becomes "Image from 14 Sep, 18:32", and
  the OS's screenshot names become "Screenshot from …".
- **Shown the instant it lands**, from its own bytes, while the capture row is made, the file goes
  straight to storage, and the row is pointed at it. If the upload fails the row goes too: the
  picture was the capture.
- **Everywhere a capture shows:** a thumbnail on its inbox row (at the row's edge, after the actions,
  so titles still line up), the picture as its Library card, a full-width figure on its page that
  opens full size, and it stays as reference material on a piece made from it.

**The decisions that mattered.**
- **Reuse the attachment spine, don't grow a second one.** A picture is `meta.image =
  attachment:<id>`, the reference covers already use. `readContent` accepts nothing else, so a
  data-URL can never grow the content JSON. The upload's three steps moved out of
  `useAttachmentUpload` into a plain `uploadAttachment(owner, file)`, because this flow creates its
  owner first. The hook now wraps it. `setContentImage` checks that the attachment belongs to that
  page.
- **One request for every picture on screen.** `useAttachmentUrl` signed one URL per call, so a
  Library page was up to 48 round trips to Seoul. A new `createBatcher` (tested: dedupe, chunking,
  partial and failed answers) sends every id asked for in the same moment to a new
  `signAttachments`: one RLS query and one `createSignedUrls`. Documents' covers and image blocks go
  through the same hook, so they batch too, with no change at their call sites.
- **An open page adopts a picture that lands after it loaded.** The editor writes the whole pipeline
  back on every save, so a page opened mid-upload would otherwise have erased the reference it was
  opened to look at.

**Verified** (`scripts/verify/verify-content-places.mjs`, now given two real PNG files): **79/79** in
light, dark and at phone width, no console errors. Covered: a stored screenshot shows its thumbnail;
a PNG set on the real file-chooser input lands first as "nike ad frame 03" with its picture; a PNG

User, on the screenshots: *"I don't want dots — use that application's logo, YouTube, Twitter, X,

**What was actually on screen.** The "dots" were favicons: whatever square icon a site serves, drawn

practice many real cards had no picture either.

### What shipped
- **Platform marks.** 16 brand glyphs joined the ONE icon family (Phosphor's own `YoutubeLogo`,
  `XLogo`, `InstagramLogo`, `TiktokLogo`, `LinkedinLogo`, Threads, Facebook, Pinterest, Behance,

  equals of every other icon rather than as someone else's colours.

  else a globe. It had been written out three times (inbox row, library card, bookmark card), each
  with its own fallback. `ChannelMark` draws a piece's channel ("YouTube", "Instagram Reels") on board
  cards and published Library cards. A saved Instagram link with no picture shows the camera mark where
  the picture would be.

  `youtube.com.evil.example` is nothing) and which a channel names ("X" is X, "Xero" is not).
- **Real pictures.**

    rather than failing, is recognised and skipped.
  - A card now takes the first picture that works: yours, then the platform's, then the page's
    og:image (`usePicture`).
  - Inbox link rows show theirs too.
- **The unfurl route asks the platforms first.** YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo, Spotify and X publish oEmbed:
  title, author and thumbnail as JSON from a fixed endpoint. The link travels only as a query

  through the same route and the same `LinkCard`.

### Checked against the real services, not guesses about them

  what the mapper expects.
- `publish.twitter.com` now answers **301 → publish.x.com**; since a redirect is a miss, the endpoint

  India. The worker runs in Singapore; a redirect falls back to the page, so nothing breaks either way.

## Content: a link's preview is remembered on the row — 2026-09-14

**The problem.** Once the Library drew its cards from link metadata, every visit paid for it again.
Each card asked `/api/unfurl` once per session: up to 48 requests to the worker on a reload, each one
an outbound fetch to someone else's site or oEmbed endpoint. A platform that rate-limited or refused
a scraper TODAY blanked a card it had described perfectly YESTERDAY. The server's own cache lives per
isolate for an hour, which on Workers is close to nothing.

**What shipped.**
- **`meta.preview`**, stored in the page's content JSON (no migration): the link's title, image, site,
  author and favicon, keyed to the URL it describes and dated.
- **`useLinkPreview`**, used by inbox rows, Library cards, and the saved, capture and live-link cards in
  the editor: a FRESH preview for this exact link is drawn with no request at all. Otherwise it is
  fetched, then remembered on the row once per session (`rememberLinkPreview`).
- **A remembered picture that stops loading** is taken as expiry, because TikTok's and Instagram's
  image addresses are signed for days. The card sets the preview aside and asks again. Only cards
  actually on screen do this, since their images load lazily.
- **Freshness is 30 days** (`PREVIEW_FRESH_DAYS`). Editing the link makes the old preview inapplicable.
- **An open page adopts a preview remembered while it was open**, like a picture, or its next save would
  forget it.

**The decisions that mattered.**
- **A cache write is not a user action.** It neither reverts nor toasts. The card already shows the
  preview, so a failed write changes nothing on screen and the next visit simply asks again.
- **The browser is not trusted with the shape.** `readPreview` guards the reader (every field capped,
  https-only image and favicon, a real date, something to show). The server action re-reads through it
  and refuses a preview for any URL the row does not actually have (its source or live link).

## Databases appear the moment you ask for one — 2026-09-14 (T1 + T2)

First two tasks of `DATABASE_EXPERIENCE_PLAN.md` (the "make databases feel like Notion" brief).
Started in one session, which hit its usage limit mid-verification; finished and verified in
the next.

**What was wrong, from the user's screenshots.**
- **Database — Full page** opened a page under a placeholder id, and its body asked the server
  about that id: the page printed Postgres's `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "tmp-…"` —
  and the error stayed on screen after the real id arrived, because nothing reset it.
- **An inline database** (`/table`, `/board`…) sat on "Creating database…" for a full round
  trip before anything appeared.

**What shipped.**
- **The browser mints the database's final ids** (`mintUuid`, `lib/temp-id.ts`; a
  `getRandomValues` fallback where `randomUUID` is missing, plain http on a LAN address). The
  server writes under exactly those ids, so nothing is ever renamed — a block's `colId`, a
  queued edit and a React key are right from the first frame.
- **`newDatabase` (`lib/db-store.ts`)** seeds a live store — the default schema in the chosen
  layout plus one empty row — and registers it by collection and by page. `persist(pageId)`
  saves it; `abandon` drops it. Every write made before the database exists (a renamed
  column, an added row) **waits for the outcome** and is sent against the same ids, or dropped
  with the database if creation fails. A database that failed leaves the registry and tells
  the views showing it, so they go back to the server instead of taking edits that can never
  be saved.
- **`createDatabase` (`lib/actions/collections.ts`)** checks every id is a uuid before asking
  anything, inserts the collection, then its first row (same `row_order` key the screen used),
  and deletes the collection again if the row cannot be written.
- **`loadPlan`**: a database view never fetches with a placeholder id — it shows what the
  device holds, waits, or fetches a real id. A load failure is stored with the id it was
  about, so it cannot outlive it.
- **Documents**: a new database page opens with its table on the first frame; the page is
  saved, its placeholder links to the real id, then the database is saved under it. "Turn
  into page" shows the live database at once and waits for a just-inserted database to reach
  the server before attaching it.

**Found on the way, fixed in this sprint's area.**
- **A failed save printed the server's words as the whole block** — measured:
  `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "collections_pkey"` — and the document
  saved it. `lib/database-failure.ts` now decides what a database says: a server's message is
  never shown, the one fix a person can make (migration 0013 missing) is named, and every
  other failure offers **Try again**. The block remembers the layout it was made with
  (`Block.dbKind`, kept by `normalize`), so a board is retried as a board.
- The database states were inline-styled billboards (`padding: 24px 8px`). They are now one
  quiet line in the document's flow (`DbLine`, `DbFailureLine` — the DS `EmptyLine`
  geometry), including the linked-view picker's.
- **The paste-as menu read `blocksRef` during render** (`pasteAsChoices`) — the previous
  commit's blocks. It reads the block being rendered now. That was the React Compiler's
  "Cannot access refs during render" in `block-editor.tsx`; the calendar view's "memoization
  could not be preserved" is gone too. Both files, and `documents-view.tsx` (dead
  `MenuSwitch`, unused imports), are eslint-clean.

**Verified in the browser** on `/dev-preview/documents`, with the page's server actions
answered by an in-page stub replaying the real response format (captured from a harness
action), and times read by a MutationObserver — a `setTimeout` poll reported ~1s that was the
poll, not the app:
- `/full` → the table 46ms after Enter; the only calls were `addPage`, then `createDatabase`
  carrying the REAL page id; nothing sent with `tmp-…`; a marker on the Status header survived
  the id swap (no remount, no flash).
- `/table` on a 2s network → the table at 61ms; a row added at 57ms reached the server at
  2,231ms, just after creation answered.
- `/board` failing → board at 66ms, failure line 28ms after the answer, no server text, `dbKind`
  saved; **Try again** → a new board at 31ms under a new collection id.
- Full page, `addPage` failing → the page shows at 50ms, then leaves with "Could not create
  the database."; `createDatabase` never sent. Full page, `createDatabase` failing → "Could
  not save the new database.", then the view loads the real page's database from the server.
- Both themes; the failure line is ink-500 with an ink-800 title on the page ground.

**Guards.** `lib/db-store.test.ts` (writes held until creation; nothing written if it fails;
the registry follows the page id; `newDatabase` persists exactly what it rendered; a thrown
failure is reported in true words), `lib/actions/create-database.test.ts` (uuid check before
any query; insert order; compensating delete), `lib/temp-id.test.ts` (`mintUuid` shape, with
and without `randomUUID`), `lib/database-failure.test.ts`, `lib/blocks.test.ts` (`dbKind`
survives a reload; unknown layouts dropped) — each watched failing first. The silent-failure
guard caught three new branches that spoke through names it did not know; they use its verbs.

## The breadcrumb, rebuilt as navigation — 2026-09-14 (T3)

The user's brief, §1: *"our current breadcrumbs look cheap because of the underline
treatment … only show information that is relevant to the current page … a native
navigation system, not a collection of links."* Their screenshots showed the Draft crumb
underlined with a caret, and its menu opening Recent, Favorites and five sections.

**What was wrong, measured.**
- Every crumb was TWO controls: a link that underlined on hover, and a caret button beside
  it that faded in. The caret's invisible 20px slot was the wide, uneven gap before every
  "/" — the cheapness in the screenshot — and made each crumb two tab stops.
- Menus led with Recent and Favorites; the open page's crumb swapped its siblings for six
  actions that duplicated the header's ⋯; the trail opened on the workspace, which every
  document shares.
- **Found with a real pointer:** moving the mouse across the trail while writing took the
  caret out of the document — focus went into the hover-opened menu, then onto the crumb.

**What shipped.**
- **One crumb, one control** (`components/ds/ui/breadcrumbs.tsx`): a 24px pill, 6px inset,
  ink-500 → ink-800 under a soft wash that holds while its menu is open; the open page is
  ink-900 at regular weight. `crumbRole` decides what a press does — a *place* goes there
  (menu on hover, ↓, Space, right-click), the open page or a picker opens its menu — and a
  `caret` is drawn only for a picker (Content's stage crumb). A finger gets Button's 44px
  hit area.
- **Relevant information only** (`lib/doc-nav.ts`, `doc-breadcrumbs.tsx`): the trail starts
  where the page lives (`Learning sources / Motion / 🎬 After Effects`); every menu lists
  what is beside the crumb under a heading (`siblingsHeading`: "Pages in Motion", "Folders
  in Learning sources") plus the create rows; no Recent, no Favorites, no crumb actions; an
  icon only where the page has its own. `branchExtras` and the trail's workspace switcher
  are gone.
- **A hovered menu keeps focus where it was**: `DropdownMenuContent keepFocus` declines
  Radix's focus-on-open and focus-return (a private-typed Radix prop, set in one place and
  guarded against a Radix upgrade), and the filter box no longer grabs focus on hover.
- **Touch by pointer, not width** (`useCoarsePointer`, `lib/use-narrow.ts`): any coarse
  pointer gets the drill-down sheets; a narrow screen still collapses to `… / Current`.

**Verified with real input** — `scripts/verify/verify-breadcrumbs.mjs` (headless Chrome,
`:hover` needs a real pointer), light and dark, 1440px and a 375px phone:
- at rest: three pills, 24px, `text-decoration: none`, weight 400; 3 tab stops (was 6)
- hover: the wash starts at once; the menu opens after its 120ms delay with the wash held
  (`data-state=open`); moving along the trail switches menus immediately; leaving closes it
- menus: "Folders in Learning sources" → Motion ✓ › · UX › · New doc · New database · New
  folder; the open page → "Pages in Motion" → After Effects ✓ › · Premiere · Blender · New doc
- **writing, then crossing the trail: focus stayed in the editor** while the menu was open
  and after it closed (it was in the menu, then on the crumb, before the fix)
- keyboard: ↓ opens with focus in the menu; Esc closes and returns focus to the crumb;
  Enter goes there. A click on a place navigates; a click on the open page opens its list
- phone: `··· / 🎬 After Effects`; a tap opens the "Pages in Motion" sheet
- Content's own `verify-page-in-pane.mjs` still passes: the stage crumb (now with its
  caret) moves the piece from Draft to Shoot.

**Guards.** `components/ds/ui/breadcrumbs.test.ts` (role rule, collapse rule, no underline,
wash held open, no caret button, 44px on touch), `components/ds/ui/dropdown-menu.test.ts`
(`keepFocus`, and the Radix pass-through it depends on), `lib/doc-nav.test.ts` (no
workspace in the trail, headings) — watched failing first (20 of them).

## An inline database uses the page's width — 2026-09-15 (T5)

The brief's §3 and §24 (*"use the available page width intelligently … it should feel like a
native block inside the page"*). Built by the previous transcript just before it hit its session
limit; verified, reviewed and written up in this one.

**What was wrong, from the user's screenshot.** An inline board clipped at the text column. Its
Done column was cut off, with a scrollbar inside the column, and a table with a few columns did
the same.

**The reference.** Notion keeps an inline database's title and view bar on the text column. Its
table or board runs out to both edges of the page and scrolls sideways there, with the first
column still on the text, and the writing below carries on in the column.

**What shipped.**
- **`lib/bleed.ts`.** `bleedInsets` measures how far a layout may reach on each side: from
  where it would sit (its parent's box) to the page's content box, which stops at the
  scrollbar rather than under it. Whole pixels, rounded down so it never passes an edge or
  jitters. The `bleed` callback ref writes `--bleed-start` / `--bleed-end` and re-measures
  whenever the page or the column resizes (a ResizeObserver on both). It is a callback ref
  because a table swapped for a board is a new element.
- **`bleed-x`** (`app/ds-theme.css`): negative inline margins, matching padding and
  `scroll-padding-inline-start`, so scrolling back home puts the first column on the text.
- **Both sides opt in.** The Docs scroll region is `data-bleed-root`; the table and board
  scrollers take `bleed-x` + `ref={bleed}`. The name and view bar stay in the column. Gallery,
  list and calendar fit the column, as Notion's do.
- **No root means no bleed.** A row page opens in a portal: the peeks under `body`, a full
  page in the shell's `[data-view-shell]`, both outside the doc's scroll region. So a database
  inside a row page, or in the client portal, stays in its column.
- Harness: "Launch plan", a doc with two inline views of one database, the second nested
  under a list item.

**Verified** with `scripts/verify/verify-bleed.mjs`, system Chrome over CDP (the in-app pane is
narrower than the breakpoint where a text column is narrower than its page):

| Width | Page | Text | Scroller | Insets (nested) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1440 | 239→1425 | 482→1182 | 239→1425 | 243 / 243 (265 / 243) |

## A database view decides how its pages open — 2026-09-15 (T6)

The brief's §8 (*"Board/Timeline/List → Side peek; Feed/Calendar → Center peek; configurable per
view"*) and Notion's "Open pages in".

**What was wrong.**
- **One preference for every row.** One preference opened every database row in the app,
  whatever the view. A gallery's items side-peeked like a table's rows, and "Set as default"
  in one database changed every database.
- **A board card could not be opened at all.** It carried drag listeners and no click handler,
  so the only way into a card's page was another layout.
- **Escape took three presses to leave a peek, found while verifying.** After using the peek's
  mode menu, the first press closed the menu. The second closed the icon button's tooltip,
  which had opened on the focus Radix hands back. Only the third closed the page. The same
  happens wherever an icon button opens a Radix menu or dialog, since every `IconButton`
  carries a tooltip.

**The reference.** Notion's view settings → Layout → "Open pages in": Side peek, Center peek or
Full page, each with a line of explanation. The default follows the layout, and the peek's own
switcher changes the view's setting.

**What shipped.**
- **`ViewDef.openIn` and `openPagesIn(view)`** (`lib/collections.ts`). Tables, boards, lists and
  timelines open pages on the side, because you work through them and the view stays live
  beside the page. Galleries, calendars, feeds and charts open them centred, because you look
  at one item at a time. It lives in the view's JSON, so no migration, and `normalizeViews`
  drops a stored value it does not know.
- **`PageView` accepts a preference the caller owns:** `preferredMode`, `onSetDefault`,
  `defaultScope`. `wantedMode` resolves the order before the viewport's veto:
  1. a forced mode;
  2. this opening's pick;
  3. the owner's preference;
  4. the per-type preference.

  With an owner, the mode menu offers one default: "Set as default for this view".
- **View settings → Layout → Open pages in.** Each mode has its glyph, name and a one-line hint.
  They come from the DS's `PAGE_VIEW_MODE_ICON` / `PAGE_VIEW_MODE_HINT`, now exported rather
  than copied.
- **Board cards open.**
  - A click opens the page; a drag past 4px moves the card (the tasks board's sensors).
  - Enter on a card's title opens it too.
  - The card is dnd-kit's keyboard activator, so Space or Enter on the card itself still
    picks it up.
- **`focusOpensTooltip`** (`components/ds/ui/tooltip.tsx`). A tooltip opens when focus arrives
  from another control, not when a menu, dialog or listbox hands focus back.

**Verified with trusted input** using `scripts/verify/verify-open-pages-in.mjs`: system Chrome
over CDP at 1440×900, because the in-app pane is narrower than the 1100px a side peek needs.
- A table row opens in side peek; Escape closes it.
- **Board card:** a click opens it in side peek (before: nothing happened).
- **Drag:** a real drag moved "Write launch post" from Not started to Done and opened nothing.
- **Keyboard:** Enter on a card's title opens its side peek (before: it picked the card up).
- **View setting:** Layout shows "Open pages in · Side peek" with three options and their hints.
  After picking Center peek, the next card opens centred.
- **Peek menu:** Side peek, Center peek, Full page and "Set as default for this view", with no
  per-type or global default.
- **Escape:** the first press after the menu closes it, focus stays on "View mode" and no
  tooltip opens; the second closes the page (before: three presses).
- Light and dark screenshots of the options panel.
- **In the in-app browser:**
  - the peek menu saved Full page to the view, and the next row opened full page;
  - a newly added gallery view defaulted to center peek.

**Guards.** Each of these was watched failing first:
- `lib/collections.test.ts`: the default for each layout, the view's own choice winning, every
  layout having a default, unknown stored values.
- `lib/page-view-mode.test.ts`: whose choice opens a page, and that the viewport still vetoes.
- `components/ds/ui/tooltip-focus.test.ts`: focus arriving versus focus handed back.

## New makes a row you can use at once — 2026-09-15 (T7)

The brief's §15–16 (*"New button: instant, default title/properties, opens per view mode"*).

**What was wrong.**
- **New made a row and did nothing else.** No page opened, nothing took the caret, and no
  values were applied: the handler was `addRow(groupProp ? {} : {})`.
- **A new row started in "No Status"** on every board. In a filtered view it could vanish from
  the view that made it.
- **Two primary buttons on one page.** Every inline database drew a filled New, so a doc with
  two databases showed two, against CLAUDE.md's one filled button per view.
- **Found in the code on the way: rows were keyed by id.** A new row's id changes when the
  server answers, so React would remount it while someone typed its name. And once defaults
  existed, a "No Status" column's New would have started its card in the default status.

**The reference.** In Notion, New creates the page and opens it the way the view opens pages,
name first. A new page takes its status's default and the values the view filters on. "+ New"
at a table's foot types in place, and a board column's New lands in that column.

**What shipped.**
- **`newRowValues(props, view, preset)`** (`lib/db-engine.ts`) is the one rule for a new row.
  - It starts in its status's first option.
  - It takes what an AND of exact filter rules decides: `is` on a select or status, `contains`
    on a multi-select, `is true` on a checkbox. An OR, a negation or a range is left alone.
  - The caller's own value, a column or a day, goes on top.
  - Every New in a view goes through it, and so does a new database's first row, which
    `createDatabase` now writes to the server with those values.
- **Toolbar, gallery, list, feed, board column and calendar-day New** create the row and open
  it per the view's "Open pages in" (T6), with the name focused (`RowPeek` `fresh`). **The
  table's foot** types in place: the caret lands in the new row's Name cell.
- **`store.currentId` and `store.stableKey`** (`lib/db-store.ts`). An open page follows a new row
  from its placeholder to the server's id, and the row keeps its React key through the swap.
- **"No Status" is a value.** A row made in that column or group stays there.
- **An inline database's New is secondary**; a database page's stays primary.

**Verified with trusted input** using `scripts/verify/verify-db-new.mjs` (system Chrome,
1440×900):
- An inline New is secondary; a database page's New is primary.
- **Toolbar New:** it opens a side peek with the caret in Name. Typing "Brief the team" named
  the row, rows went from 4 to 5, and the new row reads Not started.
- **The table's foot New:** no page opens, the caret lands in the new row's Name cell, and
  typing names it.
- **Board:** "No Status" New opens a side peek with the caret in Name, and the card stays in No
  Status (0 → 1). "Not started" New lands there (3 → 4).

**Guards.** Each of these was watched failing first:
- `lib/db-engine.test.ts`: the status default, filter values that keep the row in view, what a
  filter cannot decide, the caller's value winning, dangling rules.
- `lib/db-store.test.ts`: `currentId`, `stableKey`, a new database's first row.
- `lib/actions/create-database.test.ts`: the first row's values reach the server.

## The board, Notion's — 2026-09-15 (board rebuild + T8)

The user, with six Notion screenshots (a coloured board, its Group settings panel, a card's
hover): *"board view same to same notion style, our looks cheap … cards draggable like content
and user can enter page"*. It is also the plan's T8 (each layout's own settings), which the
previous transcript had started test-first and left with its tests failing when it hit its
session limit.

**What was wrong, from the user's screenshot of ours.**
- **Grey cards in grey wells.** A 300px house well held flat grey cards: no edge, no lift, and
  no colour anywhere except the chips.
- **The column header was plain text.** "Not started" and "No Status" were plain text while
  "In progress" was a chip, so one header row used two styles.
- **Every column repeated the card's status.** Each card carried the status chip its column
  already named.
- **A drag could only change column,** never position. The drop landed at an unmarked point,
  there was no lifted card, and nothing showed where it would go.
- **A grey scrollbar under every board,** even one that fit the page but for its own padding.
- **An empty "No Status" column on every status board,** forever.
- **Hiding a column, recolouring an option and moving a column were not possible.**
- **Found on the way:**
  - T8's tests referenced functions that did not exist, so `tsc` failed on the shared tree.
  - Board drags announced raw ids to screen readers ("dropped over droppable area __none__").

**The reference.** A Notion board in the user's screenshots:
- **Columns.** 260px wide. Each is washed in its option's colour ("Color columns"), with a
  chip header and a count; ⋯ and + appear on hover.
- **Cards.** White with a hairline and a soft shadow. The page glyph shows when the page has a
  body; the name is 14px medium, and each visible property with a value sits on its own line.
- **Adding.** A quiet "+ New page" line in the column's colour.
- **Settings.** The Group page has Group by, Hide empty groups, Color columns, then every group
  with a drag handle and an eye.
- **Dragging.** A card drops where you point.

**What shipped.**
- **`components/documents/database-board.tsx`** is the board. It draws; it does not decide.
  - **Columns** have Notion's anatomy on `BOARD_COLUMN.database` (DS): 260px, the group's wash
    as the ground, a 40px header with the option chip, a count, and ⋯ + on hover.
  - **Cards** are raised with a hairline. The page glyph shows when `hasBody`, then the name,
    then every visible property with a value except the one the board is grouped by.
  - **"+ New page"** is in the column's text colour. It opens a card-shaped name field at the
    foot; the header's + opens one at the top. Enter makes the page and leaves the field open
    for the next; Escape puts it away.
  - **The card's ⋯** offers Open, Move to (every column) and Delete. It is the keyboard's way
    to move a card.
  - **The column's ⋯** offers Rename, Color (the nine) and Hide group.
  - **Hidden groups** wait in a last column, each a click from coming back.
- **The drag follows the content board's rules.**
  - The held card is flat, shadowed and exactly the column's card width.
  - Its origin dims in place.
  - A dashed slot the card's own height opens where it will land.
  - The column comes from `columnUnderPointer`, moved to `lib/board-drag.ts` so both boards
    share one rule.
  - The place comes from the pointer, measured against each card's resting middle taken when
    the drag began, so the slot does not chase the cards it pushes down.
  - In a sorted view the sort decides the place, and the slot says so.
  - A drop writes the column and the place as **one** undoable step (`RowPatch.order`).
  - A mouse needs 4px to start a drag. A finger holds for 220ms, so a swipe still scrolls.
  - Screen readers hear names ("Twitter redesign dropped in Done").
- **`lib/board.ts`** holds the rules, pure and tested:
  - `boardGroupProp` picks the grouping property.
  - `boardColumns` and `boardGroupList` give the columns and their order.
  - `moveToGroup` sets a carried card's new value. A multi-select swaps only the value it left.
  - `groupPreset` gives a new card its column's value.
  - `landingFromPointer` and `sortedLanding` find the place.
  - `reorderKeys` writes one order key, or re-keys the column when neighbours share a key or
    have none.
- **Colour.** `--pal-*-wash` is the chip fill at 55% as a transparent layer. It tints the page
  in either theme, and the chip inside still reads as the stronger mark. `palette().wash` exposes it.
- **Chips come in Notion's two shapes** (`components/documents/option-chip.tsx`): a status is a
  pill with a dot, a select is a tag. This applies everywhere: cells, cards, headers, galleries,
  lists, table groups.
- **View settings, Notion's panel** (290px, back · title · close):
  - **Board → Group page:** Group by ›, Hide empty groups, Color columns, then Groups with Hide
    all/Show all. Every column can be dragged (keyboard too: Space, arrows, Space) and hidden
    with its eye (`board-groups-list.tsx`, `ViewDef.groupOrder` / `hiddenGroups`).
  - **Layout page (T8)** shows only the settings of the layout on screen (`layoutOptions`):
    - table: Show vertical lines; Hide empty groups when grouped;
    - board: Group by, Color columns, Hide empty groups;
    - gallery: Card size (small, medium, large → `galleryCardMin` 180/220/300);
    - calendar: Show calendar by (it replaced a native select in the month bar) and Show
      weekends (`weekdayLabels` + `withoutWeekends`). The header follows `WEEK_STARTS_ON`
      instead of a hard-coded Mon…Sun.
- **`scrollbar-quiet`** (DS utility): a sideways scroller's bar shows while the pointer is
  over it. The board and the table use it.
- Harness: the Projects tracker has seven pages across all three statuses. Two have a body,
  one sits in two Tags columns, one has a title that wraps. The inline demo database gained a
