## Pages inside pages — 2026-09-15

The user, with the board screenshots: *"all database page is nested … user can create nested
into nested infinite page … all database is just bunch of pages like notion … user can enter
page"*.

**What was wrong.**
- **A card opened a property sheet, not a page.** The name sat small in the peek's header,
  repeated as a "Name" property; a number sat 400px from its label, right-aligned.
- **A page could not hold a page.** There was no Page block, so nesting existed only in the
  Documents sidebar, and never for a database row.
- **A database inside a row's page opened a second peek on top of the first,** and a third
  level would open a third.
- **Found while verifying — a data-loss bug in Documents, older than this sprint:**
  - Switching pages cancelled the pending autosave, so whatever was typed in the last 600ms
    before opening another page was dropped.
  - The row peek had the same bug on close, at 500ms.
  - `/page` opens the page it makes straight away, so the Page block it had just added to the
    parent was lost every time, measured in both hosts.
- **Found while verifying:** Escape in a board column's name field closed the whole peek, and
  the half-typed name with it.

**The reference.** Notion:
- **A database row is a page.** Its page opens with the page's large name, its properties,
  then its body.
- **A page holds pages.** `/page` makes one and takes you straight in, with the caret in its
  name. The line left behind is the page's icon and name, underlined, and it renames with the
  page.
- **Going deeper.** Opening a page from inside a peeked page steps deeper in the same peek,
  with a trail and back/forward. A database on any page has rows that are pages again.

**What shipped.**
- **The Page block** (`type: 'page'`, `Block.pageId`, "Page" second in the slash menu with its
  own drawn preview).
  - It stores only the page's id. The line reads the name and icon from the page, so a rename
    anywhere shows everywhere it is linked (`components/documents/page-block.tsx`).
  - A block with no page, a page that failed to save and a page that could not be read each
    say so in place, with Try again. A missing page says "Page not found".
- **`lib/page-store.ts`** holds the pages this device knows, once. It follows the database's
  T1/T2 rule:
  - `newPage({ parentId })` mints the id in the browser, puts the page on screen at once and
    saves it behind (`addPage` now takes `id` and `parentId`, validated as uuids before any
    query).
  - `patchPage` shows an edit at once and saves after a pause, merged. It waits for a page still
    being created, and never saves one that failed.
  - `usePage` reads a page it has not seen; `seedPages` takes a host's listing without clobbering
    an edit still waiting.
  - `onPageCreated` lets Documents list a new page immediately.
- **The peek is a trail** (`PagePeek` in database-view.tsx, `lib/peek-trail.ts`, `PeekContext`).
  - The first page opens as its view says (T6). Every page opened from inside it — a Page block,
    or a card of a database on that page — steps deeper in the same peek.
  - The header shows the trail (database / row / page / …), each crumb a way back, with Back and
    Forward.
  - Another card clicked behind the peek starts a new trail.
- **A row's page is a page.** Its large editable name (Enter goes into the body), then its
  properties one per line with a 16px glyph (numbers left-aligned in a sheet), Created and
  Updated, a hairline, and its body. The body can hold pages and databases. A sub-page shows its
  name and body; an empty one arrives with the caret in its name.
- **Documents hosts pages inside pages.**
  - `/page` in a doc makes a child page in the parent's folder, opens it with the caret in its
    title, and the tree and breadcrumb show it at once.
  - A Page block opens its page, and Documents' autosave waits for a page still being created.
- **The save fixes.**
  - A save still waiting when the page changes, or when Documents unmounts, is written at once.
  - The row peek writes its body when it goes away.
  - The editor opens a page it just made one frame later, so its host commits the new block
    first.
- **`data-owns-escape`** (DS, `PageView`, all four modes): an element that answers Escape itself
  keeps it. Radix's document-level Escape runs before the field's own handler, so the field has
  to declare it. The board's new-card and rename fields use it.
- **`DbStore.createOption`** is the one way to add an option from any cell, wherever the cell is.
- Harness: the Projects tracker's "Portfolio site" row holds "📚 Case studies", which holds
  "TechSpark rebrand", and "Launch plan" holds "✅ Launch checklist".

**Verified with trusted input** using `scripts/verify/verify-nested-pages.mjs` (system Chrome over
CDP at 1440×900, light and dark). Every server action was answered in React's flight format with
`{ ok, id }`, 16 in all:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| "Launch plan" → the "✅ Launch checklist" line (30px, underlined) | Documents opens it; trail Draft / 🚀 Launch plan / ✅ Launch checklist |
| `/page` in "Launch plan" | a child opens, caret in its title; "Vendor list" typed; back on the parent, the line reads **Vendor list** |
| Board → "Portfolio site" | side peek: large name, properties, body with "📚 Case studies" |
| → Case studies → TechSpark rebrand | trail Projects tracker / Portfolio site / Case studies / TechSpark rebrand; Back enabled |
| Back, then the "Portfolio site" crumb | one level up, then the row again |
| `/page` in the row's body | "Page" tops the menu; the new page opens with the caret in "Page name"; "Research notes" renames the trail; back on the row, **the line is there** |
| `/board` on "Research notes", "+ New page", "Interview Ana", Enter | card made; Escape closes only the field (peek still open) |
| Click "Interview Ana" | trail Projects tracker / Portfolio site / Research notes / Interview Ana, in **one** peek |

**Guards.**
- `lib/page-store.test.ts` (11 tests):
  - a page is on screen before the server answers, under its final id, inside its parent;
  - listeners hear at once;
  - a failure is marked in place, and retry keeps the id;
  - edits are merged into one save;
  - a page being made is waited for, and a failed one is never saved;
  - a failed save is reported;
  - a seed does not overwrite a waiting edit;
  - "missing" is told apart from "could not read";
  - the server is never asked about a page still being made.
- `lib/peek-trail.test.ts` (5 tests): deeper, back and forward, the ends of the trail, a new page
  forgetting forward, breadcrumb jumps.
- `lib/blocks.test.ts` and `components/documents/slash-previews.test.ts` cover the Page entry, its
  preview and its caption.
- `app/design-system.test.ts` and `app/theme-bridge.test.ts` caught two slips in the first
  version, both fixed: a placeholder in a tint step, and a 34px row with no token.

Part of the same "board view same to same Notion" request. The bar above every layout was the

  adding another:
  - no track and no thumb;
  - the chosen option is the active wash as a pill, the rest are labels that wash on hover;
  - weight never changes, so choosing never shifts the row;
  - the row scrolls rather than wrapping, and the five-option limit applies only to the well.

  It is still a radio group, so every existing check and screen reader reads it the same.
- **The bar** has two groups:
  - **left:** the tabs and + (add view);
  - **right:** Filter, **Sort**, Search, Open as full page (inline databases), View settings,
    then New.

  Icons are 16px in 28px buttons. The tabs group is `flex-auto`, so a phone gets two lines:
  tabs, then tools.
- **Sort opens the Sort page on its own** (`ViewSettings startAt="sort"`): no Back to a root it
  was never opened from. The button shows pressed while the view is sorted.
- **Search's field owns Escape** (`data-owns-escape`), so clearing a search inside a peek does
  not close the page.

**Verified** with `verify-layout-options.mjs` and `verify-db-board.mjs` (system Chrome, 1440 and
375, light and dark):
- The tabs are Table · Board · Gallery, the chosen one on a 9% ink wash.
- The tools are Add view, Filter, Sort, Search, View settings.
- Sort opens with only Close and Add sort; after a sort is added, the button is pressed.
- The board checks all still pass.
- At 375px the tabs are one line (scrolling past Gallery) and the tools with New are another.

## The Timeline view — 2026-09-15 (T9)

The brief's §6: *"Table, Board, Gallery, List, Timeline, Calendar over one database"*.
`timeline` had been in the data model since the start, with no renderer, no menu entry and no
way to pick it.

**The reference.** Notion's Timeline view:
- each page is a bar from its start date to its end date, with its name on it;
- the axis names the months and marks the days the zoom has room for, and today is a line;
- zoom runs from Week to Year, "Today" comes home, and the pages with no date are one click
  away;
- drag a bar to move the page in time, drag an edge to change one date, click a bar to open the
  page on the side.

**What shipped.**
- **`lib/timeline.ts`** (pure, 13 tests) works in calendar days counted as whole UTC days, never
  `Date`s crossing a timezone.
  - `rowSpan`: a page's start and end; never backwards, one day when there is no end.
  - `timelineRange`: every dated page and today, padded for dragging, starting on a Monday.
  - `barBox`: a bar's position and width.
  - `axisTicks`: months, then days at Week, Mondays at Month, months at Quarter and Year.
  - `dayAt`, `dragSpan`: dragging; an edge never crosses the other.
  - `spanPatch`: writes only the dates that changed, keeping a stored time. A one-date page
    moved stays one date; stretched, it gains an end.
  - `timelineProps`: which dates the view reads.
- **`components/documents/database-timeline.tsx`.**
  - **The bar's controls:** the month under the eye ("September 2026"), "N without dates" (a menu
    that opens them), zoom (Week · Month · Quarter · Year) and Today.
  - **The axis:** month names over the finer marks, weekends washed at Week, a hairline per
    week or month at the wider zooms, and today as an accent line with a dot.
  - **Bars** are raised cards, 28px, with the page glyph and name inside. A bar too narrow for its
    name carries it beside.
  - **Mouse:** move 4px to drag, or click to open (T6 side peek). Each edge resizes when the view
    has an end date. A finger scrolls instead of dragging.
  - **Keyboard:** ← → move a focused bar a day; Shift stretches its end. Its name and dates are
    its accessible name.
  - **New page** is pinned at the text column's left, dated today, and opens with its name ready.
  - **A database with no date** offers "Add a date property", which adds one and reads the
    timeline by it.
  - The scroller bleeds to the page's edges like the board and table (T5), with the quiet
    scrollbar.
- **Settings (T8's Layout page):** "Show timeline by" picks the start date. "End date" is None
  (one-day bars) or another date property. `ViewDef.zoom` joins the normalizer.
- **Everywhere a layout is offered:** "Timeline view" in the slash menu (after Calendar, with a
  drawn preview of bars and a today line) and Timeline in Add view. Both use the layout's one glyph.
- `formatMonth` joins lib/date.ts as the one short month formatter.
- Harness: the Projects tracker gained Start dates and a Timeline view (Start → Due, Month).
  Its dates sit around the real today; two pages have none.

**Verified with trusted input** using `scripts/verify/verify-timeline.mjs` (system Chrome, 1440
and 375, light and dark):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Bar | September 2026 · 2 without dates · Month · Today |
| Axis | Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov; today line drawn |
| "Portfolio site" (17 days at 16px) | 272px wide |
| Drag it 48px right | 9–25 Sep → **12–28 Sep** |
| Drag "Client onboarding kit"'s right edge 32px | 17–20 Sep → **17–22 Sep** |
| → on a focused bar | 22 Aug–3 Sep → 23 Aug–4 Sep |
| Click "Mastership branding" | its page opens |
| Without dates | Twitter redesign · Back your own ideas… |
| Week zoom | the same bar 816px (17 × 48) |
| Scroll home, then Today | the today line is in view, "September 2026" |
| New page | a page opens with the caret in its name, Start 15 Sep 2026 |
| 375px | the page never scrolls sideways; bars drawn |

## A database's values, type by type — 2026-09-15 (T10)

The brief's §13–14 (*"each type with its icon and hover, focus, empty, loading and editing
states"*).

**What was wrong.**
- **A page's property list printed table cells.** An empty select, date or text showed
  nothing at all (a transparent "·"). A row's page and a doc's page looked unrelated below
  their titles; Documents' property list says "Empty".
- **A cell being edited showed no focus.** The inputs are chromeless by design and nothing
  else said which cell had the caret.
- **A checkbox was a hand-drawn span** with a text "✓" and no focus state, against CLAUDE.md's
  one square Radix checkbox.
- **Only a URL had an action.** An email could not be written to, nor a phone called.
- **The link was built by prefixing `https://`**, not through `lib/safe-url` (the app's rule for
  any URL it hands the browser).
- **`database-view.tsx` had grown to ~2,100 lines,** with every cell and its popover inside it.

**The reference.** Notion's properties:
- **A table cell** is quiet until edited, then outlined.
- **A page's property list** washes a value on hover and says "Empty" where there is none.
- **A link, an address and a number** stay text you can edit, with open, write or call beside
  them on hover.

**What shipped.**
- **`components/documents/db-cell.tsx`,** the one cell, for a table column or a page's sheet.
  - **Every type:** its own face, and a focus ring INSIDE its edges while it is being edited
    (the grid never shifts).
  - **A sheet:** each value washes on hover. Empty text, number, URL, email and phone fields
    read "Empty" as a placeholder, and an empty select, status, multi-select, date or computed
    value reads "Empty" as text — Documents' words.
  - **Checkbox** is the DS `Checkbox` (square, Radix, focusable).
  - **URL, email and phone** carry their action beside them, revealed on hover, focus and
    touch. `valueAction` builds the address: a link only through `safeHref` (a bare domain
    gains https), `mailto:` only for something shaped like an address, `tel:` only with
    digits.
  - **Select, status and multi-select** buttons name the property and its values for screen
    readers, and say they open a list.
- **`components/documents/db-pop.tsx`** holds the database's positioned popover (`Pop`, `POP_ROW`),
  moved out so cells and views share it without a cycle. database-view.tsx is ~1,800 lines.
- Harness: the Projects tracker gained a Link (URL) and a Paid (checkbox) property.

**Verified** with `scripts/verify/verify-properties.mjs` (system Chrome, light and dark):
- **Table:** clicking Hours puts the caret in it, with an inset 2px ring in the focus colour.
- **Table:** Portfolio site's link opens `https://zenboard.app/` in a new tab.
- **Table:** Paid is a Radix `checkbox`, checked.
- **"Twitter redesign"'s page** reads Status "Not started", then Tags, Start, Due, Hours and Link
  all "Empty", then Paid's box.
- **Page:** hovering Tags washes it at 5%; clicking Paid checks it.

**Guards.** `components/documents/db-cell.test.ts` (4 tests): a link and a bare domain; never a
`javascript:` URL, including one hidden with a tab; address-shaped emails and digit-bearing
phones only; no action for other types.

## One overlay chrome: every dropdown, popover and panel wears the menus' — 2026-09-15

The user, with two dark screenshots (a database's "5 more…" list beside the app's "New ▾" menu):
*"styling of other apps dropdown and database dropdown and popups styling is not consistent —
database uses old styling with outline, we have to use new styling"*.

**What was wrong, measured** (computed styles, both themes):
- **The app's menus** (DropdownMenu, ContextMenu): a 1px decorative edge (`--border`, #3D3D3D dark /
  #E9E9E7 light), a soft shadow, 12px corners.
- **Everything else that floats drew a 28% ink outline and a heavy lift** (`border-line-strong` +
  `shadow-lift-2`): PopoverContent, HoverCard, Select, Combobox, Filter, the text Toolbar,
  MenuPanel, and the database's own `Pop` (view settings, filters, header menus, option lists).
  A few more painted it inline or with `--line-pop`: the property panels, the focus timer menus,
  the task chips, the event composer and the callout emoji grid.
- **Inside a database's panels:**
  - an autofocused search showed the page field's double focus ring the moment it opened;
  - the view-name and property-name fields were darker wells with their own outline;
  - rows were 28px with 14px glyphs;
  - four choices (a filter's condition, a colour rule's property and condition, a sort's
    property) were the browser's native `<select>`, which draws an OS list inside a Zenboard panel.

**What shipped — the system.**
- **`OVERLAY_CLASS`** (`components/ds/ui/menu.tsx`): `rounded-lg · border-border · bg-popover ·
  shadow-md`, the menus' own chrome.
  - Every DS floating surface takes it: dropdown and context menus with their sub-menus,
    popover, hover card, select, combobox, filter, toolbar, drag ghost.
  - So does every panel outside the DS: the legacy `ui/popover`, doc-properties, focus view,
    task chips, event composer, emoji grid.
  - The rest of the vocabulary: `MENU_PANEL_CLASS` (+ p-1), `MENU_ITEM_CLASS` (32px, px-2, gap-2,
    rounded-md, 14px, 16px glyphs — what a DropdownMenuItem already measured), `MENU_LABEL_CLASS`,
    `MENU_SEPARATOR_CLASS`.
- **`MenuField`:** a text field inside a panel. Its ground is the wash; it has no edge and no
  focus ring, and its caret shows focus. An autofocused search with any edge (even 1px at 45%)
  read as the old outline.
- **`MenuSelect`** (`components/ds/ui/menu-select.tsx`): a choice inside a panel, as a
  DropdownMenu radio list with the menu's trailing check, instead of a native `<select>`.
- **The edge tiers:** the field tier (`line-strong`) stays on fields. An overlay's edge is no
  longer on it.

**What shipped — the database.**
- **`Pop` is the DS Radix Popover now** (same props, every call site unchanged).
  - It wears the chrome and is portalled, flips, hides when its anchor is scrolled away, and
    scrolls inside itself.
  - A MenuSelect opened inside it no longer reads as a click outside.
  - Escape closes the innermost layer: first the menu, then the panel.
  - Focus goes to the panel on open. Radix would have focused the first field AND selected its
    text, which put a view's name one keystroke from gone.
  - Focus returns to the opener on close only if nothing else has taken it. Radix restores a
    tick late, and a condition panel opened from the filter list shut itself when it did (found
    by the check below).
- **Panel contents:** `POP_ROW`, `POP_LABEL` and `POP_SEPARATOR` come from the DS set; glyphs and
  checks are 16px; "Filter by", "Add a group" and "Then group by" are labels.
- **Fields and choices:**
  - the view name, property name, rule value, option search, views search and rename are
    MenuFields;
  - the sort page is a SortableList (drag a level by its handle) of two MenuSelects and a
    remove button;
  - a filter's condition and a colour rule's property and condition are MenuSelects;
  - a rule's option values are OptionChips.
- **The colour rule is a hairline group,** not a fill inside the panel's fill. The linked-database
  picker wears the chrome too.

**Verified** — `scripts/verify/verify-overlays.mjs` (system Chrome, 1440@2x) opens nine kinds of
panel: a view's menu (the reference), the views list, view settings, the sort page, its menu
select, a select cell's options, the filter list, a filter's condition, a column header's menu.
- **Every one's computed edge, fill, corner and shadow equal the DropdownMenu's**, in dark and in
  light.
- **Focused search and name fields:** `box-shadow: none`.
- **The condition** is a MenuSelect ("Is") with **0** native selects.
- **Escape** closes the nested menu select first; the settings panel stays open until the second
  Escape.
- **No console errors.**
- **Re-runs:** layout options, table drag (header menu, Properties keyboard move, remove-sort
  confirm, drop into Done), view bar (rename selects the name; edit view; title toggle), board
  (Group page keyboard reorder), properties, cards and timeline all pass. The timeline script now

- **Guards** (`app/design-system.test.ts`, "one overlay chrome"): no component writes the old
  outline and lift, and every DS floating surface's chrome comes from OVERLAY_CLASS (11 surfaces

## A database's views, and moving rows and columns by hand — 2026-09-15 (T12)

Two requests from the user today, with Notion screenshots, and the plan's T12.
- *"When you right click on a database view … we need only Rename, Display as, Edit view, Copy
  link to view, Open as full view, Show data source title, Duplicate view, Delete view."*
- *"More than 3 views, the 4th is collapsed like this"* ("1 more…", with a list to search,
  drag and open).
- T12: drag rows, properties and views.

**What was wrong.**
- **Views could be added and nothing else.** There was no rename outside the settings panel,
  and no duplicate or delete. Tab order was the order views were made. Ten views were ten tabs
  scrolling off the side.
- **"Copy link to view" copied a link nothing read.** `#view-<id>` opened the first view.
- **A table's rows kept the order they were made in.** Its columns could only move one step at
  a time with ↑/↓ arrows in the settings, and that changed the order for every view.
- **Three drag lists had three copies of the same dnd-kit boilerplate,** and a fourth was coming.
- **"Open as full page" on the view left behind by "Turn into page" made a second page,** moving
  the database again and leaving the first page empty.

**What shipped — the view bar (`components/documents/database-views-bar.tsx`).**
- **Three tabs, then "N more…"** (`visibleTabs`, lib/view-list.ts). The view you are on is never
  folded away; it takes the last tab.
- **"N more…"** opens Notion's list:
  - "Search for a view…";
  - every view with a ⋮⋮ handle (drag, or Space and the arrows) and a ⋯ menu;
  - the current view washed;
  - "New view" (every layout);
  - a search disables the handles, since a filtered list has no order of its own.
- **The view menu**, from a right-click on a tab, a click on the tab you are on (the way in on a
  phone), or ⋯ in the list:
  - Rename, in a popover under the tab or row;
  - Display as: Text and icon · Text only · Icon only, "Only applies to you";
  - Edit view (opens its settings);
  - Copy link to view;
  - Open as full page (inside a document only);
  - Hide or show database title (inside a document only);
  - Duplicate view: a copy right after it, named "… copy", and shown;
  - Delete view, disabled on the last view, with an Undo toast.
- **Display as is the person's, not the database's** (`lib/view-tab-display.ts`). It is kept on
  this device per view, read through `useSyncExternalStore`, with a read-back normaliser.
- **Links to a view work.** `viewFromHash` + `useLocationHash`: a view picked here wins until the
  address changes; a link to one of this database's views shows it and scrolls the database
  into sight. Open as full page writes the link before it opens, so the page opens on that view.
- **The database's title sits inside the surface,** so each view can say whether it shows.
  Toggling writes every view, so the title does not come and go as you switch tabs.
- **Open as full page opens the page a database already has** (`pageForCollection`).

**What shipped — moving things by hand.**
- **Rows** (`components/documents/table-drag.tsx`). A ⋮⋮ in the page margin, shown on row hover:
  - drag it: the row stays in place, washed, while the DS drop line marks the gap nearest the
    pointer and the DS ghost names the row;
  - click it for Open · Move up ⌥↑ · Move down ⌥↓ · Delete (the trash button at the row's end
    is gone);
  - ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ from the keyboard; focus stays on the handle as the row moves.
- **A grouped table moves a row into another group** (sub-groups too), changing its value with
  the board's `moveToGroup`. A folded or empty group takes a drop at its end.
- **A sorted view asks before its sort goes**, as Notion does: "Remove this view's sort?".
  Removing it keeps the pages in the order you saw them, with the moved one where you put it
  (`frozenOrder` + `orderFor`).
- **Columns move by their header.** A press that travels 4px is a drag; one that does not is the
  header's click.
- **Each view has its own column order** (`ViewDef.propOrder`, `viewProps`). The table, board
  cards, gallery, list and settings all follow it. A property added later lands at the end; a
  deleted one drops out.
- **The Properties page is Notion's:** "Shown in table" and "Hidden in table", each a sortable
  list with Hide all / Show all; the name is always shown.
- **One drop is one ⌘Z.** `store.transact` gathers the row keys, the new group value and the
  cleared sort into one step.
- **Few writes.** `orderFor` keeps the longest run of keys that already agree and re-keys only
  the rest, bisected from the middle so 40 rows squeezed into one gap stay ≤ 4 characters.
  `reorderKeys` falls back to it instead of re-keying the whole list. Each changed row is one
  server write.

**The system, not the screen.**
- **`DropLine` and `DragGhost` are in the DS** (`components/ds/ui/drop-indicator.tsx`), and the
  block editor draws its drop line and ghost with them. The line's colour is a named token,
  `--color-drop-line`, because the registry guard rightly keeps `bg-accent` out of DS components.
  The ghost is solid (`w-max`), because a drag overlay is the size of what was grabbed.
- **`SortableList`** (`components/documents/sortable-list.tsx`) is the one re-orderable list:
  handle, keyboard, spoken names. The Groups list now uses it, as do the Properties page and the
  views list.
- **`bleed-x-handles`** gives a table its handle margin even where the page leaves none (a
  peek). A phone keeps its gutter and draws no handles.
- **Auto-scroll** moves only in the direction of the drag, and only near the edge. dnd-kit's
  default fifth of the screen scrolled a table away under a row aimed at its last group.

**Verified** in system Chrome (`scripts/verify/verify-views-bar.mjs`,
`scripts/verify/verify-table-drag.mjs`), light and dark, 1440 and 375:
- **Views:** 3 tabs + "1 more…"; the search focused; "time" leaves Timeline with no handles;
  picking it replaces the last tab; drag Gallery to the top, then Space/↓/Space moves Board.
- **View menu:** right-click on Table lists the six items (seven, with the title item, inside a
  document). Icon only draws the glyph with the name for screen readers, stored for this device.
  Rename selects the name and Enter keeps "Pipeline". Duplicate adds "Pipeline copy" and shows
  it. Delete shows "View deleted." and Undo brings it back. A click on the current tab opens the
  menu. Edit view opens the settings.
- **Links:** Copy link toasts "Link copied."; following the link shows Gallery.
- **Rows:** dragging Twitter redesign to the top shows the line above Portfolio site and a
  ghost reading its name; one ⌘Z restores all 7 places. The handle menu reads Open / Move up ⌥↑ /
  Move down ⌥↓ / Delete; Move down, then ⌥↑, and focus is still on the handle.
- **Columns:** dragging Due to before Status draws a 353px vertical line; the order becomes
  Name, Due, Status…; the header's click still opens its menu. Space/↑/Space on Tags in the
  Properties page moves the column.
- **Sort:** sorted by Name descending, a drop asks "Remove this view's sort?"; Remove sort puts
  the last page first with the rest in the order shown; ⌘Z restores the sorted view.
- **Groups:** grouped by Status, Twitter redesign dropped at the end of Done gets Status: Done.
- **Phone:** no handles, nothing scrolls sideways.
- **Re-runs:** board, bleed (1440/1024/375 alignment), layout options and cards all pass. The

## Speed: the first byte halves, the server sits beside the database, the date parser waits to be needed — 2026-09-11/15

**What shipped, live as `7277d17a` (deployed 2026-09-15).** 23 commits from `perf/deep-dive`, integrated into this tree on 2026-09-14. Pages verify the session locally (`getClaims`), so the first byte fell ~425 → ~220 ms on every route. Each page's reads run in as few rounds as their dependencies allow: Home 7 → 3, Clients 7 → 3, Rituals 7 → 2, Horizon and Content 5 → 2. `<PageStamp/>` on every (app) page replaced the template stamp that made every sidebar click render the page twice. `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]` drops unused design-system code: 59–65 KB gz less per app page, 144 KB less on /login. The reading font is no longer preloaded, and Home's Google sync skips when it ran in the last 10 minutes. The worker is placed in `aws:ap-northeast-2`, and live responses carry `cf-placement: remote-ICN`. Measured on production builds against a stand-in database answering in 200 ms: Home content 1,470 → 634 ms, Tasks 840 → 430, Calendar 624 → 216, Rituals 1,448 → 423.

**Date parser (`722c14c`, in this tree, ships with the next deploy).** `lib/natural-date.ts` loads chrono-node when a typed-date field is focused or the reminder panel opens, and parses synchronously once it has loaded. A submit that beats the parser is read when it arrives. First-load JavaScript is 38.6 KB gz smaller on every (app) route. Checked in headless Chrome: the chunk is absent at page load, fetched on `focusin`, and "tomorrow" + Enter commits. A guard test keeps chrono-node out of static imports.

**Built, not merged, awaiting the owner's approval: `perf/instant-nav`.** `5b88e23` makes sign-in and sign-out load a new document, because the router's memory is keyed by URL, not by account. `17bebc0` requests the whole page when the pointer rests on a sidebar or pinned link for 70 ms, or when the link is focused. Tasks 629 → 387 ms, Habits 527 → 336 ms, with no extra server renders or database calls over a scripted visit. The two decisions are in the speed-audit report.

**How it was verified.** `scripts/perf/`: a stand-in Supabase with a latency knob, a request tracer, benchmarks, pixel comparison, and scripted `session` visits. Every loaded screen stayed pixel-identical. The post-deploy smoke run was green.

**Owed.** A migration adding indexes and `(select auth.uid())` policies, shown before it is applied. Calendar events rendered with the page. The Docs gallery downloading every document's full text. Loading states built from each screen's real layout. A finding: the offline mutation queue's localStorage key is not scoped to an account. Worker headroom is 36 KiB.

## Collection is a view — 2026-09-15 (COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN C1)

> **Superseded the same day** by the user's third brief (`COLLECTION_ITEM_BRIEF.md`): Collection is its own
> item, never a database view. This view was taken back out of databases; see "A Collection is its own
> item, beside a Database" below, which lists what was kept.

The user's brief (`COLLECTION_VIEW_BRIEF.md`, verbatim), started ahead of T13–T15 on their
instruction: *"immediately start working on collection task this is imp now"*. The plan is
`COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN.md`, tasks C1–C12. This is C1 (brief §1–4, §13–14, §17, §20–22, §33, §44).

**What shipped.**
- **A layout like any other.** `collection` joins every layout registry and is never a separate
  database type:
  - `VIEW_LABEL`: "Collection";
  - "Open pages in": center peek (§17 — you inspect a reference, you do not work through it);
  - layout options: card size;
  - `VIEW_ICON` = `Images` (a new seam export, so the glyph table was regenerated);
  - the view picker;
  - `/collection` → "Collection view", with its own drawn preview in the slash menu;
  - the editor maps the kind, and a failed creation retries as a Collection.
- **A new Collection database collects.** Its properties are Name, URL, Type, Source, Tags,
  Author, Published, Description and Created, with no Status.
  - **Type** is a fixed vocabulary (Website, Image, Video, PDF, Document, Social post, Audio,
    File, Other).
  - **Source** starts empty and grows as sources appear, so a new platform needs no code (§33).
  - **The facts are ordinary properties**, so a table, a board, a filter and search all read them.
- **The rules, pure** (`lib/collection-item.ts`):
  - **Source:** a known platform by name, "Website" for everywhere else.
  - **Type:** the file at the end of the address first, so a PDF is a PDF wherever it is hosted;
    then the platform; otherwise Website.
  - **Picture:**
    1. the platform's thumbnail, a fixed address that needs no request;
    2. an https address that is itself an image;
    3. the link's own image;
    4. otherwise, a tile.
  - **Tile:** the item's type and its domain, so a card never looks broken (§8, §34–35).
- **The masonry** (`lib/masonry.ts`, `database-collection.tsx`). Cards keep their own heights and
  are placed row by row into the shortest column. The document order, the tab order and any
  manual order therefore read left to right, then top to bottom, where CSS columns would read
  column by column. Columns follow the width the view has (card size sets the narrowest card).
  Each card measures itself, so nothing reads a ref during render.
- **The card** (§14). The picture first (its natural shape, clamped), then the name (the link's
  title stands in until one is set), then the source with its mark, or the domain for a website.
  Up to three tags, only when set, and the card's menu on hover. A click, Enter or Space opens the
  item in its view's mode.
- **An empty Collection** says "Collect anything" with one Add, the DS `EmptyState`.

**Verified with trusted input** using `scripts/verify/verify-collection.mjs` on the harness's
"Brand inspiration" database:
- **Masonry:** 7 cards in 3 columns at 1440×900, first row in order, no two cards overlapping in a
  column.
- **Pictures:** the YouTube thumbnail and an image address both loaded. The PDF, website and
  no-link items drew their tiles ("PDF · example.com", "Website · linear.app", "Other").
- **Sources and tags:** the cards read YouTube, Instagram and Pinterest with their marks, and tags
  show only where set.
- **Opening:** a click and Enter both open a center peek.
- **Switching:** Table shows all 7 items, Board groups them by Type (No Type, Website, Image, Video,
  PDF, Social post, Other), and returning to Collection shows all 7 again.
- **Phone:** one column at 390×844, no overlaps.
- **Themes and console:** light and dark screenshots, no console errors.
- **A fixture lesson:** a Wikimedia thumbnail address answered 400, and its card correctly drew a
  tile. The fixture now uses an image that serves.

**Guards.** Each of these was watched failing first:
- `lib/collections.test.ts`: the layout registry and the collecting schema.
- `lib/collection-item.test.ts`: source, type, picture order, image addresses, tiles.
- `lib/masonry.test.ts`: row-major placement, left tie-breaks, one column, empty.
- `lib/blocks.test.ts`: the slash menu's order, and `/collection` finding its entry.

The icon table and view-icon guards passed after the generator run.

`tsc` clean · **2217 tests / 145 files** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean
on every file touched.

### Recorded, next in the plan
- **Tile shapes.** Tiles share one 4:3 shape, so a Collection without pictures reads as a grid.
  The next task gives each type its natural shape, and remembers picture shapes so the masonry
  does not settle after loading (C2).
- **Remembered previews.** A link's preview is fetched per session (`useLinkMeta`, signed-in
  only), not yet remembered on the row (C2/C3).
- **Width.** At a page's text width the masonry holds 3 columns; with Full width it takes 5–6. The
  columns follow the width, with no fixed counts (§46).

## A Collection's pictures are remembered, and its tiles have shapes — 2026-09-15 (COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN C2)

> **Superseded the same day,** with C1 above: the view left databases. See "A Collection is its own item,
> beside a Database" below for what was kept.

**What was wrong after C1.**
- Every tile was 4:3, so a Collection without pictures read as a grid.
- A link's preview was fetched again on every visit.
- The masonry settled as pictures loaded: cards moved once their real shapes were known.
- **Found on the way: a database row's page saved its body as `{ blocks }` alone.** Anything else
  kept in that row's content would have been erased by the first sentence typed under it,
  including a preview remembered for a collected link. Documents and Content already merged.

**What shipped.**
- **Tiles are shaped like what they stand for** (`collectionTileShape`): a video or a website
  wide, a post square, a PDF or document tall like a page. A picture keeps its own shape, clamped
  by `readPreviewShape`. The shape numbers live in one place (`lib/collection-item.ts`).
- **A card remembers on its row.** It keeps the link's preview (the Content module's
  `readPreview` / `freshPreview` / `previewFrom`, trusted for 30 days and for that exact link) and
  the shape its picture turned out to be. A revisit draws both at once, and the network is asked
  only when nothing fresh is remembered. A remembered picture that stops loading is treated as
  expired and asked for again.
- **`store.rememberContent`:** a cache write merged into the row's content. It is saved like any
  row write, never recorded for ⌘Z, and never dated as an edit.
- **`withBlocks(content, blocks)`:** the row page's body save replaces only the blocks, over the
  store's latest content.

**Verified with trusted input** (`scripts/verify/verify-collection.mjs`):
- **Every C1 check still passes.**
- **Tile shapes:** at one column width a PDF tile is 294px tall, a social post 226px and a website
  119px.
- **No settling:** returning to the Collection from the Table draws the final layout in its first
  frame, with every card within 1px of where it settles.
- No console errors.

**Guards.** Each of these was watched failing first:
- `lib/blocks-content.test.ts`: a body save keeps the other keys and never mutates its input.
- `lib/collection-preview.test.ts`: tile shapes, and validation of remembered shapes.
- `lib/db-store.test.ts`: `rememberContent` keeps the body, is not undoable and is saved whole.

`tsc` clean · **2227 tests / 147 files** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean
on every file touched.

### Recorded, not started
- A page inside a page (`SubPage`) still saves `serialize(blocks)`. Nothing else lives in a sub-page's
  content today; it should use `withBlocks` when something does.
- **Unfurl gaps:** it does not yet read a published date or a video's duration (brief §6); for C3.

## Paste a link, and it is in the Collection — 2026-09-15 (COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN C3)

> **Superseded the same day,** with C1 and C2 above: the view left databases. Collecting by paste lives on in
> the Collection item; see "A Collection is its own item, beside a Database" below.

**The problem.** A Collection could only be filled one blank page at a time.
- New made an empty row and opened it.
- The link had to be typed into a URL cell.
- Type, Source, the name and the picture were all the person's job.

The brief's quickest path (§10, "Paste → preview → done") did not exist.

**Benchmark.**
- **Notion:** pasting a link into a database view puts it into a cell. It never makes a row, and a bookmark
  unfurls only inside a page.
- **Cosmos:** "Element — Media, URL, or note" opens a small form. A failed import stays in the grid as a
  card that says why.
- **Zenboard now:** paste on a Collection's page and the items exist at once, on top. Name, author,
  description, published day and picture follow from the link, and a link that says nothing is still a
  usable card.

**What shipped.**
- **Paste on the page** (`collectInto`, lib/collect.ts):
  - links become items, one per link, on top, in the order pasted;
  - one paste is one ⌘Z step, with a toast Undo;
  - it never lands while someone is typing, or under a panel or dialog the Collection is not inside;
  - a Collection inside a document takes a paste only once focus is in it;
  - plain text is never collected unasked.
- **"Add to collection"** is a Collection's New (`collect-composer.tsx`):
  - one field: a link pasted into it is collected with no Enter; a typed link or note is collected on Enter;
  - "Blank item" still makes an empty page;
  - the empty state's Add opens the same panel, and its copy now says what a paste does.
- **The address fills in at once** (`collectedValues`): URL, Type from the fixed vocabulary, and Source. A
  Source the database lacks is made in the same step, and a deleted Type option comes back.
- **The link fills in the rest** (`fillFromLink` through the new `store.fill`): Name, Author, Description,
  Published and the remembered preview. It fills only what is still empty, is never an undo step, and
  never writes into an item deleted, or re-linked, while the answer was on its way.
- **The card says what is happening:** "Fetching preview…" (with `aria-busy`) while the link is asked, and
  "Untitled resource" over a "Preview unavailable" tile when it answers nothing (§35–36).
- **`/api/unfurl` reads a published day** (`publishedDay`): article tags, JSON-LD `datePublished`, and
  Vimeo's `upload_date`. The day is read as the publisher wrote it, never converted.

**Found and fixed on the way.**
- **Prepending ran out of keys.** `orderBefore` halved the last digit, so rows put on top walked
  'i' → '9' → '4' → '2' → '1' → '0', and the sixth tied with the fifth. A drop at the top of a table
  reached the same floor. A 1 now becomes '0i', and `orderPrepend(rows, n)` gives n keys on top.
- **An undone paste came back empty on redo.** `addRow` re-inserted what the row was made with, losing
  everything filled in since. It now keeps the row as it was when undone.
- **An empty Collection could never draw its first item.** The masonry measured its width once, on mount,
  and an empty Collection has no box then. The width is now observed through a callback ref, whenever
  the box appears. Caught by the new empty "Moodboard" fixture.
- **A card asked the network about an address that is itself a picture.** It now asks only while such an
  item has no name.

**Verified with trusted input** (`scripts/verify/verify-collect.mjs`). `/api/unfurl` is scripted
through CDP `Fetch`, with one slow answer and one failing. Clicks, typing and keys are trusted; a paste is a
ClipboardEvent carrying the text, because a trusted ⌘V would write this machine's real clipboard.
- **New:** opens the panel with its field focused.
- **Typed link + Enter:** the card is first at once, as "Fetching preview…" with `aria-busy`. It is named
  "On quiet interfaces" when the answer lands 1.8 s later, with "Item added." and Undo.
- **A link pasted into the field** is collected with no Enter, and its YouTube thumbnail draws.
- **A page paste of two links:** two items on top, in pasted order. The toast's Undo takes both back.
- **A link with no answer:** "Untitled resource" · "Preview unavailable" · randomwebsite.com.
- **A paste while typing in the database's search:** nothing collected (10 → 10) and nothing fetched.
- **The item's page** lists the author, description, URL, published day and type as properties.
- **The empty "Moodboard":** "Collect anything" → Add → paste, and the first card is drawn in a 179 px
  masonry.
- **Themes:** light and dark screenshots.
- **Console errors: two, neither from this work.** Both are the documents harness's own hydration
  mismatch, reproduced on one fresh load with no Collection involved. A DocCard rendered "2m ago" on
  the server and "1m ago" on the client, because fixture times are stamped whenever each side loads
  the module. React's "script tag" warning follows from the regenerated tree.

**Guards,** each watched failing first:
- `lib/collect.test.ts` (17): parsing, values, one step, order, fill rules.
- `lib/row-order-prepend.test.ts`: 60 prepends never tie.
- `lib/db-store.test.ts` `fill`: merges, is not undoable, is saved, and survives undo and redo of a new row.
- `lib/unfurl-published.test.ts`.

`tsc` clean · **2256 tests / 150 files** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean on
every file touched.

### Recorded, not started
- **The harness fixture times above:** scheduled next, before C13, whose checks load pages more than once.
- **Keys made before the fix can be '0'**, the floor, and a paste above one ties with it. No new key can
  reach it.
- **Undoing an edit made while a link's answer was on its way** restores the row's data without what the
  answer filled: the store restores `data` whole, not key by key.
- **A view filter that contradicts a link's facts** (Type is Image, a video pasted): the facts win, so the
  item is added but hidden by the filter. The toast still confirms it.
- **A link with nothing to show** (a PDF) is asked again each session; a negative answer is not remembered
  (C11).
- **Opened from the empty state's Add,** the panel hangs under the toolbar's New.
- **Files** are C4.

## The documents harness hydrates on every load — 2026-09-15

**The problem** (found verifying COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN C3). The documents harness stamped its fixture times
with `Date.now()` when its module loaded. The dev server keeps one evaluation of a module until something
changes, while each browser load evaluates it afresh. So any load a minute or more after the last rebuild
rendered a card "2m ago" on the server and "1m ago" in the browser. React threw the tree away, then warned
about the theme's script tag. Every check that loaded the harness twice could report console errors that
had nothing to do with its feature.

**The fix.** Fixture times count back from the start of the current UTC day (`TODAY`), which the server
and the browser agree on in any time zone. Labels still come from the real clock at render, as with real
data: the harness now reads "Updated 9h ago" instead of "1m ago". The sort order is unchanged.

**Verified.**
- **Two loads 100 s apart, no rebuild between:** zero console errors on both, and the first three cards
  read "Updated 9h ago" identically.
- **`scripts/verify/verify-collect.mjs` again:** every check passes, with `consoleErrors: []` (it loads the
  harness twice).
- `tsc` clean · eslint clean · `fixture-coverage.test.ts` 8/8.

### Recorded, not started
- **Other dev-preview harnesses** still stamp `Date.now()` at module load (36 uses across `app/dev-preview`).
  Any that shows minute-level relative times can fail to hydrate the same way.
- **Across midnight UTC,** between a rebuild and a load, the two anchors still differ once.

## A Collection is its own item, beside a Database — 2026-09-15 (COLLECTION_PLAN K1–K6)

The user's third Collection brief (`COLLECTION_ITEM_BRIEF.md`): *"Collection must NOT be a Database View"* —
a Collection is a first-class item with its own name, content and layout, created wherever a Database is.
K1–K5 were built by the docs session (transcript e71978cb) before it hit its usage limit; this is K6, their
write-up, from the plan, the code and a fresh run of the browser check (session 7061260e, 22:16 IST).

**What was wrong.** The first two briefs had built Collection as a database VIEW (COLLECTION_VIEW_PLAN C1–C3,
and C13 begun): a layout of a database's rows. The third brief reversed the architecture.

**What shipped.**
- **K1 — Collection left the database.** The view was reverted out of the database code; databases are as
  they were. Kept because they stand on their own: the `orderBefore` key floor, the row page's body save that
  keeps other content (`withBlocks`), the harness's fixture clock, and the published day `/api/unfurl` reads.
- **K2 — The model and its store.**
  - **A Collection is a `pages` row with `type: 'collection'`** — no migration, `pages.type` is plain text — so
    rename, move, duplicate, trash, search, mentions, breadcrumbs and permissions are a page's.
  - **Its items live in `content.collection = { items }`** (`lib/collection.ts`). Each has a uuid, a `kind`
    (link · image · video · audio · pdf · file · note), what it holds (a url, an uploaded file or a note), what
    is known about it (title, description, author, site, published day, picture, favicon, picture shape), and
    its canvas place `{ x, y, w, h, z }`, which is layout and never dated as a change. Read through a guard:
    anything unreadable is dropped, an id is kept once.
  - **`lib/collection-store.ts`, one store per page.** `change` is an undo step; `learn` (a link's metadata, a
    picture's shape) is saved but never a step, and taught to the history in place so undoing an earlier
    change does not forget it. Saves merge over everything else the page holds; a placeholder id holds its
    saves until `linkCollectionStore`; a page still being created is written once it exists, never if it
    failed. `lastStep` / `undoStep` let a toast's Undo take back its own change and no other.
  - **The store is the only writer of a Collection's content.** Documents saves a Collection page's title and
    tags only — otherwise a rename wrote back an older copy of its items.
- **K3 — Creation and identity.** Documents' "More to create" (Doc · Database · Collection), the breadcrumb
  folder menu, and `/collection` in the editor (a page block, `BlockMenuItem.page: 'collection'`). It opens
  on its own surface named "New collection"; a Collection glyph (`Images`) marks it wherever a page's kind shows.
- **K4 — The masonry** (`collection-page.tsx`, `collection-grid.tsx`, `collection-card.tsx`).
  - Preview-first cards: the platform's thumbnail, an address that is an image, the link's own picture or an
    uploaded image or video — else a tile naming the kind and domain, shaped like its kind.
  - **Collecting:** paste links anywhere on the page, write a note or paste into Add (`collect-composer.tsx`),
    upload or drop files. An item appears at once; its name and picture follow ("Fetching preview…",
    "Preview unavailable"). One paste is one undo step.
  - **The item's page** (`collection-item-page.tsx`, PageView `collection-item`, centre peek): picture, name to
    change, "Open website / Watch on YouTube / Open PDF / Open file", details.
  - **Select many** (⌘/Ctrl-click, Shift-click, ⌘A), delete with Undo; Escape clears.
- **K5 — The canvas** (`collection-canvas.tsx`, `lib/canvas.ts`). Grid | Canvas over the same items: unplaced
  items open where the masonry would put them; drag one or many, marquee, Shift/⌘ add, resize from the corner
  (a 44px invisible grip on a coarse pointer), arrows nudge, `[` `]` resize, + − 100% Fit, wheel/pinch zoom
  about the pointer, Space/middle-drag pan. Each move or resize is one undo step and raises what it touched;
  the first move writes down the whole arrangement, so nothing reflows. The camera is each viewer's own.

**Verified** — `scripts/verify/verify-collection-item.mjs`, system Chrome with trusted input, rerun 22:16 IST:
A cards and pictures (YouTube thumbnail, image address, PDF tile, note) · B paste on the page ("Fetching
preview…" at once, then the link's name; "Item added." with Undo) · C the composer · D upload · E the item page
in the centre peek, renamed · F select two, delete, Undo restores both · G canvas: first row aligned, a card
moved 260×140 and kept through Grid and back · H marquee, 165% / fit 37% / 100%, resize +120 and Undo, `]`
+20 and Undo, the frame never scrolled · L touch: the grip takes a finger outside the corner, the card's inside
still moves it, a fine pointer has no grip · I an empty Collection, then its first item · J New menu (Doc,
Database, Collection) → "New collection" · K `/collection` → a Collection page · phone: one column · no console
errors.

- Tags; search, filter and sort; manual order; notes on an item; hover checkbox and more card actions; card

## A Collection's tags — 2026-09-15 (COLLECTION_PLAN K7)

COLLECTION_VIEW_BRIEF §14–16, §31, §42: a card's optional line is its tags; hover and selection offer Tags;
"Branding + Web" is how a visual library is narrowed. A Collection item had no tags at all.

**What shipped.**
- **The model** (`lib/collection.ts`). A Collection keeps its own vocabulary, `content.collection.tags`
  (`{ id, name, color }`, coloured like a database's options), and an item carries tag ids.
  - `ensureTag` finds a tag by name without case ("Typography" and "typography" are one tag) or makes one in
    the next colour; `setItemTags`, `tagItems` (one tag on or off many items at once, dating only the items
    that change), `renameTag` (refused onto another tag's name), `recolorTag`, `deleteTag` (off every item,
    which are not dated — the vocabulary changed, not what anyone did to them), `resolveTags`, `itemTags`.
  - Read through the guard: a tag once each by id and by name, an unknown colour reads gray, an item keeps
    only tags its Collection has. A Collection with no tags reads exactly as before tags existed.
- **The card** shows the first three tags as chips and counts the rest ("+1", named in its title).
- **The item's page** shows its tags and "Add tags" / "Edit tags": the option picker, searchable, with
  "Create" — making a tag and putting it on is ONE undo step.
- **The selection bar** gains Tag. The tags every selected item carries are checked; picking one of those
  takes it off them all, picking any other puts it on them all; a new tag made there goes on them all.
- **The canvas's cards** show the same tags.

**Found on the way — a panel inside a dialog lost its field's focus.** The tag picker on an item's page is a
popover inside the page's dialog. React focused its search field on mount; the dialog's focus trap, still
active for that instant, took focus back; the popover then opened with nothing focused, so typing a tag
and pressing Enter did nothing. `MenuField` now marks an autofocused field `data-autofocus`, and `Pop`
focuses that field itself once it is open (and the panel otherwise, as before). The Add composer outside a
dialog is unchanged.

**Verified** — `scripts/verify/verify-collection-tags.mjs` (system Chrome, trusted clicks, ⌘-clicks and keys),
light and dark:
- **Cards:** Me at the zoo "Motion"; React mark "Branding · Web · Typography · +1"; untagged cards draw none.
- **Item page:** the picker's search takes focus; "Research" + Enter adds it (Web, Research, both checked);
  picking Web takes it off; closing leaves the card with "Research"; ⌘Z brings Web back.
- **Selection:** ⌘-click two cards → "2 selected · Tag · Delete"; Tag → Branding goes on both, and is the
  one checked tag; picking it again takes it off both; "Poster" + Enter goes on both; ⌘Z takes Poster back.
- **Canvas:** the React card draws "Branding · Web · Typography · +1".
- No console errors. `verify-collection-item.mjs` rerun: every step still passes (the composer's field
  still takes focus).
- `tsc` clean · **2298 tests / 154 files** · eslint clean on every file touched. 9 new model tests.

  settings panel).
- **"+N" wraps to its own line** when three chips fill a narrow card.

## Duplicate copies what is on screen, and a new Collection's name arrives selected — 2026-09-16 (COLLECTION_PLAN K3–K4 fixes)

**The problems.** The docs session (e71978cb) found both when it came back from its usage limit and checked
K3–K4 with trusted input.
- **A duplicate missed recent items.** Duplicate built the copy from the page list's content. A Collection's
  store is the only writer of its items and never writes back to that list, so the list still held the items
  the page was loaded with.
  - In the browser, the source showed 8 items and its copy 7.
  - The copy's first save would then have written the older items over the server's copy.
- **A new Collection's name was not selected.** COLLECTION_PLAN K3 says it opens "its name selected to
  rename"; it did not.
  - Typing straight after New → Collection went nowhere.
  - Enter in a Collection's title did nothing: in a document it moves into the first block, and a Collection
    has none.

**Benchmark.**

## The Collection Index, and a Collection without a page boundary — 2026-09-16 (COLLECTION_PLAN X1–X4)

The user's fourth Collection brief (`COLLECTION_INDEX_BRIEF.md`, verbatim) keeps Collection as its own item and
adds two things:
- a Collection Index: every Collection as a large visual card;
- a Collection workspace with no page boundary.

**Benchmark.**
- **Cosmos:** a library of clusters. Each is a mosaic of its own pictures, with a name and an element count, and
  its canvas fills the window.
- **Pinterest boards:** a cover made from three pins (one large, two stacked), with the name and pin count below.
- **Notion:** no index by kind. A database page sits in the sidebar with everything else.
- **Zenboard now:**
  - The Index is a Documents view beside All documents.
  - "New collection" comes first, then one card per Collection. The preview is one large item with two beside
    it, made from the Collection's own items, pictures first. Below it: the icon and name, "N items", and
    "Shared" when a client can see it.
  - Sort by last edited, name, most items or created; search by name.
  - Every card has the same hover controls as a doc card.
  - A Collection is as wide as the pane, and its canvas meets the pane's edges and the bottom of the window.

**What shipped.**
- **X1 — The Index** (`components/documents/collection-index.tsx`, `lib/collection-index.ts`).
  - **Where it lives:** the Documents view `collections`, with a rail row "Collections" and a deep link
    `?view=collections`. The link is replaced, never pushed, like `?page=`, because Documents' other views are
    not addresses.
  - **The preview** (`previewItems`): pictures first — an uploaded image, a platform thumbnail, an address that is
    an image, a link's own image — in the Collection's order, then tiles, three at most.
  - **An empty Collection's card** is its empty state with a +. The + opens the Collection with Add open, once
    (`startAdding` / `onStartedAdding`).
  - **Each card reads its Collection through `collectionDocFor`:** the live store for a Collection opened on this
    device (the page list's content is older), otherwise the content.
  - **Last edited** (`collectionEditedAt`) is the later of the page's own time and its newest item's.
  - **The header holds only Sort and New collection.** The tag filter, list layout, Import and the Doc/Database
    menu are document tools.
  - **A Collection's breadcrumb now starts at Collections** (`sectionOf`, `SECTIONS`, `SECTION_ICON`), and that
    crumb offers New collection.
- **X2 — What you can do from the Index.**
  - Open a Collection, or rename it in place with the pencil.
  - The page menu offers Duplicate, Move to, Star, Copy link, and Delete (to Trash, with Undo).
  - Search by name in the rail's field ("Search collections").
  - Sort (`sortCollections`) by last edited · name · most items · created, pinned first.
  - A duplicate is dated now (`created_at`), so "Created" puts it with the newest.
- **X3 — No page boundary.**
  - A Collection page drops the 820px column, and its grid takes the pane's width: 4 columns at 1440×900.
  - The page names its side padding `--collection-bleed`. The canvas reaches past it with no border or radius,
    down to the bottom of the window, and nothing pads the page under it.
  - A Collection's menu has no "Full width"; it never saved for one.
- **Shared, not forked:** `DocCardActions`, the pencil and page-menu pill, came out of `DocCard`, and both kinds of
  card use it.

## Finding and ordering a Collection — 2026-09-16 (COLLECTION_PLAN K8)

A Collection with eight things in it is a moodboard; a Collection with two hundred is a research library only if
it can be asked a question. K8 is that question, and the answer to "where should this one go?" — search, four
filters, six orders, and a card that can be carried to a new place (`COLLECTION_VIEW_BRIEF` §29, §31–32).

**Taken over** from session 7061260e, which hit its usage limit with the pure rules written
(`lib/collection-find.ts`, 15 tests) and nothing on screen.

**The bar.** Filter · Sort · Search — the three controls a database's bar already carries, in the same order and
the same clothes, because narrowing a list is one act in Zenboard whatever the list holds. They organise the
**grid only**: the canvas is the arrangement of *everything*, and hiding an item there would leave a hole where
someone deliberately put something. The count beside them says `3 of 8` while anything is hidden.

- **Search** (§32) reads a name, an address, a domain, a source, an author, a description, a note's words, a
  file's name, a kind and a tag — every word of the query, without case or accents. Nothing found says so, with
  one way out ("Clear").
- **Filter** (§31) offers only what the Collection actually has: **Type** (its kinds, each with its glyph),
  **Source** (where things came from), **Tags** (its own vocabulary), and **Collected** (any time · last 7 days ·
  last 30 days). A section with nothing to tell apart is not shown.
- **Sort** (§29) is Manual order · Recently added · Recently updated · Name · Source · Published — a real menu's
  radio group, so the current one is announced.

**Three decisions worth the words.**
- **The sort is remembered on the Collection, but ⌘Z never undoes it.** It is saved through `store.learn`, the
  path for arrangement (a canvas place, a learned shape), not through `change`. A way of *looking* is not a step
  in the Collection's history: undo after sorting takes back the last thing you did to the items, which is what
  anyone means by it. Verified: ⌘Z after Sort → Name leaves the order alone.
- **A source is an origin, not the name a page gave itself.** `itemSource` reads best for one item ("Linear"),
  but two pages of one site disagree — one announces a `siteName` and the next does not — and the filter listed
  *Example* and *example.com* as two sources. `itemOrigin` is the key (platform, else domain); `sourcesPresent`
  groups by it and labels each group with the best name anything from there gave. The Source *sort* groups by the
  same key, so a site's things sit together however each named itself.
- **Nothing moves under the pointer while a card is carried.** A line shows the gap it will drop into and the
  masonry settles once, on the drop — the vocabulary already set by a table's rows and columns
  (`lib/table-drag.ts`), chosen over live reflow so what you are aiming at stays where you saw it.
  `masonryLanding` is that gap: the nearest card decides, and which side of it — above or below first (so the end
  of a column can be dropped into, and so one column reads top to bottom), beside it otherwise.

**Every gesture has a twin.** A carry is a mouse gesture — a touch drag scrolls the page, so on a touch screen it
is not offered at all. ⌥← and ⌥→ move a focused card one place, and the card's menu carries **Move left** and
**Move right** with those keys printed beside them. All three disappear when the order is not the manual one or
something is hidden, because a drag can only rearrange the order it is looking at (`canReorder`).

**Found while building:**
- **Something collected while searching vanished.** Paste a link with "typography" in the field and the new item
  did not match, so the toast said "Item added" over a screen where nothing had. Collecting now puts down
  whatever was being looked for.
- **A menu's rows were `menuitemcheckbox` outside a menu** — a role that means nothing there. The filter's rows
  are `checkbox`es in labelled groups and the Collected window is a real `radiogroup`; Sort became a
  `DropdownMenu` with a `RadioGroup`, which is what it always was.
- **Two names for one concept:** `KIND_LABEL` in `collection-card.tsx` was a second copy of `ITEM_KIND_LABEL` in
  `lib/collection.ts`, letter for letter. One name, one home; four files now read the model's.

**Proved with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-collection-find.mjs` (new), system Chrome over CDP on the
documents harness, A–L:

- **B:** "typography" finds the item titled so, the one tagged so and the talk — `3 of 8`; Escape restores 8.
- **C:** Type → Note leaves the note alone, `1 of 8`, the button reads as set; Clear filters returns 8.

## Notes on a collected thing — 2026-09-16 (COLLECTION_PLAN K9)

A board of pictures remembers *what* you saw. §38 asks for the thing Pinterest and Cosmos cannot do: **why you
kept it.** A collected item's page now has a body — the Zenboard editor, saved on the item — so a Collection is
somewhere you think, not only somewhere you hoard.

**The model.** `item.body` is the editor's blocks, read through a guard that keeps nothing when nothing was
written (`hasBody`). `setItemBody` dates the item, because writing about something IS a change to it — that is
what "Recently updated" is for. No migration: a body is JSON inside the page's content, like everything else a
Collection holds.

**A note item IS its body.** Before this, a note item's words were read-only on its own page — you could collect
a thought and never edit it. Now the same editor holds them, and the plain `note` follows the body through
`blocksToText`, the projection search and the portal already use. One writer, one derived field, and the card,
the title and the search all keep working untouched. A note item shows no "Notes" heading and no rule: its words
are the item, so they sit under its name rather than under its details.

**Three smaller decisions.**
- **Writing settles before it saves** (400ms), and whatever is still waiting is written when the page closes.
  Without it, every keystroke re-rendered every card behind the dialog.
- **It saves through `learn`, not `change`** — the same reasoning as K8's sort. ⌘Z in a Collection takes back what
  you did to the *items*; the words you are typing are undone by the editor you are typing in.
- **The card says an item has been written about** — a small left-aligned-text glyph at the end of its source
  line, the same idea as a board card's page glyph (`hasBody`, `lib/blocks.ts`). Without it the notes are
  invisible from the grid, and a feature nobody can see is a feature nobody uses.
- **The search reads them** (§32 lists Notes): `itemSearchText` now folds in `blocksToText(item.body)`.

**The editor is loaded only when an item opens** (`next/dynamic`, `ssr: false`) — it is the heaviest thing in
Documents, and a Collection should not carry it to draw cards. A file dropped into the notes hangs off the
Collection's page (`attachTo`), except in the harness and while a page is still being created.

**Proved with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-collection-notes.mjs` (new), A–F:
- **A:** the card of the item written about carries the mark; its page shows "Notes" and both paragraphs.
- **B:** a real click into the notes of an item that had none, then typing — closed and reopened, the words are
  there, and the card now carries the mark.
- **C:** "sidebar" finds the item by its notes alone.
- **D:** a note item's editor holds its own words; typing into it flows back to the card's text, and the note
  gets no second "Notes" section.
- **E:** "/" opens the editor's own menu inside the item's page (Basic blocks · Text · Page · Heading 1…).
- **F:** dark, and a phone: the notes are 350px wide inside the viewport, fully on screen. No console errors.
- **Neighbours re-run:** `verify-collection-find.mjs` A–L green · `verify-collection-tags.mjs` `errors: []` ·
  `verify-collection-item.mjs` A–M green (its two fine-pointer controls correctly false) ·
  `verify-collection-index.mjs` green.
