## Focus goes back where it came from — 2026-09-16

Measured on `/dev-preview/shell`: focus the Search button, ⌘K, Escape — and
`document.activeElement` was `<body>`. The next Tab started again at the top of the
page, and anyone working by keyboard lost their place for having opened a palette they
then closed. Radix restores focus for every overlay IT owns, which is why the DS menus
and dialogs behave; the eighteen layers this app rolls itself did not.

**`lib/use-focus-return.ts` is the one rule.** Remember who had focus when a layer
opens; hand it back when the layer closes; and only if the close left focus NOWHERE — if
the action moved focus somewhere deliberate (the field it just created, the layer
underneath), that claim wins. It covers both shapes a layer takes here: a component that
stays mounted and flips `open`, and one mounted only while open. The restore lives in the
effect CLEANUP, which React runs after the DOM is gone, so `document.activeElement` is
honestly `<body>` by the time it looks. The decision is a pure `focusFellNowhere()` with
its own test.

Wired: the command palette · quick capture · the new-space modal · the legacy shared
`Popover` and `Modal` · `PickerPanel` (so the emoji and cover pickers inherit it) · DS
`Combobox`, `TimePicker` and `FullScreenLayer` · the week board's chip popovers, card
menu and composer · the focus view's two menus · the calendar event composer · the tasks
row menu · horizon's menus · doc-properties' three panels.

**Safe beside the tooltip**, which is not obvious: a restore leaves `relatedTarget` null,
and `focusOpensTooltip` treats null as handed-back rather than arrived, so the trigger
does not sprout a tooltip that would eat the next Escape — the exact bug recorded here in
July. Verified: after Escape the Search button has focus and no tooltip opened.

**chip-ui had already solved this, privately.** It keeps `{ open, restore }` in one piece
of state: choosing something or pressing Escape means focus belongs back on the trigger,
while clicking elsewhere means whatever was clicked should keep it. That nuance is now in
the shared hook's signature (`useFocusReturn(open, restore)`), which is the point of the
system-before-screen rule — the private answer becomes the shared one. chip-ui keeps its
own copy for now: it has no tests, it is correct, and the guard declares it rather than
pretending it is a gap.

**Guard:** "a hand-rolled layer hands focus back" — it finds every file that paints a
layer and owns an Escape (a control asserts it finds at least ten), requires the hook or
a declared exception, and fails on an exception that is no longer a layer.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` 2388 tests pass.


## The surfaces measure clean, and one script now says so — 2026-09-16

A `better-ui` pass over the twelve main surfaces, done by MEASURING the rendered page
rather than reading source: concentric radius on nested surfaces, `transition-property:
all` that actually runs, durations off the ladder, icon sizes off the five-step scale,
images with no outline, stray `will-change`.

**Two real findings, both icons off the scale.**
- `components/calendar/milestone-chip.tsx` drew its flag at `size={compact ? 9 : 11}` —
  two sizes, neither of them a rung. It takes `ICON_SIZE.xs` now.
- The DS `PanelHeader` sized its lead glyph `[&_svg]:size-[18px]` beside 14px text. 16
  (`size-4`) is both the rung and the right optical weight for that text.

**The guard had a hole, and the browser found it.** "Every `<Icon>` size is on the scale"
matched `size={12}` but not `size={compact ? 9 : 11}`, so a ternary of two off-scale
numbers sat in the calendar unnoticed. It now reads every number in the size expression,
and skips a size DERIVED from a scale factor (`Math.round(S.play * 0.44)`) because that
is the optical exception the seam's type deliberately allows. A control asserts both
halves — that the ternary is caught and the derived one is not.

**`scripts/verify/audit-surfaces.mjs` is the instrument, and its header keeps the receipts
of being wrong three times before it was right:**
- It counted small controls floating inside a row as nested surfaces — 13 "radius misses"
  that were not misses. A nested surface FILLS its parent's inner box; that is the filter.
- It counted `transition-property: all` at `0s` as a violation. That is CSS's initial
  value — the absence of a transition — and it reported 97 of them on a clean page.
- It counted horizon's 52px progress ring as an icon. An icon is a glyph from the seam,
  which draws Phosphor's 256 grid; a ring is a drawing with its own viewBox.

The failure modes are in the script's header on purpose: an audit that has been wrong
three times is only trustworthy if it says how.

Result after the two fixes: twelve surfaces, all clean — no radius misses, nothing
transitioning `all`, no duration off the ladder, no icon off the scale, no unoutlined
image, no stray `will-change`.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` 2389 tests pass.


## Phone width and dark mode, measured — once the ruler proved itself — 2026-09-16

`scripts/verify/audit-surfaces.mjs` now takes `--width` and `--theme`, checks horizontal
overflow, and writes full findings with `--out`. Twelve surfaces × {390px, 1440px} ×
{light, dark}: **all clean.** That sentence is only worth writing because of what it took
to earn it — no app code changed in this pass, and the deliverable is an audit that can
say "clean" honestly.

**The first overflow check was blind.** It asked whether the DOCUMENT scrolls sideways.
This app never scrolls the document: content lives in `scroll-region` containers
(`overflow-y: auto`, `overflow-x: hidden`). A control that dropped a 2400px element into
the page came back "clean" — the region CLIPPED it, the document never widened, and on a
phone that content would simply have been gone. The first 390px run said "all clean"
and meant nothing.

**The second version flagged eight things, and every one was deliberate.** Measuring
regions instead, it reported tab strips, chip rows, the settings nav at phone width and
the content pipeline board — all sideways scrollers on purpose. The cause is a CSS rule:
Tailwind's `overflow-x-auto` computes `overflow-y: auto` as well (a `visible` axis becomes
`auto` when the other one scrolls), so a one-row strip is indistinguishable from a
vertical region by computed style alone. My control for "a sideways scroller is allowed"
had used an explicit `overflow-y: hidden` — which is not how any real code in this app
writes it — so the control passed while the real idiom failed.

**The rule that shipped:** a layout region that cuts content off is wrong at any height;
a region that scrolls sideways is wrong only if it also scrolls down; a one-row strip and
single-line truncation are fine. And the script **tests itself on the first page before
measuring anything**: three shapes it must catch (the page overflowing, a region clipping
content, a region scrolling both ways) and three it must allow (a sideways scroller, text
truncation, and the real `overflow-x-auto` strip). If any control misbehaves it refuses to
report, because a "clean" from a broken check is worse than no answer — and this one had
been broken twice in an hour.

Smaller fixes to the instrument: full findings go to `--out` as JSON (stdout truncated
them mid-object), and a flag's VALUE is no longer read as a route (`--out /tmp/x.json`
had been audited as a page called `/tmp/x.json`).


## A finger can hit it — 49 touch targets under the floor, fixed at their sources — 2026-09-16

The surface audit gained `--pointer coarse`, which flips `(pointer: coarse)` over the
DevTools protocol before the first paint, the way a phone reports itself. At 390px it
found **49 controls under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor** across eight surfaces — and nearly
every one was the same shape: wide enough, too SHORT. 150–320px wide and 18–21px tall:
chromeless editors, titles, stage names, chips, a search field.

**The rule measures the effective target, not the visible box.** Zenboard meets the floor
with an invisible centred `::after` (`touch-min` gives 24px, `IconButton` gives 44px), so
a box-only check would have reported every accommodation that already works. The target
is the larger of the box and its `::after` — clipped by the element itself when it is
overflow-hidden, the trap ds-theme.css already records — and links inside running text
are exempt, as WCAG exempts them. It self-tests on the first page (a bare 16px control and
a clipped expander must be caught; `touch-min` and an inline link must pass) and refuses to
report if the pointer emulation did not take.

**Fixed where they come from, with the house's own two idioms:**
- **A min-height on a coarse pointer** (`[@media(pointer:coarse)]:min-h-6`) where an
  `::after` cannot help — an input cannot own a pseudo-element, and `truncate` is
  overflow-hidden, which clips one. Into the shared recipes: `inlineEdit` (every chromeless
  editor — Forms' 14 question titles went clean in one edit), the DS `Board` column title,
  `ListRow`, `LayerToggle`, and the Finance and breadcrumb search fields.
- **`touch-min`** for plain controls with room around them: the habits Skip and status
  chips, the Clients status chip and email link, Home's invoice link, Documents' title
  buttons and the New folder button.
- **The calendar's 15px tick** could take neither: it already owns an `::after` for its
  `.zb-press` wash, and `touch-min` would collide with it. It grows to 24px on a coarse
  pointer instead — it is the most-tapped kind of control there is.

**The recipe had been copied seven times.** A focusable, truncating title needs the
coarse min-height, and the task row had it — but the same class string lived on in the
task rail, projects (twice), habits, content and meetings without it. All seven carry it
now, and `app/design-system.test.ts` asserts that ANY class which both focuses and
truncates carries the floor, proven by stripping it from the habits title (the guard named
`habits-board.tsx:327`) and restoring it.

Measured after: **twelve surfaces, 390px, coarse pointer — all clean**, both self-tests
passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` passes.


## Emil Kowalski's skill is the source of truth — the first pass — 2026-09-16

User directive: *Emil Kowalski's skill is the source of truth; make Zenboard a world-class
application with it.* So the whole app was audited against `emil-design-eng` — its
animation decision framework, easing curves, durations, component rules and review
checklist — with evidence per rule, and fixed at the token and seam level. CLAUDE.md now
says so in its Interaction section, so the next session starts from the same rulebook.

**Already compliant, measured:** no `transition: all`, no `scale(0)`, DS popovers grow
from their trigger, the keyboard-opened palette and capture composer do not animate,
exits are faster than entrances, lists stagger, and Tailwind v4 gates its own `hover:`
utilities behind `@media (hover: hover)` (62 blocks in the compiled CSS).

**Fixed in this pass:**
- **Emil's exact curves.** `--ease-out-quiet` is his ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32,
  1)` (it was 0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), `--ease-standard` his in-out `(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` for
  movement on screen, and a new `--ease-drawer` `(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` — the iOS curve — for
  every sheet and drawer sliding in or out. The JS seam's `MOTION.ease` matches.
- **The press.** It used to land in 20ms and release on an overshooting spring. Emil's
  press feedback is one transition of 100–160ms, ease-out, both ways, no bounce: it is
  100ms on `--ease-out-quiet` now, and `--ease-spring` is gone.
- **A subsequent tooltip opens instantly.** `data-[state=instant-open]` still ran
  `animate-emerge`; once one tooltip is open, its neighbours should not animate at all.
- **Hover washes only where hover exists.** `.zb-nav-item:hover` and `.zb-press:hover::after`
  were hand-written and ungated, so a tap on a phone left a sticky wash. Both sit inside
  `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
- **Transform strings, not Motion shorthand.** `Appear`, the tasks list and the content
  calendar animated `y`/`x`, which runs on requestAnimationFrame and drops frames under
  load — exactly when a page is arriving. They animate full `transform` strings now.
- **The JS side had its own curves.** `EXIT_ROW` left on `[0.4, 0, 1, 1]` — an ease-in —
  and the board and content calendar each hand-wrote a near-copy of the house curve with
  their own durations (0.24s, 0.2s). All take the seam's `MOTION` values.

**Reduced motion: fewer and gentler, not zero.** The app collapsed EVERY animation and
transition to 0.01ms, so a reduced-motion reader lost the fade that says a menu opened
along with the slide that could have hurt. Now transitions keep colour, background,
border, shadow and opacity and lose everything that moves or resizes; every keyframe that
moves has an opacity-only twin of the same name inside the reduced-motion block (a later
`@keyframes` of the same name wins, so no call site changed); and the seam's `Move`
strips movement from caller-supplied Motion targets — deliberately not a root
`MotionConfig`, because the root providers ship on `/login` and the portal. Declared
exceptions: `spin` (its turning is its status) and `shimmer` (motion-safe gated). The
flat-wash fallback for block-anchor flashes is gone too; it only existed because of the
kill-switch, and a colour pulse is what reduced motion keeps.

**Verified live, on a real menu opened by a real click** (DevTools, `document.getAnimations()`):
without the setting the menu runs `emerge` on opacity and transform and the button presses
on transform; with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated, the same menu runs `emerge`
on opacity ONLY, the press movement is gone, and the colour wash still plays.

**Guards** in `app/design-system.test.ts`: the vocabulary's three curves; press and wash on
the quiet curve with no bounce; no curve literal outside the motion seam and every seam
curve starts fast (proven by restoring the old ease-in, which it named: x1=0.4, y1=0);
every moving keyframe has a twin, no twin moves, and the kill-switch cannot return (proven
by deleting the `emerge` twin, which it named).

**Recorded for the next pass:** the latency probe (`scripts/verify/measure-interactions.mjs`)
is NOT trusted yet — its self-test injected a 150ms click handler and the probe saw nothing,
so every "fast" it printed is void until that is fixed · toasts still animate on keyframes
(Emil: rapidly-triggered UI uses transitions) · the mobile sheet dismisses only past a
25% distance (no velocity), clamps upward drag at zero so its swipe-up branch can never
run, and lets a second finger reset the drag · `fadein` is defined twice under one name
(ds-theme.css opacity-only, globals.css with a 4px lift; the later one wins) · the DS
`Board` imports `motion/react` directly rather than through the seam.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` passes.


## Toasts on transitions, and a sheet that obeys a flick — 2026-09-16

Two more rows from the Emil Kowalski review, both verified with real input in a real
browser.

**Toasts animate on transitions, not keyframes.** Emil's rule from building Sonner:
rapidly-triggered UI uses transitions, because a keyframe restarts from zero when it is
interrupted and a transition retargets from wherever the element already is — and toasts
are the canonical case. The card now enters from `@starting-style` (Tailwind's
`starting:` variant: translate 8px, scale 0.98, opacity 0) and leaves on a transition when
`leaving` is set; it reports its own `transitionend` on opacity, with the 400ms floor still
underneath for a hidden tab. The toast-only `toast-out` keyframe and its reduced-motion
twin are gone. Measured on `/dev-preview/confirm` with real clicks: while entering, the card
runs `CSSTransition` on opacity, scale and translate with `animation-name: none`; on
Dismiss it runs the same three transitions, reaches opacity 0 by ~140ms having moved 8px
down, and is removed. Guarded: "a toast animates with transitions, not keyframes".

**The bottom sheet follows Emil's gesture rules.** `BottomSheet` (the breadcrumb sibling
picker on a phone) dismissed only by distance — past 25% of its height — so a quick flick
did nothing; it clamped upward drag at zero, which made its own swipe-up-to-expand branch
unreachable (it tested `dragY < -h * 0.15` on a value that could never go negative); and a
second finger re-anchored the drag. Now:
- a **flick** (over 0.11px/ms, and more than 8px so a jittery tap is not one) acts
  regardless of distance, in either direction;
- pulling **up** meets an iOS-style rubber band instead of a wall;
- **one finger drives** — the drag remembers its pointerId and ignores the rest, and a
  cancelled pointer ends it;
- the drag writes `transform` **straight to the element** instead of React state on every
  pointermove, and the release eases home on `--ease-drawer`.
The decision is a pure `sheetRelease(dy, ms, height)` with `rubberBand`, tested in
`components/ds/ui/drawer.test.ts`.

Measured on a 375px phone with trusted TOUCH input over DevTools, on the real breadcrumb
sheet: opened at half (487px) · a 60px flick down in ~160ms stepped to peek (325px) · the
same flick from peek dismissed it · a 60px drag over ~1.8s left it at 487px · a 50px flick
up expanded it to full (788px) — the branch that could never run · a slow 260px drag down
still stepped a detent without any velocity.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` passes.


## Six overlays that never faded, one fade with two meanings, and the motion seam closed — 2026-09-16

The two hygiene items left from the Emil pass turned out to be three bugs.

**`animate-fadein` compiled to nothing.** Six call sites — PageView's in-pane and
full-page modes and its centre-peek scrim, both Drawer scrims, and the CommandMenu scrim —
used `data-[state=open]:animate-fadein`, but no `--animate-fadein` token existed, so
Tailwind generated no rule at all: 0 in the compiled stylesheet. Every one of those layers
cut in. The centre peek's `animate-pop-in` was dead the same way. There is now one fade
token, `--animate-fadein` (the old `--animate-ds-fadein` was a second name for the same
job; its four users moved over), and the centre peek enters on `animate-rise`, exactly as
the DS Modal does. Compiled after a clean rebuild:
`.data-\[state\=open\]\:animate-fadein[data-state="open"]` exists, where before there
was nothing.

**`fadein` meant two things.** ds-theme.css defined it as a pure fade; globals.css defined
it again with a 4px lift, later in the cascade, so it won — every scrim and page-level fade
quietly lifted 4px, the "movement bought for nothing" globals.css itself warns against for
pages. `fadein` is opacity only and defined once; the lift is its own keyframe,
`fade-rise`, kept by name by the anchored panels and cards that were written for it (the
picker panel, focus-view menus, the block editor's menu, the triage cards, the onboarding
card and the ritual step). The reduced-motion twin moved with it.

**The motion library had two side doors.** The DS `Board` and the content calendar
imported `motion/react` directly; the seam (`components/ds/ui/motion.tsx`) re-exports
`AnimatePresence`, `LayoutGroup` and `motion`, and both import from it now.

**Guards** — "an animation class draws something, and a keyframe has one name": every
`animate-*` class in the app has an `--animate-*` token or is a Tailwind default; no
`@keyframes` name is defined twice outside a reduced-motion block; only the seam imports
the animation library. Proven by putting `animate-pop-in` back and redefining `fadein` —
the guard named `page-view.tsx:367 animate-pop-in` and `fadein (app/ds-theme.css and
app/globals.css)` — then restoring both.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` 2412 tests pass.


## The latency probe, trusted at last — and the frequent interactions are fast — 2026-09-16

`scripts/verify/measure-interactions.mjs` measures how long the most frequent things
take to answer, with real input over DevTools. It was wrong twice before it could be
believed, and its self-test caught both.

**Event Timing does not work headless.** The first version used the Event Timing API,
INP's own source. Its self-test injects a button whose click handler blocks for 150ms,
and the probe reported nothing. Traced link by link: the API was supported, the page
visible, the button hit and its handler RAN — but an Event Timing entry is finalised at
the next paint, and headless Chrome does not produce a frame unless asked. A
requestAnimationFrame loop made the entry appear (handlers=150, exact, but a 1248ms total
from irregular presentation) — on one run. The identical run next recorded zero entries.
An instrument that answers sometimes cannot back a claim.

**So it times the dispatch directly.** A capture listener on `window` runs before any
handler the app has (React listens on its root); a `setTimeout(0)` queued from it fires
only after the whole dispatch, React's synchronous re-render and layout effects
included, has finished. That gap is handler time; `event.timeStamp` to the capture
listener is input delay. Neither depends on a paint.

**And `pointerup` and `click` share a task.** Both timers fire after the click's handlers,
so summing per event read the self-test's 150ms handler as 305ms. Handler time is the
union of overlapping intervals now. Self-test after: a 150ms handler reads as 154ms,
deterministically — and the probe refuses to report if it does not.

**Result, dev build, median of three runs** — input delay 0ms everywhere (the main thread
is idle when input arrives):

| Interaction | Handlers | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| open the command palette | 14ms | first open 41ms |
| type into the palette | 5ms | first keystroke 70ms |
| tick a task | 31ms | first tick 67ms |
| switch a view (segmented control) | 45ms | |
| open a task | 46ms | on screen 132–158ms after the press, ~70ms of which is the harness pressing |

These are React DEVELOPMENT numbers, which do extra work on every render, so production
is faster still. Nothing here is near Emil Kowalski's budgets or INP's 200ms "good" line,
so no code changed: the finding is that the frequent interactions are already fast, and
the first-of-a-kind spikes are warm-up. What remains unmeasured is paint cost, which
needs a headed browser — the script says so rather than guessing.

## Frame by frame — Emil Kowalski's slow-motion review, eight plans, all shipped — 2026-09-17

Emil Kowalski's `improve-animations` audit, run against the whole app, with the jakubkrehel
`better-ui` skill as a second lens (where the two disagree on a motion value, Emil wins, per
the standing directive). The audit wrote eight self-contained plans (`plans/`, index in
`plans/README.md`); all eight shipped in order 001 → 003 → 004 → 002 → 005 → 006 → 007 → 008.

**The instrument came first.** `scripts/verify/slow-motion.mjs` does what Emil's skill asks a
reviewer to do by eye: it slows every animation to 10% over DevTools, triggers a real input,
then pauses each animation and SEEKS it to fixed fractions, reading geometry, opacity, transform
and origin at each. Seeking a paused animation is deterministic, so every number below repeats.
Self-test first: a probe travelling 100px must read 50px at 50%, or it refuses to report. On the
code as audited, seven of its checks FAILED and the pointer control passed; after the plans,
all twelve scenarios pass.

**What shipped, with the measurement that justified it:**

| Plan | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 001 Selection toolbar | faded in 146px right and 46px low of where it lives — over the selected words — then jumped. A running keyframe replaced its positioning `transform` | positioned with `translate`; mid-entrance drift 0.1px/0.16px; grows from the edge facing the selection |
| 003 Menus, selects, popovers, tooltips | the dropdown's Radix origin `0% 0px` lost to `data-[side=bottom]:origin-top`; the anchored corner slid 5.8px and the whole menu rose 4px toward its trigger | every Radix surface takes `--radix-*-content-transform-origin`; `emerge`/`zb-pop-in` scale and fade without travelling; corner travel 0px; tooltip grows from its arrow tip |
| 004 Dialog exit | a quarter of the way out, the scrim was already unmounted and the dialog a ghost over a bright page | `--animate-fadeout` on every DS overlay, in sync with the panel; PageView's centre peek got the exit it lacked |
| 002 Keyboard | `s` opened the Schedule menu on a 100ms `zb-pop-in`; `/` the slash menu; every g-chord page faded; each triage decision rose in | `lib/input-modality.ts` stamps `<html data-input>`; one rule turns off anything wearing `zb-enter` while the keyboard drives; a pointer still animates; Escape closes with no exit; the DS CommandMenu never animates |
| 005 Phone nav drawer | a LEFT drawer entered from the right, across the page (left edge 238px at frame 0), on the arrivals curve, and vanished on close | `slide-in-left`/`slide-out-left` on `--ease-drawer`, 200ms in, 100ms out, unmounts after; scrim fades |
| 006 Transition curves | colour ran on three curves: the strong ease-out (97% of a 100ms wash in 50ms), Tailwind's default (12 of 52 elements on the tasks page) and the in-out movement curve; 11 raw-ms transitions; buttons' Tailwind utilities silently dead under the unlayered press rule | `--ease-hover` = CSS `ease` (Emil: hover/colour → ease); Tailwind's defaults set to `--duration-fast`/`--ease-hover`; movement names `ease-standard`; the press rule carries opacity and filter; live tally: 314 colour transitions on the hover curve, 0 on Tailwind's |
| 007 Layout properties | progress fills animated `width`, switch thumbs `left` | fills slide with `translateX`, thumbs with `transform`; the shell's Focus switch lands track and thumb on the same 100ms |
| 008 State icons | Copy→Check and Play↔Pause blinked in one frame | `IconSwap` in the motion seam: better-ui's values (scale 0.25→1, opacity, blur 4px→0, spring 0.3s, bounce 0); at 30% the leaving icon reads opacity 0.24 / blur 3.05px; the button holds its 86px; Space swaps with zero animations |

**Five traps, each of which produced a wrong first answer:**
- **A must-fail control that passed exposed a hole in every guard.** The shared `code()` helper in
  `app/design-system.test.ts` looked for an unclosed block comment BEFORE discarding line comments,
  so `// documents/*.` on `components/ds/ui/menu.tsx:10` opened a "block" that blanked the next fifty
  lines — `OVERLAY_CLASS` and `MENU_PANEL_CLASS` included — for every guard in the file. Fixed; the
  whole suite still passed afterwards, so nothing had been hiding there, but it could have.
- **A fixed window let a reverted fix through.** The toolbar guard read 9 lines below the class; the
  explanatory comment pushed `transform` past it. Guards now read to the end of the opening tag.
- **Opacity on a parent fades its whole subtree.** Giving the drawer's scrim a fade made the drawer, its
  child, see-through while it slid (effective opacity 0 → 0.775 → 1). Scrim and drawer are siblings;
  the instrument multiplies opacity up the tree, and a control with the old nesting fails it.
- **`AnimatePresence` animates a leaving child with the props of its LAST render.** A key that swapped the
  icon still played the exit the previous click had set up (3 animations). The hand is passed through
  `custom`, which reaches leaving children fresh.
- **Turbopack served a stale `globals.css` while `ds-theme.css`, which it imports, was fresh.** The keyboard
  rule was missing from the compiled CSS with no error anywhere. `rm -rf .next` and restart, then read
  the compiled CSS before measuring.

**Guards added** (all with must-fail controls): an element that animates in does not position itself with
`transform` · an anchored surface grows from its trigger · a scrim leaves with its panel · nothing a
keyboard opens animates · a drawer enters from the edge it lives on · transitions take Emil's curves and
the ladder's numbers (hover curve, Tailwind defaults, no raw ms, movement names its curve, a button's
inline transition keeps the press, no `transition: all`) · a fill or a thumb moves with transform
(declared exceptions: the sidebar collapse, the bottom sheet's height, and the segmented thumb and tabs
underline, whose rounded ends `scaleX` would distort) · an icon that changes with state cross-fades.
`audit-surfaces.mjs` now also checks curves per property, with its own self-test.

**Verified:** `tsc` clean; 2,445 tests in 160 files pass; `slow-motion.mjs` 12/12; `audit-surfaces.mjs`
clean on 12 routes at 1440 light and at 390 dark with a coarse pointer; latency probe in the same range
as yesterday (tick 35ms, open a task 23ms, switch a view 46ms, type 7ms, palette 22ms, dev build).
`CLAUDE.md` (root) now names `--ease-hover`, the keyboard marker and the origin rule.

**Owed, with reasons:** `eslint` still reports `set-state-in-effect` errors in effects this work did not
change (`app-shell.tsx` sidebar mode, `focus-timer.tsx`, `portal-document.tsx`, `task-detail-drawer.tsx`)
— hydration-sensitive refactors that belong to their own features. Recorded, not planned: the desktop
sidebar collapse (labels vanish on frame 0, icons then drift ~93px), and rows a key removes still
collapse (kept for spatial continuity). The phone drawer has no Escape or focus trap — an accessibility
gap outside motion.

**Then verified on the real app, signed in, read-only** (menus opened and closed with Escape, nothing
selected, nothing toggled or typed): the DS `Switch` on Settings → Notifications computes track colour
0.1s on the hover curve and thumb 0.1s transform on the in-out curve, so they land together; `g k` reached
`/tasks` with `data-input="keyboard"` and the page entrance computing `animation: none`; a sidebar click
played `zb-page-in`; `j` then `s` on a real task opened the Schedule menu computing `animation: none` with no
animation started, and Escape closed it with none; the Sidebar control menu opened by pointer played
`emerge` from its Radix origin (`0% 134px`, side top: the corner facing its trigger). The embedded pane
reports `document.hidden`, which delays `animationstart` events, so every keyboard result rests on computed
style, never on an absent event.

## The sidebar collapses in place — 2026-09-17

The one motion defect the frame-by-frame review recorded but did not plan. Measured at 10% playback:
collapsing the desktop sidebar re-rendered every row on the FIRST frame — labels unmounted, rows
re-centred, the header swapped its wordmark for the mark, the "Pinned" heading unmounted — while only
the panel's width animated. So the text was gone while the panel was still 230px wide, every icon (now
centred in that shrinking panel) slid about 90px left to meet the rail, the pinned icons travelled
further as their 12px indent vanished, and the pinned list jumped up when its heading went.

**One geometry for both states** (`components/shell/rail-motion.ts`). A row stretches to its column, so
in the 50px rail it is the 32px square by construction, and only its inset changes: `--nav-px` (8px)
beside a label, `--nav-rail-px` (a derived 6px that centres a 20px glyph in the rail) in it — a 2px
glide. Labels stay mounted and FADE: out in 100ms as the rail closes, in after a 100ms delay as it opens,
so they are never revealed mid-reflow. The brand is one element whose wordmark fades (a new
`wordmarkStyle` on the DS `Logo`); the pinned indent glides out; the "Pinned" heading folds with
`grid-template-rows: 0fr`. Width, insets, indent and fold share one duration and curve —
`--duration-slow` on `--ease-standard`, Emil Kowalski's ease-in-out, because the sidebar is changing
shape on screen, not arriving. Both resting states are pixel-identical to before (measured: expanded
icons 17px, labels 45px, mark 13px; collapsed icons, control and mark 15px, rows 32px).

**Two fixes the measurement found on the way:** in the collapsed rail, hovering a pinned row faded its
glyph to nothing (the grip that takes the slot only exists expanded); and the pinned list's reserved
scrollbar gutter clipped every collapsed pinned pill to 26px beside the module rows' 32px squares, with
their icons 3px off the module icons' line. Now they share one line and one square.

**Verified:** `slow-motion.mjs sidebar` seeks every transition in the panel to the same MOMENT (0, 50,
100, 150, 200ms): collapse and expand both jump 0px on frame 0, module glyphs drift at most 2px, labels
are gone by 100ms, and every rail glyph ends on one line (spread 0px). Guard "the sidebar collapses in
place" (no re-centring, no label unmount, the heading folds, one shared motion) with a must-fail control;
`nav-rhythm.test.ts` updated; the layout-property guard now sees template-literal and grid-row
transitions (it read straight past `` `padding-left ${RAIL_MOTION}` ``). tsc clean; 173 tests in the
three affected files pass. Shown in the signed-in app, then the sidebar preference put back to default.

**A harness trap, not an app bug:** a debug branch in a scratch script left via `process.exit(0)`, which
skips `finally`, so its headless Chrome stayed alive on the debugging port — and every later run
silently connected to THAT browser, with the previous run's `zb-sidebar=collapsed` cookie. A "fresh
profile" read collapsed. Never exit inside the `try` of a CDP script; throw.

## A pause pauses — the toast clock — 2026-09-17

Emil Kowalski, from building Sonner: handle edge cases invisibly — "pause toast timers when the tab is
hidden", and fill the gaps between stacked toasts so hover holds. Zenboard's stack claimed "hover pauses
ALL timers", and measured on the Undo toast in `/dev-preview/confirm` it did not:

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rest the pointer on the Undo toast for 9s (its life is 8s), then leave | gone within 700ms | still there |
| Hidden tab for 9s, then back | gone | still there |
| Left alone, visible, 8.5s later (the control) | — | expired on time |
| Walk the pointer down an expanded stack of 5 | collapsed to 3 at the first gap | stayed 5 |

**Why.** Expiry was `Date.now() - createdAt`, the wall clock, so pausing the interval only POSTPONED
expiry: the moment the pointer left, every overdue toast went at once. A hidden tab kept aging them. And
each 8px gap between cards counted as leaving the stack, which resumed the clocks and collapsed an
expanded "+N more" while the pointer was on its way to a toast.

**Now** (`components/ds/ui/toast.tsx`): a toast clock (`toastLife`) that advances only by `lifeTick` —
no time while the pointer or focus rests on the stack or the tab is hidden — with the count restarted on
`visibilitychange` so a throttled hidden tab's first tick back cannot carry the whole absence. Each toast
is `bornAt` on that clock; a repeat restarts its life. `createdAt` stays wall-clock, for the dedupe window
only. Each card's `before:` bridges the gap above it.

**Verified:** unit tests (held or hidden counts nothing; a 60s pause gives back exactly the life left; a
repeat restarts; expiry never reads `Date.now()`; the bridge is present) · live, both halves above against
real input, each with the old behaviour reproduced first · the gap check fails with the bridge removed.
153 tests in the two files pass; tsc and eslint clean.

## The phone navigation drawer is a dialog to a keyboard — 2026-09-17

The drawer that plan 005 taught to enter from its own edge was still hand-rolled, which CLAUDE.md forbids
for a dialog, and measured with real keys at 390×844 it behaved like one nobody had tried with a
keyboard: **Tab walked straight out of it** into the page behind, **Escape did nothing**, and closing it
left focus nowhere near the button that opened it.

It is a Radix `Dialog` now (`components/shell/app-shell.tsx`): Escape closes it, Tab stays inside it, the
page behind is inert and stops scrolling, and Radix's Presence holds it for its exit — which retired the
`'closing'` state, the `animationend` handler and the 400ms timer floor plan 005 had needed. Because the
menu button lives in TopBar and BottomTabs rather than being a `Dialog.Trigger`, the opener is remembered
when the drawer opens and focus is handed back to it on close (Radix only restores to its own trigger).
The motion is unchanged: `slide-in-left` / `slide-out-left` on the drawer curve, the scrim a sibling that
fades, `zb-enter` so a key closes it at once.

**Verified** with `slow-motion.mjs navDrawer`, which now also drives the keyboard: before the change it
failed on `tabStaysInside`, `escapeCloses` and `focusReturns` with the motion checks passing; after, all
pass (40 Tabs never leave the drawer; Escape closes it; focus returns to "Open navigation"), and the
entrance still reads opaque from -230px to 8px. tsc clean; 150 tests in the affected files pass.

## A resize drag moves the panel, not the page — 2026-09-17

PageView's side peek and the DS Drawer each carried a copy of one resize handle ("identical to
PageView's", said the Drawer's comment), and both committed the width on every `pointermove`. PageView's
went through `usePeekWidth`, so each move wrote localStorage synchronously and re-rendered the whole open
page. Emil Kowalski's drag rule is the opposite: the pointer drives the element, and state is committed
once.

`components/ds/ui/panel-resize.tsx` is now the one handle. During a drag it writes the panel's
`style.width` in the same `min(<w>px, calc(100vw - 64px))` expression the panel renders, keeps
`aria-valuenow` current, lets one pointer drive, and commits once on release or cancel — so the commit
re-renders to exactly where the drag left it. The arrow keys still resize by 24px.

**Measured** (`/dev-preview/page-view`, 40 real pointer moves of 5px, dev build, a deliberately light page):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| localStorage writes during the drag | 40 | 0 (1 on release) |
| handler time per move, median / p90 / worst | 3.7 / 8.6 / 14.8ms | 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.4ms |
| handler time across the drag | 216ms | 35ms |
| final width | 755px | 755px |

A real document in the peek re-renders far more than the harness, so the before column is the floor. The
Drawer on `/dev-preview/panel-parity` measures 0.6ms per move after, follows the pointer the same 195px,
and the arrow key still adds 24px on both. Guard "a resize drag moves the element and commits once". tsc
and eslint clean.

## A Collection of hundreds — 2026-09-19 (COLLECTION_PLAN K12)

§45: "Collection could potentially contain hundreds or thousands of visual items. Design for this from the
beginning." Before this, every card of a Collection was in the page at once — each one signing a URL for its
upload and, for anything loaded without its metadata, asking its link what it is.

**The grid draws only what is near the screen.** Past 60 items, the masonry still places all of them (the page is
as tall as 250 cards, the scrollbar is honest) but only the cards meeting the window, plus 800px either side, are
in the DOM. Whatever scrolls — the pane, the window, a peek — is caught in the capture phase and the answer is read
from the grid's own box, so it works in every host. The window moves in 200px steps on an animation frame, not on
every scroll event. `cellsInView` (`lib/masonry.ts`) is the rule; a masonry's order is not its vertical order, so it
looks at every card rather than bisecting — 250 comparisons is nothing.

**The canvas draws only what the camera is looking at.** `viewRect` (`lib/canvas.ts`) turns the camera and the
frame into a world rectangle with a margin; the existing `hitTest` says which cards meet it. A card being dragged is
in the arrangement at its moved place, so it stays drawn wherever it is carried.

**Found while proving it: a card scrolled into view pushed everything under it.** The grid guessed an unmeasured
card at 4:3; the card itself drew a link's tile at 0.525. Every card that arrived corrected the guess, and the
whole grid shifted 2.7% as you scrolled. The grid now guesses exactly what the card will draw before its picture
answers (`tileShape`, exported from the card): **0.2%**.

**Deliberately not done:** YouTube thumbnails "at the size shown". `hqdefault` (480×360, ~25KB) is the only
variant whose absence is detectable — a missing video answers with a 120×90 grey image we treat as no picture.
`mqdefault` answers a missing video with a 320×180 grey image that would draw as a real one, and
`sddefault`/`maxresdefault` do not exist for many videos at all. The largest card needs ~700px on a 2× screen;
hqdefault is within reach and safe. Recorded, not "fixed".

**Measured with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-collection-many.mjs` (new): 250 links pasted into the
empty Moodboard in five pastes (one paste takes 50, as anyone's would):
- **A:** "250 items", a grid 13,113px tall — and **28 cards drawn, 588 elements, where all 250 would be ~5,250.**
- **C:** scrolled 4,000px, a different run of cards is drawn (54, by id), the grid height moved 0.2%.
- **D:** back at the top, the same first card.
- **E:** a search that finds one draws one.
- **F:** the canvas at 100% draws 24 of 250; after Fit (10%) all 250 are genuinely on screen and all are drawn.
- `consoleErrors: []`. The 250 `/api/unfurl` requests are the COLLECT path asking each link once, by design
  (`lib/collect.ts`), not drawing — the check says so rather than counting them as a win or a loss.

**Guards,** watched failing first (4 new): `cellsInView` — what meets the window and a margin, and nothing
elsewhere; `viewRect` — the frame in world terms at any zoom and pan, and what `hitTest` takes.

`tsc` clean · **2457 tests / 160 files** (the suite grew with other sessions' work) · eslint clean.

### Recorded, not started
- **Below 60 items everything is drawn** — no window math and no settling for the Collections most people have.
- **Keyboard focus cannot reach an undrawn card** by Tab; ⌘A, Select all and the item's page do not depend on it.

## Editing a task, and putting it in a project — 2026-09-21

**The report (user, 2026-09-19):** "There not way to edit task and add project in task need add this." It was
right, and more than one thing was missing:
- **The task's panel had no Project control at all,** nor a List one. A task's project could be changed only by
  the Tasks list's `p` key or by dragging a card on the board — with a mouse, from the list or the panel, it
  could not be done.
- **Its Schedule chip offered Today and Inbox, nothing else** — "Friday" could not be said.
- **A row's ⋯ menu** offered Highlight · Today · Tomorrow · Inbox · Delete: no Open, no Project, no List.

**What shipped.**
- **The task's panel:** a **Project** chip (this space's projects, a check on the current one, "No project"), its
  **Workstream** chip right beside it, a **List** chip, and **Schedule is the DS date picker** (Today · Tomorrow ·
  This weekend · Next week · No date · a calendar). The subject's round toggle is now the square DS checkbox the
  list uses (CLAUDE.md: a task is never a radio circle).
- **Every row's ⋯ menu:** Open · Highlight · Schedule › · Project › · List › · Delete. Each submenu shows the
  task's current answer beside it, the way Linear's do; Project and List are radio groups, so the current one is
  announced. The `p` menu gained "No project", as `l` already had "No list".

**The rules, one place each** (`lib/task-scopes.ts`, the server applying the same ones):
- `afterProjectChange` — choosing the project a task already has writes nothing (a reorder inside its board
  column is not a move); **leaving a project leaves its workstream** (before, a task moved from Balluji to New
  life kept Balluji's "Design" workstream — a row that could never draw correctly again); joining one leaves the
  Inbox; and a task left with **no project, no day and no list goes back to the Inbox** instead of living
  nowhere the rail shows.
- `afterDayChange` — "No date" keeps a task in its project or list (un-scheduling client work must not throw it
  back into triage); only a task with neither goes to the Inbox.
- `moveTaskToProject` applies the rule in the database with a filter, so a same-project call touches no row, and
  validates the id before it goes into a filter string. `rescheduleTask(id, null)` is the new "no day".

**Found while proving it, and fixed in this sprint (it is this sprint's area):**
- **Opening a task threw the page behind it away.** Every opener wrote `${pathname}?task=${id}` and the panel
  closed to the bare `pathname`: open a task from the Balluji project, close it, and you were in the Inbox.
  `lib/task-address.ts` (`taskOpenHref` / `taskClosedHref`) keeps every other setting of the page; the Tasks page,
  Home, Projects and the panel's close all use it.
- **⋯ → Open opened the panel and it shut at once.** The closing menu handed focus back to its button, outside
  the panel, which read that as a dismissal. Open alone asks the menu not to (`onCloseAutoFocus`).
- **The panel's writes were fire-and-forget.** The new chips put the chip back and say so when the server refuses
  ("The server refused it. Your change was undone.").
- **"ScheduleInbox".** A submenu row's current value, placed in its label, ran straight into the label — the DS
  submenu trigger wraps its children in one truncating span. The DS gained the slot instead of the screen
  working around it: `DropdownMenuSubTrigger value=…`, right-aligned before the chevron in secondary ink that
  steps up on the highlight wash (the item `description`'s rule). Every other submenu is unchanged — the slot
  draws nothing when it is not given.

**Proved with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-task-edit.mjs` (new). The panel reads the database
directly, so it had never been staged; the tasks harness now mounts it as the app shell does, and the check
answers every `/rest/v1/` and `/auth/v1/` read itself (nothing reaches the real database) and RECORDS every save's
arguments:
- **A** the ⋯ menu reads Open · Highlight · Schedule · Project · List · Delete.
- **B** Project › Balluji saves `["t1","p1"]` and the task leaves the Inbox (that is what filing means).
- **C** inside Balluji, List › Priority saves `["t3","L1"]`; the row reads Balluji · Priority.
- **D** ⋯ → Open shows the task over Balluji (`?scope=project%3Ap1&task=t4`) and closing returns to Balluji.
- **E** the panel: a square 16px checkbox, chips Inbox · Project · List · High · 30m · Timebox · …
- **F** Project offers Balluji and New life — never "Other studio", another space's project.
- **G** New life saves `["t1","p2"]`; the Schedule chip moves from Inbox to Schedule.
- **H** Balluji · Design → New life: the Design workstream chip goes with it; saves `["t3","p2"]`.
- **I** No project, with nowhere else to be: the chip reads Inbox; saves `["t3",null]`.
- **J** List › Priority saves `["t3","L1"]`.
- **K** Tomorrow saves `["t3","2026-09-22"]`; No date saves `["t3",null]` and — in a list — stays out of the Inbox.
- **L** a refused save puts the chip back and says so.
- **N** from the keyboard: Enter opens the Project picker with focus inside, ↓ moves, Enter picks
  (`["t3","p2"]`), focus returns to the chip.
- **M** dark; and at 390px the picker stays on screen (127→347). No console errors.

**Guards,** each watched failing first: `lib/task-scopes.test.ts` (7 new — both rules), `lib/task-address.test.ts`
(5 new — open keeps the page, swaps rather than stacks a task, close removes only the task).

`tsc` clean · **2469 tests / 161 files** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean on every file
touched (two dead lines in `today-view.tsx` removed to get there: an unused icon and an unused value).

**Motion and polish (Emil Kowalski's rules and better-ui, applied to what changed):** nothing new animates. The
chip panels already obey "nothing a keyboard opens animates" — `zb-enter` with `!important`, which beats their
inline entrance — and scale in at 0.98 from the chip when a pointer opens them. The row menu's submenus are the
DS's origin-aware Radix menus. A chip that carries a value fills its glyph (the folder takes the project's
colour); an empty one is the outline — one icon, recoloured per state.

### Recorded, not started
- **The harness rail writes absolute `/tasks?…` addresses,** so a rail click leaves the harness for the real
  route; the check loads scopes by address instead. Pre-existing, harness-only.
- **The Tasks list behind an open panel updates when the panel closes** (the navigation re-renders the route), as
  it always has for every chip in the panel.
- **"Inbox" is not in the panel's date picker.** It is a place, not a date: the row menu, the `s` key and Triage
  offer it; "No date" on a task with nowhere else to be puts it there.

## The task panel, decluttered — 2026-09-21

**The brief** (user, with a screenshot of the dark panel): "we have to enhance this design and match right so
much cluttered". Measured on that screenshot: ten equal grey pills under the title (Inbox · Buildojo · List · High
· Estimate · Timebox · Waiting for · Remind · Repeat · Labels) of which three carried a value; three empty section
headings each with a sentence saying it was empty (Subtasks, Files, Comments); and the header repeating the title.
The reference is Linear's issue panel and a Notion page: a property with no value is either absent or a quiet
outline of itself, and a section with nothing in it says nothing.

**What shipped**
- **Fill marks the value; the empty control is its outline.** `chipClass(active)` (task-detail/chip-ui): a chip
  with a value is filled; an empty one is a ghost — its word and glyph in secondary ink, a wash only under the
  pointer or while its panel is open. One control recoloured by state (better-ui), never two.
- **Secondary properties fold.** Schedule, Project and Priority always show; List, Labels, Estimate, Timebox,
  Remind, Repeat and Waiting for show when they carry a value, the rest behind **More** ("Show 7 more
  properties"), which is remembered (`zb:task-panel:all-properties`). A set property never hides.
- **The header names where the task lives** — its project (tinted folder), list, Inbox or Tasks — not the title a
  second time. A subtask's header keeps its crumbs.
- **Sections speak only when they have something to say.** No "No subtasks yet" / "No files yet" / "No comments
  yet"; the Subtasks and Activity headings appear with their first item; Files is `AttachmentsPanel quiet`.
- **One add line.** "Add a subtask…" and "Add file" are the DS's new `AddLine` / `addLine` (field and button
  shapes of one geometry): glyphs on the panel's column (x 899 = the checkbox = the description), words on one
  column (921), both 14px on 36px rows in ink-500. They had drifted 4px, a weight step and a type size apart. Under
  existing subtasks the line becomes the tree's next row — + on the box column (925 = 925), words on the names
  (947 = 947) — by moving only its inset, so the field is never remounted under a typing hand.
- **Every field is a DS field.** The panel's four page editors adopt `inlineEdit` (+ a new `ui` size) and declare
  `data-chromeless`; the chip menus' three fields (New label…, Wait for another task…, reminder time) are
  `MenuField`, per the overlay-chrome directive.
- **A selection mark is drawn or not.** Every chip menu drew EVERY row's check at 15% opacity, which read as "all
  ticked". `SelectMark` keeps the slot (names stay aligned) and draws the check only on the chosen row; the rows
  now say so to a screen reader (`aria-pressed`), and Priority marks its current value, which it never did.
- **A subtask row is a task row:** `text-ui` like `TaskRow`, not a step smaller. File rows take the DS icon
  scale's list-row glyph (`sm`, 8px gap), so a file's name starts where Add file's word does.
- **An emptied name is not a rename:** leaving the field restores the name instead of showing a blank title over a
  task that still has one (nothing is saved).

**Found while proving it, and fixed in this sprint (its area):**
- **The placeholders were a faded ink.** The panel's editors wore their chrome in style objects, which the
  chromeless guard (it reads class strings) cannot see — so they also had no placeholder rule and wore Chrome's:
  the text colour at 50% alpha. Measured in dark: L 0.51 against the house ink-500's 0.70.
- **Escape inside a chip's menu closed the whole task.** Radix's document listener on the side peek ran first;
  the chip panel now declares `data-owns-escape` (PageView's rule).
- **A keyboard → pointer hand-change replayed the panel's entrance.** `html[data-input=keyboard]` switches
  entrances off; flipping back to pointer switched the side peek's `slide-in-right` back ON and replayed it from
  off-screen under the press, so the click landed on nothing. At the flip, `lib/input-modality.ts` now stamps
  every entrance already on screen `data-entered`, which keeps it settled.
- **Pressing a toast closed the side peek**, and toasts sat over its message box. PageView's three surfaces exempt
  `[data-toaster]` from "interact outside", and an open side peek publishes `--peek-inset`, which the toast stack
  uses to rise beside the panel (measured: toast right 860, panel left 876).
- **`transition-colors` on the chips was dead**: the global button rule is unlayered and outranks every
  transition utility — it already carries the press and the hover curve (measured on a chip: transform 100ms
  ease-out-quiet, colour 100ms ease). Removed; the press guard now states the class-helper invariant.

**Proved with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-task-edit.mjs`, extended: E–N as before, plus
**R** (refusals: priority, name, done, a label, a message — each reverts and says so; Escape in a chip menu
closes only it; the Labels chip reopens after the keyboard → pointer change; a toast rises beside the panel and
pressing it leaves the panel open), **S** (a three-line name and notes grow whole; the subtask box is square with
its priority edge; a focused row action shows; the tree add line's columns; an emptied name restores with no
save), **T** (folded chips + "Show 5 more properties", remembered, folded again; header "Inbox" / "Balluji"; no
empty sentences; ghost vs filled computed colours and the ghost's hover wash; the chip's computed transitions; the
two add lines' columns, sizes, rows and inks; every placeholder = ink-500; Labels/Project/Priority marks and
`aria-pressed`; the new-label MenuField's chromeless declaration, wash and ink), **M** (dark; 390px keeps the
Project picker on screen). No console errors.

**Guards**, each watched failing on a mutated copy first: `app/design-system.test.ts` — "the task panel's quiet
parts are the system's" (every field in the panel is `inlineEdit`/`MenuField`; no faded selection mark anywhere in
the app; both add lines are the DS add line) and the press guard's chip-helper clause; `lib/input-modality.test.ts`
(entrances on screen are settled at the keyboard → pointer flip).

`tsc` clean · **2473 tests / 161 files** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean on every file
touched.

### Recorded, not started
- **The DS mirror is not a mirror.** `design-system`'s `sync:web:check` reports 50 drifted files and 35 web-only
  ones; the web copy is ahead (dropdown-menu ≈426 lines, toast ≈206), so `sync:web` would silently overwrite them
  (the 2026-07-18 incident). `AddLine` and `inlineEdit`'s `ui` size exist only in the web copy, like `menu.tsx` and

  it is its own sprint.
- **The panel body's insets are literals** (22 for the subject, 14 for row lists) rather than a token like
  `--panel-px`; they now agree with each other, but the number lives in the drawer.

## An uploaded image survives reopening its doc — 2026-09-21

**The report** (user, with a screenshot of "Discussion call with client" showing three empty "Add an image"
blocks): "when I upload image on this document it's visible but when I reopen that same document image is not
visible."

**Root cause.** `normalize()` (lib/blocks.ts) is the trust boundary every document is read through, and it keeps
only the fields it names. Since uploads moved to storage (0033) an uploaded image is stored as `{ fileId, fileName,
fileSize }` with `src` cleared — and normalize named `src`, `width` and `align`, never `fileId`. So: upload → visible
(editor state) → autosave writes the `fileId` (the database was right) → reopen → normalize drops it → "Add an
image" → the NEXT autosave writes the stripped block over the stored one. Uploaded PDFs and files the same. It is
the second field this function dropped in silence (line-item prices were the first). The files were never touched:
each is an `attachments` row owned by its page, and nothing garbage-collects them.

**What shipped**
- **The fix:** `uploadOf` in `normalize` keeps `fileId` (only if uuid-shaped — a forged path is dropped),
  `fileName` (≤200) and `fileSize` (finite, ≥0) on every media block.
- **The guard** (`lib/blocks-roundtrip.test.ts`): `FIELDS: Record<keyof Block, true>` — TypeScript refuses the file
  until every field of `Block` is listed — plus one full fixture per block type; each must survive save → JSON →
  reopen unchanged, and every field must be exercised. A new field that normalize forgets now fails a test.
- **Recovery for docs already re-saved without their images:** an empty image, PDF or file block offers "Uploaded to
  this doc" — the page's uploads that nothing on it shows (not a block, not the cover, not a property:
  `unplacedUploads` over the stored row; `unplacedPageUploads`, one round trip, asked only when a block could take
  one). One press puts a file back. The person places them; the editor does not guess which block each belonged
  to. Placements subtract live, so a file put back in one block stops being offered in the others.
- **Signed proposals stay signed:** a signature taken before the fix hashed an uploaded image as nothing, so the fix
  alone would have marked it "edited". A doc now carries every fingerprint it may have been signed under
  (`canonicalizeForSignature(…, { uploads: false })`; `acceptanceStatus` over a list).
- **Found proving it — a row that never repainted:** `BlockRow`'s custom memo comparator lists the data a row
  paints from, and missed everything that arrives after the row does. The offer landed and never appeared; and in
  production a signed proposal opened showing the UNSIGNED form until something else repainted its row. The
  comparator now names `uploads`, `acceptance`, `docHashes`, `acceptInvoices` (handed only to the rows that paint
  them, as stable references, so typing still skips every row).
- The PDF/file block's link row wraps at phone width (its field was squeezed to "Pa").

**Proved with trusted input** — `scripts/verify/verify-doc-uploads.mjs` (new), on the documents harness's
`pUploads` and `pProposal` docs. Server actions are answered BY NAME from Next's own action manifest, reads and
storage are answered locally, and every save's arguments are recorded. 18 assertions: **A** the stored image opens
as its file; **B** image blocks offer images only, the PDF block its PDF; **M** 390px has no overflow and 56px
thumbnails; **C** a pick fills the block, the other block stops offering it, the save carries the `fileId`; **D** an
upload runs ticket → storage PUT → record, the block shows it, the save carries its `fileId`; **E** Tab reaches the
offered PDF with a visible focus ring and Enter picks it; **F** leave the doc and reopen it — every image is still
there, each the right file (the report); **P** a signed proposal repaints to "Accepted by …" when its signature
lands, a pre-fix signature reads accepted, and one no reading matches reads edited. No console errors.
**Must-fail controls:** the old normalize fails A and F exactly as the screenshot did (every image back to "Add an
image"); the old comparator never shows the offer; without the signature props a signed proposal opens unsigned.

`tsc` clean · **2512 tests** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean on every file touched.

### Recorded, not started
- **Deploy.** The fix reaches the live app only when deployed (needs the owner's Cloudflare login). Until then every

## The Calendar, made to read — 2026-09-21

**The brief** (user, via Emil's skill): "there are lots of things we have to enhance visually and make the calendar
more visually good" — and mid-sprint, with two screenshots: grabbing an ochre event turned it magenta and "New e…".
Audited every view at 1440×900 in both themes before touching anything (`scripts/verify/capture-calendar.mjs`
writes the same frames before and after). Benchmarked against Notion Calendar and Google: neutral cards on a white
grid, a later overlapping event stacked on the earlier one, the grid's zone named in its gutter, the dragged block
previewed as itself.

**What was wrong — four of them correctness, not taste**
- **Every month column was named for the wrong day.** The cells start on the app's week start (Monday) but the header
  printed a fixed Sunday-first list: Monday the 21st sat under "Sun".
- **Event cards did not read as objects.** The grid sat on `paper-2` and the neutral card fill is almost the same
  grey: measured card/grid contrast **1.01** in light, and in dark the card was the DARKER of the two. The user's
  2026-09-07 decision (the accent marks the bar only, never floods the card) is kept — the fix is the surface.
- **Overlaps split the column evenly whatever their times.** A 15-minute standup half an hour into a meeting took
  half the column; the meeting read "Des…" and its time wrapped onto three lines ("09:30 / – / 10:30").
- **The gutter said "GMT" in India**, beside a composer that said "GMT +5:30 Calcutta".
- **Month chip times read "07"** — `.replace(':00', '')` was a 12-hour trick, and the house clock is pinned 24-hour.
- **The neighbouring months outshone this one** (`paper-3/60` is white in light, lighter than the grid in dark).
- **The drag preview was hard-wired to the default colour and "New event"** (the user's report).
- The composer grew from its own centre beside the click, and its footer had two filled buttons (a solid red Delete).

**What shipped**
- `lib/calendar-layout.ts` (new, pure, tested): the one layout rule. A later event at least `CASCADE_MIN` (30)
  minutes past the start of what it overlaps STACKS on it, stepped in 12px per level (to `MAX_DEPTH` 3); only close
  starts take columns; an event widens into columns free for its whole span; on a tied start the longer goes left.
- The grid is the bright surface (`bg-paper`: grid container, sticky header, all-day lane; cards' gap ring
  follows). Measured after: card/grid **1.12 light, 1.11 dark**, card lighter than grid in dark.
- One `EventFace` for the card and the drag ghost: a moved or resized block previews as itself; only a new block is
  "New event". Times never wrap (`truncate`); a block under ~half an hour is one line, name then start time, and a
  narrow card (container query, < 9rem) keeps the name and drops the time its position already shows.
- The gutter names the zone (`gmtLabel` → "GMT+5:30"), client-only via `useSyncExternalStore` (the server's zone
  is UTC).
- Month: header from `monthHeader(anchor)` (the cells' own first week), neighbouring months on the page tone
  (`bg-background`), chip times as the house clock ("07:00").
- Composer: grows from the click point (`transformOrigin` from its anchor; centred only when unanchored); Delete is
  the DS default destructive (`dangerGhost`) — Save is the one filled button.

**Proved** — `scripts/verify/verify-calendar.mjs` (new), trusted input on `/dev-preview/calendar` (the harness gained
an ochre event), **20 assertions**: S surfaces (contrast measured as painted pixels, both themes) · Z zone label ·
O stack geometry (review spans its column, standup stepped in 12px and drawn above, review's title whole) · T no
wrapped times, short names whole · D the ochre event's ghost has the card's own bar colour and name, and lands an
hour later · C composer origin = the click clamped into the panel, Delete unfilled · M Monday-first header with
today under its own weekday, neighbouring months darker, every chip time `dd:dd`. **Must-fail controls:** the old
surfaces measure 1.01 and a darker card in dark; the old ghost is magenta "New event" beside an ochre card (the
report, reproduced). Unit tests watched failing first: the layout (4 behaviours red on the old rule), the header and
clock guards (red on the old month grid), the composer-origin guard (red without the origin).

`tsc` clean · **2529 tests** in UTC, Asia/Kolkata and America/Los_Angeles · eslint clean on every file touched.
`calendar-view.tsx` is shared with the perf session's planned server-side week load: one token changed there, and
they were told the exact line first.

### The default event colour is a palette colour — 2026-09-21 (same sprint, user follow-up)

"Why does the default colour look so bad and other colours look good?" — two screenshots: an ochre event and a
default one. Every palette hue is a TRIO (dot · a pale fill · a softened ink, one family); after 2026-09-07 the
default was the accent bar alone on a neutral card with neutral text — a stripe pasted onto grey beside cards that
looked finished. The 09-07 complaint ("a wall of one hue") was real, but its cause was the saturated accent used AS
TEXT over a 16% wash, not colour on the card as such.

- `--event-accent-bg` = `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) var(--event-tint), var(--color-paper))` and
  `--event-accent-text` = `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 45%, var(--color-ink-900))` (globals.css); `--event-tint`
  is 7% in light and 12% in dark (tokens-light.css), as pale as the palette's own fills. `eventTokens('accent')`
  returns the trio; all of it follows Appearance → Accent.
- `lib/event-color.test.ts` (new, 26): recomputes the trio from the CSS's own percentages for all six accents in both
  themes — text on its fill ≥ 4.5:1 (worst measured 5.39), the fill 1.03–1.16 off the card (the palette's band).
  Watched failing first.
- Browser: default card `#FBEFF5` on white (1.12) in light, `#34202A` on `#202020` in dark (1.08, lighter than the
  grid); the drag and all 20 calendar assertions still pass.
- Turbopack served a stale `globals.css` (its import updated, it did not): `rm -rf .next` + restart, checked in the
  served stylesheet. The compiler also emits a plain-accent fallback before an `@supports (color-mix)` block — expected.
- The user's screenshots came from the old build (times still wrap, grid still grey): none of today's calendar work
  is visible to them until it is deployed.

## One task, drawn one way — 2026-09-22 (product polish, sprint 1)

The user's brief (2026-09-22): Zenboard feels "immature, inconsistent, and somewhat like an AI-generated
application"; use `emil-design-eng` and `better-ui` throughout and make it feel like one carefully made product.
The sprint began with an audit, not a screen: every `/dev-preview` harness captured at 1440×900 in light and dark
(`scripts/verify/capture-surfaces.mjs`, new) and read side by side. Findings, ranked, and the order of work are in
`plans/PRODUCT_POLISH_2026-09-22.md`. The first finding is the app's central object drawn five ways.

**What was wrong**
- Two task rows. Home and a project's Tasks tab drew one 36px line; the Tasks page kept a roomy row of its own
  (title over a line of grey capsules), 61px or 82px depending on whether a row had a chip — the Inbox stepped
  61 → 82 → 61 down the page.
- Four priority marks: bars with a red word (Home), bars in a grey capsule (Tasks), a flag (Focus), a 3px tick
  whose label vanished when a week column narrowed. Three project marks: a dot, a filled folder, a rounded square.
  A second `PriorityBars` (raw colour) in `components/ui/panels.tsx` drew Home's highlight card.
- Circles for tasks in Focus — a hairline ring for "Up next" that only switched tasks, a filled disc for done that
  did nothing — against CLAUDE.md's "Tasks are never radio circles". Focus's checked subtask was the accent; every
  other checked box is ink.
- Four ways to add: `QuickAddRow` (a 48px grey slab reading "Add Task", title case — and a second copy of it in
  `ui/primitives.tsx`), Focus's ⊞ "Add a task to today…", the board's hand-spelled line, and the DS `AddLine`.

**What shipped**
- `components/tasks/task-meta.tsx` (new): THE facts of a task — blocked · project · list · labels · priority ·
  subtasks · repeat · when · estimate · star, in that order, only what is set (a bare task draws nothing). Glyph and
  word in meta ink, no capsules (`Blocked` keeps its tag: it asks you to wait). At phone width where a task lives goes
  to screen readers whole and priority gives up its word — measured at 390px, the busiest row's title went from
  **28% to 41%** of the row.
- `PriorityBadge` has one shape: coloured bars, neutral word. A red "High" beside red bars said it twice with the
  larger area; the chroma rule puts the hue on the glyph. The `chip` variant is gone with the row that needed it.
- `TaskRow` is the one row: one height (`--row-task`), facts through `TaskMeta`, and ONE ••• that always carries Open
  and Highlight, then the surface's own verbs (`menu`: the Tasks page's Schedule · Project · List · Delete) and a
  project's Move to. A highlighted row's star is the filled glyph — the toggle's grey tile behind it was the heaviest
  thing in the list. The Tasks page's `Row` is deleted; inside a project's own list the row no longer names that
  project on every line (same for a list).
- `AddLine lead="checkbox"`: under task rows the + sits in the checkbox's 16px slot and the word where titles start.
  The Tasks page, Focus (Add subtask, Add task) and the board use it; `QuickAddRow` (both copies) is deleted.
- Focus: the house checkbox everywhere (the hero a step larger), `TaskMeta` for the focused task, an Up next box that
  COMPLETES (the title still switches), a done box that reopens (`reopen`, new), plain `text-overline` labels (the
  `tracking-[0.08em]` was a leftover from the uppercase era). The board's cards and Home's highlight card draw
  `TaskMeta`, so the highlight card and its row in the plan say exactly the same facts.

**Proved** — `scripts/verify/verify-task-row.mjs` (new), trusted input, nothing reaching a database: A every Tasks row
36px (control: the Completed disclosure measures 32 — the ruler tells heights apart) · B the add line's + on the
checkboxes' centre line and its word on the titles' start, both **0px** off (control: its word is 20px off the
boxes) · C `j` moves the cursor and the row takes the selected wash · D facts in the one order · E phone: where-it-
lives gone, priority glyph-only, estimate whole · F Focus: 6 square boxes, 0 circles; complete, reopen and a subtask
tick each saved (`["f2",true]`, `["f4",false]`, `["s1",true]`) · G Focus's add lines 0px off · H Home's highlight
card and plan row both read TechSpark · High · 5h · I a project row's ••• = Open · Highlight · Move to (4 streams).
`verify-task-edit.mjs` re-run end to end (A–T, M): the row menu, filing into a project and a list, Open over a
project, and every panel edit — its helpers now read the shared row. Unit: `task-meta.test.ts` (new, 10) watched
failing first (module missing, then 5 source guards red on the old code); the phone rule mutation-checked (red with
the project fact's class removed). Existing guards moved with the code: quiet-list, task-row-quiet, row-surface,
project-phone.

`tsc` clean · **2565 tests / 166 files** · eslint clean on every file touched (the Home harness's pre-existing
set-state-in-effect is fixed: it reads the query through `useSearchParams`).

**A trap worth keeping.** The first full run of verify-task-edit "closed the task panel on Send". It was the Next.js
dev badge (`<nextjs-portal>`), which sits exactly over the panel's Send button at 1440×900: the click landed on the
badge and Radix rightly read it as a press outside. Production has no badge; both scripts now hide it on every
document (`Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`). Traced with Radix's own `dismissableLayer.pointerDownOutside`
event, which names the element that was pressed.

## Home reads as a page, not a dashboard — 2026-09-22 (product polish, sprint 2)

Second finding of the product-wide audit (`plans/PRODUCT_POLISH_2026-09-22.md`). Captured whole
(`capture-surfaces.mjs` now takes `FULL=1` for the entire page), Home was **seven stacked panels, each with a grey
header band and an icon** — highlight, plan, a separately boxed "Completed", waiting, content, schedule, habits — so
every section weighed the same and the page read as an admin dashboard, the most "generated" look in the product.

**What was wrong, besides the boxes**
- The highlight was named three times: in the greeting's sentence ("You've committed to 2 tasks. Highlight: …"), in
  its own banded panel ("Today's highlight — Do this first", with a › to Tasks and a "Details ›" beside a clickable
  title), and as the first starred row of the plan under it.
- Four row heights on one page: tasks 36px, waiting/content 41px, habits 48px (15px type), schedule entries ~100px.
- The schedule labelled Zenboard's own timeboxes "Google Calendar" (`source !== 'manual'` counted a timebox as
  synced), put a duration pill on every entry, drew "now" as a black slab (the Calendar draws it in the accent), and
  had a "Today Tue 22 ⌄" row whose caret opened nothing.
- Habits and Schedule hand-rolled their hover actions (`opacity-0 … group-hover`) — unreachable on a phone.

**What shipped**
- Each section is the shared `SectionHeading` (the one Projects and Clients use; it gained a `summary` slot for prose
  beside `count` for figures) over rows that share ONE surface — `components/today/home-rows.ts`, the task row's own
  `rowSurface` at `--row-task`. Headings sit on the rows' inset, so every word on the page starts on one line.
- The highlight is the page's one card (`bg-surface-raised`, the house card), said once: "Highlight", the title, its
  `TaskMeta`, Start focus and Mark done; its star puts it down. The plan lists everything else, and the keyboard
  cursor walks that list. No highlight, no card.
- The greeting is one line and the day's load (the capacity sentence); the mark beside it is gone.
- The day's prompt (§7V staging unchanged) is one line — icon, sentence, "Plan the day ›" / "Shut down ›", dismiss —
  not a banded panel with a body and a button card.
- The plan's add is the house add line in its field shape; Completed sits in the plan, not in a second box.
- The schedule is an agenda: the range in its own column, then the name; the now marker is the Calendar's accent
  chip and line, in its own 20px slot (drawn on the boundary it covered the next entry's time). No duration pill, no
  source chip, no dead caret.
- Empty Schedule and Habits say one quiet line under their heading (the Add beside it is the action).
- A bordered card first used `bg-surface`, which no theme declares — the dead-colour guard caught it before a browser
  did. The card is `bg-surface-raised`, as Money's are.

**Proved** — `scripts/verify/verify-home.mjs` (new), trusted input: A no banded panel; headings Plan · Waiting on others
· Content today · Schedule · Habits; all 12 list rows 36px (control: the Completed disclosure 32) · B the card holds the
highlight and the plan lists only the rest · C `j` lands on the plan's row · D the card's star: card gone, the task
joins the plan, `["t1",false]` sent · E Mark done: card gone, "Completed (2)", `["t1",true]` · F typing shows the one
filled "Add"; Enter adds "Call Sam" with its parsed priority and estimate · G a habit tick sends `["h2",true]`; a
hovered row's actions at opacity 1; Add focuses "New habit", Escape puts it away · H the now chip is the accent and
overlaps no entry; Schedule's Add focuses "New event", Escape puts it away · I 09:00 shows the plan prompt and it
dismisses; 20:00 shows the shutdown prompt. Page height at 1440: **1,714 → 1,280px**; checked in dark and at 390px.
`components/today/home-page.test.ts` (new, 11), mutation-checked three ways (the plan listing the highlight again, a
"Google Calendar" string back in the schedule, a section dropping the shared row) — each turns it red.

`tsc` clean · **2576 tests / 167 files** · eslint clean on every file touched.
