## The Week board, on the design system — 2026-09-22 (product polish, sprint 3)

Third finding of the audit (`plans/PRODUCT_POLISH_2026-09-22.md`): the Week board was the last legacy island in
Tasks. **What was wrong:** a hand-rolled `ChipPop` portal (its own outside-click, scroll and Escape handling), a
hand-rolled ••• menu and a hand-rolled date picker, all inline styles on legacy tokens; a priority-ringed CIRCLE for
"done"; three always-on chips on every card, ghosts reading "Low", "Project" and "Estimate" where nothing was set; its
own capture grammar ("!!" meant high) beside the app's one; "TODAY" and "MOVE TO" in tracked capitals; empty days
that said "Open." or "Rest." and an empty staging column that said "Inbox zero. Enjoy it."; today's whole column
filled with ink at 6% — the largest tinted area on screen for the smallest fact on it — and **a card you could not
open**: drag, tick and delete, but no way into the task.

**What shipped**
- `components/tasks/task-card.tsx` (new): THE task card — the row stood up. Square box, a title that opens the task
  (three lines at most), the task's facts through `TaskMeta`, one ••• with Open and Highlight and then the surface's
  own verbs. The Tasks board's card and the Week board's are now this one component.
- `TaskMeta`'s phone rule is a ROW rule (beside a one-line title the facts compete for width; under a card's title
  they wrap and take nothing), and each word is marked `data-fact-word` so the week column's own container query can
  put it away — with the sr-only recipe, never `display:none`. `ds-theme.css`'s `@container weekcol` block is
  re-aimed at the shared card (`data-task-card`, `-title`, `-menu`) from the retired `data-week-chip*`.
- The week card's ••• is the DS menu: Open · Highlight · Move to (this week's days and Unscheduled) · Project · Delete.
- Adding is the house add line; pressed, it is a field in the ONE grammar (`lib/task-parse`) with the parsed chips as
  confirmation, like Home's. The column is the day, so a "when" token is left in the title rather than silently
  moving the task out of the column it was typed into.
- A day's heading is the Calendar's own: short weekday and date, today's date in the accent circle; every column
  heading is 44px, so every column's cards start on one line. Today wears the Calendar's `surface-row` whisper; a
  column held over takes the house `surface-active` wash with no accent outline through the carried card.
- Empty days say nothing (their add line is the invitation); the Unscheduled column says "Nothing unscheduled.".
  The capacity footer, the collapse spine and the stat line are on tokens.

**Proved** — `scripts/verify/verify-week.mjs` (new), trusted input on `/dev-preview/week`: A 5 cards, square boxes,
no ghost chips, no poetry, no capitals, one heading height (44), today's wash = `--color-surface-row` and its date
pill = `--accent` (both compared as computed colours) · B clicking a card's title sets `?task=u2` · C a real
multi-step drag from Unscheduled onto Wednesday lands there and saves Wednesday's date with the column's order ·
D the ••• reads Open · Highlight · Move to · Project · Delete; Move to › Friday moves it and saves · E Project ›
Balluji: the card names Balluji, `{"project_id":"p1"}` sent · F "Call Sam !high 30m" in Thursday's add line shows
High and 30m chips, then a card with High and 30m, `addTask` sent with Thursday's date · G Delete removes it and sends
`["u2"]` · H Unscheduled collapses to its spine and returns · I at 1280px a day is 140px: the card's words are
out of flow, its 3 glyphs stay, its ••• is absolute. Dark checked by eye. `components/week/week-board.test.ts`
(new, 9), mutation-checked (the grey today column back → red); `task-meta.test.ts` gained "a card keeps every word".

## Words as they are read — 2026-09-22 (product polish, sprint 4)

The house has been sentence case since 2026-09-08, guarded four ways (a `uppercase` class, an inline
`textTransform`, `{x.toUpperCase()}` in markup, the shared label role). The audit still found capitals on screen,
because all four guards look for capitals MADE by code — none could see capitals TYPED in: the Week board's "TODAY"
and "MOVE TO" (fixed in sprint 3), the database row's hover "OPEN" pill, the Rituals eyebrow "DAILY PLANNING" /
"DAILY SHUTDOWN" / "WEEKLY REVIEW" (tracked 0.12em). And the tracking that existed only to keep capitals legible
outlived them: seven files spelled a section label as `text-caption font-medium tracking-[0.02em] text-ink-500` —
an 11px private copy of the 12px `text-overline` role — and five more carried `tracking-wide` or 0.04–0.12em on
sentence-case words.

**What shipped**
- Three guards in `app/design-system.test.ts` (casing): **no capitals typed into markup** (JSX text or a string of two
  or more capitalised words; acronyms and IDs pass) · **no capital-era tracking on words** (initials drawn
  `aria-hidden`, monospaced IDs and the DS menus' shortcut glyphs pass) · **a section label is the `text-overline`
  role**, never the 11px copy. Each proven red by a mutation of the old spelling (the eyebrow tag, the OPEN pill, a
  0.04em label, the private recipe), green after.
- The seven label copies are the role (Tasks rail, Clients, Automations, Projects, Meetings, the formula editor, doc
  properties); the Calendar rail's collapsible heading moved from ink-600 to the same ink-500 as the Tasks rail's, so
  the two rails' headings are one thing. Forms (Link, Embed, Where people stop) and Finance's table headers dropped
  their tracking; the lightbox counter dropped a 0.02em the caption token already carries.
- The database row's pill reads "Open" — Notion's anatomy, Zenboard's voice.
- **Rituals:** the eyebrow is the ritual's own name in sentence case ("Plan your day"), not a second, shouted name;
  subtitles are the house family (they were an italic serif at h2 size — a second typeface on the screen the day
  starts on); **the morning ritual starts on its first real question** — the intro step was a slogan ("A calm
  start." / "Three minutes to shape the day before it shapes you.") and a Begin button, one more click every
  morning; statement titles lost their full stops and the slogans went: "That's a lot of day." → "More than fits in
  today", "Today's rhythm." → "Habits due today", "Ready. Your day is set. Go make it count." → "Your day is planned"
  (its summary line already says the rest), "One honest line." → "A note on today", "Carry the lesson, not the
  guilt." → "What would you keep, and what would you change?".
- Touched files are now lint-clean including their older warnings (Clients' unused `PropDot`, `lastTouch`, two
  unused props; Finance's ternary-as-statement).

**Proved** — the guards above (watched red, then green) · `/dev-preview/rituals` captured: "Plan your day" eyebrow,
"Step 1 of 4 · Pick today's highlight", body-font subtitle · Tasks and Calendar rails captured with the one heading.
`tsc` clean · **2589 tests / 168 files** · eslint clean on every file touched.

### Recorded, not started
- Rituals is still inline styles and hand-rolled step buttons and pick rows — its own sprint (the copy and casing are
  done).
- The Tasks and Calendar rails each keep their own collapsible-heading component (now typographically one);
  merging them is a component job.

empty." Plain sections under headings had left a mostly white page; the cards give each part of the day a place and a
weight even when it is nearly empty. The cards are the design; the improvements live inside them.

- `PanelHeader`'s title is an `h2` — the cards were absent from the page's heading outline; it looks exactly the same.

each broken moment into the open tab. Both were fixed within the minute and every run since is clean.

## Goals and the portal on the house card — 2026-09-22 (product polish, sprint 5)

Two screens still spoke a softer, older dialect than the app around them. A goal was a grey-filled panel on the grey
page that drew ONE percentage twice — a 52px ring and a bar under it — faded a dropped goal's whole card to 60%
(title, dates and all, below readable contrast), opened a hand-rolled menu that closed the moment the pointer left
it, picked its project in a native `<select>` (the OS's blue list inside a Zenboard card), set its note and retro in an
italic serif, and fired every save without reading the answer: a refused write left the screen claiming a change the
server never made. The client portal — the one screen a studio's clients see — drew its own card language (`paper-2`
fill at the larger `r-xl`/`r-2xl` radii) with a filled button on every card, so a review list read as a row of
competing calls to action.

**What shipped**
- **A goal is the house card**: `rounded-lg border border-line bg-surface-raised`, title at `text-h4`, facts on one
  meta line (tasks or steps · target date · project). **One progress mark**: `CircularProgress` gained a 16px GLYPH
  — an outline and a filled pie, the way Linear marks a project. At 16px the large ring's arc read as a spinner
  ("wait"), not "60% there"; the number is in the meta line, so the glyph carries none.
- A dropped goal is struck through in ink-500 with a "Dropped" badge — never faded; a done goal gets "Done" (success)
  and reads its retro line back.
- On the design system: the ••• is the DS `DropdownMenu` (Mark done / Reopen / Drop); the project is `MenuSelect`; the
  target date is `DatePicker` in a `Field`; steps are the square `Checkbox`; "Add a step" is the shared `addLine`

- **Every write reads its answer**: one `save(id, next)` patches optimistically, and on refusal puts the old value back
  and says so (`toastReverted`); adding and ticking steps do the same.
- **`cn()` knew none of the theme's type sizes.** tailwind-merge files an unknown `text-*` under colour, so
  `cn('text-h4', 'text-ink-900')` silently dropped the SIZE — the goal title fell back to the inherited size, and

  font-size group; `lib/cn.test.ts` reads the theme's `--text-*` sizes from the CSS, so a size added later is covered

- **The portal on the house card**: one `CARD` recipe for stat, form, status, approval and request cards; Approve,

  is tested; the Home and Goals harnesses read their flags with `useSearchParams` instead of setting state in an effect.

screenshot had made it look like a spinner). Portal captured in light and dark. Guards

## One card, and a first screen that shows the product — 2026-09-23

Two consolidations under the cohesion brief ("the whole product should feel like one design family;
consolidate multiple versions of the same pattern").

### One card

A card was spelled five ways for one job, and two of them were WRONG in a theme nobody had audited:

| spelling | fill in dark | sites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-paper` | **L12.3**, on an L8.7 canvas | Documents' gallery, the Collection Index |
| `bg-surface-raised` / `bg-paper-3` / `bg-card` | L21.2 | Goals, the portal, databases, boards |

In LIGHT all three names are pure white, which is why the audits (run in light) never saw it: the
Documents gallery's cards were a different object from every other card in the app only after dark.
The edge split the same way — 13 cards used `border-line-soft`, ink at 7%, which measures **1.01:1
against the light canvas**: the exact failure recorded in "Documents gallery contrast" (2026-09-11),
where a card read as "a white strip with a hole under it". The database board had already diagnosed
the dark half of this on 2026-09-15 and fixed it IN ITS OWN FILE; the DS and Documents kept the bug,
which is the case for fixing the system instead of the screen.

**What shipped** — `CARD_CLASS` / `cardClass()` / `cardInteractiveClass()` in `components/ds/ui/card.tsx`:
`rounded-lg border border-line bg-surface-raised`, no resting shadow (a card SITS; elevation belongs to
overlays and to the thing being dragged), and one hover language for an openable card — a wash over its
own fill (`wash-over`), never a border that thickens or a lift. Twenty call sites swept onto it across
Clients, Collections, databases, Feedback, Habits, Goals, Finance, the portal, Projects (×4), Tasks and
Triage, plus the DS `<Card>` component itself and the database board's card. Dropped on the way: two
resting `shadow-xs`, a third hover language (`hover:border-line`), and a `duration-fast` that only
restated the Tailwind default.

### The first screen showed nothing

The user, on the dark sign-up page: **"This also looks so boring."** A 400px card in the middle of an
empty 1440px page, carrying two slogans — "Two minutes from here to a calmer day.", "Sign in to your
quiet workspace." — which the house forbids and which say nothing true. Every sign-up form on earth has
an email field and a password field; if that is all a screen has, the screen IS the form.

**What shipped** — the page is a split from `lg`: the form on the left (no card — it is the page now),
and on the right the PRODUCT AT REST: today's plan and the day's schedule, drawn with the app's own

gradient, not a tilted screenshot — the same components the app ships, inert, `aria-hidden`, with no tab
stop, so a screen reader hears the form and nothing else. Below `lg` the still drops away entirely
rather than stacking above the form. The slogans are gone, the title is left-aligned at `h1`, and the
submit lost its trailing arrow (a button that says what it does need not point at itself).

## The Paper skin — the whole app as a printed sheet — 2026-09-23

The user, with nine references (a studio works index, a draw-entry form, a Govino spec sheet, a CAD
title block, a Herman Miller order form, manila folder tabs): a second theme, "mostly paper … the
entire theme changes the app into paper … it looks like 100% real paper". Two themes, Default and
Paper.

**What those references share is not a beige colour.** It is stock with visible fibre sitting on a
darker desk; rules that BOX things rather than hairlines that hint at them; square corners; no
elevation, because a scan is flat; and monospaced labels and figures set the way a form sets
SKU / QUANTITY / TOTAL. A beige repaint would have missed every one of those.

**What shipped**
- **A skin axis, separate from light/dark** (`lib/theme.ts`): `data-skin` on `<html>`, stored as
  `zb-skin`, stamped by the blocking boot script so the first paint is already paper. Paper resolves
  to the LIGHT surfaces — paper is a light material, and a dark paper is a different material
  (kraft, newsprint) — and the stored light/dark choice is untouched while it is on, and comes back
  when it is off. A skin flip holds transitions exactly as a theme flip does.
- **`app/theme-paper.css` overrides the ~25 SEMANTIC tokens and nothing else.** Zenboard's 558
  primitives derive from those, so one layer re-colours every card, menu, rail, chip, field and wash
  in the product without a single component knowing the skin exists. Radius tokens square every
  corner at once (the pill stays a pill — a switch is an object, not a box); every `--shadow-*`
  becomes `none` or the rule it was standing in for.
- **The grain is the part that had to be measured.** Grey noise laid over a fill at low alpha just
  greys the page: at 16% it was invisible (spread of 8 levels out of 250) and at 40% it was dirty.
  Paper does not work that way — its tooth subtracts light where a fibre sits proud. So two inline
  SVG turbulences (a fine tooth, a coarse mottle), each compressed into the top of the range by a
  component transfer and **multiplied** into the stock: measured spread 21 levels on the sheet, 19 on
  the desk, mean luminance down ~4%, ink contrast still 13:1. `stitchTiles` makes the tile seamless;
  no image request. A hover wash stacks ON the grain, so the texture never blinks off under the
  pointer.
- **The print voice, with no string changed**: the skin re-sets the ROLES — `text-overline` becomes
  monospaced capitals with the tracking capitals need, and `tabular-nums` / `[data-numeric]` become
  monospaced. Finance reads as a ledger (NUMBER · CLIENT · ITEMS · STATUS · DUE · TOTAL over ruled
  rows), the Tasks rail as a form's index. Internal row dividers move from ink 7% to 14%, because a
  form rules its rows.
- **Settings → Appearance → Theme** is now Default | Paper, with Light/Dark/System beneath it as
  the default skin's own control — disabled under paper, and saying why instead of doing nothing.
- `scripts/verify/capture-surfaces.mjs` takes `SKIN=paper`, stamped before the document runs so a
  capture photographs the skin rather than the first frame of the default one.

**The one declared break with the house rules.** CLAUDE.md caps surface chroma at 0.004 and forbids
monospace outside IDs. Both are DEFAULT-skin rules from the Notion palette directive (2026-09-08),
which reversed a warm pass that had put 3–4× Notion's tint on the largest surfaces. Paper is that
warmth on purpose, chosen by the person using it, in one switch they can turn off. CLAUDE.md now
says so, and the default skin is byte-for-byte untouched.

**Proved** — `app/theme-paper.test.ts` (10): the contrast ruler self-tested on two known pairs
first; every semantic token overridden (mutation-checked by deleting `--popover` — two tests go
red); ink and secondary ink ≥ 4.5:1 on all four stocks and the control edge ≥ 3:1; no shadow with a
blur; corners ≤ 4px; the grain inline, turbulent and stitched; and every selector in the file scoped
to `html[data-skin='paper']`, so the default skin cannot be changed from here. In the browser: the
switch flipped live in Settings both ways (`data-skin` + storage + the dependent row's copy and
disabled state), Home, Finance, Tasks, the shell and `/login` captured on paper, and the grain
measured through a canvas probe rather than eyeballed from a smoothed screenshot. `tsc` clean ·
**2641 tests / 173 files** · eslint clean on every file touched.

## Entering focus is one movement — 2026-09-23

Two notes from the user, one problem. First, with a screenshot of macOS's screen-recording border:
"when I go in focus mode on/off I want this gradient edge, like the OS and other applications."
Then, on the control: "just a toggle in the header looks boring… I want a smooth interaction that
feels like I'm entering focus mode, everything changes smoothly, like magic — one click and you're
in focus, quietly."

Focus mode already changes everything — the sidebar goes, the chrome goes, eleven ways out become
one — and the only thing that said so was a 28px switch, after which the screen was simply
REPLACED between two frames. A mode with no visible boundary is a page that lost its navigation.

**What shipped**
- **The room's light** (`components/shell/focus-edge.tsx`, `.zb-focus-edge`): the app frame lights
  from its edge for as long as the mode lasts — four inset shadows (a hairline that closes the
  frame, then three widening pools), in the accent, so it follows the accent the person chose and
  is the only accent on a focus screen. Mounted ALWAYS and carrying `data-on`, because focus is a
  route: a component rendered only while focused unmounts before it can fade out. It arrives over
  600ms on the arrival curve, blooming past its resting level and settling back (light steadies, it
  does not snap) and leaves in 100ms. Opacity only, in CSS, off the main thread — which matters
  because turning focus on navigates, and that is the busiest moment in the app's life.
  Its corner is CONCENTRIC with the frame (`--app-gutter`, now a token the shell reads too): the
  ring is at the viewport edge, the panels sit 4px inside it, so its radius is theirs plus the
  gutter. The user caught the mismatch with a zoom of the corner.
- **The change is one movement, not a cut** (`lib/view-transition.ts`): the navigation runs inside
  a view transition, so the sidebar leaving and the pane growing into its place are animated
  between — layout included, as composited snapshots rather than a width re-laid-out sixty times a
  second, which is the one thing plain CSS could not do here. React's `<ViewTransition>` needs a
  flag in `next.config.ts` (a file this session does not own); the raw API needs no configuration.
  The helper's whole trick is the promise: `router.push` returns long before the new route renders,
  so it settles when the URL has become the destination AND the browser has painted it, with a
  900ms guard so a slow or redirected navigation can never leave the page frozen.
- **Named pieces, so each one moves rather than dissolving**: the sidebar steps 12px towards the
  edge it lives on and fades in 200ms (an exit is the system responding); the main column morphs
  over 300ms; the header's control cluster is named in BOTH top bars, so entering focus TRAVELS it
  from six controls to one. The first build ghosted — every line of the header painted twice at two
  widths — because the browser scales each snapshot to fill the animating box; pinning both to
  their natural size at their own anchor (top left for the column, top right for the cluster) puts
  what is unchanged exactly on top of itself. A page's own entrance fade is suppressed while a
  transition runs (`html[data-vt]`), or it fades in content the browser is already cross-fading.
- **The toggle states the mode**: one glyph in two weights — an outline you are outside of, a
  filled disc you are inside — crossfaded with Emil's values (scale 0.25→1, blur 4px→0), both in
  the DOM so it reads as one mark transforming. It carries a tooltip naming its key.
- **`F` now TOGGLES.** It pushed `/focus` unconditionally, so the one key bound to the mode could
  enter it and never leave; pressing it again re-entered the route you were already on. Settings'
  shortcut list says "Focus mode on or off" from the same source.

**Proved** — `lib/view-transition.test.ts`: the helper settles only once the route has landed
(not on `router.push` returning), gives up rather than freezing when a navigation never lands,
marks and unmarks the document, and falls through to a plain navigation with no API or under
reduced motion. `components/shell/focus-interaction.test.ts` (13): the edge's mounting, inertness,
falloff stack, token timings, reduced-motion twin; the named pieces, the pinned snapshots, the
suppressed page fade; the toggle's glyph values and the key's toggle (mutation-checked by putting
the old `router.push('/focus')` back). In the browser: a real view transition driven in a VISIBLE
page — the in-app pane reports `document.hidden`, and the API aborts there — paused at 60/150/240ms
to read the frames, which is how the ghosting was found and then confirmed gone; and a real CLICK
on the toggle, which started exactly one transition, marked the document, and cleared it after the
navigation redirected (the guard doing its job, since `/focus` needs auth). `tsc` clean ·
**2658 tests / 175 files** · eslint clean on every file touched.

### Recorded, not started
- `app-shell.tsx` carries one pre-existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error in the sidebar's
  older-install migration — untouched by this work, and restructuring it is its own change.

## One optical scale, surfaces that catch light, and a focal point — 2026-09-24

The user: the app "looks so much boring and old… I like Linear and Notion quality and smoothness and
all experience in my application and aesthetics also, but more better way". Measured before touching
anything, because "boring" is a symptom and three of its causes were findable.

**What was actually wrong**
- **Two type systems disagreeing at the same size.** Zenboard carries the Tailwind-v4 pairs in
  `ds-theme.css` (`--text-ui--letter-spacing`) and the role tokens in `globals.css`
  (`--text-h1-tracking`). They overlap at the same pixel sizes and did not agree there — measured
  in the browser: 12px `caption` **+0.02em** vs `meta` normal · 16px `editor` −0.0144em vs `lead`
  **normal** · 24px `title-2` **normal** vs its neighbours at −0.018 · 30px `title-1` −0.0143em vs
  `h1` **−0.01em**. The same size set differently depending on which class a component happened to
  reach for. That is what makes an interface look like several hands built it, and no screenshot
  review finds it.
- **No surface was made of anything.** Every dark surface is a flat fill with one hairline. Linear,
  Raycast, Vercel and Arc all draw a single pixel of light along the top of raised material, where
  a real surface catches the room; Notion (a document, lit like paper) does not — and Zenboard had
  Notion's palette with neither.
- **Home had no focal point.** Five cards, five identical grey header bands, and the ONE thing you
  are meant to do first — the highlight — carried exactly as much weight as "Content today".

**What shipped**
- **One optical curve**, applied across BOTH families by size: 12px `0` · 13 −0.006 · 14 −0.011 ·
  15 −0.013 · 16 −0.014 · 18 −0.016 · 20 −0.017 · 22 −0.018 · 24 −0.019 · 30 −0.021 · 40 −0.025em.
  The caps roles (`label`, `micro`, `nano`) keep their positive tracking — capitals need the air,
  which is the tracking CLAUDE.md deliberately kept in 2026-09-08 — and monospace keeps its own
  advance. Fixed on the way: `caption` was declared 11px in one file and rendered at 12px from the
  other, so its 0.04em landed as 0.037em on the app's most common meta text; and `stat` (the number
  on a StatCard) sat at −0.01 while every other 24px role was −0.019.
- **`--edge-light`**, the specular edge: `inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.045)` in dark, carried
  by `--shadow-md` (every menu and popover), `--shadow-panel` (every Home card) and the card recipe
  through a new `surface-edge` utility — a card SITS, so it gets material, not elevation. In light
  it is `inset 0 0 0 0 transparent`, **not `none`**: `none` inside a box-shadow list invalidates
  the whole declaration and would have silently deleted every composed shadow in the light theme.
- **The highlight is the hero**: its title is `text-title-3` (22px on the curve) where it was 16px,
  its flame and star carry the accent — the one hue, on the one thing that means "this one" — and
  it has the room to breathe. No second filled button: the house allows one, the plan's Add holds
  it, so the hierarchy is type and hue.

**Proved** — `app/type-scale.test.ts`: reads both families, normalises px and em to one unit, and
asserts one tracking per size (allowing only the rounding that two units of the same decision
produce), a curve that never loosens as it grows, no positive tracking on anything ≥12px, and the
biggest type tightest — mutation-checked by loosening 28px, which fails the curve. It also pins the
edge in both themes, including that the light value is a transparent SHADOW rather than `none`.
Home, Tasks captured before and after in dark, Home in light (no regression, shadows intact).
`tsc` clean · **2665 tests / 176 files** · eslint clean on the files touched.

### Recorded, not started
- `--shadow-popover` is a phantom: no component uses the class, nothing defines the token in the
  default skin, and CLAUDE.md's popover rule still names it. Overlays actually use `OVERLAY_CLASS`
  (`shadow-md`). Either define it or amend the rule — one line, its own change.

## First run, first second, and paper you can see — 2026-09-24

Three pieces, from three notes in one sitting: the Adaline reference for the sign-up/onboarding
flow, "when 1st time open application I want an animated Zenboard logo animation like this"
(Figma's boot screen), and "current paper UI looks so basic — think deeper; I want a 100% real
looking authentic analog paper experience".

### Onboarding builds the first day, beside what it builds

The reference puts the product next to the form and lets it answer what you type. Zenboard's
onboarding does more than collect facts — it creates a project, today's tasks with the first one
starred, and a day-end time — so the preview is **Home itself**, drawn with the app's own `Panel`,
rows, `Checkbox` and star, filling in as the answers arrive: the tasks appear as rows, the project
rides along on each one, and the first task carries the accent star, which is exactly what
`finish()` writes. It is inert (`aria-hidden`, no pointer events, no tab stop) and drops away below
`lg`. The step header carries the progress the reference uses — a dash per step and "2 of 3", with
the count in words.

**The defect underneath it was worse than the layout.** Every step wrote through a server action and
read NONE of the results. These actions RETURN `{ error }` — they do not throw — so a try/catch
would not have helped either: step 1 advanced with no profile saved, `finish()` navigated to a Home
with no project and no tasks, and `skip()` could leave `onboarding_complete` unset, which hands the
same person the same flow at their next sign-in. Every write is now read, every failure says so and
keeps the answers, and nothing navigates until what it promised exists.

Also fixed: the preview computed its greeting from `new Date()` during render, so the server and the
browser disagreed about the time of day and React threw the tree away — the page went blank. The
hour is a prop from the server now, which is how Home has always done it.

### The first second

`BootSplash`: the mark and a filling bar on the app's own ground, **once per session**, gone the
moment the app is ready (a minimum 420ms so it cannot flicker past, then a 260ms fade). It covers
the frame where fonts swap and the shell measures itself — the least finished the app ever looks.

The flag is stamped by the blocking boot script in `lib/theme.ts`, before first paint, so a session
that has already booted never paints the splash at all; doing it in an effect would flash it on
every route change. The component holds NO React state — its whole lifecycle is two attributes on
`<html>` — so it can never be mid-unmount while the CSS is mid-fade. Reduced motion keeps the cover
and drops the movement, through same-name keyframe twins.

### Paper you can see

More texture was never going to fix "basic". Measured: the desk was `#EAE6DB` against a `#FAF8F2`
sheet — **1.17:1**. Nothing was lying on anything, which is why the skin read as a beige app no
matter how good the grain was. A sheet on a real desk sits at ~1.4–1.6:1 against what it is lying
on. The desk is linen board now at **1.43:1**, with the ink still at 10.5:1 for the few things that
sit directly on it.

With that separation earned, the material became worth modelling:
- **A sheet has thickness.** The first pass modelled a SCAN (flat, shadowless — a scanner presses
  the depth out of paper). A sheet on a desk has a cut edge that catches light, light that falls off
  toward its border, and a short contact shadow — in INK, never black, because a shadow on paper is
  the colour of the light that made it.
- **Laid lines** — the mould's fine ribs, at 2%, felt rather than seen.
- **The desk is ruled** (engineering paper, from the references) — on the DESK only: a grid running
  under text is a spreadsheet, not a sheet.
- **The page lies ON the desk**: in this skin the content pane is a sheet with a real measure
  (1120px), centred, with the ruled desk showing on every side and its own contact shadow between.

**Proved** — `components/onboarding/onboarding.test.ts` (8): every write read back, each guard
above the navigation, the split, the inert preview drawn from real components, the star matching
what `finish()` writes, no clock in render, the progress in words. `app/theme-paper.test.ts` now
holds the sheet-on-desk model instead of the scan: ink-coloured contact shadow with ≤6px blur, the
cut edge, **the ≥1.35:1 desk separation**, ruling on the desk but not on sheets, and the page on
the desk. Browser: onboarding driven at each step (typing a project and two tasks put them in the
preview with the project chip and the accent star), the splash captured mid-flight in both themes
and confirmed once-per-session, the paper shell and Documents re-captured on the new desk.
`tsc` clean · **2676 tests / 177 files** · eslint clean on the files touched.

### Recorded, not started — what "100% authentic analog paper" still needs
The remaining gap is STRUCTURE, not texture, and it is a design project rather than a token pass:
sheets as discrete objects with real page proportions (not panels that span the pane), slips and
index cards for short-lived things, the sidebar as folder tabs (the manila reference), statuses as
printed stamps, and checkboxes as printed boxes with an ink tick. Each of those trades density or
full-width views for realism, which is a decision to take deliberately rather than by drift.

### Printed objects, not web controls — 2026-09-24 (paper, continued)

The last thing giving the skin away was the controls. A checkbox that fills solid with the accent,
a badge shaped like a pill, a chooser with a sliding thumb: none of those exist on paper, and no
amount of stock underneath fixes it. On a form, a checkbox is a PRINTED BOX and the tick is added
in ink; a status is a STAMP, boxed and set in capitals in the ink it was stamped with; a chooser is
a row of RULED CELLS with the chosen one inked solid.

All three are reached through the design system's own `data-slot`, so no component knows the skin
exists — `Badge` and `SegmentedControl` had no slot and were given one (the house already marks its
parts that way) rather than taught about paper. Measured in the browser: a checked box in this skin
is `background: transparent`, border and tick `#24221C` — where the default skin fills it with the
accent. Finance now reads as a printed ledger: mono column heads, mono figures, ruled rows, and
DRAFT / SENT / OVERDUE / PAID / VOID stamped in their own inks.

Guarded in `app/theme-paper.test.ts` (printed controls + every control reached through a slot);
**2678 tests / 177 files**, `tsc` and eslint clean.

## The board said six and showed fourteen — 2026-09-24

From a screenshot of the user's own week board: the header read **"Unscheduled 6"** above a column
of roughly fourteen rows, nearly all struck through. Two readings of the same pile — the header
counted only OPEN tasks (`!t.done`), the column rendered `order['inbox']` whole, finished work
included. A task that is done and was never scheduled is not waiting to be planned; it is just
done, and it was burying the six things that were.

**What shipped** — the column and the count are one derivation now (`inboxIds`), used by the list,
its sortable context and its empty line. It is NOT a blunt `!done`: the board took the shared
settling hook (`lib/use-settling.ts`, SETTLE_MS 3000) that every other list already uses, so a task
ticked ON the board holds its place, struck through, for the beat before it leaves — it never
vanishes under the pointer that ticked it. The DAY columns keep their completed tasks, because
there a finished task is the record of that day, and the "1 done" stat beside it counts exactly
those.

**Proved** — `components/week/week-board.test.ts` gained three: the single derivation (and that
`order['inbox']` is no longer mapped directly), the settling hold/release on toggle, and the day
columns still rendering their full order. In the browser the header and the column now agree (2 and
2); the disappearance after the beat could not be exercised there because the harness's toggle is a
server action that rejects without a session and the optimistic update correctly reverts.
`tsc` clean · eslint clean.

## The sheet stopped being a fixed size, and paper learned to speak — 2026-09-24

Two notes from the user on the live Paper skin: "there is a responsiveness issue, that fixed size
looks weird", and "fonts also need to match the paper aesthetics — the fonts are not matching".

**The fixed size was mine.** Making the page a sheet, I capped it at 1120px — which turned every
wide screen into a narrow app sitting in a field of desk. A bigger desk holds a BIGGER SHEET, not
the same sheet with more desk around it. The margin scales now (`clamp(8px, 1.5vw, 28px)`), the
sheet takes the rest, and the working surfaces — a board, a calendar, a table — keep every pixel
they can get at any width.

**The voice was the last thing saying "web app" out loud.** Geist is a screen grotesk, drawn for
pixels and at home beside a cursor; paper has two voices and neither is that. TEXT is set in a book
serif and DATA on a typewriter's grid, which is exactly the division every one of the references
uses. Source Serif 4 was already loaded by the app (`--font-serif`), so re-voicing the skin costs
nothing to ship and nothing to download: two lines, and every word in the skin changes, while the
overline labels, tabular figures and IDs stay monospaced.

**Proved** — `app/theme-paper.test.ts`: the scaling margin (and that the sheet carries NO
`max-width`), and the two voices — the serif on `--font-sans`/`--font-ui`, the mono still on the
label and figure roles. Captured at 1920, 1600 and 820: the desk margin holds at every width and
the sheet fills the rest. `tsc` clean · **2682 tests / 177 files** · eslint clean.

## Paper, reworked against its references — and PAUSED — 2026-09-24

The user sent a letterpress invoice, a vintage book cover and two photographs of a Kindle, asking
for the Paper skin "same to same". Eleven commits (`8dc4766` → `f993133`). **Paused on the user's
word** ("pause on paper theme") with everything committed and green; nothing is half-applied.

**What shipped**
- **Two colours, enforced by measuring the rendered page.** Three separate families carried hue and
  each looked correct in the stylesheet: the accent came back as an INLINE style from `lib/theme.ts`
  (no stylesheet can beat that — now branched on the skin in both the runtime and the pre-paint boot
  script), entity labels via `--color-label-*`, and an amber that outlasted both via `--scope-*`.
  Home measures 0 coloured elements.
- **Rules are ink** (`#5E5849`, 6.2:1), not a mid-beige hairline — the "sharpness looks weird" note
  was about a line that was neither ink nor absent. Panels draw their own ring because `.shadow-panel`
  does not read `--shadow-panel`; the token override had drawn nothing.
- **White cells on a dark ground.** Two wrong turns first: a desk model that made everything grey mud,
  then one flat pale sheet that fixed the mud by deleting the contrast. The reference's own header
  settled it — the cells are white, the ground between them is dark. Beige CELLS were the problem.
- **Nothing is filled.** The tinted panel ground served neither reference: the invoice's cells are
  white and its bands hatched; a Kindle has no fills at all. Panel headers are ruled instead.
- **One grain, because `multiply` compounds.** Four layers tuned in isolation multiplied a white `#FC`
  card to `#8D`. Mottle and fibre deleted; the guard now checks the PRODUCT arithmetically.
- **Ink breaks up** on the mark and icons via an ALPHA mask (a blend cannot lighten dark ink).
- Also: flat page (no gloss, no drop shadow), register dots at cell corners, boxed table cell grid,
  hatched table heads, loaders as blank ruled cells, e-ink motion (the ladder collapses to a repaint).

**The decision that mattered.** Four bugs this sprint shared one cause: styling a hook the app does
not use. Only probing computed styles in the browser caught them. The standing rule for any skin work:
measure what RENDERS, never trust the stylesheet.

**Verified** — 2686 tests / 177 files, tsc and eslint clean at every commit; each change checked in
the browser, several at 4–6× zoom.

**Owed, for when Paper resumes**
- **An invoice and a Kindle are opposite objects** (boxed and dense vs unboxed and typographic). Paper
  has faithfully built the invoice. The Kindle feeling belongs on READING surfaces — the Docs editor —
  as its own sprint: serif at reading size, ~1.6 leading, a real measure, no chrome.
- Invoice line items are a hand-rolled CSS grid, not the DS table, so the cell grid cannot reach them.
- The ground's hatch is declared but covered by the shell's `var(--canvas)`, so it renders only in gaps.
- **Push blocked**: no GitHub credential on this machine; all commits are local.

## One table, and the row vocabulary it shares with every list — 2026-09-24

The user's brief: make the whole app feel like ONE product — "documents, invoices, tasks" — at
Linear/Notion quality. Measured first, not eyeballed: **zero modules used the DS `DataTable`**, and
`--row-table` (44px), the row token it exists for, was used zero times. Every tabular screen built its
own; Finance built two.

**Why nothing used it** — it was worse than what it should have replaced. Its rows opened on
`<tr onClick>` (no keyboard, no cmd-click, no prefetch — Finance's own rows were real `<Link>`s and had
all three), numbers were set in mono, rows were 40px against their own 44px token, selection washed
in `berry-100` where every other row uses `surface-selected`. Adopting it would have LOST quality.

**What shipped**
- `components/ds/ui/row-state.ts` — the one row vocabulary: divider, transition, and the wash. The task
  row (`rowSurface`) and the table both read it now; they had already drifted (berry vs
  surface-selected, instant vs fast) while each file stayed internally consistent.
- **A row is a link**: `rowHref` puts a real Next `<Link>` in the primary cell, its `::after` stretched
  over the row. Keyboard focus washes the ROW. `onRowOpen` rows are focusable, Enter/Space opens.
- **Hover means clickable**: a row that opens nothing gets no hover wash. A wash is a promise.
- Numbers in the UI face with `tabular-nums`; mono only for identifier columns (`mono: true`).
- Finance's invoice list and an invoice's line items both moved onto it; the list gained sorting.
  The line-item EDITOR stays a grid of inputs — it is a form, not a table.

**Proved** — `components/ds/ui/data-table.test.ts` (11): the token, the stretched link, keyboard open,
mono-for-IDs, the shared vocabulary, hover-only-when-interactive, and a scan that fails any module
hand-rolling a table (`gridTemplateColumns`) outside six declared, reasoned exceptions — with a
stale-exception check that doubles as the scanner's control. In the browser: invoice rows 44px, and a
click at the centre of EVERY cell hits the row's `<a>`; line items 44px, no wash, no link, no divider
under the last. **2697 tests / 178 files** · tsc clean · eslint clean.

**Owed** — other lists (clients, projects, forms responses) are flex rows, not tables; each should be
checked against the same vocabulary next.

## Chat, C1 — a Slack-style conversation per project, with the client in it — 2026-09-25

The user: *"introduce a chat feature — from the client to me and other users of the application"*, then
*"same to same like Slack"*. Plan and benchmark in `CHAT_PLAN.md`.

**What shipped** — Messages in the sidebar and ⌘K; a channel per project with a client, grouped by client
like Slack's sections; unread counts; the conversation with author runs, day dividers and a "New" line;
a one-line composer (Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks, an IME's Enter never sends); optimistic sends that
turn into "Not sent · Retry" rather than vanishing. The CLIENT has the same conversation, drawn by the
same components, as a Messages section in their portal. Migration `0043_project_messages.sql`, gated by
`chatSupported()`: before it is applied the page says so and the portal shows no Messages section.

**The decisions that mattered**
- **A conversation belongs to a PROJECT**, because the portal token is a project token. A leaked link can
  then never read more than the portal already exposes; per-client chat would widen that to every project
  the client has.
- **The client has no RLS policy at all.** Every client call re-resolves the token on the service role,
  scoped to that one project, can only author as `client`, and is burst-capped. The owner's inserts are
  held to `author = 'team'` by the database itself.
- **Delivery**: the owner's side streams over its OWN realtime channel into state — never the shared
  `RealtimeSync`, which answers every change with a ~1.2s `router.refresh()`. The client polls through
  the token action while the tab is visible, because streaming to an anonymous reader would need an anon
  SELECT policy exposing every project's messages.
- **Team chat was NOT built**: Zenboard has no multi-user model, and adding one means rewriting RLS on
  every table. Awaiting the user's decision; nothing here is wasted by it.

**Proved** — `lib/chat.test.ts` (16: runs, dividers, the unread line, optimistic ordering, the body bound),
`lib/actions/chat.test.ts` (15 security guards, MUTATION-TESTED: exporting the service-role resolver,
posting as the team through a link, trusting a disabled portal and dropping the burst cap each fail a
guard — the burst guard first MISSED its mutant and was tightened), `lib/chat-ui.test.ts` (6: a failed
send renders an alert; markup in a message renders as text). In the browser, both sides and both themes:
Shift+Enter breaks without sending, Enter sends instantly (pending ink → confirmed ink), the author name
holds through confirmation (a harness flicker was caught and fixed), the unread badge clears on open.
**2733 tests / 181 files** · tsc clean · eslint clean on every chat file.

**Owed**
- **Migration 0043 must be applied** (paste `supabase/migrations/0043_project_messages.sql`). Until then
  Messages says so and nothing breaks.
- C2: edit/delete, hover actions, a "New messages" jump pill, older history. C3 threads and reactions.
  C4 files and Bell notifications.
- Two PRE-EXISTING `set-state-in-effect` lint errors in `components/shell/app-shell.tsx` (line 669) and
  `command-palette.tsx`, present at HEAD before this sprint; left for their own change.
